title: Manual QA
description:
We are seeking a Manual QA Analyst to support testing for a Point of Sale (POS) project. The role involves developing test cases, executing functional tests, tracking defects, and validating application behaviour across devices and connected peripherals. The ideal candidate is a strong individual contributor who can work independently and communicate effectively with cross-functional teams.

Office Location: Toronto – North York

Employment Type: Permanent

Role Type: New position – current requirement

Work Arrangement: Hybrid (4 days in office)

Position Responsibilities:

  • Review business requirements and acceptance criteria to identify test scenarios and ensure comprehensive test coverage.
  • Develop, maintain, and execute manual test cases for functional, regression, integration, and end-to-end testing.
  • Validate POS application functionality and interactions with devices such as PIN pads, receipt printers, and other connected peripherals.
  • Test transaction workflows, device connectivity, error handling, and recovery scenarios.
  • Identify, document, and track defects, providing clear reproduction steps and supporting evidence.
  • Collaborate with developers, business analysts, and product teams to clarify requirements, resolve defects, and validate fixes.
  • Prepare test execution reports and communicate testing progress, risks, and blockers.
  • Manage assigned testing activities independently and contribute to timely delivery.


Requirements

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 5–7 years of experience in software quality assurance, with a strong focus on manual testing.
  • Strong experience in functional testing, test scenario identification, and test case development and execution.
  • Experience with defect tracking throughout the defect lifecycle, including reporting, retesting, and closure.
  • Ability to translate business requirements into clear, comprehensive test cases.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently and take ownership of assigned deliverables.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Device or mobile testing experience is highly preferred, particularly testing involving PIN pads, printers, or other POS peripherals.
  • Experience in retail or Point of Sale environments.
  • Familiarity with retail transaction workflows, including purchases, returns, refunds, discounts, and payment processing.
  • Experience using test management and defect tracking tools.



Benefits

Salary Range: $50,000 to $65,000 CAD/ year

title: Quality Inspector
description:
Worker Type

Regular


Job Description

Summary

AV is seeking a Quality Inspector to become a part of a dynamic Quality team, reporting directly to the Quality Manager. The candidate will perform Inspection of purchased parts and materials for conformity to standards, specifications, and processing requirements as materials are received from external providers. This person shall determine or assist in determining methods, sequences, and procedures necessary for inspection. Works from released drawings, procedures, and specifications. Adapts inspection measuring devices and procedures where necessary. The candidate would be required to communicate between multiple departments and report key information to stakeholders in a timely manner. Must be dedicated to the quality function and possess a drive to enhance the quality of both the product and processes.


Position Responsibilities

  • Good team player who can work efficiently with minimal supervision.
  • Maintain a clean and organized workspace.
  • Able to comply with all health, safety, and security regulations.
  • Prioritize daily inspection requirements.
  • Excellent attention to detail and critical thinking skills.
  • Review and comprehend engineering and program requirements such as engineering drawings, models, and specifications, and perform inspections using tools such as micrometers, gauges, microscopes, micrometers, telescope gauges, and optical comparators.
  • Verifies specifications referencing purchase orders, blueprints, drawing or inspection instructions, and checklists.
  • Apply sampling principles to material inspections.
  • Makes pass/fail decisions on inspected goods. Maintains records of results
  • Visually inspects for obvious defects or damage such as corrosion, cracks, dents, scratches, and pits.
  • Prepare inspection reports regarding conformance, initiate nonconformance reports, and quarantine material when needed.
  • Create discrepancy reports for suspect or identified counterfeit parts.
  • Perform inspections per IPC-610/620.
  • Perform First Article Inspections, incoming inspections, and final inspections.
  • Assist with calibration of quality control equipment.
  • Calibration Technician backup.
  • Able to train a quality inspection level 1 and 2.
  • Foreign object debris/damage point of contact.
  • Run statistical studies such as reproducibility and capability.
  • Familiar with statistical process control methodologies.
  • Prepare and maintain test data for review.
  • Identify areas for quality control improvements.
  • On material returned from repair, confirm repairs and product quality.
  • Perform mechanical, dimensional, visual, and documentation inspections of machined, fabricated, molded, and assembled components.
  • Interpret engineering drawings, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T), datum structures, revisions, and inspection criteria.
  • Use precision measuring equipment --including calipers, micrometers, height gauges, pin and plug gauges, thread gauges, surface plates, optical comparators, and coordinate measuring machines (CMMs) as applicable.
  • Verify material certifications, special-process certifications, first-article inspection documentation, and other supplier or production records.

Basic Qualifications (Required Skills & Competencies)

  • High School Diploma or Equivalent
  • IPC-610-620 Certified or able to be re-certified
  • Familiar with ISO and AS Quality Management Systems.
  • Experience with inspection tools (calipers, micrometers, height gauge, etc.).
  • Experience reading and understanding engineering drawings, aerospace certifications, and test reports.
  • Experience receiving packages, data entry, organizing, and scanning documentation.
  • Familiar with ESD and proper material handling procedures.
  • Qualified candidates should possess a high school diploma or equivalent.
  • Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications.
  • Technical Math: Basic shop math; Measurement systems (units and conversion); and Numeric conversions (decimals, fractions, scientific notation)

Other Qualifications & Desired Competencies

  • 3+ years of inspection, precision, mechanical, or metrological inspection experience.
  • Experience with the use of metrology tools and gauges.
  • Experience within the aerospace, automotive, semiconductor, or electronic fields.
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and specifications.
  • Associate degree, technical certificate, or completed vocational training in mechanical technology, manufacturing technology, metrology, quality, or a related field.
  • Experience with advanced inspection methods or equipment, including:
    • CMM programming or operation
    • Portable CMM or articulated-arm measurement systems
    • Vision systems or optical comparators
    • Surface-roughness measurement
    • Digital inspection and reporting software
  • Familiarity with inspection of machined parts, sheet-metal components, composites, additive-manufactured parts, electrical-mechanical assemblies, or flight hardware.
  • Experience performing or supporting AS9102 first-article inspections.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

  • Ability to work in an office, engineering laboratory, and manufacturing environment
  • Ability to wear required personal protective equipment
  • Frequently required to stand, walk, sit, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls, reach with hands and arms, climb stairs, talk or hear
  • Occasionally lift or move up to 25 pounds with or without assistance
  • Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus


Clearance Level

No Clearance

The salary range for this role is:

$56,500 - $86,250

title: Cloud & DevOps Engineer
description:
Company Description


EZAC Technologies is a technology firm that delivers intelligent, secure, and scalable digital solutions for businesses and organizations. The company combines AI, software development, automation, cloud infrastructure, IT solutions, and cybersecurity to solve complex challenges through practical technology. Its focus is on building innovative, purposeful, and reliable solutions that support long-term digital transformation. EZAC Technologies helps organizations improve efficiency, strengthen capabilities, and adopt future-ready digital strategies. By aligning technology with strategic thinking, the company creates digital products, AI-driven automation, cloud solutions, IT infrastructure, and security services that deliver meaningful impact.


Role Description


The Cloud & DevOps Engineer is a full-time, on-site role based in Islamabad. The person in this role will design, implement, and maintain cloud infrastructure, ensuring scalability, security, and high availability for production and development environments. Day-to-day responsibilities include building and managing CI pipelines, automating deployments, monitoring system performance, and troubleshooting infrastructure or application issues. The Cloud & DevOps Engineer will collaborate closely with software development teams to streamline release processes, optimize environments, and improve reliability through proactive automation and configuration management. This role also involves documenting infrastructure, following best practices, and contributing to continuous improvement of DevOps workflows and cloud architecture.


Qualifications



  • Strong skills in Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and cloud configuration management to build and maintain reproducible environments.

  • Experience with Software Development practices to collaborate effectively with engineering teams and support application lifecycle workflows.

  • Hands-on expertise in Continuous Integration and related tooling to automate builds, testing, and deployments.

  • Solid System Administration background with proficiency in Linux for managing servers, containers, and cloud resources.

  • Knowledge of major cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP) and containerization/orchestration tools (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes).

  • Familiarity with monitoring, logging, and alerting tools to ensure reliability, performance, and incident response.

  • Ability to write scripts (e.g., Bash, Python) to automate routine tasks and optimize infrastructure operations.

  • Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and ability to work in a collaborative, cross-functional environment.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

title: Interactive Response Technology (IRT) Implementation Analyst
description:
Use Your Power for Purpose

The Global Clinical Supply (GCS) Interactive Response Technology (IRT) Implementation Analyst is a position within Global Central Operations Network (GCON) GCS Strategic Hubs (GSH) team and will be based in Philippines. The IRT Implementation Analyst will be reporting to the GSH Team Lead in Philippines, with a matrix reporting relationship to the Engagement Leader, IRT Global Oversight Team (IGOT) within Clinical Supply Informatics & Technology (CSIT).

GCS manages the execution of supply chain strategies to deliver Investigational Medicinal Product to patients involved in Pfizer’s clinical research trials across the globe.

IGOT is a well-established high performing team within Pfizer's GCS unit striving to deliver best in class IRT systems providing randomization and drug management capabilities in support of Pfizer's dynamic investigational product portfolio. The patients we serve are our number one priority and IGOT aims to employ the highest quality standards across our internal and vendor IRT solutions. As part of an innovative clinical supply chain, we routinely challenge the status quo in efforts to optimize our systems and processes.

The IRT Implementation Analyst is an individual contributor who performs defined implementation activities under the direction of an accountable IRT Lead, Design Lead, or functional lead. Responsibility and independence will expand progressively based on completion of required training, demonstrated proficiency, and role readiness.


This role requires providing support across other global time zones based on business need, specifically from 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m Philippine Time or 9:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. Philippine Time (equivalent to 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. U. S. Eastern Time).


What You Will Achieve


The IRT Implementation Analyst is a new role within the IRT IGOT that will support requirements and system development. The implementation of this dedicated function within IGOT is intended to ensure the delivery of high-quality IRT systems through focused system expertise while improving velocity in support of Pfizer’s evolving portfolio.


The IRT Implementation Analyst will go through a robust onboarding and technical training period where they will partner closely with IGOT’s IRT Leads and Design Leads to develop proficiency in conducting preliminary protocol assessments, eliciting protocol requirements, and designing and configuring study builds on Pfizer’s internal IRT system.


The IRT Implementation Analyst will support Implementation team members by organizing and facilitating meetings, capturing meeting minutes, creating and reviewing IRT supportive documents, and delivering investigator meeting slides to clinical teams and site personnel. IRT Implementation Analysts will also support line leads in collaborating with study team and supply chain personnel to resolve issues, understand how study requirements are configured and supported post study go-live, and for ongoing studies, be available for guidance on IRT resupply settings and any requisite system amendments.


The IRT Implementation Analyst will also learn how quality investigations, Correction Action/ Preventive Action (CAPA) commitments and continuous improvements, Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) review and revision activities, support regulatory inspections, and limited duration teams are created and executed.


For this position candidates will need to have excellent technical and analytical thinking skills, be a creative problem solver, and have a strong commitment to quality to successfully deliver optimal IRT systems across a diverse and dynamic portfolio


Role Responsibilities:

  • Support the delivery plan for IRT configuration and testing activities.
  • Support the elicitation and documentation of system requirements for new and amended studies in partnership with the study team.
  • Support the development and execution of User Acceptance Testing (UAT) test plans.
  • Participate in cross line initiatives, quality investigations, SOP development, and process improvement.
  • Will be trained to create IRT supportive documents and deliver investigator meeting slides to clinical teams and site personnel.
  • Support for Assigned Projects: Aid in the design, delivery, and management of activities related to assigned projects.
  • Participate in study and functional meetings and provide clear updates on assigned activities, risks, actions, and deliverables under the guidance of the accountable IRT Lead, Design Lead, or functional lead
  • Coordinate and execute assigned activities across multiple studies or projects, manage competing priorities, and meet agreed timelines and quality expectations.
  • Use appropriate metrics to measure progress on goals, develop and implement key performance indicators (KPI) to track and measure progress towards strategic goals and ensure value-driven outcomes.
  • Adapt and response quickly to changing business needs and deliver results in challenging first-time situation.
  • Provide timely and actionable insights to stakeholders to support decision-making and strategic planning.
  • Apply approved procedures, standards, and training to resolve routine issues within assigned activities; identify risks, exceptions, or unclear requirements and escalate them promptly to the accountable lead undefined
  • Attend periodic meetings with teams in other global time zones outside of normal work hours.

Here Is What You Need (Minimum Requirements):

  • Associate degree or BA degree in computer science, life science, or business field desired in biopharma industry
  • 1-3 years demonstrated and relevant experience in pharma/biotech and cross-functional team,
  • Possess excellent English language written and verbal communication
  • Interpersonal, collaboration and business partnership capabilities required
  • Comfortable working with a global team, partners, and customers in a change agile environment

Bonus Points If You Have (Preferred Requirements):

  • Clinical supply chain, project management, business analysis, and/or continuous improvement experience
  • Adaptability to changing priorities and requirements
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment

Work Location Assignment: Hybrid

title: FA Hub Lead
description:
Job Title

FA Hub Lead

Job Description Summary

Responsible for managing CMFA Pool requests, conducting financial analysis, developing and auditing pricing, valuation, and Argus models, and presenting key insights and summaries to stakeholders.

Job Description

About the Role:

  • Support the execution of financial analysis/modeling requests according to quality and timeliness standards
  • Prepare pro forma statements, discounted cash flow analysis using Argus Enterprise, and Excel-based financial models with consideration of market conditions (both current and historical)
  • Conduct audits of existing financial models for accuracy of model inputs and validity of assumptions
  • Conduct market research to analyze property and market conditions; synthesize findings in a clear, concise manner
  • Communicate with the onshore Pool team to confirm request scope and review analysis findings; demonstrate the ability to communicate findings in a clear, compelling manner, answer clarifying questions, and make timely, accurate revisions
  • Identify and communicate any missing information or unclear requests to ensure accurate analysis
  • Develop high-level analysis summaries by identifying transaction considerations (strengths/weaknesses), trends, outliers, and logical inconsistencies
  • Assist and mentor Analysts as they gain experience
  • Track and develop a working knowledge of real estate fundamentals and industry trends
  • Support the CMFA Pool’s maturity by supporting process improvement and automation initiatives through communicating improvement opportunities and suggesting potential solutions
  • Performs other related duties as required or requested.

About you:


  • Bachelor’s Degree (Business, Finance, Accounting, Real Estate, etc.) preferred
  • 8-10 years of financial analysis and modeling experience.
  • Experience with Argus and other discounted cash flow tools required
  • English language proficiency (verbal and written) to communicate with US-based CMFA Pool team members is required
  • Highly proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, especially in Microsoft Excel
  • Passion for client delivery, with strong emphasis on producing high-quality work, meeting deadlines, and exceeding requestor expectations
  • Strong analytical skills with high attention to detail and accuracy
  • Demonstrated strong time management and organizational skills

Job Title

Commercial Painter- 2nd Shift

Job Description Summary

Does skilled work in preparing surfaces and in mixing, matching, and applying paint and related materials by brush, roller, or spray equipment to machinery, equipment, furniture, and the interior and exterior of buildings and other structures; acts as lead or supervises other employees engaged in such work; and does related work.

Job Description


Distinguishing Features: Painters and Senior Painters are responsible for the proper preparation and application of painting materials to a wide variety of interior and exterior surfaces. They frequently work with unpleasant or poisonous fumes and materials and may work in high places or in confined spaces, in the vicinity of energized, high voltage electrical equipment, or under other potentially hazardous conditions. Painters and Senior Painters may occasionally paint automotive equipment, signs, or traffic and other control markings.


However, full-time assignments to such painting work are performed by employees in the classes of Auto Painter, Sign Painter, and Traffic Painter and Sign Poster.

A Painter normally receives assignments from a Senior Painter or a Painter Supervisor who inspects the work for quantity, quality and safe performance. A Senior Painter usually receives assignments from a Painter Supervisor who also inspects the Senior's work. A Senior Painter spends a substantial portion of time working with the tools of the craft while acting as a lead-worker for a small crew of Painters and helpers.

A Painter Supervisor is responsible for determining painting needs, estimating costs, deciding on methods of preparation and types of materials to be used, and assuring that all necessary safety precautions are enforced. A Painter Supervisor typically supervises several painting crews and is evaluated in terms of the success achieved in directing a diversified painting program.

Examples of Duties: Painter: Removes old paint and other finishes by chipping, burning, scaling, scraping, sanding, dissolving, water blasting, or sandblasting; mixes paint and matches colors; prepares surfaces for painting by dusting, wire brushing, washing, and patching holes, dents, and cracks; applies a variety of primers, paints, and other materials by brush, roller, or spray equipment to such surfaces as wood, metal, fiber, plaster, wall board, brick, cement, and canvas; mixes and applies protective coatings such as epoxy and fiberglass; refinishes floors and furniture; protects other surfaces from spattered or sprayed paint; adjusts and maintains spray equipment; cleans brushes and other painting equipment; glazes, re-putties, and makes minor repairs to metal and wood sash; applies decals, warning stripes, and slip proof materials; inspects ladders for defects; erects scaffolding; may rig and use swing stage equipment and boatswain's chairs for painting high exterior walls; may hang wallpaper and other wall coverings and patch plaster; may apply roof coatings and sealers by spray application; may estimate time and materials required for jobs; orders paint and other supplies; and maintains inventories; and may occasionally do sign painting with stencils and paint automotive equipment.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.

Under the supervision and direction of the Senior Family Partner, the Family Partner is responsible for support and advocacy to parents/caregivers, and facilitation of peer support groups for caregivers. They are directly responsible to the Senior Family Partner and to the Program Director of the Community Service Agency.

Child and Family Services recognizes the power in Diversity and believes that Equity is a Human Right.

$1 per hour Language Differential! (eligible languages include: Cape Verdean Creole, Haitian Creole, Portuguese, Spanish or ASL)

Child & Family Services carefully considers a wide range of factors when determining compensation including, but not limited to, prior experience, education, certification(s), license(s), skills and expertise, location, internal equity and other factors that are job related and consistent with business need. Job Responsibilities & Essential Functions

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

  • Assist the family in understanding the scope and services of the CSA and the family’s roles and responsibilities in the program.

  • Teach parent/caregiver how to network/link and secure necessary community resources and treatment providers. Provide home and community mentoring and education to the parents/caregivers in order to enhance problem-solving, parenting effectiveness, and communication.

When requested by the family, and when clinically appropriate, attends and supports a youth and family at meetings related to the youth's behavioral health needs treatments in any setting.

title: Work Control Clerk
description:
Purpose and Scope:

The Work Control Clerk performs specialized clerical work in coordinating functions for dispatch and maintenance of USAF vehicles, AGE, BEAR Base, and other commodities managed by the Global Prepositioned Materiel Services Program (GPMS).

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Plan and schedule preventive and corrective maintenance; track services; track costs; and record work performance details.
  • Gather, input, retrieve and maintain maintenance information in both computer and manual systems.
  • Provide general clerical work to assure the smooth operation of the Maintenance Department.
  • General clerical duties, including filing, photocopying, faxing, posting of notices, and ordering of parts and supplies as directed.
  • Develop and issue computer reports as requested.
  • Assist with and/or prepare materials.
  • Prepare summary reports of transportation and maintenance costs.
  • Research availability and source of purchase for emergency and critical spare parts and repair parts.
  • Compile information such as identification of items, costs, vendor, freight charges, etc. for purchasing of all maintenance materials.
  • Prepare all purchase requisitions, coordinate, and expedite approvals as required, maintain all budgetary records, and provide follow-up action with accounting, buyers, vendors, requestors and receiving.
  • Review documents for sufficiency and maintaining any necessary follow-up.
  • Maintain all files and inventory records of all orders placed and received, including delivery time schedules.
  • Keep an up-to-date record of materials used so that minimum stock levels are maintained.
  • Performs other duties as assigned

Minimum Position Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Required:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • One (1) to Three (3) years of related clerical experience in related field.
  • Experience with Air Force work order Automated Management Systems (AMS) (e.g., ACES, IEMS, TRIREGA) is preferred.
  • Experience with Maximo is preferred.
  • Must be able to take direction / supervision and work cooperatively with others.
  • Ability to perform general office work.
  • Good communication skills.
  • Ability to use computer and related software programs to accomplish assigned tasks.
  • Knowledge of office practices and procedures.
  • Skill in typing statistical tabulations accurately.
  • Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.
  • Ability to write routine reports and correspondence.
  • Ability to maintain complex records and to assemble and organize data.
  • Must be able to speak, read and write English.

title: Billing Specialist
description:
Position Summary
The Billing Specialist drives the continuous optimization of the end-to-end financial workflows and safeguards the financial integrity of Charter Oak Health Center. Operating within a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) model, this position manages complex medical claims from encounter closure through final adjudication using the eClinicalWorks (eCW) electronic medical record (EMR) and practice management platforms.

Key objectives include safeguarding net revenue capture, maximizing clean claim rates, accelerating cash flow, and proactively managing underpayments and denials. The Revenue Cycle Specialist minimizes revenue leakage, actively reduces Days Sales Outstanding (DSO), and ensures strict adherence to HRSA guidelines, Medicaid/Medicare regulations, and HIPAA compliance laws.

Essential Position Duties

1. Claims Management & Front-End Revenue Capture

  • Daily Claim Auditing: Review, scrub, and validate high-volume medical, dental, and behavioral health encounters within eClinicalWorks to ensure structural and regulatory compliance prior to payer submission.
  • Coding Integrity & Quality Assurance: Audit clinical charts to ensure exact alignment with ICD-10-CM, CPT, and HCPCS Level II coding guidelines, validating proper documentation of modifiers, time-based codes, and FQHC encounter triggers.
  • Clearinghouse Exception Management: Monitor and instantly correct electronic front-end edits and clearinghouse rejections to prevent workflow bottlenecks and maintain a clean claim target of >95%.
  • Data Optimization: Review, append, and modify patient demographic profiles, insurance coordination of benefits (COB), and sliding fee scale tiers within the practice management system to guarantee accurate upfront adjudication.
  • Bottleneck Escalation: Isolate and flag open encounters missing provider signatures, clinical charts, or documentation anomalies, escalating them systematically to providers and the Revenue Cycle Manager to preserve timely filing windows.

2. Denial Management & Accounts Receivable (A/R) Optimization

  • Proactive Denial Resolution: Identify, trend, and appeal unpaid or rejected claims by researching payer-specific policies, utilizing advanced electronic health records (EHR) tools, and executing formal redetermination requests.
  • A/R Aging Management: Aggressively audit outstanding insurance balances within designated 30-, 60-, 90-, and 120+ day aging buckets; formulate strategic follow-up queues to extract overdue reimbursements.
  • Underpayment & Variance Tracking: Review electronic remittance advices (ERAs) and explanation of benefits (EOBs) against FQHC Prospective Payment System (PPS) rate schedules to detect underpayments or unauthorized contractual adjustive variances.
  • Payer Policy Surveillance: Stay current on evolving commercial, Medicaid, and Medicare coverage policies, state filing limitations, and regulatory changes to adjust internal front-end system edits dynamically.
  • Root-Cause Denial Analysis: Review, categorize, and track inbound claim denials within eClinicalWorks (eCW) using standard CARC (Claim Adjustment Reason Codes) and RARC (Remittance Advice Remark Codes) to identify systemic front-end or clinical documentation vulnerabilities.
  • End-to-End Appeal Execution: Draft, assemble, and submit comprehensive, evidence-based appeal packets—including clinical notes, proof of timely filing, and medical necessity documentation—to overturn erroneous payer denials and secure maximum reimbursement.

3. Payment Posting & Financial Reconciliation

  • Review the posting of all insurance payments and contractual adjustments for accuracy; communicate and resolve any payment discrepancies.
  • Process and accurately post patient credit card payments, checks, and cash transactions.
  • Make appropriate financial adjustments, transfer patient balances, and perform fee write-offs in accordance with practice protocols.
  • Reconcile daily payment postings and accounts receivable.
  • Prepare and complete daily bank deposits accurately and maintain cash accountability.
  • Process patient refunds efficiently upon verification of credit balances.

4. Accounts Receivable & Denials Management

  • Regularly follow up on outstanding accounts receivable balances for both insurance payers and self-pay patients.
  • Initiate inquiries and appeals on questionable claim denials, rejections, or unexpected payment adjustments.
  • Monitor aging accounts receivable reports to identify trends, root causes for non-payment, and systemic billing issues.
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of third-party payer guidelines, billing updates, and healthcare regulations impacting claim processing.

5. Patient Financial Counseling & Customer Service

  • Answer inquiries promptly, courteously, and professionally from patients, insurance carriers, and staff regarding accounts and billing statements.
  • Counsel patients regarding high-deductible policies, co-insurance responsibilities, payment plans, and expectations for payment.
  • Assist front office staff with insurance verification, fee schedule inquiries, and patient balance clarity to support smooth check-in and checkout workflows.
  • Manage billing-related telephone calls and written correspondence in a clear and empathetic manner.

Join Cleveland Clinic’s Medina Hospital where research and surgery are advanced, technology is leading-edge, patient care is world-class, and caregivers are family. This 148-bed community-based hospital has been providing the communities in and around Medina County with top-quality patient care for over 75 years. Here, you will work with and learn from some of our best caregivers, receive endless support and appreciation, and build a rewarding career with one of the most respected healthcare organizations in the world.

As an Operating Room (OR) Service Assistant, you will support caregivers by transporting patients and preparing the OR for procedures. Working in an environment focused on advanced technology and innovative patient care, you will gain valuable hands-on experience with medical instruments, surgical procedures, sterilization processes and perioperative support.

This role offers an excellent opportunity to build foundational clinical experience while exploring advanced career paths, professional development opportunities and long-term growth within our caregiver community.

A caregiver in this position works days from 8:00AM – 6:30PM or 7:00AM – 7:30PM, with on-call requirements.

A caregiver who excels in this role will:

  • Maintain surgical instrument sets and equipment and ensure proper sterile conditions.
  • Provide limited assistance to surgeons (e.g., holding limb/retractors, suctioning, sponging wounds).
  • Clean used instruments after surgery (e.g., assembly and maintenance of some instruments for proper cleaning and sterilization).
  • Ensure proper sterile conditions, order supplies and stocks and maintain storage areas in the Operating Room for service.
  • Assist in transporting patients.
  • Assist RN in maintaining a safe environment for the patient.

Minimum qualifications for the ideal future caregiver include:

  • High School Diploma/GED

Preferred qualifications for the ideal future caregiver include:

  • Sterile Processing Certification
  • Two years of experience in sterile processing
  • Prior experience working in an OR setting or with direct patient care experience

Physical Requirements:

  • Requires full range of body motion including handling and lifting patients, manual and finger dexterity and eye-hand coordination. Requires standing and walking for extensive periods of time.
  • Frequently lifts and carries items weighing up to 25 pounds and ability to push, pull, and navigate supply carts weighing up to 200 pounds.
  • Requires corrected vision and hearing to normal range.
  • Requires working under stressful conditions of working irregular hours.
  • Requires some exposure to communicable diseases or bodily fluids.

Personal Protective Equipment:

  • Follows standard precautions using personal protective equipment as required.

description:
As we create a colorful, capable and cleaner world through chemistry, we invite you to join our team to harness the power of chemistry to shape markets, redefine industries and improve lives for billions of people around the world.

CREATING ESSENTIAL CHEMISTRY THAT THE WORLD NEEDS

Powered by chemistry, our products are used in applications that make the products we rely on, processes, and new technologies possible. In key sectors such as clean energy, advanced electronics, high-performance computing and AI, climate friendly cooling, and high-quality paints and coatings for homes and industrial infrastructure---sustainable solutions and more modern living depend on Chemours chemistry.


Chemours is seeking a Site Safety & Occupational Health Specialist to join our growing Thermal and Specialized Solutions Operations team! This position will report directly to the Plant Manager in our El Dorado, Arkansas location.


This is a highly visible, hands-on role serving as the sole Site Safety & Occupational Health Leader onsite. The role provides in-depth safety and health expertise, partnering with site management and serving as a key resource to employees and other stakeholders. Areas of responsibility include safety, contractor safety, occupational health, process safety, fire protection, and ergonomics. As a member of the Site Leadership Team, this role advises site leadership on safety and occupational health risks, priorities, and compliance matters, while serving as the primary liaison between the site and Corporate EHS.

The responsibilities of the position include, but are not limited to, the following:


Occupational Health Function:

  • Serve as a site occupational health resource to leadership and new and existing employees providing knowledge, interpretation, and input for key decision making while understanding the health and status of the program.
  • Maintain up to date and compliant manuals, policies, procedures, record keeping, and make appropriate changes/improvements to create a comprehensive and effective Occupational Health program.
  • Conduct routine OH compliance audits, champion PPE program, HAZCOM program, and serve as the site’s Ergonomic Facilitator and SDS coordinator while providing training and implementation of these programs.
  • Coordinate with the landlord Radiation Safety Officer to ensure Chemours compliance with policy and regulatory requirements.
  • Manages the Air and Noise Monitoring Programs and maintains monitoring equipment.
  • Connect the outside resources to the site that may improve the OH program
  • Maintain the site’s control and documentation of Chemicals and Proprietary products
  • Maintain the Chemical Data Management System

Safety Resource Function:

  • Serve as a site safety resource to leadership and new and existing employees providing knowledge, interpretation (Corporate and OSHA standards), and input for key decision making while understanding the health and status of the program.
  • Maintain up to date and compliant manuals, policies, procedures, record keeping, and make appropriate changes/improvements to create a comprehensive and effective safety program.
  • Lead and participate in First party and Second party Responsible Care audits related to safety and OH practices
  • Represent the Safety in Process Hazards Reviews and Pre-startup Inspections
  • Conduct frequent safety observational behavior-based engagements in the process areas and perform Job Safety Analysis
  • Manage maintaining the site’s Safety Equipment - fire extinguishers, oxygen meters, respirators, ELSA packs, Gastec meters, etc.
  • Serve as site contract administrator to drive contractor safety and engagement.
  • Emergency Response Coordinator to ensure compliance with standards including training, drills and working with landlord EOC.
  • Fire Safety Resource for El Dorado, Arkansas
  • Manage the OSHA recordkeeping in classifying injury and illnesses, including assisting in case management, investigation of information to document rationale for classifying injuries and illnesses, and document information
  • Participation with corporate S&OH, Emergency Response, Fire Safety, Operational Learning and appropriate corporate network meetings.

In order to be qualified for this role, you must possess the following:

  • 3+ years occupational safety experience in the petrochemical/chemical industry, a refinery, or a similar industry
  • Strong leadership abilities to motivate and coach personnel to accomplish regional, department and company-wide strategic goals
  • Experience with OSHA Regulation Compliance and Interpretation
  • Experience conducting safety data analysis and continuous improvement
  • Demonstrated ability to handle multiple tasks and deadlines as well as manage change and work independently.

The following skill sets are preferred by the business unit:

  • Graduate degree in Occupational Safety or Engineering
  • Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university in Occupational Safety and Health, Industrial Hygiene/Safety, Environment Management/Safety Engineering or related field
  • Experience supporting Process Safety Management (PSM) programs in a chemical manufacturing or other high-hazard industrial environment.
  • Preferred candidate would be credentialed as a Certified Safety Professional (CSP), or in the Comprehensive Practice of Industrial Hygiene by the American Board of Industrial Hygiene (or equivalent certification recognized by the International Occupational Hygiene Association National Accreditation Recognition Committee).
  • Experience applying Lean methodologies to maintenance processes and supporting the implementation of business systems

Job Summary:

The Asset Management Coordinator is responsible for coordinating the day-to-day maintenance, upkeep, preservation, and service activities associated with Allied Fabricators LLC’s facilities, property, grounds, offices, restrooms, common areas, and other physical assets.

This position serves as a key coordination point between the Asset & Infrastructure area, internal departments, maintenance personnel, contractors, and service providers to ensure that company property and facilities remain safe, functional, clean, well-maintained, and aligned with company standards.

The role is also responsible for identifying and reporting wear, tear, deterioration, damage, deficiencies, and maintenance needs across company property and ensuring that corrective actions are properly tracked through completion.

Responsibilities:

Facilities & Maintenance Coordination

  • Coordinate day-to-day facility maintenance, repairs, and service needs for buildings, offices, restrooms, common areas, and company property.
  • Receive, prioritize, and track maintenance requests and work orders through completion.
  • Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance activities with internal maintenance personnel and external service providers.
  • Monitor outstanding facility issues and escalate significant or recurring concerns


Property Inspection & Condition Monitoring

  • Conduct routine inspections of buildings, property, and facility assets to identify damage, deterioration, maintenance needs, and potential safety concerns.
  • Document identified deficiencies and initiate appropriate maintenance or service requests.
  • Track corrective actions and verify completion of repairs and services.
  • Maintain inspection and facility condition records to support ongoing maintenance planning.


Grounds, Landscaping & Exterior Areas

  • Coordinate the upkeep of landscaping, parking areas, sidewalks, fencing, signage, exterior lighting, drainage areas, and other exterior property.
  • Monitor grounds and exterior conditions and coordinate required maintenance or corrective action.
  • Coordinate landscaping, pest control, exterior cleaning, and other contracted property services.
  • Help ensure exterior areas remain safe, clean, functional, and professionally maintained.


Restrooms, Offices & Common Areas

  • Monitor the condition, cleanliness, functionality, and appearance of offices, restrooms, conference rooms, break areas, and common spaces.
  • Coordinate repairs, cleaning, replenishment, and other facility services as needed.
  • Monitor facility and janitorial supply levels and coordinate replenishment.
  • Support office moves, workspace changes, furniture installation, and facility setups.


Procurement of Office & Facility Materials

  • Coordinate purchasing of facility supplies, maintenance materials, janitorial products, fixtures, and other Asset & Infrastructure needs.
  • Obtain quotes, prepare purchase requests, track orders, and assist with resolving purchasing or delivery discrepancies.
  • Maintain appropriate inventory levels for commonly used facility supplies and materials.
  • Maintain organized purchasing, warranty, and service documentation.


Vendor & Contractor Coordination

  • Coordinate scheduling, site access, and work requirements for facility vendors, contractors, and service providers.
  • Monitor service completion and contractor performance and communicate concerns as appropriate.
  • Maintain vendor quotes, service records, warranties, invoices, and related documentation.
  • Assist with identifying and coordinating new service providers when needed.


Asset & Infrastructure Support

  • Maintain accurate records for assigned facility assets, equipment, furniture, fixtures, warranties, and service histories.
  • Assist with asset identification, tagging, tracking, transfers, and disposition.
  • Support facility improvement and infrastructure projects through scheduling, procurement, vendor coordination, and documentation.
  • Prepare basic reports on work orders, facility conditions, asset status, maintenance activities, and related expenditures.


Requirements

Qualifications:

  • Experience: 2–4 years of experience in facilities coordination, property management, maintenance coordination, operations, procurement, asset management, or a related field.
  • Experience coordinating contractors, vendors, maintenance personnel, or service providers.
  • Experience with purchasing, work orders, maintenance records, or facility inspections is preferred.
  • Valid driver’s license may be required depending on company operational needs.
  • Education: High school diploma or equivalent required. Associate or Bachelor’s degree in Facilities Management, Business Administration, Operations, Asset Management, Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field is preferred.


Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Basic knowledge of building and facility maintenance.
  • Understanding of preventive and corrective maintenance principles.
  • Ability to identify common facility deficiencies and signs of wear and deterioration.
  • Basic understanding of plumbing, electrical, HVAC, lighting, flooring, doors, fixtures, landscaping, and general building systems.
  • Knowledge of purchasing and vendor-management processes.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Outlook, and Word.
  • Ability to use maintenance, work order, inventory, procurement, or asset-management systems.
  • Strong organizational and recordkeeping skills.
  • Ability to prepare basic reports and maintain accurate documentation.



Benefits

Job Title

Business Intelligence Engineer

Job Description

How You’ll Add Value:


The Business Intelligence (BI) Engineer is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining enterprise data and analytics solutions that enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. This role will build and optimize cloud-based data platforms, design scalable ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines, and develop curated datasets that support reporting, dashboards, advanced analytics, and Artificial Intelligence initiatives.

Working within AWS, Snowflake and PostgreSQL-based data environments, the BI Engineer will transform complex business and operational data into trusted, actionable insights while ensuring data quality, governance, and scalability.


What You’ll Do:


Data Engineering and ETL Development:


  • Design, develop, and maintain ETL pipelines that integrate data from enterprise applications, operational systems, APIs, and third-party platforms
  • Build automated processes to extract, load, and transform structured and unstructured data into analytics-ready datasets
  • Implement data validation, cleansing, enrichment, and monitoring processes
  • Optimize data pipelines for performance, scalability, and reliability

Snowflake Data Platform:


  • Design and manage Snowflake databases, schemas, tables, views, and data models
  • Develop and maintain dimensional, operational, and semantic data models to support analytics and reporting. Create structured and governed datasets that enable self-service business intelligence
  • Optimize Snowflake performance through effective clustering, partitioning, and query tuning

AWS Data Lake & Cloud Analytics:


  • Develop and support AWS-based analytics solutions utilizing:
    • Amazon S3
    • Amazon SageMaker
    • AWS Glue
    • Amazon Athena
    • AWS Lambda
    • Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
  • Design and maintain S3 data lake structures and table architectures that support enterprise reporting and analytics
  • Support data ingestion and transformation processes from multiple internal and external data sources
  • Design, develop, and optimize PostgreSQL database objects including schemas, tables, views, materialized views, stored procedures, and data transformation logic to support analytics and reporting workloads

Reporting & Business Intelligence:


  • Partner with business stakeholders to understand reporting and analytics requirements
  • Create and maintain reusable datasets, KPIs, metrics, and reporting structures
  • Support dashboard and visualization development utilizing BI and reporting tools
  • Enable self-service analytics through governed data models and semantic layers

AI & Advanced Analytics Enablement:


  • Collaborate with Data Science and AI teams to prepare and curate datasets for machine learning models
  • Support data engineering activities required for Amazon SageMaker and AI initiatives
  • Develop scalable data assets that support predictive analytics and operational intelligence

Data Governance & Quality:


  • Establish and maintain data quality standards and controls
  • Document data lineage, mappings, business rules, and transformation logic
  • Ensure compliance with data governance, security, and regulatory requirements
  • Participate in master data and metadata management initiatives

What You Will Bring:


  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Engineering, or related field
  • 4+ years of experience in Business Intelligence, Data Engineering, Analytics Engineering, or related disciplines
  • Strong experience with ETL development and data integration.
  • Hands-on experience with Snowflake
  • Hands-on experience with PostgreSQL, including query optimization, schema design, indexing strategies, and performance tuning
  • Strong SQL development, data modeling, and PostgreSQL database development expertise
  • Experience working within AWS cloud environments
  • Experience developing and managing enterprise reporting datasets
  • Knowledge of dimensional modeling, data warehousing, and analytics best practices
  • Experience with Python or other scripting languages for data processing

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Experience with Amazon SageMaker and machine learning data preparation
  • Experience with AWS Glue, Athena, Lambda, and S3-based data lake architectures
  • Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or similar analytics platforms
  • Familiarity with Apache Iceberg, Parquet, or modern data lake table formats
  • AWS and/or Snowflake certifications
  • Experience supporting AI, predictive analytics, or enterprise data strategy initiatives
  • Experience with PostgreSQL advanced features such as partitioning, materialized views, JSON/JSONB, extensions, and analytical query optimization
  • Experience implementing medallion architecture (Bronze/Silver/Gold) or similar multi-layer data lake design patterns
  • Experience with Change Data Capture (CDC), event-driven architectures, data products, and operational analytics platforms

Your Working Conditions:

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.

The Opportunity

As a dedicated Property Adjuster Specialist, you will work within defined guidelines and framework, investigate, evaluate, negotiate, and settle complex property insurance claims. You will confirm/analyze coverage, recognize liability exposure and negotiate equitable settlement in compliance with all state regulatory requirements. You will recognize and empathize with members' life events, as appropriate.


Property Adjuster Specialist focus on using technology and desk adjusting for a virtual first approach to inspections and claims handling. USAA also provides a company vehicle to physically inspect losses within your locally assigned territory. Field Adjusters may travel outside of their local territory to respond to claims in other regions when needed. This is an hourly, non-exempt position with paid overtime available.


This is a field-based role for San Antonio, TX. Candidates currently living in this location or willing to self-relocate are encouraged to apply.


What you'll do:

  • Proactively manages assigned claims caseload comprised of complex damages that require commensurate knowledge and understanding of claims coverage including potential legal liability.
  • Partners with vendors and internal business partners to facilitate complex claims resolution. May also involve external regulatory coordination to ensure appropriate documentation and compliance.
  • Investigates claim damages by conducting research from various sources, including the insured, third parties, and external resources.
  • May identify and resolve potential discrepancies and identifies subrogation potential resulting from unusual characteristics.
  • Identifies coverage concerns, reviews prior loss history, determines and creates Special Investigation Unit (SIU) referrals, when appropriate. Determines coverage through analyzing information involving complex policy terms and contingencies.
  • Determines and negotiates complex claims settlement within authority limits. Develops recommendations and collaborates with management for determining settlement amounts outside of authority limits and accurately manages claims outcomes.
  • Maintains accurate, thorough, and current claim file documentation throughout the claims process.
  • Advance knowledge of estimating technology platforms and virtual inspection tools.
  • Utilizes platforms and tools to prepare claims estimates to manage complex property insurance claims.
  • Supports workload surges and catastrophe (CAT) response operations as needed, including mandatory on-call dates and potential evening, weekend, and/or holiday work outside normal work hours.
  • May be assigned CAT deployment travel with minimal notice during designated CATs.
  • Works various types of claims, including ones of higher complexity, and may be assigned additional work outside normal duties as needed.
  • Works independently solving complex problems with minimal guidance; acts as a resource for colleagues with less experience.
  • Adjusts complex claims with attorney involvement.
  • Recognizes and addresses jurisdictional challenges such as applicable legislation and construction considerations.
  • May require travel to resolve claims, attend training, and conduct in-person inspections.
  • Ensures risks associated with business activities are effectively identified, measured, monitored, and controlled in accordance with risk and compliance policies and procedures.



What you have:

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalency Diploma.
  • 2 years of relevant property claims adjusting experience of moderate complexity losses that includes writing estimates, involving dwelling and structural damages.
  • Advanced knowledge of estimating losses using Xactimate or similar tools and platforms.
  • Proficient knowledge of residential construction.
  • Proficient knowledge of property claims contracts and interpretation of case law and state laws and regulations.
  • Proficient negotiation, investigation, communication, and conflict resolution skills.
  • Proven investigatory, analytical, prioritizing, multi-tasking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to travel 50-75% of the year (local & non-local) and/or work catastrophe duty when needed.
  • Acquisition and maintenance of insurance adjuster license within 90 days and 3 attempts.
  • Successful completion of a job-related assessment may be required.

What sets you apart:


  • 2+ years of field experience handling higher severity/complex losses (i.e. vandalism, malicious mischief, foreclosures, earth movement, collapse, liability, etc.)
  • Experience as a field property adjuster handling DWG, APS and ALE adjustments
  • Experience adjusting property claims using virtual technologies
  • Experience working directly for a standard insurance carrier
  • Full file ownership of a claim, from start to finish
  • Industry designations such as AINS, CPCU, AIC, SCLA (or actively pursuing)
  • Xactimate Level 1 and/or Level 2 certification
  • Deployments in support of catastrophes
  • Active Adjuster License
  • Currently reside in the San Antonio, TX area
  • US military experience through military service or a military spouse/domestic partner

Physical Demand Requirements:

  • May require the ability to crouch and stoop to inspect confined spaces, to include attics and go beneath homes into crawl spaces.
  • May need to meet all USAA safe driving requirements including verification of driving record through MVR & possession of valid driver's license.
  • May require the ability to lift a minimum of 35 pounds to include lifting a ladder in and out of the trunk of a car.
  • May require the ability to climb ladders and traverse roofs, this includes the ability to work at heights while inspecting roofs and attics.

Compensation range: The salary range for this position is: $69,920.00 - $133,620.00.


USAA does not provide visa sponsorship for this role. Please do not apply for this role if at any time (now or in the future) you will need immigration support (i.e., H-1B, TN, STEM OPT Training Plans, etc.).

Compensation: USAA has an effective process for assessing market data and establishing ranges to ensure we remain competitive. You are paid within the salary range based on your experience and market data of the position. The actual salary for this role may vary by location.

Employees may be eligible for pay incentives based on overall corporate and individual performance and at the discretion of the USAA Board of Directors.

The above description reflects the details considered necessary to describe the principal functions of the job and should not be construed as a detailed description of all the work requirements that may be performed in the job.

Benefits: At USAA our employees enjoy best-in-class benefits to support their physical, financial, and emotional wellness. These benefits include comprehensive medical, dental and vision plans, 401(k), pension, life insurance, parental benefits, adoption assistance, paid time off program with paid holidays plus 16 paid volunteer hours, and various wellness programs. Additionally, our career path planning and continuing education assists employees with their professional goals.

For more details on our outstanding benefits, visit our benefits page on USAAjobs.com

title: Undergraduate Research Assistantship - Bee Products
description:
Serve as an undergraduate research assistant on the project: Chemical Characterization of Bee Products Using Spectroscopic and Chromatographic Techniques.

This project aims to characterize the chemical composition of bee products, particularly honey and propolis, using Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy and Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS). These techniques will be used to examine functional groups, identify selected organic compounds, and compare the chemical profiles of different samples.

Students will prepare and extract bee product samples, perform FTIR and GC-MS analyses, interpret spectra and chromatograms, and document experimental results. They will also assist in data analysis and the preparation of research reports and presentations.

* You must have Federal Work Study funding added to your awards BEFORE applying for this position. You are potentially eligible for Work Study if you are a US Citizen or permanent resident, have filed a FAFSA, are enrolled in at least 6 credits, and are in good academic standing.

This position requires the following:
• Must be Work Study eligible
• Prior hands-on experience with analytical instruments is required, preferably FTIR, GC-MS, or related spectroscopic and chromatographic techniques
• Must have basic laboratory skills
• Attention to detail
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively

Instructions to find your Work Study eligibility status:
• Log into your MyPacePortal and click on “Student Home” and then the “Financial Aid” box (middle of screen).
• Once in Financial Aid, select the “Award Offer” tab and the correct Award Year.
• Scroll down to “Options to Pay Net Cost” and take a screenshot of the funds that are allocated specifically to Work Study for the academic year. Make sure your name is captured in the screenshot, then upload the screenshot, and submit it along with your application.

* If these details are not available in the “Award Offer” section of your profile, you are NOT currently eligible for Work Study funding. title: QA - HIM Services
description:
About Us:


Our purpose is to help clients exceed their financial health goals. Across the reimbursement cycle, our scalable solutions and clinical expertise help solve programmatic needs. Enabling our teams with leading technology allows analytics to guide our solutions and keeps us accountable achieving goals.


We build long-term careers by investing in YOU. We seek to create an environment that cultivates your professional development and personal growth, as we believe your success is our success.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Note: The essential duties and responsibilities below are intended to describe the general duties and responsibilities of this position and are not intended to be an exhaustive statement of duties. This position may perform all or most of the primary duties listed below. Specific tasks, responsibilities or competencies may be documented in the Team Member’s performance objectives as outlined by the Team Member’s immediate Leadership Team Member.

Roles and Responsibilities:

Auditing and reviewing medical documentation for appropriate ICD and CPT coding
and ensuring that codes tally with doctors’ diagnosis.
Asking explanation from physicians when code assignments are not straightforward or
documentation in the record is inadequate, ambiguous, or unclear for coding purposes
Ensuring compliance with medical coding policies and guidelines.
Be updated about new coding rules as codes change from time to time.
Collecting and distributing coding related information and billing issues.
Exceptional Knowledge of medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, disease
processes, and pharmacology.
Work as part of a team and achieve the team quality and productivity standards.

Required Expertise & Qualification:

Life Science graduation or any equivalent graduation with Anatomy/Physiology as
main subjects
3 to 5 years of work experience as a medical coder.
Any one of the following coding certifications CPC, COC, CRC, CPCP from AAPC CCS,
CCSP, CCA from AHIMA
Proficient computer skills.
Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written.
Strong people skills & Outstanding organizational skills.
Ability to maintain the confidentiality of information.


Speciality of the QA needed for this job is Pro/Ed facility & Urgent care


Job Overview

The ED Facility Medical Coder ensures the accurate and timely assignment of ICD-10-CM, CPT, and HCPCS codes for all emergency room encounters. This role is critical to the hospital’s Revenue Cycle Management (RCM), as it determines the facility’s reimbursement based on the "intensity of resources" used during a patient’s visit.

Key Responsibilities

1. Medical Record Review & Abstracting

  • Analyze clinical documentation, including nursing notes, triage reports, physician assessments, and discharge summaries, to identify all billable services.
  • Abstract key data points such as admission/discharge dates, patient disposition, and trauma-related details.

2. Facility-Level E/M Assignment

  • Assign Evaluation and Management (E/M) levels (CPT 99281–99285) based on facility-specific leveling guidelines (e.g., the ACEP point system or staff intervention models).
  • Evaluate resource consumption (e.g., nursing time, supplies, and number of diagnostic tests) to justify the appropriate facility level.

3. Infusion, Injection & Procedural Coding[1][2][3][4]

  • Apply the Infusion Hierarchy for facility reporting: Chemotherapy > Therapeutic/Prophylactic/Diagnostic > Hydration.[5][6][7]
  • Assign codes for specialized ED procedures, such as laceration repairs, splinting, intubation, and central line insertions.
  • Accurately report "start" and "stop" times for infusions to capture the correct initial and sequential units.

4. Compliance & Quality Assurance

  • Ensure all coding follows National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) edits and payer-specific policies.
  • Append appropriate modifiers (e.g., -25, -59, -X{EPSU}) to avoid unbundling and ensure clean claim submission.
  • Identify and report documentation deficiencies to clinical staff to improve Documentation Integrity (CDI).

Required Skills & Qualifications

  • Education: Related life-science field.
  • Certifications (One or more required):COC (Certified Outpatient Coder) – Preferred for facility-specific roles.CPC (Certified Professional Coder)CCS (Certified Coding Specialist)CEDC (Certified Emergency Department Coder) – Specialty credential.
  • Experience: 1–3 years of experience in Emergency Department or Outpatient coding.

title: Anaesthetic Practitioner
description:
Theatre Practitioner – Anaesthetics
London, The Portland Hospital
Full time, 37.5 hours per week
Shifts: Monday to Sunday, early, late and long day shifts. Participation in the on call and standby rota is required, including a regular overnight stay commitment of approximately one night per week. Typically one in four Saturdays, with occasional Sunday overtime available.
Permanent Contract
Salary: Competitive + Shift Allowance


We’re looking for an Anaesthetic Practitioner to join our Theatre team at The Portland Hospital. As the only private hospital in the UK dedicated entirely to the healthcare of women and children, The Portland Hospital offers a highly specialised environment where colleagues can develop expertise across paediatric, maternity and women’s health services.


With more than 46 paediatric beds, a dedicated Paediatric Intensive Care Unit, neonatal intensive care services and over 175 paediatric consultants, you’ll be part of a hospital that cares for more than 40,000 children each year while also supporting one of the UK’s leading private maternity services. Working here means joining a close knit clinical community where compassion, collaboration, professional growth and continuous learning are central to the way we care for patients and support one another.


As a Theatre Practitioner – Anaesthetics in our Theatre Department, you’ll work alongside a highly skilled multidisciplinary team supporting a broad range of surgical specialities, including paediatric surgery, gynaecology, obstetrics and general surgery. Our five fully integrated theatres are equipped with advanced technology, creating an environment where you can continue to build your clinical expertise while delivering exceptional patient care.


This role offers the opportunity to further develop your anaesthetic skills within paediatrics, supported by experienced colleagues who are passionate about learning and professional development. You’ll play a vital role throughout the perioperative pathway, ensuring every patient receives safe, compassionate and personalised care. With a varied shift pattern, participation in the on call and standby rota, and a regular overnight stay commitment of approximately one night per week, you’ll gain exposure to a diverse caseload while helping to provide responsive support when patients need it most. It’s important that you're able to participate fully in this rota, as overnight cover forms a key part of how we deliver safe and effective care to our patients.


At HCA UK we care about what you care about. We care that you want to deliver the very best care. We care that you want a career you can be proud of. We care that you want working conditions that support your health and wellbeing. Let us care for you and your career, the same way you do for others.


What you’ll do:

  • Prepare, check and maintain anaesthetic equipment to ensure safe and effective use
  • Support anaesthetists during a wide range of paediatric, maternity and general surgical procedures
  • Monitor patients throughout anaesthesia, maintaining the highest standards of safety and care
  • Deliver compassionate care throughout the perioperative journey, ensuring patient comfort and wellbeing
  • Work collaboratively with the wider theatre team across multiple specialities to support excellent clinical outcomes

What you’ll bring:

  • Current HCPC registration as an Operating Department Practitioner or NMC registration as a Registered Nurse
  • Extensive post registration experience within anaesthetic theatres
  • Recognised anaesthetics qualification or anaesthetic course
  • Experience preparing and managing anaesthetic rooms and equipment safely and effectively
  • Commitment to delivering high standards of patient care within a multidisciplinary theatre environment

Why HCA UK?

Originally founded over 50 years ago by Dr Thomas Frist, HCA has gone on to become one of the world’s leading healthcare providers. In the UK, we’re one of the largest providers of privately funded healthcare and have invested over £500 million in the latest treatments, technology, techniques, medication and facilities. Being part of a large multisite, established healthcare group we can offer you unrivalled opportunities for career progression through internal and external courses, as well as working conditions that prioritise both your mental and physical wellbeing.


We believe that by caring for our colleagues, we empower them to provide exceptional care for our patients. That’s why we offer a host of flexible benefits that reflect the invaluable contribution they make every day. As a Theatre Practitioner – Anaesthetics, Theatre Department you’ll be eligible for:

  • 25 days holiday each year (plus bank holidays) increasing with service, with option to buy or sell leave to suit you
  • Private Healthcare Insurance for treatment at our leading hospitals
  • Private pension contribution which increases with length of service
  • Season Ticket Loan and Cycle to Work scheme
  • Group Life Assurance from day one
  • Critical illness cover
  • Enhanced Maternity and Paternity pay
  • Corporate staff discount for all facilities including Maternity packages at The Portland
  • Comprehensive range of flexible health, protection and lifestyle benefits to suit you
  • Discounts with over 800 major retailers

Culture and values

At HCA UK we believe exceptional care starts with our people. We celebrate the unique perspectives and different experiences each of us bring as we know that when you feel seen, heard and supported you can be at your best for our patients, and each other.

Our mission is simple, above all else we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life, a clear statement that extends to both our patients and colleagues. To achieve this, we live and breathe four core values:

  • Unique and Individual: We recognise and value everyone as unique and individual
  • Kindness and compassion: We treat people with kindness and compassion
  • Honesty, integrity and fairness: We act with absolute honesty, integrity and fairness
  • Loyalty, respect and dignity: We trust and treat one another as valued members of the HCA UK family with loyalty, respect and dignity

Reasonable adjustments

We believe everyone should feel comfortable to bring their full self to work and be afforded the same opportunities. As a Disability Confident committed organisation, we’re happy to discuss flexible working arrangements to suit your needs as well as offer reasonable adjustments throughout our recruitment process, and in the workplace, to anyone that needs them.
