title: Global Expert Contracting & Partner Management
description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections, where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

As the Global Expert Contracting & Partner Management, you will set, govern, and continuously elevate global standards, templates, and best practices for project delivery methods, contracting strategies, and partner management across our capital investment portfolio. Joining our Global Capital Investment team in Basel, you will act as a trusted advisor to project teams and key stakeholders, translating strategy into fit-for-purpose commercial solutions. In this high-impact role, you will build strategic supplier relationships, mitigate contractual risks, and drive capability building across our international sites network.


The Opportunity

  • Establish global contracting standards: Define, govern, and continuously improve global contracting frameworks, tools, templates, and governance standards across the global sites network.
  • Shape delivery and contracting strategies: Advise project teams and facilitate workshops to select fit-for-purpose project delivery models (e.g., DBB, EPC, EPCM, IPD) and commercial risk-allocation frameworks tailored to project complexity and market conditions.
  • Mitigate contractual and commercial risks: Participate in independent project reviews to identify, assess, and manage commercial risks, scope changes, claims, and disputes across the complete project lifecycle.
  • Lead partner and supplier relationship management: Partner with Global Procurement to drive collaborative management of engineering and construction partners, evaluating supplier performance and leveraging market capacity intelligence.
  • Build organizational capability: Design and deliver technical training, playbooks, and communities of practice across Engineering and Procurement to systematically capture and share lessons learned globally.
  • Drive cross-functional collaboration: Work closely with Project Managers, Project Controls, Legal, Finance, and Procurement to ensure integrated decision-making and leverage market trends for strategic advantage.



Who You Are

  • Educational & Professional Credentials: You hold a Master’s degree (MSc or equivalent) in Law, Business Administration, Construction Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related discipline, ideally supported by professional certifications in procurement, contracting, or project management.
  • Capital Project & Industry Experience: You bring at least 15 years of relevant experience in contracting, commercial management, procurement, or project delivery for major capital investment projects within Life Sciences, Oil & Gas, or similar capital-intensive industries.
  • Matrix Leadership & Stakeholder Influence: You possess exceptional leadership, communication, and cross-cultural skills, with a proven track record of influencing senior stakeholders and building lasting relationships across global matrix organizations without direct authority.
  • Strategic Thinking & Digital Mindset: You demonstrate strong systematic thinking, transparent decision-making, and commercial acumen, with familiarity in Lean methodologies, digital tools, data analytics, or AI-enabled solutions being a distinct advantage.
  • Language & Mobility: You are fluent in English (with German proficiency or a willingness to learn) and are open to up to 20% international travel.


We look forward to your application!


Who we are

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.


Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Client Services Product Delivery Leader
description:
Intapp's clients trust us to get complex implementations right, and the Product Delivery Leader is accountable for making sure we do. This leader owns the business performance, client outcomes, and delivery excellence of their organization, bringing deep product expertise to every engagement and ensuring the right capability and capacity are in place ahead of committed work. The role sits at the center of how Intapp earns and keeps its reputation as a delivery partner for legal, accounting, consulting, private capital, and real assets firms.


Day to day, this leader manages a Product Delivery P&L, oversees demand and capacity planning, and intervenes early when resourcing, performance, or execution puts an engagement at risk. The role requires experience running a professional services delivery organization, ownership of services financials, and a track record of building estimation models, quality standards, and reusable delivery assets across a portfolio of enterprise SaaS implementations.


What you will do

As a Product Delivery Leader, you can expect to:

  • Own the Product Delivery P&L, translating revenue, margin, and utilization targets into staffing, pricing, and capacity decisions, while managing demand and capacity ahead of committed work.
  • Protect margin and anticipate delivery risk by addressing what causes concessions, rework, and leakage, including estimation, staffing, quality, and execution, and by maintaining a forward-looking view of delivery health so you can act on risks to business performance before the quarter is decided.
  • Ensure every engagement has the right skills, experience, seniority, architecture support, and capacity for its complexity and risk, and adjust staffing or leadership as engagements evolve.
  • Lead a high-performing team by setting clear expectations for quality, timeliness, and accountability, managing performance directly, and developing and retaining strong talent.
  • Hold delivery teams accountable to the integrated project plan, identify and remediate risk before it causes delays or escalations, and work with Delivery Management on portfolio health and recovery plans.
  • Strengthen delivery expertise across the organization by owning estimation models and quality review gates, building reusable accelerators, and feeding recurring implementation issues back to Product and Engineering.
  • Be a trusted delivery partner to Sales by engaging early on strategic and complex opportunities to align on requirements, risk, and expertise, balancing commercial responsiveness with disciplined commitments that protect client outcomes and delivery economics, and building credibility through predictable execution and referenceable clients who reinforce Intapp's value in the market.

What you will need

Intapp is looking for intellectually curious, self-motivated professionals who like to get hands-on to contribute to the overall success of the business and their team. To apply for this Product Delivery Leader role, you will ideally have:

  • 15+ years delivering technology solutions to clients, including 5-8 years in a senior leadership role at a SaaS or enterprise software company
  • Experience leading a professional services delivery organization, including managing managers, with a record of hiring, developing, and retaining talent and addressing underperformance directly.
  • Ownership of a services P&L or product-line financials, with fluency in margin, utilization, revenue forecasting, and revenue recognition.
  • A track record of building estimation models and effort baselines, and of establishing delivery quality standards, review gates, and reusable accelerators across an engagement portfolio.
  • Experience remediating at-risk engagements, identifying risk early, and leading recovery with clients and internal teams.
  • Commercial acumen across services scoping, pricing, and statement of work authoring, with credibility as a delivery partner to sales.
  • Experience serving professional firms in highly regulated industries, such as accounting, consulting, investment banking and advisory, legal, private capital, or real assets, and working knowledge of enterprise SaaS implementations, including configuration, integrations, and data migration.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience
  • Ability to travel up to [25]% for client and prospect meetings

What you will gain at Intapp

At Intapp, you'll get the opportunity to bring your talents and intellectual curiosity to create better outcomes for our people and our clients. You'll be part of a growing public company, with a modern work environment that's connected yet flexible and where your professional growth and well-being are top priorities. We'll collaborate and grow together, supporting each other in a positive, open atmosphere that fosters creativity, innovation, and teamwork.

Here, you will have the opportunity to:

  • Expand Your Skills: Unlock your potential with professional development opportunities supported by a community of experienced professionals. We offer reimbursement for training and continuing education to help you stay ahead in your career.
  • Enjoy Where You Work: Thrive in our modern, open offices designed to inspire creativity and collaboration. Our complimentary lunches and fully stocked kitchens ensure you have everything you need to stay energized throughout the day.
  • Support What Matters Most: Our comprehensive wellness and flexible time off programs and our benefits are designed to care for you and your family. Our family-formation benefits and support during your family-building journey ensure you have the resources you need when it matters most. We believe in giving back and supporting our communities with paid volunteer time off and a donation matching program for the causes you care about.

Join us and be a part of a collaborative and welcoming culture where your contributions are valued, and your professional growth is a priority. Together, we are building a company of long-term value that we can all be proud of.


#LI-SF1


Your actual base salary will be determined by factors such as relevant experience, geographic location, and internal equity. In addition to base salary, variable compensation and equity may also be included.

title: Outside Superintendent
description:
About the Job

Job Title: Outside Superintendent
Location: Frederick, MD
Job Type: Full-Time, Field-Based
Salary/Compensation: $80,000–$90,000 annually to start, depending on experience
Additional Compensation: Company vehicle and gas card

Key Skills: Construction Site Supervision, Mechanical Construction, Sheet Metal, HVAC Ductwork, Project Scheduling, Crew Management, Blueprint Reading, Subcontractor Coordination, Quality Control, Jobsite Safety, Material Management, Construction Documentation

About the Company

An established, family-owned mechanical and sheet metal construction company with more than 70 years of industry experience. The company serves Frederick, Maryland, and surrounding communities, with projects typically located within approximately 40 miles of Frederick.

Position Summary

The Outside Superintendent oversees field operations and coordinates construction activities across assigned project sites. This role ensures work is completed safely, efficiently, and according to project plans, specifications, quality standards, and established schedules.

The Superintendent works closely with project managers, foremen, field crews, subcontractors, vendors, and other trades to coordinate manpower, materials, equipment, and daily site activities. The ideal candidate has strong construction field leadership experience, understands mechanical or sheet metal construction, and can manage multiple jobsite priorities while maintaining schedule and quality expectations.

Responsibilities

Field Operations and Project Oversight

  • Oversee day-to-day construction activities at assigned project sites.
  • Monitor project progress and ensure work follows approved plans, specifications, submittals, and schedules.
  • Coordinate field activities with project managers, foremen, subcontractors, vendors, and other trades.
  • Ensure work is sequenced efficiently and completed within allocated labor hours and project deadlines.
  • Identify field issues, delays, and resource constraints and coordinate corrective actions.
  • Conduct regular site visits to assess progress, workmanship, productivity, and overall project conditions.
  • Communicate project status, challenges, and schedule concerns to project management.

Crew and Subcontractor Management

  • Coordinate field personnel and help ensure appropriate manpower is available for scheduled work.
  • Support and guide foremen in managing crews, assignments, and daily production goals.
  • Promote accountability, teamwork, and professional conduct across project teams.
  • Address performance issues and escalate personnel concerns when necessary.
  • Coordinate work between trades to minimize conflicts, rework, and delays.

Scheduling and Resource Management

  • Review project schedules and monitor progress against key milestones.
  • Coordinate material deliveries, equipment, tools, lifts, and other jobsite resources.
  • Verify materials are available, correctly staged, and suitable for planned work.
  • Monitor inventory and identify shortages, damaged materials, or equipment issues.
  • Coordinate with fabrication and purchasing teams to ensure materials are prepared and delivered as required.

Quality Control and Technical Coordination

  • Review and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and approved submittals.
  • Help resolve field conflicts and coordinate required clarifications with project managers and other stakeholders.
  • Monitor installation quality and ensure work meets project requirements.
  • Identify deficiencies and coordinate timely corrections.
  • Maintain project progress photos, field reports, and other relevant construction documentation.

Safety and Compliance

  • Promote a strong jobsite safety culture and enforce company safety procedures.
  • Monitor field activities for unsafe conditions and ensure corrective actions are taken.
  • Inspect tools, lifts, and equipment for safe operating condition.
  • Coordinate safety expectations with employees, subcontractors, and other trades.
  • Participate in project and supervisory meetings as required.

Reporting and Communication

  • Maintain accurate field records, including daily reports, progress updates, timekeeping information, and project documentation.
  • Communicate labor requirements, schedule changes, material needs, and field issues to project management.
  • Attend construction coordination meetings and provide updates on site progress.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned based on business needs.


Work Environment

  • Full-time, field-based position requiring regular travel between construction sites.
  • Projects are generally located within approximately 40 miles of Frederick, Maryland.
  • Requires working on active construction sites and coordinating with field crews and subcontractors.
  • May involve walking jobsites, climbing stairs or ladders, navigating uneven surfaces, and working outdoors or in varying weather conditions.




Requirements

  • At least 3–5 years of relevant construction experience, preferably in a supervisory or field leadership role.
  • Experience in mechanical construction, HVAC, sheet metal, ductwork, or a related construction trade preferred.
  • Previous experience as a Superintendent, Assistant Superintendent, General Foreman, or Construction Foreman preferred.
  • Strong ability to read and interpret construction drawings, blueprints, specifications, and submittals.
  • Understanding of construction sequencing, labor planning, scheduling, and jobsite coordination.
  • Experience coordinating field crews, subcontractors, materials, and equipment.
  • Strong knowledge of jobsite safety and construction quality standards.
  • Excellent organizational, communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and meet project deadlines.
  • Reliable transportation and a valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
  • Ability to travel between project sites within the Frederick, Maryland, region.


Benefits

Why Join Us?

  • Starting annual salary of $80,000–$90,000, depending on experience.
  • Company vehicle and gas card provided for field responsibilities.
  • Join a family-owned company with more than 70 years of industry experience.
  • Comprehensive insurance and retirement benefits.
  • Projects generally located within approximately 40 miles of Frederick, Maryland.
  • Company vehicle
  • Gas card
  • Health insurance
  • Onsite clinic and nurse available 24/7 for enrolled employees
  • Dental and vision insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability insurance
  • Life insurance with long-term care
  • 401(k)
  • Paid vacation and sick leave
  • Paid holidays

title: Access Value Partner
description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections, where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

Location: Ljubljana, Slovenia (Office-based with field engagement)

Department: Access and Policy Chapter

Reports to: Access and Policy Head


As an Access Value Partner (AVP), you will shape sustainable access strategies and drive the transition toward value-based healthcare in Slovenia.

Sitting at the heart of our Access and Policy Chapter, you will act as a strategic catalyst—connecting health economics, scientific evidence, and policy insights to ensure innovative medical solutions reach patients faster and more efficiently.


You Will:


  • Build and nurture long-term, trusted partnerships across the Slovenian healthcare ecosystem to co-create sustainable access solutions.
  • Articulate compelling health economic and scientific evidence to demonstrate the value of Roche’s innovations to key decision-makers and policy-makers.
  • Drive market access strategies and lead key value-based healthcare initiatives in collaboration with cross-functional teams locally and globally.
  • Shape national access and reimbursement pathways by staying ahead of regulatory frameworks and healthcare financing developments.
  • Translate complex health economic data into meaningful insights and impactful value propositions for external stakeholders.
  • Champion seamless collaboration across internal network chapters to maximize impact for patients, society, and the healthcare system.

Who You Are:


You are a strategic, curious, and collaborative partner with a passion for transforming healthcare systems and expanding patient access to innovation.

You thrive on system thinking, evidence-based storytelling, and driving meaningful impact.


Qualifications & Experience:

  • University Degree in Life Sciences, Health Economics or related field.
  • Practical experience in market access, health economics, or healthcare policy within life sciences or related sectors.
  • Strong baseline understanding of healthcare financing, health economic principles, and reimbursement pathways in Slovenia.
  • Proven capability in engaging external healthcare stakeholders and communicating scientific or health economic value concepts clearly.
  • Entrepreneurial, growth-oriented mindset with the ability to navigate complex environments and partner cross-functionally.
  • Native/fluent proficiency in Slovenian and professional fluency in English, alongside a university degree in Life Sciences, Health Economics, Business, or a related field.

Please submit your CV in English.

Who we are

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.


Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Technical Product Manager - CPU Hardware Program
description:
NVIDIA is transforming accelerated computing, and our Data Center CPU Product Management team is developing the silicon and platforms that power the next generation of AI and data center infrastructure. We are seeking a Technical Program Manager, CPU Hardware Programs to lead progress across complex CPU silicon and platform projects. Working closely with the CPU Hardware Lead, this role links technical priorities and trade-offs to actionable plans involving architecture, silicon, platform, firmware, validation, performance, operations, and product teams. You will clarify complex dependencies, ensure critical decisions and commitments result in action, and build program mechanisms that keep teams coordinated from development through customer readiness. This is a highly visible technical program leadership position for someone who can work deeply within complex hardware programs while influencing engineering, product, operations, and customer-facing teams.


What you'll be doing:

  • Drive coordinated progress across CPU silicon and platform programs, maintaining a clear view of achievements, dependencies, risks, decisions, owners, and readiness criteria.
  • Collaborate with architecture, silicon, platform, firmware, validation, performance, operations, and product teams to recognize cross-functional dependencies and advance essential steps to completion.
  • Identify schedule, scope, quality, and readiness risks early, outlining technical trade-offs and bringing the right collaborators together to make timely decisions.
  • Translate complex engineering inputs into concise, technically accurate program plans, requirements, decision records, risk assessments, and executive updates.
  • Coordinate responses to hardware and platform questions from customers, partners, sales, and executives while ensuring commitments align with product requirements, technical evidence, and program capacity.
  • Establish traceability across customer commitments, product requirements, program decisions, and delivery owners as schedules and configurations evolve.
  • Improve program efficiency through focused source-of-truth management, dashboards, lightweight automation, and operating mechanisms that reduce manual coordination and accelerate decision-making.

What we need to see:

  • 8+ years of proven experience in technical program management, systems engineering, hardware program management, or a comparable role leading complex hardware and software products.
  • BS or MS degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related area, or equivalent experience.
  • Working knowledge of server or silicon development, including dependencies across CPU, memory, I/O, firmware, board, system, validation, and manufacturing.
  • Proven experience building and driving coordinated technical programs across architecture, engineering, validation, operations, product, and customer-facing teams.
  • Ability to grasp complex gaps in evidence, dependencies, assumptions, and implementation plans.
  • Strong technical and executive communication skills, including experience developing requirements, decision documents, risk assessments, program updates, and customer-facing responses.
  • Excellent judgment, organization, and follow-through while operating in ambiguous, fast-paced environments with multiple senior collaborators.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience delivering server CPUs, accelerated computing platforms, rack-scale systems, or complex silicon programs.
  • Experience with silicon bring-up, platform qualification, OEM/ODM execution, firmware, validation, or production readiness.
  • A track record of building program mechanisms or artifacts that measurably improved decision speed, schedule predictability, or issue resolution.
  • Experience handling customer commitments and technical readiness for pre-production hardware.
  • Knowledge of CPU driven platforms and data center client needs.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 168,000 USD - 258,750 USD for Level 4, and 208,000 USD - 327,750 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until October 19, 2026.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

NVIDIA uses AI tools in its recruiting processes.

NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.

¿Por qué PwC?

title: Folder-Gluer Operator I
description:
JUB SUMMARY:

Folder-Gluer Operator is responsible for safely and efficiently operating process specific machines and equipment that convert materials into WIP or finished product. Operator is responsible for running machines to meet established production requirements and for performing activities associated with safe machine operation, set up and changeover, scheduled preventative maintenance and machine service, quality, documentation, housekeeping, and sanitation.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Run converting machines at established rates, follow the production schedule, continuously monitor machine performance, and document any variables that may cause machine downtime
  • Complete the process and machine specific make-readies to prepare for machine set up, install machine components, set up the machine according to product specific requirements, and perform process specific changeovers
  • Monitor machine operation observing indicators such as lights and gauges to detect machine malfunctions and use those indicators to troubleshoot to maintain machine operation
  • Perform adjustments and service on machine/equipment as required by specific process
  • Perform preventative and machine specific repair/ machine service tasks
  • Perform machine specific cleaning and service to the machine such as maintaining the machine glue system and other process specific auxiliary equipment
  • Use RF scanner to scan transactions to the Warehouse Management System and use Warehouse Management System to generate a label that corresponds to the item
  • Maintain process specific production supplies and materials such as glue, tape, bags and other production supplies and materials in the work area using a manual and/or electric pallet jack
  • Perform process specific quality checks and make machine adjustments to resolve quality issues
  • Record data on specified forms and complete required line documentation
  • Communicate production and machine issues to the supervisor and other production personnel
  • Perform housekeeping and machine sanitation requirements
  • Assist other operators as required and relieve other line personnel for breaks and lunch
  • Assist in training other process operators and process support personnel such as helpers, feeders, and packers
  • Comply with all company policies and procedures including GMP, PPE, HACCP, LOTO, and JSA regulations
  • Responsible for ensuring, where applicable, the product safety, quality, regulatory compliance and legality of all products produced and sold
  • Work in accordance with all company policies and procedures regarding employment, safety, quality, product safety and legality, security, and regulatory compliance as applicable. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent, or trade school preferred
  • 3+ years of equivalent experience or experience multi-tasking in a fast-paced work environment with 1+ years of machine operator experience

Other Required Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities:

  • Ability to operate manual pallet jack and/or electric pallet jack. Ability to use RF scanner for WMS transactions. Knowledge of the use hand tools and the ability to use hand tools. Knowledge of machine operation and electronic and/or manual machine controls to operate the machine and run production. Knowledge of machine systems that may include mechanical, pneumatic, and hydraulic systems.
  • Ability to read, understand and comprehend documents such as safety rules, internal quality procedures, and machine operating procedures. Ability to communicate production and machine issues to supervisors and others in work area. Ability to work in an operating environment that may include a machine configuration that requires interface with packers and feeders.
  • Basic mathematics (i.e. counting), basic arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division), and basic measurement using measuring device such as a ruler

WORKING CONDITIONS:

  • Working Environment: Safety glasses with side shields, hearing protection, and steel-toed shoes are required. In addition, task specific PPE may be required.
  • Physical Demands The following is a general overview and is used in conjunction with the process specific Physical Requirements document.
    The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
    While performing the duties of this job, the employee may continuously use hands and fingers to position, and arms to reach. The employee may frequently bend and move about the work area. The employee may occasionally remain in a stationary position, ascend/descend stairs, push and pull, and communicate.
  • The employee may occasionally move and position up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this position. Additional duties and responsibilities may be required for this position based on business needs and at the request of management.

title: Operating Engineer
location: Client Site - USA - FL - Dania Beach - 137 S. Compass Way
description:
Job Title

Operating Engineer

Job Description Summary

Responsible to ensure the efficient operation and maintenance of mechanical, electrical and plumbing equipment and systems for the assigned property(s). Responsibilities include (but are not limited to) maintaining a clean and safe working environment, performing rounds, conducting routine assessments, performance of day-to-day preventive and corrective maintenance, painting, and housekeeping for assigned properties

Job Description



• Perform all plumbing, electrical, or HVAC requirements of the building(s)
• Maintain heating equipment, chillers (air and/ or water cooled), DX units, pumps, cooling towers, fan coil units, VAV, and air distribution systems, etc.
• Monitor and adjust all mechanical/pneumatic equipment, steam stations, control gauges, distributor panels, valves, thermostats, diffusers, and other equipment necessary to provide a comfortable environment for the buildings
• Verify field conditions and perform any necessary repairs or adjustments
• Monitor Energy Management
• Repair doors, ceilings, hand railings, and floors and other general repairs, adjustments and installations about the property
• Perform repairs to plumbing fixtures (water closets, urinals, flush valve assemblies, lavatories, etc.)
• Perform preventive maintenance duties in accordance with C&W standards, building protocol, manufacturer recommendations and industry best practices. including changing filters, cleaning coils, flushing condensers, punching tubes, greasing fan, pump and motor bearings as required, inspecting and adjusting belts, replacing motor bearings, aligning pulleys and shafts, monitor condenser, chilled, heating and secondary water chemical treatment and its associated feed equipment, clean and maintain cooling towers, and perform annual inspections and other scheduled routines as directed.
• Inspect engine room equipment, fan room equipment, cooling tower, all motors, house pumps, electric rooms, back-up generator, fire pump(s), sump pump(s), and ejector pumps. Replace lamps, light fixtures, reinstall or replace signage, verify rooms are clean and clear of obstructions and debris
• Check for properly operating emergency exit signs and lights and ensure free and clear access to emergency stairs and exits. Perform additional fire and life safety inspections as per NFPA and local jurisdiction, C&W standards, building protocol and as directed by superiors and property management
• Document and report activities to supervisor
• Respond immediately to emergency situations (fire, evacuation, equipment failure, etc.) and customer concerns
• Comply with all applicable codes, regulations, governmental agency, and company directives as relates to building operations and practice safe work habits
• Complete all required C&W Safety Training as scheduled annually
• Comply with C&W Uniform Dress Code while working and maintain a neat and clean appearance while on the property at times other than working hours

KEY COMPETENCIES
• Technical Proficiency
• Initiative
• Flexibility
• Multi-Tasking
• Sense of Urgency

IMPORTANT EDUCATION
• High School Diploma of GED Equivalent
• Graduate of apprentice program or trade school preferred

IMPORTANT EXPERIENCE
• 5+ years of related work experience in operating mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems in a commercial property setting

ADDITIONAL ELIGIBILITY QUALIFICATIONS
• Appropriate license/permit for trade as may be required, i.e. Journeyman or Master Electrician License or City Licenses, such as Refrigeration Certificate of Fitness, High Pressure Boiler License, High Pressure Steam Operator, etc.)
• May be required to have certification as a Universal Technician for CFC’s depending on market licensure requirements
• Possess and maintain a valid driver’s license and good driving record with periodic checks (where applicable)
• Basic Computing Skills in Outlook, Excel & Word
• Experience in operation, maintenance and basic repair of HVAC, boilers, heaters, pumps, refrigerant systems, compressors, water systems, etc.
• Knowledgeable in energy management systems, techniques and operations.
• Thorough knowledge in all building systems operations, maintenance and repair.

May be only maintenance staff member on duty during certain shifts; may be required to work extended periods of time without relief when responding to priority/emergency situations (including overtime type assignments); may require shift work and/or on call duties

WORK ENVIRONMENT
This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines. Regularly required to travel outside between properties in varying weather conditions.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.
• Must have ability to stoop, stand, climb, frequently lift a minimum of 50 lbs. of equipment (pumps, tools, ladders) and safely install rigging/lifting devices
• Regularly required to crouch and reach to install/move equipment by bending forward at the waist or by bending legs and spine
• Involves movement between departments, floors, and properties to facilitate work
• Ability to speak clearly so others can understand you
• Ability to read and understand information presented orally and in writing
• Regularly required to utilize vision abilities, allowing reading of printed material, drawings, and schematics


OTHER DUTIES
This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

title: Tax - Tax Reporting Graduate Trainee - Milton Keynes - September 2027
description:
Forvis Mazars is a leading global professional services network providing audit & assurance, tax, and advisory services. Forvis Mazars in the UK spans 14 offices across the nation and has over 3,400 professionals, with 190 partners. We have a clear purpose and a shared commitment to shape a better future.

Kickstart your career by helping businesses understand, calculate and report their Tax responsibilities accurately. As a Graduate Tax Trainee, you’ll learn how Tax connects to financial performance, regulation and business decisions, while working with a diverse range of clients, studying towards a fully funded professional qualification and building the confidence to make a real impact from day one.

About our Team
Join our Corporate Tax Reporting team, supporting a diverse range of businesses from ambitious owner-managed companies to large multinational organisations. You'll help clients navigate complex tax requirements, changing legislation and an evolving business environment while developing valuable technical and commercial skills.


Hear from our trainee, Harvey: 'My journey as a school leaver apprentice has been eye-opening and an experience at Forvis Mazars that has enabled me to learn and grow confidently and gain invaluable knowledge within Corporate Tax. The combination of on the job learning, as well as studying for both an accounting and tax qualification, has led to my development increasing faster than I could of ever imagined when I first joined.' #LI-DNP’

Does this sound like you?
• Enjoy working with numbers, analysing data, spotting patterns and solving problems with accuracy and attention to detail.
• Are curious about how businesses operate and how tax influences financial performance, reporting and decision-making.
• Can communicate clearly, build strong relationships and explain complex information in a practical, easy-to-understand way.
• Are interested in how technology is changing tax, including data analytics, automation, digital reporting and AI-powered tools.
• Are adaptable, motivated to learn and ready to study towards a professional qualification alongside your day-to-day role.

To apply for our Graduate Programme, you’ll need
• GCSE Maths and English Language at Grade 4/C (or equivalent qualifications).

• Achieved a minimum of 112 UCAS tariff points from your top three A Levels, BTECs, Scottish Highers/Advanced Highers, or other recognised Level 3 qualifications.

• Achieved or predicted a 2:1 degree classification (or equivalent).


We know everyone’s circumstances are different. If exceptional circumstances have affected your academic results, we’ll consider the context you provide as part of your application.

What you'll work on
• You’ll work on Tax Reporting, helping businesses understand, calculate and report their tax obligations accurately, meet tax requirements and clearly report tax in their financial statements.
• Prepare corporation tax computations, tax returns and supporting schedules using client financial information.
• Analyse accounts, financial statements and tax data to understand how a client’s business operates and identify key tax reporting requirements.
• Use tax software, spreadsheets and digital tools to organise data, check accuracy, spot issues and support efficient reporting processes.
• Research changes in UK tax legislation and help summarise what they mean for clients in a clear, practical and commercially focused way.
• Support client communications by gathering information, responding to queries and contributing to reports, emails and meeting preparation.
• Work with specialists across tax, audit and advisory teams to understand wider client issues and contribute to joined-up solutions.
• Take on increasing responsibility as you progress, moving from supporting compliance work to managing tasks, building client relationships and contributing to advisory projects.

Your development and benefits
You do not need to be a tax expert before you join. We’ll help you build your knowledge through professional study, practical client work and day-to-day support from your team.

Develop technical knowledge through funded ACA/CTA study, structured training and study leave. Build digital confidence by learning how tax technology, data and automation support modern client work.

Learn in a supportive team, with access to a buddy, mentor and colleagues who will help you settle in. Put your learning into practice through real client work and see how your contribution supports clear and valuable outcomes. You will benefit from balanced study and client work with structured support, regular check-ins and practical guidance.


If you’re curious, analytical and ready to keep learning, Tax Reporting gives you the chance to build specialist skills, work with real clients and grow your confidence in a career shaped by data, technology and change.

title: Compliance Specialist
description:
FIND YOUR FUTURE

We're excited about the potential people bring to our organization. You can grow your career here while enjoying first-class perks, benefits and a culture that fosters growth, innovation and collaboration.

Overview

The Compliance Specialist shall be responsible for the overall execution, administration and monitoring of the compliance programs as it relates to contractual and general/pharmacy regulatory compliance to necessitate companywide adherence. The Compliance Specialist will support various contract and regulatory activities. The Compliance Specialist will report to the Deputy Counsel-Regulatory Compliance Manager and under their direction will be the liaison between Reliance Rx business units, the parent company Compliance Department and related departments, and applicable outside vendors or regulatory bodies related to these compliance matters.

They will conduct regulatory research and analysis as it relates to proposed, pending or effective laws, rules, and regulations impactful to Reliance Rx pharmacy operations. The position will work closely with the Reliance Rx Leadership Team to ensure leadership is appraised of and in compliance with regulations governing Reliance Rx programs, as well as work closely with the pharmacy team, business development, and internal audit to ensure compliance with relevant regulations and contractual provisions.

Qualifications

  • Associate’s degree required. An additional two (2) years of experience will be considered in lieu of degree.
  • Three (3) years of compliance, quality assurance/audit or program/process management experience required. Healthcare experience preferred.
  • Experience with specialty pharmacy/pharmacy preferred.
  • Experience with payor and regulatory enrollment and maintenance preferred.
  • Advanced computer and Windows skills required. Experience with Microsoft Office applications and demonstrated ability to learn new software applications.
  • Excellent research skills and ability to exercise independent judgement to determine which changes in regulatory landscape should be presented in collateral and training.
  • Excellent analytical skills, ability to analyze components of legislation and implement and draft necessary policies and procedures based upon regulatory requirements.
  • Excellent composition and drafting skills, with emphasis on various compliance/regulatory documents and correspondence.
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, and excellent interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively build and maintain relationships with both internal and external stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in performing necessary research and preparing substantive work which requires knowledge of compliance concepts, with emphasis on HIPAA.
  • Possess initiative, creativity, project management and organizational abilities.
  • Proven examples of displaying the Reliance values: Collaborative, Accessible, Results-Oriented, Empowering, Supportive.

Essential Accountabilities

  • Monitor and research federal and state laws, regulations, and guidance related to pharmacy operations, specialty pharmacy, distribution, 340B, Medicare, Medicaid, HIPAA, and other applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Track regulatory changes and coordinate with operational leaders, pharmacists, and other stakeholders to communicate, implement, and maintain compliance with new and existing requirements.
  • Maintain subject matter knowledge of compliance obligations and provide recommendations, guidance, and updates to leadership as needed.
  • Develop and maintain processes to monitor compliance with contractual obligations and regulatory requirements.
  • Collaborate with Compliance, Finance, Business Development, and other stakeholders during contract review, negotiation, implementation, and ongoing administration.
  • Facilitate contract processing, document management, compliance obligation tracking, and required approvals, revisions, signatures, and record retention.
  • Research regulatory requirements for Reliance Rx to support acquisition and maintenance of Medicare and Medicaid enrollment(s) in all states and US territories.
  • Support resident and non-resident pharmacy state licensing renewals processing accurately and in a timely manner.
  • Support timely completion and renewal of state PDMP waivers or alternative zero reporting.
  • Coordinate internal resources and complete required updates to licensing and credentialing entities regarding changes in corporate information, changes to pharmacy staff or other relevant personnel, changes in hours, and related updates.
  • Support maintenance of tracking mechanisms regarding licensing and credentialing.
  • Ensure timely renewal and ad hoc updates to the business NCPDP profile are completed.
  • Complete and facilitate all necessary application and documentation requirements for the timely submission of initial and renewal payor credentialing.
  • Develop and maintain tracking and monitoring processes to ensure compliance with business operations, application and renewal requirements, including coordination with other departments.
  • Support the development, implementation, and communication of the organization's compliance, privacy, and security programs in coordination with parent Compliance and Information Risk teams.
  • Manage compliance policies and procedures, including drafting, review, updates, regulatory citation validation, and organization of related documentation.
  • Develop and maintain compliance metrics, dashboards, tracking tools, and process improvements to support program effectiveness and regulatory oversight.
  • Coordinate compliance training, onboarding, annual education, attestations, assessments, and awareness activities for associates.
  • Serve as a liaison between business units and parent Compliance, facilitating committee activities, issue escalation, investigations, corrective action plans, and regulatory inquiries.
  • Support privacy and security monitoring, incident reporting, remediation efforts, audits, and government investigations as required.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for associate compliance, privacy, security, and conflict-of-interest inquiries and concerns.
  • Collaborate with operational teams, data management, and internal audit to support compliance-related system access, controls, and oversight.

This is a hybrid position with onsite attendance required at our Williamsville location.

Immigration or work visa sponsorship will not be provided for this position

Hiring Compensation Range: $30.00 - $35.00 hourly

title: Undergraduate Research Assistantship - Mathematics in the Bronx
description:
Serve as an undergraduate research assistant on the project: College preparatory mathematics in the Bronx: A quantitative policy analysis of introductory, intermediate- and college preparatory-level mathematics coursework in secondary public schools.

This project seeks to better understand how Bronx public high schools with a self-reported four years of mathematics, offer college preparatory, or advanced mathematics coursework, require students to graduate with an Advanced Regents Diploma, or implement some combination of these policies compare to schools without such stated requirements or goals. Using longitudinal administrative and policy data from New York City public schools, the study will examine patterns in mathematics course-taking, school-level graduation requirements, advanced course availability, and student outcomes. The broader goal is to better understand how school-level mathematics policies may be associated with college readiness and academic opportunity.

Depending on how long they partake on the project, the research assistant may:
• Assist with preparing large educational datasets for analysis, identifying and documenting variables, validating data integrity, and organizing research files and supporting materials.
• Conduct systematic searches of the scholarly literature on mathematics education, college readiness, educational policy, and quantitative research methods.
• As the project progresses, students will receive training in literature synthesis, research design, quantitative policy analysis, and academic writing.
• Gain a strong foundation on writing well, and clearly. Specifically, students will learn how to report an abstract, education policy briefs, and memoranda.
• Have opportunities to assist with statistical analyses and conference or manuscript preparation.

* You must have Federal Work Study funding added to your awards BEFORE applying for this position. You are potentially eligible for Work Study if you are a US Citizen or permanent resident, have filed a FAFSA, are enrolled in at least 6 credits, and are in good academic standing.

This position requires the following:

  • Must be Work Study eligible
  • Mathematics and Computer Science majors are particularly encouraged to apply.
  • Students majoring in Quantitative Social Sciences or related fields are also welcome and will be considered based on their quantitative background.
  • The ideal candidate will have completed at least one intermediate-level statistics or research methods course beyond an introductory statistics class, such as MAT 117, MAT 131, MAT 134, MAT 234, or equivalent coursework.
  • A strong knowledge of excel spreadsheet and macros, data management, or programming is desirable.
  • Completion of MAT 137 (Discrete Mathematics), CIS 113, or similar coursework is not required but will be considered an asset.
  • Successful applicants should demonstrate intellectual curiosity, strong attention to detail, persistence when working with complex datasets, and an interest in quantitative and social oriented research.
  • While students will be under the direct supervision of the PI, it is expected that students be able to work independently at time for long periods of time.

Instructions to find your Work Study eligibility status:

  • Log into your MyPacePortal and click on “Student Home” and then the “Financial Aid” box (middle of screen).
  • Once in Financial Aid, select the “Award Offer” tab and the correct Award Year.
  • Scroll down to “Options to Pay Net Cost” and take a screenshot of the funds that are allocated specifically to Work Study for the academic year. Make sure your name is captured in the screenshot, then upload the screenshot, and submit it along with your application.

* If these details are not available in the “Award Offer” section of your profile, you are NOT currently eligible for Work Study funding. If you are a US citizen or permanent resident, and you have filed a FAFSA, you can open a Help Desk ticket with Financial Aid to determine your Work Study eligibility.

description:

groups.

title: Associate, Global Investment Banking
description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit

What you'll be doing


The Global Mining team is a leading provider of investment banking services to existing and prospective metals & mining companies globally. The team’s coverage strategy spans North America, Europe, South America, Asia, and Australia. Our client-centric approach incorporates Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A) and other financial advisory services with access to the debt, equity and loan capital markets, as well as complex risk and hedging solutions. The Global Mining team manages a market leading platform from our offices in Toronto, Vancouver, London, Sydney, Hong Kong, Tokyo, Singapore and Bogota.

Clients across the world turn to CIBC’s Global Mining team for M&A advisory, debt and equity financing and lending products. We have led many of the industry’s largest gold and base metals equity transactions and have played integral lead strategic advisory roles to global mining companies in some of the largest industry defining merger and acquisition transactions. Our specialized global platform and subject matter expertise enables us to help our clients meet their goals, including those related to the global energy transition.

With guidance from Managing Directors, Executive Directors or Directors, you will complete assignments that impact the firm's bottom line through the execution of M&A advisory and financing mandates, supporting client relationships and the Global Mining team’s origination efforts, and contributing to the overall communication flow across our global offices. The role provides you with steep learning opportunities and the ability to observe and influence the strategic direction of our clients’ businesses with exposure to company executives and board of directors.

Associates on the Global Mining team will be expected to provide a broad range of analytical, research and presentation preparation support to all the professionals within their group and play a critical role in mentoring and training Analysts on the team. Typically, Associates are assigned to a variety of transactions and advisory projects, such as mergers & acquisitions, divestitures, equity and debt financings, and capital structure and strategic advisory projects, and must have strong prioritization and multi-tasking capabilities. You will also be expected to maintain an awareness of the strategic priorities of our clients and key developments and trends in the industry. Applying your strengths in quantitative analysis to create and direct complex financial analysis and models while extracting the “big picture” implications of such analysis will be critical to your success.


The role of an Associate is challenging and fast-paced. It requires dedication, passion for the industry and a very solid work ethic. You must be able to accept flexibility in required personal time commitments to complete work assignments.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. To successfully perform the work, you'll be on-site full-time.


The expected annualized base salary for this role is $135,000.

The base salary is determined by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s skills, experience, and job-related knowledge, as well as geographic location and specific business needs. Our compensation philosophy supports ongoing growth and development, enabling progression within the salary range as team members advance in their roles.

In addition to base pay, compensation for this role includes participation in an annual discretionary incentive or bonus program.

We are committed to providing fair, equitable, and competitive compensation opportunities for all employees and we encourage open conversations about compensation throughout the recruitment process.


How you'll succeed


  • Research - Conduct industry research and analysis to assist in the identification and/or analysis of investment banking business opportunities.
  • Proposals - Play a key role in the preparation of client proposals, pitchbooks and the execution of new and existing client mandates, including overseeing the work of Analysts. Prepare industry and financial analysis to assist with the development of client recommendations.
  • Financial Modelling - Develop and audit sophisticated financial models.
  • Analysis - Lead the completion of analysis including comparable company analysis. and precedent transaction analysis.
  • Due Diligence - Assist in company due diligence investigations.
  • Support - Support senior investment banking colleagues and directing and training Analyst teammates.
  • Relationship Building - Grow your internal and external networks coordinating client-focused and/or deal-focused brainstorming sessions with relevant team members and product specialists. Developing relationships and actively communicating with various appropriate contacts at our clients. Developing and maintaining an internal network with product groups and other business groups. Developing and maintaining an external network with the market (i.e. key stakeholders, clients, prospects, etc.). Liaising with other units of CIBC Capital Markets in preparing proposals for clients.
  • Culture - Support CIBC’s “Culture of Care” through involvement in community activities.

  • The successful candidate will work with their supervisor to independently design, plan, and conduct cell culture experiments at different scales, including shake flasks, ambr15, ambr250, and 3L/10L bench-top bioreactors to support platform development initiatives.

  • Process and analyze experimental results using data automation platforms, interpreting outcomes such as growth rates, nutrient uptake/secretion profiles, and intracellular metabolite levels to support media development efforts.

  • You will be exposed to cell culture development platforms and potentially involved in multiple projects, such as fed-batch process development, perfusion process development, media development, and high-throughput automation development.

  • Currently enrolled in a Master's or PhD degree program in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biological Engineering or a related field.

Students currently on CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT usually require future sponsorship for long term employment and do not meet the Internal requirements for this program unless eligible for an alternative long-term status that does not require company sponsorship.

  • Must be able to relocate to the office location and work 40hrs/week, Monday to Friday for the full duration of the co-op/internship.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with aseptic technique and mammalian cell culture.

  • Strong interest in integrating experimental and computational approaches to study cell metabolism.

  • Familiarity with metabolic modeling frameworks such as flux balance analysis (FBA), metabolic flux analysis (MFA), or kinetic modeling.

  • Experience with automated liquid handlers (Tecan, Hamilton) and high-throughput automation.

  • Experience with statistical analysis and data visualization tools.

  • Strong computer skills and comfort working with large datasets.

  • Demonstrated coding proficiency (Python, MATLAB, R, or similar)

Why Choose Us

  • Learn from inspiring mentors and collaborative teams while contributing to real projects that shape the future of healthcare.​

The salary for this position is $45-57 USD hourly. All compensation will be determined commensurate with demonstrated experience.

title: Principal Digital & Data Performance Excellence Lead
description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections, where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

At Roche, we are committed to delivering life-changing therapies to patients by scaling cutting-edge digital, data, and operational solutions across global operations. As a Principal Digital & Data Performance Excellence Lead, you will act as a hands-on internal consultant and delivery lead - bridging the gap between digital strategy, advanced analytics, direct technical execution, and operational reality. You will join an elite, internal advisory and delivery team within PT Digital and Operational Excellence (PTE). Acting as an internal consultancy, you will serve as a high-impact catalyst for digital evolution across Pharma Technical Operations (PT).


In this role, you will lead high-stakes transformation initiatives across Pharma Technical Operations (PT). Using our structured Methodology (Preparation, Diagnose, Design, Implement, and Sustain), you will combine advanced analytics, Agentic AI-driven process optimization, and behavioral change management to replace legacy operational models with scalable, tech-enabled capabilities. You are an empathetic, outcome-obsessed advisor and strong consultant who bridges strategy and direct hands-on implementation, actively putting solutions into practice, challenging the status quo, and delivering measurable business value.


Core Responsibilities

  • End-to-End Program Ownership: Design, build, and implement the scoping, delivery, and value realization of high-impact digital initiatives, ensuring direct, hands-on technical execution and strategic alignment with executive stakeholders, site leaders, and operations-wide roadmaps.
  • Digital & Data Product Delivery: Lead the technical scoping and end-to-end deployment of e.g. complex data governance efforts, operational AI/ML models, AgenticAI initiative and shopfloor automation into daily manufacturing routines.
  • Value Realization & Diagnostics: Utilize hypothesis-driven diagnostics and quantitative metrics (e.g., yield, cycle time, data integrity) to build compelling business cases and track real-world value acceleration.
  • Behavioral Change & Adoption: Partner with OCM leads to design and scale behavioral-based adoption strategies, translating user analytics and behavioral data into product design improvements. Partner with dedicated Principal OCM and Program Leads to ensure technical iterations align with user analytics and overarching governance roadmaps.
  • Quality & Regulatory Compliance: Ensure all digital and data interventions strictly adhere to GxP, Data Integrity standards, and emerging global regulations (e.g., EU AI Act, Annex 11).
  • Scale & Industrialization: Drive digital initiatives out of "pilot phase" into fully scalable operations-wide digital products integrated across the global operational network.
  • Agile Coaching & Capability Building: Coach site process owners and local teams in Agile, Lean, and Design Thinking to build repeatable, long-term internal digital capabilities.
  • Knowledge Transfer & Continuous Improvement: Systematize methodologies, digital blueprints, and transformation models across the global network to drive consistent, scalable performance improvements.

Who You Are

You are a hands-on, executive-level transformation leader who thrives at the intersection of complex digital and data technology, human behavior, and large-scale operational environments. You combine deep technical literacy and direct implementation experience with strategic foresight, empathy, and a proven track record of driving change across matrixed organizations. Experience in Change Management and Stakeholder Coaching is as critical as your technical program management expertise. You possess the ability to drive high-stakes execution through both direct technical involvement and cross-functional influence and matrixed leadership.

Qualifications & Expertise:

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Life Sciences, or a related field (Master’s or equivalent preferred).
  • Professional Experience: Minimum requirements include:
    • 8+ years of experience leading digital, data, or operational excellence transformations within complex, matrixed environments.
    • 5+ years of experience within pharmaceutical operations, biotechnology, healthcare IT, or highly regulated GxP process industries.
  • Technical & Digital Literacy: Solid grasp of operations-wide data architecture, AI/ML operational applications, digital adoption platforms (e.g., WalkMe, Pendo), and shopfloor automation.
  • Methodology Mastery: Proven expertise combining Lean/Six Sigma principles with Agile, SAFe, Design Thinking, and Organizational Change Management (e.g., Prosci) frameworks.
  • Stakeholder Influence: Exceptional executive communication skills, with a track record of challenging senior leadership, navigating cross-functional resistance, and translating complex technical concepts into clear business cases.

Value & ROI Accountability: Demonstrated capability in defining, modeling, and delivering concrete financial and operational value (e.g., EBITDA impact, yield increase, COGS reduction) via digital & data solutions.


Who We Are

At Roche, more than 100,000 people across 100 countries are pushing back the frontiers of healthcare. Working together, we’ve become one of the world’s leading research-focused healthcare groups. Our success is built on innovation, curiosity, and diversity.

What We Offer:

  • Impact for Patients: Direct contribution to optimizing the global manufacturing and supply chain operations that bring life-saving therapies to millions of patients.
  • High-Visibility Scope: Broad strategic influence across the global Pharma Technical Operations network.
  • Growth & Culture: An empowering environment that values psychological safety, flexible hybrid working models, continuous learning, and personal development.

Who we are

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.


Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: People (HR) Lead
description:
People Lead

San Francisco Bay Area | $80,000–$100,000/yr | Full-Time, Exempt

Reports to: CEO | Department: G&A

ABOUT OFF THE GRID

Founded in 2010, Off the Grid has pioneered food-driven community spaces through curated food experiences, temporary event production, and experiential elements. Best known for hosting some of the Bay Area's biggest recurring night markets, such as Fort Mason Night Market, Off the Grid brings local authenticity and operational excellence to small or large scale events. Our unique creator network continues to break ground by transforming everyday spaces into vibrant destinations for public and private experiences. Our values-centered approach creates meaningful opportunities for small businesses to thrive and communities to connect, designing unforgettable experiences that celebrate local talent and foster the sense of discovery and place that communities crave.

THE ROLE

The People Lead is the person who makes working at OTG an amazing experience in the same way we create amazing experiences for our guests. You'll own the full employee experience — from a candidate's first conversation to the last day of the season — for a lean headquarters team and the event professionals who bring our markets and catering to life.

We're looking for a builder. OTG has grown on the strength of its people and the goodwill of its managers. Much of what this role needs involves turning practice into standards. The right person for this role will know how to facilitate hiring that's ready before the busy season begins, design onboarding that accelerates new hires' ability to contribute, and craft policies people can actually want to understand and actively use as a resource.

This is not a role that watches from the sidelines. While managers own leading their teams; you make them better at it. You know how to balance coaching and encouragement, connect thoughts and ideas across different perspectives, and if a conversation gets hard, you're the steady presence in the room that helps all parties move forward productively.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned HR generalist who has run People for an hourly, event-driven, or a multi-site workforce, who loves building the operating system as much as running it, and who brings warmth and backbone in equal measure.

HOW THIS ROLE CONNECTS TO OTG'S SUCCESS

Everything OTG does is delivered by people — those who book the events, those who plan them, and those who show up at sunrise to turn an empty lot into a community gathering place. When people's operations are well designed and empowering, our work runs smoothly and the best people stay engaged. This is where OTG's purpose meets its people: every great hire means a better event for a client, a better day for a local food creator, and a better place to work for the team around them.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Build the People Operating System

  • Own the employee lifecycle end to end in Rippling — onboarding, records, leaves, and offboarding — so every step is consistent and every record is clean
  • Build and refine OTG's People/HR knowledge base and own the employee handbook, so answers are easy to find and policies are easy to follow
  • Keep OTG compliant and ahead of risk, with real depth in California wage-and-hour rules for hourly event production staff

Hire and Onboard Great People

  • Own full-cycle recruiting for headquarters and field roles, and get seasonal hiring underway in January, not May
  • Design an onboarding experience that gets new hires confident and productive fast
  • Build clear growth paths for field roles, so advancement and pay have criteria people can see

Partner with Leaders

  • Be the trusted partner to the CEO and department heads — the person who spots the pattern early and arrives with a recommendation, not just a problem
  • Lead employee relations, from conflict resolution to progressive discipline to separations, with fairness and clear documentation
  • Coach managers through feedback and the conversations they'd rather avoid, so they grow into the leaders our teams need
  • Build an ongoing development plan beyond onboarding: identify shared skill gaps, source relevant external training, and help managers apply consistent approaches to leading their teams
  • Help establish the core practices behind how OTG works — from preparing presentations to running all-hands meetings — so the management team operates with greater consistency

Rewards and Employee Experience

  • Own the employee side of benefits and open enrollment with our broker, and partner with Finance on renewal strategy and clean payroll inputs
  • Bring a clear, consistent philosophy to compensation, so every rate can be explained
  • Take the pulse of the team through regular check-ins, and turn what you hear into action

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 5+ years in HR, including time as the accountable HR lead for an hourly, event-driven, or multi-site workforce — hospitality, events, or retail strongly preferred
  • Fluency in California employment law, especially wage-and-hour for hourly teams
  • Hands-on HRIS ownership; Rippling strongly preferred
  • A People program you built from scratch that outlasted you
  • Employee relations experience, including separations, handled in a way people on both sides would call fair
  • A partner's instinct: you read between the lines, earn trust across departments, and know when to coach and when to be direct
  • Strong writing discipline; policies, documentation, and recommendations carry their full context
  • SHRM-CP or PHR a plus; Bachelor's degree preferred, not required

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

This role is primarily office-based, with regular time at OTG events — standing, walking, and outdoor work in variable Bay Area weather. Occasional lifting up to 25 lbs. Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with disabilities.

OFF THE GRID IS FOR EVERYONE

We're committed to building a team that reflects the communities we activate in. Off the Grid is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or protected veteran status.

description:

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

It is all about learning and growing. Our Associate Auto Adjuster role may be a new career for you. There’s a lot to learn, but the pathway is mapped out and USAA is willing to invest in you! Our comprehensive, fully paid eight week training program includes all training materials, licensing costs, class discussions, hands-on training, e-learning modules, and the instructor led guidance will help you to support our members independently. Our in-office development program provides the training you need and the encouragement to create a proactive and independent support style to service our membership. We are currently seeking dedicated professionals to work in our San Antonio office as an Associate Auto Adjuster.
