title: Director, Analytics Excellence & Governance
description:
Job Description Summary

The AIDE organization enables Insights & Analytics to create an optimal decision environment for the US business by integrating insights and analytics across therapeutic areas, functions, and the enterprise.

The Director, Analytics Excellence and Governance will lead the execution, governance, and continuous evolution of the enterprise analytics capability strategy across Decision Intelligence & Analytics. The role will translate enterprise direction into integrated capability roadmaps, investment priorities, governance frameworks, operating models, and measurable outcomes across patient, customer, field intelligence, analytics modernization, and portfolio management.

Serving as the AIDE counterpart to the ED, AEG in East Hanover, the role will co-own the enterprise analytics capability ecosystem and act as the AIDE business owner for field-orchestration analytics. This includes providing strategic direction, executive governance, investment oversight, and SteerCo leadership for analytics, insights, measurement, and decision-support capabilities that enable coordinated field decisions and execution.

The role will also partner with SPT on analytics products, platforms, AI solutions, CRM capabilities, and data-enabled decision support, while governing a globally integrated US-HYD capability model through common standards, aligned priorities, shared accountability, and scalable operating practices.


Job Description

Director, Analytics Excellence & Governance

Location – Hyderabad #LI Hybrid

Major Accountabilities:

Enterprise Capability Strategy & Roadmap

  • Translate enterprise analytics strategy into integrated capability priorities, investments, roadmaps, and operating plans.
  • Ensure alignment across patient, customer, field, decision intelligence, modernization, data, AI, and technology priorities.
  • Design integrated capability roadmaps, resolving cross-capability gaps, overlaps, dependencies, and priorities.
  • Continuously evolve the portfolio based on business needs, outcomes, and emerging capabilities.

Integrated Capability Architecture

  • Establish the business capability architecture connecting intelligence, analytics, decision support, workflows, measurement, and execution.
  • Define capability boundaries, ownership, decision rights, and operating-model expectations.
  • Ensure analytics domains operate as an integrated ecosystem, promoting scalability, reuse, interoperability, and consistency across brands and therapeutic areas.

Enterprise Governance & Standards

  • Establish and drive enterprise analytics governance, executive review mechanisms, decision rights, and operating principles across AIDE.
  • Set standards for definitions, methodologies, quality, information stewardship, privacy, compliance, risk, and responsible AI, while holding capability leaders accountable for domain governance, lifecycle management, and adoption.

SPT Partnership

  • Serve as the AIDE counterpart to SPT for analytics products, data capabilities, AI solutions, CRM analytics, and field-orchestration enablement, ensuring capability needs translate into coherent product, data, AI, and technology plans.
  • Enable joint governance across roadmaps, investments, capacity, dependencies, issue escalation, and value realization, while resolving key business-to-technology trade-offs and maintaining clear ownership boundaries.

Analytics Modernization & Operating Model Transformation

  • Set the enterprise direction for analytics modernization, productivity, process re-engineering, and human-plus-agent ways of working, including responsible AI-enabled workflows, reusable patterns, human oversight, and measurable productivity improvements.
  • Drive elimination of fragmented, duplicative, manual, and obsolete analytics processes while holding AIDE leaders accountable for adoption, quality improvement, capacity release, and realized value.

Global Capability Operating Model

  • Help govern the globally integrated operating model across EH and HYD capability teams, establishing expectations for decision rights, shared accountability, governance, workforce planning, and delivery collaboration.
  • Partner with AIDE leadership on capability roadmaps, capacity, talent priorities, and operating-model evolution, while driving adoption of common standards, methodologies, reusable assets, and scalable delivery practices.
  • Foster a One-Team culture grounded in transparency, trust, knowledge sharing, capability development, and shared outcomes.

Field-Orchestration Analytics Capability Leadership

  • Provide executive oversight and enterprise governance for analytics and insights capabilities supporting field orchestration, including investment guardrails for field intelligence capabilities.
  • Sponsor integrated planning with AIDE Commercial I&A, capability leaders, and SPT, ensuring clear decision rights across business strategy, analytics requirements, decisioning capabilities, and technology ownership.

Enterprise Portfolio Oversight

  • Establish portfolio governance, investment criteria, prioritization principles, and capacity guardrails, approving cross-capability priorities, material resource trade-offs, and major roadmap decisions within delegated authority.
  • Review performance against strategic imperatives, roadmaps, investments, productivity objectives, capacity plans, risks, and value commitments, while resolving portfolio conflicts and cross-domain dependencies.
  • Hold capability leaders accountable for delivery against approved priorities and outcomes.

Minimum Requirements:

Education: Bachelor’s degree required. Advanced degree in Business, Analytics, Data Science, Engineering, Life Sciences, Public Health, or a related field not mandatory but preferred.

  • 12+ years of leadership experience in analytics, insights, decision intelligence, commercial strategy, capability management, or business transformation.
  • Proven success translating enterprise strategy into integrated analytics or decision-intelligence capability roadmaps and measurable outcomes.
  • Experience establishing governance, operating models, decision rights, portfolio practices, and value-realization frameworks.
  • Experience leading analytics modernization, automation, AI adoption, process transformation, or operating-model change.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate business priorities into integrated analytics, data, AI, product, and technology plans.
  • Strong track record partnering with senior business and technology leaders in complex matrix organizations.
  • Experience with commercial analytics, field effectiveness, CRM-enabled capabilities, customer engagement, or field-orchestration analytics.
  • Experience leading and developing senior talent and globally distributed teams.

Preferred Requirements:

  • Experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, life sciences, or healthcare, with strong understanding of pharmaceutical commercial and customer-engagement models.
  • Experience serving as an executive business owner or sponsor for enterprise analytics, digital, AI, CRM, customer-engagement, or field-orchestration capabilities.
  • Exposure to AI-enabled analytics, intelligent automation, decision intelligence, next-best-action, human-plus-agent operating models, and Insights-to-Action interfaces.
  • Proven experience leading enterprise transformation, capability adoption, product management, agile delivery, enterprise architecture, and capability-management initiatives.
  • Strong executive storytelling, strategic facilitation, and senior stakeholder engagement skills.

Leadership skills:

  • Lead, inspire, and develop a high-performing team through Associate Director and SM leaders, with clear accountability for value creation, strategic decision-making, business impact, and delivery quality.
  • Own end-to-end talent and capability planning, including hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, succession, career development, engagement, and retention, while building the team’s strategic consulting and executive advisory capabilities.
  • Align business, analytics, data, AI, technology, and global delivery teams; resolve ambiguity, conflicts, and dependencies across capabilities; and ensure disciplined execution against strategic priorities and measurable outcomes.
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, constructive challenge, innovation, inclusion, continuous improvement, and accountability across Hyderabad and cross-functional teams, while supporting I&A and AIDE leadership on talent priorities, operations, capability planning, and site-level initiatives.

Success Measurements:

  • Capability roadmaps, investments, and operating plans are aligned with enterprise strategy, governed through clear ownership and decision rights, and delivered against measurable outcomes.
  • Field-orchestration analytics strategy, investments, and governance remain aligned across Commercial I&A, field functions, SPT, and capability owners, with timely resolution of key risks, issues, and dependencies.
  • Enterprise standards, governance frameworks, and reusable assets are consistently adopted across capability domains, enabling modernization benefits across productivity, quality, scalability, cycle time, and capacity.
  • US and HYD teams demonstrate shared ownership, common operating practices, and effective delivery, with capability leaders accountable for approved roadmaps, adoption commitments, and value outcomes.

Skills:

  • Enterprise analytics and capability strategy execution
  • Integrated business capability architecture
  • Executive governance and decision-right design
  • Enterprise portfolio and investment oversight
  • Business-to-product translation
  • Analytics modernization and operating-model transformation
  • Field-orchestration analytics and decision-support capabilities
  • Executive communication, influence, and conflict resolution
  • Global operating-model leadership
  • Responsible AI, data governance, privacy, and risk management
  • Talent and succession leadership

Location: Hyderabad NKC | Hybrid | 3 days a week in office is mandatory.

Direct Reports: Associate Director and Senior Manager level leaders across Intelligence Strategy & Governance team with influence to broader AIDE leadership and talent .

Impact on the Organization:
Enterprise-wide impact through capability strategy execution, governance, business architecture, investment oversight, modernization, and global operating-model leadership. Shapes how analytics and intelligence are translated into scalable decision-support capabilities that improve customer, patient, field, and business outcomes.


Skills Desired

Brand Analysis, Brand Awareness, Commercial Excellence, Cross-Functional Collaboration, Customer Engagement, Customer Insights, Digital Marketing, Influencing Skills, Inspirational Leadership, Media Campaigns, People Management, Product Marketing, Product Roadmap, Return on Investment (ROI), Stakeholder Engagement, Stakeholder Management, Thought Leadership, Trend Analysis

title: WINDER ATTENDANT - 2nd Shift -  $18.52 - $16.90
description:

As one of the largest woven textile mills in the world, Valdese Weavers designs and manufactures residential and contract-grade fabrics for furniture manufacturers, fabric distributors, and large retailers.

2nd and 3rd shift do receive a shift premium of $1.00. We offer a $50 attendance bonus for every two weeks in which you miss no time, not including our shutdown periods. This bonus would provide an extra $0.62 to your hourly rate.

title: Tax - Tax Reporting School Leaver Apprenticeship - Leeds - September 2027
description:
Forvis Mazars is a leading global professional services network providing audit & assurance, tax, and advisory services. Forvis Mazars in the UK spans 14 offices across the nation and has over 3,400 professionals, with 190 partners. We have a clear purpose and a shared commitment to shape a better future.

Kickstart your career by helping businesses understand, calculate and report their Tax responsibilities accurately. As a School Leaver Apprentice, you’ll learn how Tax connects to financial performance, regulation and business decisions, while working with a diverse range of clients, studying towards a fully funded professional qualification and building the confidence to make a real impact from day one.

About your Team
Join our Corporate Tax Reporting team, supporting a diverse range of businesses from ambitious owner-managed companies to large multinational organisations. You'll help clients navigate complex tax requirements, changing legislation and an evolving business environment while developing valuable technical and commercial skills.


Hear from our trainee, Harvey: 'My journey as a school leaver apprentice has been eye-opening and an experience at Forvis Mazars that has enabled me to learn and grow confidently and gain invaluable knowledge within Corporate Tax. The combination of on the job learning, as well as studying for both an accounting and tax qualification, has led to my development increasing faster than I could of ever imagined when I first joined.' #LI-DNP’


Does this sound like you?
• Enjoy working with numbers, analysing data, spotting patterns and solving problems with accuracy and attention to detail.
• Are curious about how businesses operate and how tax influences financial performance, reporting and decision-making.
• Can communicate clearly, build strong relationships and explain complex information in a practical, easy-to-understand way.
• Are interested in how technology is changing tax, including data analytics, automation, digital reporting and AI-powered tools.
• Are adaptable, motivated to learn and ready to study towards a professional qualification alongside your day-to-day role.

To apply for our School Leaver Apprenticeship, you’ll need
• GCSE Maths and English Language at Grade 4/C (or equivalent qualifications).

• Achieved or predicted a minimum of 112 UCAS tariff points from your top three A Levels, BTECs, Scottish Highers/Advanced Highers, or other recognised Level 3 qualifications.


We know everyone’s circumstances are different. If exceptional circumstances have affected your academic results, we’ll consider the context you provide as part of your application.

What you'll work on
• You’ll work on Tax Reporting, helping businesses understand, calculate and report their tax obligations accurately, meet tax requirements and clearly report tax in their financial statements.
• Prepare corporation tax computations, tax returns and supporting schedules using client financial information.
• Analyse accounts, financial statements and tax data to understand how a client’s business operates and identify key tax reporting requirements.
• Use tax software, spreadsheets and digital tools to organise data, check accuracy, spot issues and support efficient reporting processes.
• Research changes in UK tax legislation and help summarise what they mean for clients in a clear, practical and commercially focused way.
• Support client communications by gathering information, responding to queries and contributing to reports, emails and meeting preparation.
• Work with specialists across tax, audit and advisory teams to understand wider client issues and contribute to joined-up solutions.
• Take on increasing responsibility as you progress, moving from supporting compliance work to managing tasks, building client relationships and contributing to advisory projects.

Your development and benefits
You do not need to be a tax expert before you join. We’ll help you build your knowledge through professional study, practical client work and day-to-day support from your team.

Develop technical knowledge through funded ACA/CTA study, structured training and study leave. Build digital confidence by learning how tax technology, data and automation support modern client work.

Learn in a supportive team, with access to a buddy, mentor and colleagues who will help you settle in. Put your learning into practice through real client work and see how your contribution supports clear and valuable outcomes. You will benefit from balanced study and client work with structured support, regular check-ins and practical guidance.


If you’re curious, analytical and ready to keep learning, Tax Reporting gives you the chance to build specialist skills, work with real clients and grow your confidence in a career shaped by data, technology and change.

We value our people's unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experience, and know this diversity create better outcomes for our clients. We seek to attract, develop, and retain the best talent, inclusive of sex, ethnicity, disability, socio-economic background, sexual orientation, gender identity, nationality, and faith. We select candidates based on skills, knowledge, qualifications, and experience and aim to support all our team members to reach their potential. title: Medical Representative - CVRM - Jordan
description:

An inclusive culture that champions diversity and collaboration, and always committed to lifelong learning, growth and development. We’re on an exciting journey to pioneer the future of healthcare.

As a Medical Representative, your primary role is to drive product awareness and adoption by engaging healthcare professionals with scientific, ethical, and impactful communication; supporting AstraZeneca’s mission to improve patient outcomes and achieve business goals within the assigned territory.

  • Collaborate with sales managers to develop and implement effective territory sales plans.

  • Adhere strictly to all industry regulations and company policies regarding interactions with healthcare professionals, including the distribution of product samples.

Job Requirements:


  • Bachelor’s degree in Pharmacy.
  • 0-2 years of experience as a Medical Representative in the pharmaceutical industry.

  • Commitment to continuous learning, with a proactive approach to maintaining up-to-date product and market knowledge.
  • Proficiency in both English and Arabic is required.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
**Senior Backend Software Engineer — Enterprise Data Platform**

*United Global Technologies, Inc. | Remote (U.S.) | Full-Time*


**About the Role**


UGT is seeking a Senior Backend Software Engineer to design and build the data layer, APIs, and system integrations for a mission-critical engineering data platform for an enterprise client. This is a prototype-first, greenfield build: you'll be one of the first engineers establishing the backend architecture, working in a small, fast-moving, cross-functional team with direct exposure to end users and technical leadership.


**What You'll Do**

- Design and build core backend application logic for a multi-module platform using a Python-based async web framework (e.G., FastAPI) and a typed ORM (e.G., SQLAlchemy 2.0)

- Build a workflow/statusing engine that tracks progress, sequencing, and dependency logic across interrelated application modules

- Design, build, and document REST API endpoints supporting form-driven CRUD workflows, including request/response validation schemas

- Design and implement a relational database (PostgreSQL) with version-controlled schema migrations, data integrity safeguards, and revision history

- Build integrations between the platform and external enterprise systems of record — specifically IBM DOORS Next (requirements management) and PTC Windchill (PLM) — implementing data synchronization, translation, and provenance tracking without duplicating system-of-record ownership

- Implement authentication, role-based access control, and secure credential management for external API connections

- Support CI/CD pipeline setup, version-controlled repositories, and automated build/deploy processes

- Implement backend logic to auto-generate structured reports/documents from configuration-controlled data

- Collaborate directly with front-end developers to define stable API contracts enabling independent, parallel development

- Respond to client-led security assessments and remediate findings in backend code under your responsibility

- Participate in schema, API, and workflow-engine design discussions with client technical staff;
deliver small, independently reviewable code changes and migrations rather than large infrequent releases


**Required Qualifications**

- 5+ years of professional backend software development experience

- Strong hands-on experience with Python, async web frameworks (FastAPI or comparable), and typed ORMs

title: Transformation Communications Lead
description:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

User Experience

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

The Transformation Communications Lead will be part of our Experience Design organization. Experience Design includes Product Design professionals, UX Engineers & Architects, Researchers, Operations, and Storytellers. Our mission is to turn extraordinary technological capability into extraordinary human value: making the complex coherent, the possible trustworthy, and Salesforce something people can build their work around.

Whether we are discovering the next product innovation or refining our operations, we aim to create experiences that are useful and connected in an agentic enterprise.

We're looking for a Transformation Communications Lead to navigate the organization's transformation to AI-native design and research. You'll be in the room while the transformation is still being defined, helping name what it actually means for designers and researchers, not just explaining it after decisions have landed. In addition to building the messaging infrastructure for priority programs, you'll shape how the org understands and adopts AI-augmented ways of working, from clarifying what the change asks of people all the way through tracking whether it actually landed.

What You’ll Actually Be Doing

Success looks like program leads and exec sponsors using your impact analysis to make better decisions before moving forward, producing shared language around the transformation, and increasing adoption of change.

  • Build and run segmented readiness programs, leveling the org into readiness cohorts, designing differentiated messaging per cohort, and tracking migration from awareness to active adoption over time.
  • Co-define change impact for 2-3 priority transformation programs directly with executive sponsors and design program managers, facilitating structured working sessions, producing change summaries, like heat maps and alignment briefs, that align leadership before anything ships.
  • Shape the shared language and organizational narrative that helps the team understand how work is evolving, including who Experience is becoming and why it matters.
  • Write the audience-based communications that help individual contributors and managers understand the direct impact to their day to day practice addressing all dimensions of a change (people, process, tech).
  • Develop the communications that translate the organization's transformation narrative into what it means for daily practice — helping teams understand not just what is changing but what it asks of them.
  • Co-own the end-to-end reinforcement system for each program.

You're Our Person If...

  • 7+ years of experience in change management, organizational communications, or internal communications in a matrixed technology organization, with demonstrated accountability for program adoption outcomes.
  • Demonstrated experience developing audience-segmented communication plans with evidence of producing distinct messaging for different audience groups (e.g., individual contributors, managers, senior leaders) within the same program.
  • Demonstrated experience partnering with senior or executive stakeholders to assess and define the scope of organizational change including producing written artifacts (impact assessments, alignment briefs, stakeholder maps) used to inform program decisions.

title: Scheduler (3901)
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY:

The Production Scheduler is responsible for developing, maintaining, and optimizing the master production schedule within a powder metal manufacturing facility operating in a multi-shift, capital-intensive environment. This role ensures efficient utilization of presses, sintering furnaces, secondary operations, and labor resources while meeting customer delivery requirements and inventory targets.

The Scheduler coordinates closely with Sales, Customer Service, Purchasing, Tooling, Maintenance, and Production to balance demand, capacity, and material availability. This position plays a critical role in minimizing changeovers, maximizing press and furnace throughput, and maintaining on-time delivery performance.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Develop and maintain daily and weekly production schedules for compaction presses, sintering furnaces, and secondary operations.

Align schedules with customer demand forecasts and firm orders.

Monitor WIP flow through compacting, sintering, sizing, machining, heat treat, and finishing processes.

Optimize sequencing to reduce die changes, alloy changeovers, and furnace disruptions.

Identify capacity constraints and recommend corrective actions.

Coordinate raw material and powder availability with Purchasing.

Track schedule adherence and report KPIs (OTD, schedule attainment, etc).

Adjust schedules in response to machine downtime, quality issues, or priority changes.

Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on flow, lead time reduction, and inventory control.

Attends and participates in various meetings to discuss project progress, and plant/production/customer related issues

Participate and prepare for various events; including cycle count programs and physical inventory processes and assist customer service to discuss delivery issues directly with customers.

Work with leadership team on budgeting and quarterly forecasts.

Work closely with Quality and Engineering on engineering changes.

Work closely with Tool Designer/Tool & Die shop to ensure tooling is available to meet the production schedule.

Performs other duties as assigned by immediate supervisor and upper management.

Minimal travel required.

SPECIFIC DUTIES and RESPONSIBILITIES:

Duties and responsibilities as assigned by management.

SKILLS EXECUTED:

High level of analytical ability to solve complex problems.

Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to prioritize.

Ability to present organized and thorough information and data appropriate for intended audience

Strong oral and written communication skills.

Strong interpersonal skills to collaborate with highly effective teams

Strong customer service focus.

Be flexible, adaptable, able and willing to modify activities and direction with an ever-changing business environment.

Strong interpersonal skills and work ethic. Ability to get along with diverse personalities. Tactful and mature.

Possess a professional attitude and promote the same in others.

About the Company:

At NARA NW, we provide essential services and support to Native American and Alaska Native people, empowering them to lead healthy, fulfilling lives. As an organization rooted in cultural heritage and community values, we offer a unique and rewarding opportunity to make a direct positive impact in the lives of others.

We have over 400 employees in a wide range of programs and services, including medical and dental care, addiction treatment, housing assistance, and cultural enrichment programs, there are endless opportunities to grow and thrive in your career while making a difference in the lives of others.

Position Overview:

The Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) Specialist works with young adults ages 18-24 and provides community and home-based housing support services to individuals and families who have experienced homelessness, and whose health, mental health, substance use history and socioeconomic issues create barriers to accessing housing. Services are focused on supporting the individual and/or family to stabilize their housing, end their experience with homelessness, and improve their health and move forward in their recovery. Duties include creating an individualized housing plan with program participants to identify needs, barriers, and resources to achieve long-term housing stability; assisting new program participants through the housing application process, addressing barriers to housing approval, developing positive relationships with collaborative partners, external providers, and property managers; being responsive to property managers as concerns arise in order to support participants in successfully maintaining their housing and preventing eviction; providing home and community based services to clients utilizing strengths-based case management while embracing the philosophies of Motivational Interviewing and Housing First. The PSH Specialist works independently and collaboratively with multiple NARA NW teams. The HUD CoC Youth PSH project is a scattered-site project, and staff will work primarily in the community.

What you will do:

  • Develop a client-centered individualized housing stability plan with all program participants.
  • Assist program participants through the housing process including identifying and applying to an apartment, addressing possible barriers to housing approval, accessing funding for move in costs and furnishings for their home, and provide ongoing retention services.
  • Work in close coordination with other providers/ support systems to address the needs of clients. Includes initiating clinical consultations, assuring coordination of service planning and ongoing support services.
  • Provide home and community based engagement services to clients utilizing strengths-based case management while embracing the philosophy of Motivational Interviewing and Housing First. Utilize assertive engagement techniques to meet clients where they are willing to participate and coach clients in setting goals and identifying realistic steps in order to achieve them.
  • Develop positive relationships with collaborative partners, external service providers, and property managers.
  • Be responsive to property managers as concerns arise in order to support participants in successfully maintaining their housing and preventing eviction. Follow up with property managers to determine outcome of any needed interventions.
  • Consistently use strong clinical and professional judgment while providing services to program participants; including taking appropriate safety precautions while transporting clients and providing services to clients in the community/homes.
  • Demonstrate responsibility for safety of participants and property. Must be familiar with fire and building regulations and evacuation procedures.
  • Provide ongoing assessment of needs and risk of harm for each individual and respond appropriately.
  • Complete housing-related service plans, progress notes, discharge summaries, and other documentation as required.
  • Complete program specific initial and annual paperwork with client to assist with housing stability.
  • Complete appropriate documentation and processes for use of client assistance funds.
  • Meet regularly with clinical supervisor for supervision and seek supervision, as needed.

title: Project Controls Lead
description:
APM Terminals

At APM Terminals, a global leader in port and terminal operations, we enable global trade and drive sustainable growth. What drives us forward is a mindset of always improving — observing how work happens, identifying what creates value, and removing what gets in the way. We constantly look for smarter, simpler, and safer ways of operating. If you thrive in environments where people value learning and are committed to continuously improve daily operations, join us and be a part of our journey.


You will join the Bid Team within Business Implementation Management, supporting APM Terminals’ growth strategy by developing competitive bids for new terminals, acquisitions and expansions of existing facilities. Your main goal as Project Controls Lead will be to bring together operational, technical and project execution inputs across scope, cost, schedule, organisational requirements and risk to create a coherent and competitive bid. By aligning these inputs across teams, you will provide the critical information needed to evaluate opportunities, understand key trade-offs, support informed investment decisions and establish a strong foundation for successful project delivery.


What We Can Offer

At APM Terminals, we foster a dynamic learning and training culture that empowers our employees to excel. Our commitment to improvement means every team member has the opportunity to develop their skills and advance their careers by continuously refining how we work. Experience a diverse, multinational workplace where your operational insights directly influence how we work.


  • Contribute to growth opportunities involving new terminals, acquisitions and expansions of existing facilities.
  • Work across operational, technical and project execution domains in a complex, international stakeholder environment.
  • Help strengthen a standardized, optimized and continuously improving business implementation setup.
  • Apply your project controls expertise across multiple concurrent opportunities and throughout the bid lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own and drive the development, alignment and maintenance of operational, technical and project execution scope within bids, in line with APM Terminals standards.
  • Lead the overall bid preparation process across the probe, develop and secure stages as the main Business Implementation Management and COO function representative.
  • Coordinate with internal stakeholders, including Investment and Finance teams, and facilitate workshops such as risk identification sessions.
  • Challenge business and technical content from an overarching perspective, ensuring a coherent, consistent and competitive bid approach.
  • Develop high-level schedules in Primavera P6, connecting technical and business operational deliverables to the overall project and business ramp-up narrative.
  • Develop cost estimates using input from internal and external subject-matter experts, including benchmarking against comparable projects and established norms.
  • Conduct basic risk analysis, support time and cost contingency development, facilitate scenario planning, integrate organisational or joint venture considerations, and secure high-quality tender documentation in English.



What We Are Looking For:

  • Continuous improvement mindset: we are looking for someone who brings a thoughtful improvement mindset—curious about how work gets done and motivated to make meaningful, sustainable improvements over time.
  • Leadership expectation: We are looking for people who consistently put customers first, lead by example with respect for people, deliver results with integrity, and drive continuous improvement by solving problems at the root, developing people, and raising standards every day.
  • Relevant experience: Bring 5–10 years of project controls or project management experience, including exposure to pre-bid scheduling, risk management, cost estimating and document control.
  • Technical foundation: Hold a graduate degree, preferably an MSc or equivalent, in a technical discipline, with experience using Primavera scheduling software and Microsoft Office.
  • Sector exposure: Experience in terminal construction or large civil construction projects is desired; experience in container operations would be advantageous.
  • Bid capability: Demonstrate experience in bid or proposal development, strong planning and analytical skills, and the ability to understand technical and commercial trade-offs.
  • Communication and collaboration: Communicate fluently in professional English, build effective stakeholder relationships and work constructively across organisational levels and cultural backgrounds. A second language, such as Spanish, is an advantage.

11. Performs medical record reviews; investigates and troubleshoots medical record issues in multiple electronic platforms; appropriately escalates complex issues to HIM leadership.

18. Supports Privacy Code call center, assists patients, researches/investigates/resolves issues and escalates issues appropriately to HIM leadership.
19. Investigates and researches regulatory issues and requirements; identifies applicable state and federal requirements, such as for release of information and medical record amendments.
20. Works highly-technical Epic and other system work queues to resolve issues and insure accurate posting of patient information.
21. Performs quality assurance reviews of various HIM workflows and reports findings and recommendations to HIM leadership.
22. Serves as HIM Department subject matter expert for testing and validating system upgrades and implementation of new workflows and technology.
23. Develops training tip sheets and assists with educating HIM staff on Epic and other regulatory workflows.
24. Provides ongoing patient education and assistance on all areas of HIM services.
25. Assists HIM leadership with coordinating MyChart Committee meetings, MyChart communications and related activities.
26. Attends and participates in various meetings related to scope of work.
27. Performs other duties as assigned.

description:

.

About Salesforce

Modern high-scale software as a service (SaaS) and AI infrastructure demand a proactive, risk-driven approach to the vulnerability lifecycle that goes far beyond static compliance tracking. You serve as a technical authority and strategic operator, partnering with engineering, infrastructure, and product security groups to identify, prioritize, and neutralize infrastructure vulnerabilities, software flaws, and novel AI-specific security risks at cloud scale. You gain the opportunity to shape how a global enterprise secures its AI-forward platforms and to present your work directly to executive security leadership.

What You'll Actually Be Doing


  • Own the internal Vulnerability Operations roadmap end to end, driving strategy and execution for traditional infrastructure, container and microservice ecosystems, and secure development.

  • Report systemic posture trends, emerging AI threat vectors, model vulnerability metrics, and cross-group Service Level Agreement (SLA) performance directly to executive security leadership and C-level stakeholders.

  • Proven success influencing senior engineering and product stakeholders without direct authority to drive rapid, systemic remediation across complex enterprise software environments.
  • Clear communication of complex technical risk, systemic vulnerability findings, and strategic remediation roadmaps to executive leadership and non-technical stakeholders alike.
  • A bachelor's degree in a technical field such as computer science, cybersecurity, information systems, or engineering, or equivalent technical education.

Even Better If...


  • Experience building automated continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) security gating, automated ticket routing, and orchestration workflows.
  • Hands-on experience securing containerized environments such as Kubernetes and Docker, and infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform and CloudFormation.

Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. title: Software Engineer (Falls Church)
description:
Our team is currently recruiting for an innovative employee owned research and development firm located in Falls Church Virginia. This organization specializes in solving sophisticated national security issues and is looking for a Software Engineer with a strong background in Scientific Computing to join their technical staff.

The primary focus of this role is to bridge the gap between theoretical research and operational software. You will collaborate closely with physicists and engineers to transition advanced image and signal processing algorithms from high level languages like Python into high performance C or C plus plus code. This involves the full software lifecycle from prototyping to deployment including performance analysis on real world data sets.

The ideal candidate will possess a degree in Mathematics Physics or Engineering with a specialized focus on scientific computing. You should have a clear passion for applying math and physics to develop practical solutions. Proficiency in both Python specifically using libraries like numpy scipy and pandas and C or C plus plus is essential. Excellent technical writing skills are required to document algorithm performance and code functionality.

This is a full time onsite position that requires the ability to obtain and maintain a TS SCI security clearance. Applicants must be US citizens and willing to undergo a comprehensive background check and drug screening.

Preferred individuals will have experience with data visualization Linux environments and GPU optimization using CUDA. Knowledge of parallel programming models such as MPI or OpenMP and experience with remote sensing EO or SAR or classical signal processing techniques like target tracking and detection is highly desirable.

The company provides an extensive benefits package including a five percent company contribution to a 401k and an additional five percent contribution to an Employee Stock Ownership Plan. Other perks include medical dental and vision coverage fitness and vision reimbursements continuing education assistance and flexible scheduling with generous paid time off.

Salary ranges are determined by education and professional experience.

Engineer Level 1 ranges from 90,000 to 125,000 dollars.

Engineer Level 2 ranges from 110,000 to 145,000 dollars.

Staff Engineer ranges from 130,000 to 165,000 dollars.

If you are a curious problem solver looking to contribute to vital national security projects within a collaborative and inclusive environment we encourage you to apply.

This position will also perform tasks as assigned to include, but not limited to, planning, bidder prequalification, development of bidder lists, development of bid solicitation packages, bid analysis, negotiations, administration, change management and close-out of service, and construction type subcontracts. Tasks may include cradle-to-grave or managing the turnover transition of the awarded subcontracts for field administration.

This position participates in planning, work hour calculations, and budgeting as it relates to project subcontracting activities; and develops and monitors project work-hour estimates and master contracts forms. This position may also provide guidance to project team personnel, during the planning, bid, evaluation, award, administration, and close-out phases when required by workload, complexity, or other factors. Additionally, the Subcontracts Administrator participates in the planning, staffing, training, and development of subcontracts personnel.

This position requires the successful candidate to support the Sentinel Project at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. Relocation assistance will be provided for this role. Candidates desiring a short-term assignment (<12 months) will also be considered. Furthermore, the successful candidate must be able to complete and pass a pre-employment drug screen and background check, which includes verification of employment and education.

Key relationships for this role include, but are not limited to:
  • Reports directly to the Subcontracts Manager / Subcontract Supervisor.
  • Receives technical and functional guidance from the Purchasing and Subcontracts Manager / Subcontract Supervisor.
  • May provide guidance to subcontract formation and/or subcontract administration personnel.
  • Maintains contact with management and participates in negotiations with bidders and subcontractors.
  • Works closely with Subcontract Coordinator / Subcontract Technical Representative (SC/STR), safety, quality, security, project controls engineers, Project Managers, etc., who have been assigned subcontract management tasks in accordance with the Division of Responsibility (DOR) matrix. #LI-SF1


Major Responsibilities:

Subcontract Formation -
  • Conforms and ensures subcontract execution
  • Directs negotiation in the commitment of subcontracts
  • Develops and issues subcontracts and services agreements as assigned
  • Prepares bidders' lists and pre-qualifies bidders
  • Forms bid request packages and issues bid request packages to approved bidders
  • Receives bids and evaluates bids commercially
  • Prepares Commercial Bid Summary and recommendations
  • Recommends and secures approvals in accordance with established procedures
  • Prepares subcontract documents for execution
  • Prepares and organizes assigned meetings, such as pre-bid, bid clarification and pre-award meetings, for the purpose of ensuring complete understanding and agreement between Bechtel, the customer and contractor on all contractual matters
  • After reviewing plan and agenda with supervisor, conducts meeting and prepares and issues meeting notes delineating important statements, required actions and schedules
  • Represents Bechtel in contractual discussions of advanced complexity. Administers information programs to ensure mutual understanding of subcontract terms and conditions. Prepares periodic status reports for management and client personnel.
  • Assists with various data-calls from project management, Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA), Inspector Generals (IG) office, and customer/client, etc.


Additional Responsibilities:

Subcontract Management -
  • Implements the Supply Chain Assignment Schedule which records the Project's agreed assignment of various subcontract management tasks and the Standard Work Process Procedures applicable to Subcontract Management
  • Manages assigned subcontracts maintaining a continual review of progress and providing management with information regarding projected financial or technical difficulties
  • Coordinates with designated staff on operational activities affecting contractual rights and obligations, subcontract performance, and other major matters
  • Manage moderately complex contract changes by negotiating with customer personnel and obtaining settlement


Education and Experience Requirements:

  • Requires bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 10-13 years of relevant experience or 14-17 years of relevant work experience


Required Knowledge and Skills:

  • Advanced knowledge of the fixed-price and flexibly-priced family of subcontracts with stated experience in construction type subcontracts according to procurement regulations, policies, and practices.
  • Demonstrated administrative and organizational skills.
  • Demonstrated oral and written communication skills.
  • Experience in developing various subcontract types, fee arrangements, contract terms, and legal requirements.
  • Working knowledge of construction and technical service type subcontracts with proven experience in change management requirements.
  • Experience in developing and recommending potential solutions to contractual problems and concerns to management.
  • Working knowledge of contract law, negotiations, accounting, or cost engineering gained through education or work experience.
  • Solid working knowledge of Federal Acquisition Regulations and applicable Agency Supplements with emphasis on construction type subcontracts.
  • Working understanding of Federal Contracts and the flow-down of applicable clauses and requirements.
  • Working understanding of Cost Accounting Standards, and determination process for applicability to the work.

title: Northland Transportation Liability Claim Litigation Specialist
description:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That’s the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Job Category

Claim

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$85,600.00 - $141,200.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

As a Northland Claim Litigation Specialist, you will be responsible for managing and investigating moderate complexity injury and/or property damage claims including customer contact, determining coverage, evaluating liability, assessing damages, establishing timely reserves, and issue timely and accurate payments within appropriate authority and oversight.

In this technical role, you will leverage your expertise in claims management, investigative techniques, coverage evaluation, and settlement negotiation to ensure timely and fair resolution.

You will foster positive, professional relationships with customers and stakeholders on claims that may involve significant litigation or span extended periods.

You will provide guidance and mentorship to Claim Reps and Associate Claim Reps, sharing knowledge and best practices to support their development.

What Will You Do?

  • Independently manage an active caseload of injury and/or property damage claims and litigation from first notice of loss through resolution within level of authority. Typically, handles personal and/or business insurance high complexity liability claims which may include coverage disputes and contractual indemnity issues.
  • Gather and thoroughly investigate information by contacting all relevant parties to determine coverage, evaluate liability exposure, assess bodily injury and/or property damage, and establish appropriate reserves in accordance with policy terms and management guidance.
  • Provide timely and professional communication to customers, representatives, opposing counsel, third-party vendors, and internal stakeholders.
  • Leverage resolution strategies and coordinate internal and external resources to conduct comprehensive claim investigations and evaluations.
  • Actively negotiate with multiple constituents (e.g., claimants, attorneys, contractors, representatives) and convey claim settlements within authority and issue payments timely and accurately.
  • Assist in coordinating with Counsel to support litigation management strategies.
  • Maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.
  • Identify areas in which we can improve or enhance current best practices and offer creative solutions.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) to comply with state and Travelers’ requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • May require travel, including overnight stays, to attend mediations, trials, arbitration, etc.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.



What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor’s Degree.
  • Three years of liability, bodily injury or comparable claim experience.
  • Two years of litigation claim experience.
  • Active adjuster license, where required by state law.
  • Experience with claims management systems, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to comprehend, synthesize, and clearly articulate complex information to multiple stakeholders.
  • Ability to analyze complex situations, exercise sound judgement, and make effective decisions independently.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for customers; ability to manage difficult conversations with empathy and professionalism.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills with the ability to manage a high-volume workload and prioritize effectively.
  • Proven conflict resolution and negotiation skills; ability to handle complex or disputed claims, negotiate settlements, and manage litigation.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Thorough understanding of insurance principles and terminology, state insurance regulations, fair claims practices, and legal requirements applicable to claim handling.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret, apply, and clearly articulate complex policy language, endorsements, exclusions to assess coverage and claim eligibility.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Two years of bodily injury liability, property damage liability, or comparable claim related experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members – including spouses, domestic partners, and children – are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit .

title: Plant Metallurgist
description:
Do you ASPIRE to join a new growth story in West Australian gold? Join us!

Accountable. Sustainable. People First. Integrity. Results. Empower.

Job Title

Plant Metallurgist

Job Roster

  • Located in Laverton at our Mount Morgan operation
  • Lifestyle 8 days on 6 days off FIFO or DIDO roster
  • 6 month fixed term contract

Job Summary

Be responsible for monitoring and improving metallurgical performance, supporting process optimisation, operational excellence, and quality control outcomes at our Mount Morgans operation.

Job Statement

Due to an internal development opportunity, an exciting 6 month fixed term opportunity exists for an experienced Plant Metallurgist to join the Processing Team at Genesis Minerals' Laverton Operations.


Join a close knit, supportive team where safety, collaboration, and continuous improvement are at the core of what we do. This role would suit an experienced metallurgical professional who can quickly integrate into the operation and provide hands on technical support from day one, making a meaningful contribution across our processing plant. As Genesis Minerals continues to grow, this role offers exposure to a diverse range of metallurgical activities, operational challenges, and improvement initiatives, providing an excellent opportunity to broaden your experience across a dynamic and expanding gold mining business.


Reporting to the Superintendent Metallurgy, you will be responsible for monitoring and improving metallurgical performance, supporting process optimisation, operational excellence, and quality control outcomes at our Mount Morgans operation.


This role is offered on a Lifestyle 8 days on, 6 days off roster and may be FIFO from Perth or DIDO from Kalgoorlie or surrounding communities.


Key responsibilities include:

  • Monitor and optimise metallurgical performance to maximise plant throughput, gold recovery, and operational efficiency
  • Analyse plant data and metallurgical information to identify improvement opportunities and support informed decision making
  • Provide technical support to operations, laboratory, and processing teams to achieve production and quality targets
  • Coordinate metallurgical test work, surveys, sampling programs, and process improvement initiatives
  • Prepare metallurgical reports and forecasts while ensuring compliance with quality, safety, and operational standards
  • Support the effective operation of process control systems and key plant monitoring activities

About You

You are a motivated and adaptable professional who thrives in a dynamic operational environment. You enjoy partnering with operational teams to solve problems, identify improvement opportunities, and deliver practical outcomes that enhance plant performance. You will also bring:

  • Substantial experience in a similar role/s within the gold industry
  • Tertiary qualification in Metallurgy or Chemical Engineering
  • Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) qualification (desirable)
  • Exposure to metallurgical test work and plant survey techniques
  • Experience with Citect and Pronto systems (desirable)
  • Process control knowledge, with VBA, SQL, or similar coding capabilities highly regarded
  • Strong analytical and problem solving skills with the ability to translate data into operational improvements

What you can expect from us

Enjoy a welcoming site community and a positive team culture that makes Laverton feel like a home away from home, together with:

  • Opportunity to work with experienced leaders that support your growth
  • Be part of a growing organisation during an exciting phase of expansion and operational development
  • Exposure to diverse projects, sites, and technical challenges that will accelerate your professional growth
  • A strong commitment to developing and promoting talent from within
  • Competitive remuneration and salary sacrifice options
  • Excellent camp amenities including a gym and sports facilities, recreation room, BBQ facilities, and regular social activities
  • Our team lives by the ASPIRE Values – Accountable. Sustainable. People First. Integrity. Results. Empower.

About Genesis Minerals Limited

Are you ready to be part of a dynamic and ambitious team at a growing ASX-listed gold house? At Genesis, we're dedicated to realising our vision of becoming The Trusted Australian Gold Miner, delivering high-quality, progressive operations with a target of +500koz annually. Genesis offers unparalleled opportunities for growth and innovation in the prolific Leonora and Laverton region of Western Australia.


Submit your application

To be considered for this opportunity, please submit your CV and a brief covering letter by following the APPLY NOW prompts.


We encourage applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Further information about Genesis Minerals can be found at www.genesisminerals.com.au.


Shortlisting will commence immediately, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

title: Helpdesk Technician
description:

#LI-hybrid

Job Summary:
SEGA of America is seeking a detail-oriented and technically skilled IT Helpdesk Technician to join our Technology Services team in a hybrid capacity based in Glendale, CA.

This is more than a traditional ticket-queue role. SEGA's Technology Services team is collaborative and multifaceted, providing opportunities to contribute to initiatives involving access management, automation, security, A/V support, endpoint management, and AI tools while learning from experienced technicians across the team. This position requires onsite support at least three days per week, with two work-from home days.

Success in this role requires strong troubleshooting fundamentals, excellent customer service, sound judgment, curiosity, and a willingness to learn. The ideal candidate takes ownership from triage through resolution, delivers a consistently positive employee support experience, and communicates clearly with both technical and non-technical users. This individual will be responsible for supporting device deployments, onboarding activities, access management, and asset tracking with a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail.

The successful candidate continuously looks for opportunities to improve the support experience through documentation, process enhancements, and operational efficiencies. They demonstrate technical judgement to troubleshoot complex issues, determine when escalation is appropriate, and continue to broader team initiatives, including automation, endpoint improvements, security projects, and other strategic Technology Services priorities.

Duties and Responsibilities:

End-User Support

  • Support employees across a fast-paced video game publishing environment with a professional, responsive, and customer-focused approach.
  • Own onsite and remote support requests from initial triage through resolution, keeping users informed and escalating issues appropriately when additional expertise is needed.
  • Troubleshoot computers, mobile devices, peripherals, software, printing, and other end-user technology issues.
  • Diagnose and resolve common LAN/WAN, Wi-Fi, VPN, DNS, DHCP, and endpoint connectivity issues.

Events and A/V Support

  • Partner with internal teams to provide technical support for events, including live streams, executive presentations, playtests, meetings, and other company activities.
  • Set up, operate, and troubleshoot conference room and event A/V technology, including displays, audio systems, video conferencing equipment, and related peripherals.
  • Provide onsite technical support during events as needed to help ensure a smooth experience for presenters and attendees.

Devices, Applications & Employee Lifecycle

  • Utilize the latest device management platforms such as Microsoft Intune, Jamf, Endpoint Central, and others to configure, deploy, and maintain end-use equipment.
  • Support onboarding, employee changes, and departures, including device preparation, account and access coordination, and equipment recovery.

Identity, Access & Security

The ideal candidate will have strong mechanical knowledge and extensive experience working with conveyors, motors, pulleys, screw augers, bucket elevators, bearings, gearboxes, and related equipment. description:
At Cleveland Clinic Health System, we believe in a better future for healthcare. And each of us is responsible for honoring our commitment to excellence, pushing the boundaries and transforming the patient experience, every day.

Job Summary

Job Details

Join Cleveland Clinic’s Fairview Hospital where research and surgery are advanced, technology is leading-edge, patient care is world-class, and caregivers are family. Fairview Hospital has been recognized as one of the top hospitals in Cleveland and Ohio. Here, you will work with and learn from some of our best caregivers, receive endless support and appreciation, and build a rewarding career with one of the most respected healthcare organizations in the world.

Cleveland Clinic Children's Breastfeeding Medicine Clinic provides comprehensive breastfeeding care and support to families in need to help them reach their personal breastfeeding goals. If patients are worried that they’ll have issues breastfeeding, or are looking for additional support from breastfeeding experts, our team can assist.

This is a regular PRN position, with caregivers working rotating day/evening shifts from 7:00 a.m. – 7:30 p.m. and 3:00 p.m. – 11:30 p.m.

A caregiver who excels in this role will:

  • Set up sterile table assuring appropriate supplies, drugs and equipment are available.

  • Participate with RN in counting all sponges, instruments, etc., at appropriate times during the surgical procedure.

  • Assist in draping patient.

  • Assist surgical team members with gowning and gloving.

  • Assure aseptic condition is maintained by the scrubbed surgical team throughout the procedure. Provide for patient safety by actively participating in the intra-op "timeout."

  • Utilize other safety measures such as safety belts, positioning devices and alarms.

  • Collect, identify and label specimens removed during surgical procedures. Give specimens to circulator for disposition per surgeon's instructions.

Minimum qualifications for the ideal future caregiver include:

  • Meets educational/licensing requirements for the International Board of Lactation Consultant Examiners (IBLCE)

  • Basic Life Support (BLS) through American Heart Association (AHA) Healthcare Provide

  • Neonatal Resuscitation Program (NRP) certification within 6 months of hire

  • Certified Lactation Counselor (CLC) certification or equivalent upon hire, with successful completion of IBCLC certification within 24 months of hire

Preferred qualifications for the ideal future caregiver include:

  • Registered Nurse (RN)

  • One year of hospital or community-based nursing experience working with breastfeeding mothers and infants OR two years of nursing experience in a non-related field OR two years of verified lay-experience (paid or voluntary) working with breastfeeding mothers and infants in a hospital-sponsored or community setting under the supervision of an International Board Certified Lactation Consultant (IBCLC) OR two years of experience as certified health and wellness educator/instructor

  • Experience developing and delivering staff education related to breastfeeding management and lactation care

  • Experience in perinatal nursing, obstetrics, pediatrics, neonatal intensive care nursing or related field

  • Experience counseling breastfeeding families inpatient, ambulatory and/or community settings

Our caregivers continue to create the best outcomes for our patients across each of our facilities. Click the link and see how we’re dedicated to providing what matters most to you:

  • Even though the weight lifted may be only a negligible amount, a job should be rated Light Work: (1) when it requires walking or standing to a significant degree; or (2) when it requires sitting most of the time but entails pushing and/or pulling of arm or leg controls; and/or (3) when the job requires working at a production rate pace entailing the constant pushing and/or pulling of materials even though the weight of those materials is negligible.

Education:

Required: Bachelor’s degree or four (4) additional years of experience as Residency Coordinator/Manager in lieu of degree

Preferred: Master's degree


Licensure/Certification:

Preferred: Training Administrators for Graduate Medical Education (TAGME) Certification

Required: Three (3) years of experience in Graduate Medical Education within a residency or fellowship program; Two (2) years of experience with Master's degree

Ages of Patients: N/A

Skills, Knowledge, Abilities:

Able to prioritize and meet deadlines, maintain confidentiality, Able to work independently with minimal supervision; able to supervise and delegate, Demonstrate leadership skills, Excellent interpersonal skills in dealing with the public, hospital and medical staff; ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines; must be “detailed oriented”, Is proficient with computer applications, online resources and equipment utilized by the program, department and institution, including Microsoft Word, Outlook, Office and Excel, Knowledge of Electronic Residency Fellowship Application System (ERAS), NRMP Ranking System, FREIDA, Institution/Department Intranet, ACGME WebAds, Institution computerized financial system, MedHub, Knowledge of Windows applications, graphics applications, spreadsheet applications, internet applications, Participate in institutional, departmental, community, and/or national meetings to remain informed about current academic trends and processes, Possess critical thinking, problem-solving and decision-making skills, Possess effective written and verbal communication skills and exceptional administrative and organizational skills, Understand and apply general financial and budgetary processes, principles and planning, Understand and apply GME program accreditation requirements and guidelines, as well as all other governing agencies, Understand department and institution policies and implementation of these policies within prescribed limits of authority, Understand graduate and continuing medical education, Understand principles of record keeping and confidentiality (including HIPAA compliance), Understand the organizational structure of GME and the relationship between the program, the accreditation and institutional entities, Understand the pressures that physicians face and encourages residents to use appropriate wellness tools

Essential Responsibilities

1. Demonstrates compliance with Code of Conduct and compliance policies, and takes action to resolve compliance questions or concerns and report suspected violations. 2. Responsible for administration of the residency/fellowship program in accordance with the Accreditation Council of Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) accreditation requirements. 3. Oversee the daily operation and logistics of the residency/fellowship program. Direct the work flow and supervise the necessary administrative paperwork, records and complex filing systems to support the program. 4. Provide administrative support to the Program Director of the residency/fellowship and act as an educational liaison between attending physicians, fellows, residents, and institutional and regulatory administrative offices. Serve as a representative and liaison for the Residency/Fellowship Program in cooperative efforts with the faculty, other specialty departments, outside institutions, GME Office, and Medical Staff Office. 5. Oversee projects to achieve Residency/Fellowship goals and objectives. 6. Direct the annual revision of residency/fellowship handbook and website. 7. Assist the Director/Administrator of GME and Program Director in the creation and implementation of new policies and procedures. 8. Assume leadership role, under the direction of the Director/Administrator of GME and Program Director, in accreditation and re-accreditation activities. The Residency/Fellowship Program Manager is a member of the Clinical Competency Committee and Program Evaluation Committee. Maintain all evaluations and annual residency/fellowship review. 9. Assist the Director/Administrator of GME and Program Director in maintaining program accreditation, institutional and departmental compliance. Ensure compliance and maintain an updated fund of knowledge of current ACGME accreditation requirements for the program and institution. Ensure all accreditation documentation is accurate and up to date to meet the ACGME Milestone requirements for the program. Manage annual accreditation reviews and site visit preparations. 10. Develop and oversee the updating of recruitment information (websites, brochures, application software services). Act as liaison between program and prospective candidates. Oversee applicant feedback to improve the recruitment process. Develop and represent programs' image and exposure. Implement residency/fellowship program recruitment plan, time-line and guidelines for the department. 11. Manage the applicant screening and selection of resident/fellow applicants to interview. Oversee the organization of the interview day, including materials, schedule, meals, events, etc. Participate in interviewing residency/fellowship applicants. Manage the preparation and submission of the rank list to the NRMP. Develop all materials used by faculty during interview of candidates. Oversee ERAS installation and applications for the department. Prepare applicant ranking materials. 12. Assist in resident/fellow counseling meetings regarding elective planning, remediation, and disciplinary actions, etc. Ensure and maintain confidentiality and security of all resident/fellow’s files. Oversee the human resource functions at the departmental level, including leave, travel, and other personnel questions. 13. Prepare and manage residency/fellowship department budget. Prepare all administrative processes and systems to maximize IME and DME distribution to the institution. Initiate actions that improve the efficiency of work, reduction of costs, and/or improvement of quality of services. 14. Ensure that incoming residents/fellows are informed of documentation required by the primary institution and state licensing board and maintain records of compliance. Assist and advise Program Director in creating yearly rotation schedule for residents/fellows, incorporating curriculum requirements, and creating yearly elective and vacation schedules for the program. 15. Assist the Program Director with block and assignment schedules to ensure accreditation compliance regarding duty hours. Develop new policies and procedures in response to new or revised policies ensuring compliance with ACGME requirements. 16. Oversee and assist with enforcement of program and resident/fellow compliance according to the policies and regulations set by the accreditation council, program, department, and institution. Manage the preparation and submission of reports to governing bodies and professional organizations. Manage the preparation and submission of all post graduate training verifications. 17. Verify accuracy of statistics used for reporting to FREIDA, AMA and the National Resident Matching Program (NRMP). 18. Schedules in-service/in-training annual exams. 19. Ensure residents/fellows are compliant with current documentation for licensing and institutional requirements. Ensure that licensing and credentialing processes for foreign medical applicants are adhered. 20. Assist Program Director in the faculty development process. Ensure that faculty credentials are current. 21. Allocate and manage resident/fellow housing for offsite rotations. 22. Prepare and manage of contracts for faculty, residents/fellows, outside affiliations, program letters of agreements, and vendors. 23. Assist with the orientation of the new residents/fellows, including training and accesses to institutional systems (pager, security access, phone, computer, etc.). Assist with the transitioning of new residents/fellows into the program. Oversee general orientation of new residents/fellows (includes department, clinical areas and institution). 24. Oversee and assist Program Director with resident/fellow events and activities (graduation, retreat, resident/fellow events, etc.). 25. Performs other duties as assigned

Ticketmaster is the global leader in event ticketing with over 500 million tickets sold annually and more than 12,000 clients worldwide. For additional information, visit .

Who are you?

Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on!

The Role:

The Venue Nation Analytics team is looking for a talented intern to support Food & Beverage (F&B) analytics across our owned and operated venues. This is a paid internship that will be expected to start as soon as possible in 2027 on part-time hours (10-20 hours a week).
