Job Summary

Job Details

Join our team at Cleveland Clinic Weston Hospital!

Our team manages all cases, excluding trauma, OB, open heart, and liver. Most of our AAs work 12-hour shifts. These positions do not involve weekday call or working nights.

Embrace the opportunity to be a part of a collegial work environment, where CRNAs, AAs and MDAs come together to ensure the highest level of patient care.

The city of Weston is in Broward County, just west of Fort Lauderdale. Weston is ~30 miles northwest of Miami and part of the Miami metropolitan area.

We are proud to offer a competitive benefits package including:

  • Competitive compensation and supplemental pay rate

  • Sign-on bonuses for eligible new graduates and experienced providers

  • Student loan repayment

  • Paid time off plus 6 paid holidays

  • CEU package and internal CEU opportunities

  • Professional reimbursements

  • Exceptional Medical, Dental, Vision Benefits - effective day one of employment

  • Employer paid life insurance

  • Short and long-term disability coverage for full-time caregivers

  • Parental leave equal to 100% pay up to 12 weeks (full-time caregivers)

  • Relocation reimbursement

  • Paid interview expenses

  • Retirement Savings Plans (up to 5.5% total Cleveland Clinic contributions immediately upon hire/ increases with years of service)

  • Malpractice covered at no cost to the AA

  • Research and teaching opportunities (not required, but available if interested)

  • Cleveland Clinic is an eligible employer for PSLF (Public Student Loan Forgiveness)

Working under the direction of a Staff Anesthesiologist, administers anesthesia to patients rendering them insensitive to pain during surgery. Monitors the patient's physical reaction to the anesthetic and informs the physician of any adverse condition. Administers emergency measures when complications arise.

Responsibilities:

  • Obtains a comprehensive patient history and performs relevant elements of a physical exam.

  • Discusses findings and anesthetic plan with anesthesiologist before induction of anesthesia.

  • Reviews patient's condition with anesthesiologist immediately prior to induction of anesthesia.

  • This includes changes in patient's condition, review of administration of any pre-anesthesia medication, selection of anesthetic agent and technique.

  • Pretests and calibrates anesthesia delivery systems.

  • Administers anesthetic drugs, adjuvant drugs and accessory drugs.

  • Assists anesthesiologist with the implementation of medically accepted monitoring techniques, epidural anesthetic procedures, spinal anesthetic procedures and other regional anesthetic techniques.

  • Recognizes and takes appropriate action for abnormal patient responses during anesthesia, including resuscitation, until patient regains control of vital functions.

  • Administers blood, blood products and supportive fluids. Provides post-anesthesia recovery care to the patient for as long as necessary, keeping anesthesiologist informed as to the patient's progress.

  • Displays title of Anesthesiology Assistant as a means of identifying the individual's authority to practice.

  • Other duties as assigned.

Education:

  • A baccalaureate or higher degree from an institution of higher learning accredited by an organization recognized by the board of regents.

  • Completion of an anesthesiologist assistant training program that has been accredited by the commission on accreditation of allied health education programs, or equivalent.

Certifications:

  • Certification by the National Commission for Certification of Anesthesiologist Assistants (AA).

  • Current, valid Anesthesiologist Assistant (AA) license in the state of Florida. Basic Life Support (BLS) Certification.

  • Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS).

title: Assistant Residence Director
description:
We are located approximately 20 miles north of Boston and parking is free. We are also accessible by commuter rail on the Newburyport/Rockport line. Come and explore Endicott’s seaside locale where employees are an important part of the bustling campus community!

Please apply today if this opportunity looks like the right fit for you.

.

Under the guidance and supervision of a Residence Director (RD), the Assistant Residence Director (ARD) plays a vital leadership role within the Office of Residence Life. The ARD is responsible for the day-to-day oversight of a residential community, including the supervision and development of a team of Resident Assistants (RAs), supporting a diverse population of students living in Endicott housing, and serving as a conduct hearing officer. This position also participates in an on-call duty rotation, providing crisis response and support for residential students.


The ARD is a live-in, full-time, 10-month professional staff position designed for individuals pursuing a Master's degree. The role provides an opportunity for hands-on experience in student affairs and higher education administration while contributing to a supportive, engaging, and inclusive campus community. This position is offered as a three-year term.


This live-in role requires the Residence Director (RD) to maintain their primary residence in the assigned on-campus housing as a condition of employment. Housing must be vacated immediately upon separation from the College, regardless of the reason for termination.

Key Outcomes
50%: Residential Community & Supervision

  • Provide direct supervision, training, and performance evaluations for a team of Resident Assistants (RAs)
  • Implement residential education initiatives, including RA-led engagement programming, departmental signature events, and cross-departmental collaborations
  • Support departmental initiatives that foster student engagement, inclusion, and community building in the residential experience
  • Oversee the occupancy management of assigned residential areas, including coordination of check-ins/check-outs, room changes, building and room condition reports (BCRs/RCRs), roommate agreements, safety inspections, and damage billing
  • Assist with broader Residence Life operations such as housing selection, break closings, and summer transition planning

30%: Student Conduct and On-Call

  • Participate in the on-call duty rotation, providing crisis response for psychological, medical, Title IX, and facilities-related emergencies, and following established College protocols
  • Serve as a conduct hearing officer to address student behavioral concerns and policy violations in accordance with the Office of Community Standards
  • Facilitate conflict resolution and follow-up with students involved in conduct-related matter

20%: Departmental Initiatives Support

  • Lead and support departmental programming efforts through RA engagement initiatives, signature events, and collaborative programs with other campus offices
  • Promote initiatives that align with the College’s goals around student learning, belonging, and development in the residential setting

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

  • Bachelor’s degree required and preference of candidates who are pursuing a Master’s degree in Student Affairs, Higher Education Administration, or related field.
  • Previous experience in Residence Life and/or Student Affairs highly recommended.
  • Ability and willingness to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends.
  • Ability to represent Office of Residence Life, and Endicott College in a professional demeanor in person, on the phone and in written correspondences.
  • Must be energetic and detail oriented with excellent management and organizational skills
  • Must be detail oriented
  • Professional and pleasant manner with outstanding interpersonal and leadership skills is essential

In compliance with Massachusetts pay transparency law, the annual base salary range for this position is $32,000 - 34,000. Endicott College considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, relevant work experience, education, specialized skills, internal equity, and external market data when extending an offer. The final salary is determined by the Human Resources Office based on these factors. This range reflects base salary only and does not include benefits or other compensation.

title: Job Posting Title:  AI Pilot & Data Senior Technical Writer
description:
Job Title: Job Posting Title: AI Pilot & Data Senior Technical Writer

Job Category: Engineering and Technical Support

Employee Type: Regular

Percentage of Travel Required: Up to 10%

Type of Travel: Local

* * *


The Opportunity:
CACI is seeking an experienced AI Pilot & Data Senior Technical Writer to support the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of the Inspector General (OIG). This role offers a unique opportunity to document how artificial intelligence is tested and put to work in federal oversight, where accuracy matters as much as it does in an audit report or an investigation.
As the AI Pilot & Data Senior Technical Writer, you will turn the work of AI engineers, data engineers, and analysts into clear, accurate documentation that Government decision-makers, reviewers, and the next team can rely on. You will write the deliverables for OIG's AI pilots, from pilot charters and solution designs to validation reports and transition and knowledge-transfer packages, and you will build the data dictionaries for each pilot's data sets, which become the starting content for the enterprise data catalog on the new data platform. Working closely with the AI & Data Use-Case Program Manager, AI engineers, and Government Product Owners, you will make sure every pilot is documented well enough to decide on, support, and build on. The position is primarily remote, with on-site work at DHS OIG headquarters in Washington, DC as requested, during core hours of 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM Eastern. Join us to make OIG's AI work understandable, auditable, and ready to scale.




Responsibilities:
The Opportunity:
CACI is seeking an experienced AI Pilot & Data Senior Technical Writer to support the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of the Inspector General (OIG). This role offers a unique opportunity to document how artificial intelligence is tested and put to work in federal oversight, where accuracy matters as much as it does in an audit report or an investigation.
As the AI Pilot & Data Senior Technical Writer, you will turn the work of AI engineers, data engineers, and analysts into clear, accurate documentation that Government decision-makers, reviewers, and the next team can rely on. You will write the deliverables for OIG's AI pilots, from pilot charters and solution designs to validation reports and transition and knowledge-transfer packages, and you will build the data dictionaries for each pilot's data sets, which become the starting content for the enterprise data catalog on the new data platform. Working closely with the AI & Data Use-Case Program Manager, AI engineers, and Government Product Owners, you will make sure every pilot is documented well enough to decide on, support, and build on. The position is primarily remote, with on-site work at DHS OIG headquarters in Washington, DC as requested, during core hours of 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM Eastern. Join us to make OIG's AI work understandable, auditable, and ready to scale.

Responsibilities:
• Write and maintain pilot charters, requirements, and solution design documents for AI pilot applications, working from discovery sessions, engineering notes, and Government Product Owner input
• Document test plans, output validation methods and results, and user acceptance testing outcomes in reports that show Government reviewers how each pilot was tested and what it can and cannot reliably do
• Produce transition-to-sustainment and knowledge-transfer packages, including runbooks, administrator guides, known limitations, and hand-off checklists, so operations staff and the help desk can support a pilot before it is called done
• Build data dictionaries and data set documentation for each pilot's data, covering sources, fields, definitions, sensitivity, lineage, data owners and stewards, and approved uses, written to seed the enterprise data catalog
• Document responsible AI information for each pilot, including intended use, data used, evaluation results, human review steps, and limitations, in a consistent format across pilots
• Edit technical analyses, decision packages, and recommendations into plain language for non-technical Government leaders while keeping them technically accurate
• Interview AI engineers, data engineers, UX researchers, and Government subject matter experts to verify technical accuracy, and manage reviews and versions through Government acceptance
• Apply document standards, templates, and naming conventions, and keep the document library current so each deliverable can be found from the service it supports
• Ensure deliverables meet Section 508 accessibility requirements and handle SPII, Law Enforcement Sensitive, and FOUO information according to DHS and OIG rules
• Support quality reviews and contract deliverable timelines, and provide documentation status for monthly progress reports


Qualifications:

Required:
• Associate's degree + 6 years of experience in technical writing or documentation for software, data, or IT systems; equivalencies considered (Bachelor's + 4 years; 8 years with no degree)
• U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a DHS Public Trust (High Risk) fitness determination
• Demonstrated experience writing technical documentation for software or data systems, such as requirements, design documents, test reports, runbooks, or user guides, based on interviews with engineers and subject matter experts
• Experience documenting data, such as data dictionaries, data models, metadata, or catalog entries, including definitions, lineage, and data sensitivity
• Experience producing Section 508 conformant documents and working to style guides, templates, and version control in a federal or other regulated environment
• Ability to explain complex technical content clearly and accurately for non-technical readers
Desired –
• Familiarity with AI and generative AI concepts, such as model evaluation, output validation, prompts, and retrieval, and with documentation practices such as model cards
• Experience with data catalog or governance tools such as Unity Catalog, Microsoft Purview, or Collibra, and with platforms such as Databricks or Microsoft Azure
• Certification such as Certified Professional Technical Communicator (CPTC) or DHS Trusted Tester, and experience with Confluence, SharePoint, Jira, or docs-as-code tools such as Git and Markdown
• Background in federal oversight, audit, investigative, law enforcement, or legal documentation, where accuracy and evidentiary standards matter


-

A culture of integrity.

At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation.

CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.

title: Dental/Oral Surgery Assistant
description:
The following position is for employment with:

George A Maranon, DDS., MD Shahe Dishakjian, DDS

16311 Ventura Blvd, Suite 820 Encino, CA 91436

Dental Assistant – Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery

We are seeking an experienced Dental Assistant with hands-on oral surgery experience to join our patient-centered Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery practice in the Mid-San Fernando Valley.

POSITION PURPOSE

The Oral Surgery Assistant plays an essential role in providing safe, efficient, and compassionate surgical care. This position assists the surgeon during consultations and surgical procedures, supports patients throughout their treatment experience, and helps maintain an organized and efficient clinical environment.

The ideal candidate is dependable, detail-oriented, comfortable in a dental surgery setting, and committed to providing an exceptional patient experience.

PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES

  • Dental/Surgical Assistance: Assist the surgeon during oral and maxillofacial surgical procedures, including tooth extractions, wisdom tooth removal, dental implant placement, and bone grafting procedures.

  • Patient Preparation: Seat and prepare patients for consultations and surgical procedures, obtain and document vital signs, and confirm required consent forms and treatment documentation are complete.

  • Anesthesia Monitoring: Assist with and maintain competency in patient monitoring during IV sedation and anesthesia in accordance with established office protocols.

  • Pre and Post Operative Care: Provide patients with clear pre-operative and post-operative instructions and reinforce the surgeon's recommendations regarding surgical care and recovery.

  • Patient Coordination: Assist in obtaining medical clearances and other necessary documentation prior to treatment.

  • Radiography (X-Rays): Obtain diagnostic dental radiographs using appropriate exposure techniques, patient positioning, and radiation-safety procedures.

  • Clinical Documentation: Accurately document patient information, treatment, and clinical notes in accordance with established practice standards.

  • Surgical Setup and Breakdown: Prepare operatories, surgical equipment, instruments, and materials before procedures and complete proper breakdown following treatment.

  • Equipment Maintenance: Ensure clinical and surgical equipment is properly maintained and in good working condition.

  • Safety and Compliance: Follow applicable OSHA, radiation-safety, infection-control, and office safety policies and procedures.

  • Patient Experience: Promote patient comfort, address concerns professionally, and help create a positive and reassuring experience throughout each visit.

  • Team Collaboration: Maintain professional and cooperative relationships with surgeons, patients, and team members. Communicate effectively and contribute constructively to problem-solving.

  • Confidentiality: Protect patient and practice information and maintain confidentiality in accordance with applicable requirements and office policies.

  • Additional Responsibilities: Assist with special projects and other clinical responsibilities as needed.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Minimum of 1 year of dental assisting experience

  • Experience assisting with:
    • Tooth extractions, including wisdom teeth
    • Dental implant procedures
    • Bone grafting procedures
    • Oral surgery setup and breakdown
    • Sterilization and instrument processing
  • Experience obtaining dental radiographs (X-rays)
  • Experience monitoring patients during IV sedation and following anesthesia protocols
  • Strong patient care and interpersonal skills
  • Clear and professional verbal communication skills
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to work efficiently
  • Ability to follow clinical protocols, safety procedures, and office policies
  • Ability to work effectively as part of a team
  • Ability to remain attentive and composed in a surgical environment

  • Flexibility to adapt to changing responsibilities and schedules

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 2+ years of dental assisting experience
  • Previous experience working as an Oral Surgery Assistant
  • Experience assisting with dental implant procedures and systems such as Nobel Biocare, DTX, and Straumann
  • OMSA and/or DAANCE certification

  • Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Assisting or Dental Assistant certification

CERTIFICATIONS AND HEALTH/SAFETY REQUIREMENTS

  • Current Basic Life Support (BLS)/CPR certification required

  • California Registered Dental Assistant (RDA) license OR completion of a Dental Board of California–approved 8-hour Infection Control course required

  • Hepatitis B vaccination and/or documented immunity/titer as required by applicable practice policies and regulations
  • TB screening/testing as required by applicable practice policies and regulations

ABOUT US ORAL SURGERY MANAGEMENT

By joining US Oral Surgery Management (USOSM), you become part of a dynamic and forward-thinking organization made up of best-in-class Oral and Maxillofacial practices. Together, we have the POWER to achieve more, by creating a positive impact on the communities we serve and reinforcing our position as a top leader in the industry. We believe in the POWER of teamwork, where every member contributes to our collective success. Whether you're in clinical operations, administration, support services, etc., your role is crucial to achieving our shared mission: fueling innovation and clinical excellence, while driving worthwhile outcomes for our practices.

Our POWER Values form the foundation of our ability to deliver exceptional healthcare experiences and achieve sustainable growth.

description:
Campbell Oil Company - Financial Analyst I

Elizabethtown, NC

Join us as we grow together personally and professionally! Four generations of family leadership continue to make it our vision to leave people better than we found them. We are more than an oil company, convenience store or restaurant, we are family! We are improving the lives of those we touch every day by valuing the customer, caring for our 1000+ team members and supporting our communities that we are honored to serve.

Position Overview

The Financial Analyst is a member of the Financial Services team at Campbell Oil Company responsible for evaluating customer creditworthiness, underwriting credit terms, monitoring account performance, and driving timely collections. This full-time position safeguards the company’s accounts receivable (“AR”) by reducing financial risk, ensuring accurate billing and payment compliance, and maintaining strong professional relationships with customers and internal sales teams. The ideal candidate will be a self-starter with a continuous improvement mindset exercising strong communication and analytical skills while seamlessly toggling between multiple priorities and financial procedures to ensure all deadlines are met in a timely matter.

Benefits

  • Family first atmosphere
  • Benefits to fit your needs: Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Disability, 401k

  • Paid time off in first year
  • Team first environment
  • Remote work in select roles
  • Monthly teambuilding exercises
  • Flexible schedules to attend family events
  • Professional training
  • Advancement opportunities
  • Leadership training

Key Responsibilities:

Credit/Underwriting

  • Review and analyze new and existing customer credit applications, financial statements, credit reports, and trade references.
  • Assess creditworthiness and establish appropriate credit limits and terms according to company policies.
  • Monitor ongoing credit risk and proactively adjust credit limits based on customer performance, industry trends, and exposure.
  • Maintain organized records of credit decisions and ensure compliance with internal approval guidelines.

Accounts Receivable & Collections

  • Manage assigned portfolio of accounts to ensure timely payments and reduce past due balances.
  • Communicate with customers regarding outstanding invoices, payment discrepancies, and account issues.
  • Resolve billing disputes in coordination with internal teams (sales, billing, logistics, etc.).

Collaboration & Customer Support

  • Partner with sales teams to balance credit risk with business growth opportunities.

  • Support process improvements that drive AR efficiency and enhance credit risk management practices.

description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections, where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

This is an exciting time to join the Roche Support Network. If you are passionate about problem solving then this is the position for you! As a research-focused healthcare company, Roche discovers, develops and provides innovative diagnostics and therapeutic products and services that deliver significant benefits to patients and healthcare professionals - from early detection and prevention of diseases to diagnostics, treatment and treatment monitoring.


Roche is a successful company that can offer exciting career opportunities. We encourage and support your development in areas of your interest which will prepare you for the next level in your career path. We know that people are responsible for our success and we value our employees. Our commitment is to create a work environment where feeling valued, respected, and empowered is a daily experience.


As a Field Applications Specialist, you will be a key member of our Customer Support team as the primary scientific and technical representative in the Omaha, NE area for Roche systems in customer laboratories within the Core Lab space. You will be responsible for providing best-in-class on-site customer support, including activities such as application implementation, operator training, and troubleshooting for diagnostic instrumentation and assays throughout the entire product life cycle.


The Opportunity:


  • Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with customer stakeholders, ensuring a high level of customer satisfaction and creating value within the customer’s lab operations. Consult with customers on lab needs and act as a partner by supporting the customer throughout the product lifecycle which could include supporting product upgrades and other changes.
  • Perform and/or assist with the installation of complex diagnostic instruments, software, and reagent applications in customer laboratories. Validate system performance to ensure it meets manufacturer specifications. Ensure effective and cohesive application of the newly installed solutions.
  • Deliver and, in some cases, develop comprehensive on-site training to laboratory personnel on the proper use and maintenance of Roche systems, including theory of operation, workflow, quality control, and data interpretation.
  • Act as the primary on-site resource for resolving complex technical issues related to instrumentation, software, and assay performance. Perform root cause analysis and implement corrective actions to minimize instrument downtime. Partner with other Roche team members to implement and support total solutions, such as automation, digital tools, etc.
  • Provide scientific and applications expertise to laboratory stakeholders (this could include supervisors, managers, directors, technologists) and medical professionals (this could include pathologists, doctors), helping them ensure cohesive lab operations by optimizing workflows, implementing new assays, and interpreting results for Roche's portfolio.
  • Serve as the customer liaison and collect feedback from customers on product performance, features, and usability, and then relay this information back to support and commercial teams, maintaining a competitive advantage.
  • Partner with the sales team and leverage in-depth technical knowledge during pre-sales activities, including product demonstrations, technical consultations, menu optimization, and other post-sales, revenue-generating opportunities.
  • Ensure consistent customer experiences by following Roche protocols and procedures. Maintain accurate and timely records of all service activities, customer interactions, and technical issues using Roche’s CRM system. Complete all administrative duties, such as travel and expense reporting, as required.
  • Overnight travel within a designated territory, which can range from a specific state to a larger region.
  • This is a field-based role - the territory will cover the Omaha, NE area. 50% travel is expected for this position. The ideal candidate for this role will reside in the Omaha, NE area

Who you are:


  • Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Chemistry, Cell Biology, Biochemistry, Medical Technology, Clinical Laboratory, and/or relevant experience.
  • 3 years of previous experience in a clinical laboratory or IT in a clinical lab environment (including internships, college, certification time, etc.)

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Medical Laboratory Technologist/Scientist (ASCP/AMT) or equivalent clinical laboratory experience in a clinical environment.
  • Experience working in a clinical environment with a demonstrated knowledge of clinical chemistry and immunoassay.
  • Ability to learn Roche solutions for applicable franchises (i.e. chemistry, immunology, life sciences, IT solutions), and stay current with industry trends.
  • Diagnose and solve technical problems efficiently and effectively.
  • Experience implementing new instrumentation or methodologies in a clinical or research laboratory environment
  • Effective written/verbal communication skills as well as project and stakeholder management experience.
  • Effective customer consultative skills which includes advanced scientific knowledge and analysis, training, exceptional customer engagement, and fostering of strong customer relationships.
  • Demonstrated ability to coach and mentor junior staff and lead by example.
  • Ability to work as a field based individual contributor with independence and autonomy.

title: Learning Experience Designer
description:

  • Contribute to the evolution of learning design standards and best practices across curricula.

  • Strong experience as a Learning Experience Designer (LXD) or Instructional Designer, with a proven track record of building complex, skill-based learning programs from scratch.
  • Proficient level of English (from B2 level) with exceptional writing skills, capable of crafting clear, engaging, and pedagogically sound learning materials.
  • Demonstrated mastery of curriculum mapping, competency-based education, instructional scaffolding, and assessment design.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills to effectively interview SMEs, extract implicit knowledge, and align with product and content teams.
  • Data-informed approach to learning design, using qualitative feedback (CustDev) and quantitative performance data to iterate on educational content.

Nice-to-have:

  • Experience working in fast-paced EdTech or modern product environments.
  • Hands-on experience with modern LXD tools, LMS platforms, and user research methodology.

From a small family business to a multi-billion-dollar global company, Sonoco has been changing the face of products and packaging since 1899 — all while keeping the heart of “People Build Businesses” alive.

Reporting directly to the Department Manager, the Tool Room Supervisor is responsible for leading and developing a team of machinists while overseeing tool room operations, work scheduling, quality assurance, tooling inspections, safety compliance, equipment calibration, and continuous improvement initiatives to support efficient manufacturing operations.



What you’ll be doing:

  • Supervising 6 - 8 direct reports in the Machinist classification.

This includes correcting unsafe acts/conditions, communicating facility wide Leading 2 Lean (L2L) level 1, 2 & 3 safety incidents, performing monthly safety inspections, and investigating accidents, as required.

  • Monitors machine shop finished products by inspecting the quality, analyzing trends and deviations, and making recommendations for improvement.
  • Performs quality assurance inspections on tooling received by suppliers. Provides specialized inspection service by analyzing the fitness of incoming materials and determining the fitness to standards. Informs plant leadership of and significant tooling deviations received from tooling suppliers or assembled in the machine shop that would impact the manufacturing process. Uses judgment in determining the significance of process deviations to prevent production or shipment of substandard products, isolates defective products, and executes sampling plans to determine fitness for use.
  • Originates activity reports on daily inventories, tooling usage, and process deviations.
  • Maintains all machine shop measurement gauges and inspections on the equipment. Control system to provide and calibrate gauges and instruments as required. This includes the initiation of requisitions to ensure compliance with group standards.

  • Interacts with vendors and suppliers. Accesses, inputs, and retrieves information from the computer.

title: Production Specialist
description:
At Curriculum Associates, we believe in the potential of every child and are changing the face of education technology with award-winning learning programs like i-Ready that serve a third of the nation’s K–8 students. For more than 50 years, our commitment to making classrooms better places, serving educators, and supporting accessible learning experiences for all students has driven the continuous improvement of our innovative programs. The Production Specialist will provide composition, layout, and graphic support to both our internal and offshore Production teams. The successful candidate in this role will take an active part in the development, fulfilment, and maintenance of print and digital educational material, ensuring the timely delivery of high-quality products. In addition to core composition work, this role collaborates with cross-functional design, editorial, and production teams to resolve production bottlenecks — including a growing set of automation and scripting tasks (e.g., InDesign ExtendScript, Acrobat JavaScript) to increase efficiency.

  • Work extensively with files in Adobe InDesign and Acrobat, owning the fidelity of InDesign files for assigned projects — including illustration and photo work in Illustrator and Photoshop.

  • Apply or maintain accessibility features according to guidelines and best practices, including PDF remediation and InDesign accessibility.
  • Communicate regularly with supervisors, vendors, and internal and external teams to accomplish project goals and meet deadlines.

  • Support automation and scripting initiatives (e.g., InDesign Extend Script, UXP Plug-ins, Acrobat JavaScript) to streamline recurring production tasks.

Here’s how you’ll contribute:

  • Ensure the product's adherence to all laws pertaining to copyrighted and public domain material usage and permissions, including but not limited to images, fonts, and texts.
  • Support metadata collection and file structure to meet content re-purposing goals.
  • Read, understand, and apply information from a Style Guide across assigned projects.
  • Attend and participate in project meetings. Document and follow up on important actions and decisions.
  • Ensure projects adhere to best practices, and all documentation is maintained appropriately.
  • Deliver final products and project deliverables successfully according to prioritized schedules.
  • Manage multiple responsibilities across multiple projects at once.
  • Apply InDesign ExtendScript (JSX), UXP Plug-ins and Acrobat JavaScript, where applicable, to automate recurring composition and QA tasks.
  • Build and maintain existing InDesign, Acrobat scripts and plug-ins to support the wider Production team across US and India.
  • Design and build AI-enabled automation workflows, including integrations with Claude, GitHub Copilot, and AWS Bedrock, to accelerate content production and QA.
  • Ensure automated outputs meet accessibility and production requirements to support efficient handoffs.
  • Demonstrate accuracy and attention to detail across all deliverables.

What You’ll Bring

  • Experience with Adobe products, including InDesign, Acrobat, Illustrator, and Photoshop.
  • Understanding of Editorial markup and how to implement.
  • Working knowledge of InDesign ExtendScript (JSX), UXP Plug-ins, Python, and Acrobat JavaScript to support automation initiatives.
  • A strong understanding of Adobe Creative Cloud scripting environments and production workflow best practices.
  • Successful delivery of final products and project deliverables according to prioritized schedules.
  • Ability to manage multiple responsibilities across multiple projects.
  • Effective communication with coworkers, managers, other teams, and offshore Production vendors/partners.
  • Excellent time management and ability to multi-task; ability to work independently.
  • Demonstrated accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Hands-on experience with AI tools, including Copilot, Claude, and AWS Bedrock.

Key Skills & Expertise

Experience with Adobe InDesign, Acrobat, Illustrator, and Photoshop publishing workflows is required; exposure to automation and scripting knowledge.

Software:

  • (Proficient) Content management systems, Woodwing preferred
  • (Expert) InDesign Extend Script (JSX), Python and UXP plug-in development for automation
  • (Proficient) Acrobat JavaScript scripting for PDF automation and remediation
  • (Bonus) Exhibited ability to learn new software, tools, and systems
  • (Bonus) Experience in creating AI agents and working with different LLM models

Experience & Education

  • 5+ years of related Education publishing/production experience in EdTech (Print Books and Digital), GK-12 with a bachelor's degree or equivalent field.

title: MISTC Instructor/Site Lead
description:
Job purpose

Provides unit and individual training via the Command and Control Training, Education Center of Excellence (C2TECOE), and the MAGTF Integrated Systems Training Centers (MISTC) in COC Operations, tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) as well as COC systems training Special Purpose MAGTF staffs, Battalion Staffs, Regimental Staffs, and individuals on the proper functioning, employment, roles and responsibilities, and COC system integration, TTPs, and concepts. The COC Specialist is the MISTC’s Subject Matter Expert for Command and Control and primary instructor for C2 courses and training events. The COC Specialist reports to and receives work direction derivatives from the Project Manager in coordination with the Academics Manager.

Duties and responsibilities

  • Provides instruction and training on the operations and employment of digital and analog command and control systems and tools that support the integration of maneuver, fires, intelligence, force protection, logistics, command and control, and aviation operations in the Command and Control (C2) node.
  • Provides instruction and training to Unit Staff members on Command and Control as a warfighting function, Information Management, employment of C2 Systems, and the roles and responsibilities of Watch Officers, Watch Chiefs, and Watch Standers and all members of the C2 node for Operating Force Units.
  • Assists with the maintenance of Master Lesson Files, After Course Management, and Program of Instruction Development in order to support Academics Management.
  • Acts as a Subject Matter Expert, Mentor, and/or Faculty Advisor during Battle Staff Training Exercises and the execution of scheduled POI Events.
  • Coordinates with Commands and Staff Sections to tailor and execute a C2 Training Continuum in support of the MAGTF Training Plan (MCO 3500.11F)
  • Mentors MISTC Staff on the functions of the Exercise Control (EXCON)/White Cell operations in support of the Watch Officer/Watch Chief Course and COC Battle Staff Training exercises.
  • Assists with Operation Order development during preparation and execution of Battle Staff Training Events.
  • Maintains currency with the C2 METS.
  • Incorporates new concepts and TTPs in accordance with available resources and doctrine.
  • Performs other related duties incidental to the work described.
  • Provides instruction IAW approved POI.

title: Population Health Coding & Documentation Integrity (CDI) Auditor
description:
Use your expertise in value-based care, HCC coding, and documentation integrity to improve population health outcomes.


Pennant Services is seeking an experienced Population Health Coding & Documentation Integrity Auditor to join our Population Health team.


This role is ideal for a professional with deep expertise in ACO operations, value-based care, risk adjustment, CMS-HCC methodology, ICD-10-CM coding, and clinical documentation integrity who enjoys translating complex clinical information into accurate, compliant documentation and coding practices.

This is not a traditional coding role focused solely on claim submission. Instead, you will serve as a strategic partner to providers and operational leaders, ensuring that documentation accurately reflects patient complexity, supports value-based care initiatives, and strengthens population health performance.

The successful candidate will be responsible for reviewing medical records, conducting documentation and coding audits, identifying risk adjustment opportunities, educating providers, and helping improve the quality and accuracy of clinical documentation across Pennant's value-based care programs.


What You'll Do

  • Conduct prospective and retrospective documentation and coding reviews for Medicare and value-based care populations.
  • Perform detailed chart audits to evaluate documentation accuracy, coding compliance, and risk-adjustment capture.
  • Identify missed, unsupported, under-documented, or inaccurately reported diagnoses.
  • Validate ICD-10-CM diagnosis coding and clinical support for reported conditions.
  • Review documentation for compliance with CMS-HCC and other risk-adjustment methodologies.
  • Identify opportunities to improve documentation specificity, clinical accuracy, and risk capture.
  • Analyze coding and documentation trends across providers, practices, and patient populations.
  • Partner with physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, coders, and population health leaders to improve documentation quality.
  • Develop and deliver provider education focused on HCC documentation, risk adjustment, coding compliance, and value-based care performance.
  • Research CMS regulations, coding guidance, and risk adjustment requirements to support operational excellence.
  • Create audit reports, educational materials, provider scorecards, and documentation improvement resources.
  • Support ACO, MSSP, Medicare Advantage, and other value-based care initiatives.
  • Collaborate with operational and clinical leadership to improve documentation workflows and population health outcomes.

What We're Looking For

We are seeking a highly analytical professional with significant experience in documentation integrity, coding audits, risk adjustment, and value-based care.


Required

  • Minimum 3 years of experience in risk adjustment, coding compliance, clinical documentation integrity, population health, value-based care, or a related healthcare field.
  • Expertise in MSSP, HCC capture, provider auditing, RAF optimization, documentation integrity, and value-based reimbursement.
  • Strong knowledge of:
    • ICD-10-CM coding
    • CMS-HCC risk adjustment methodology
    • Clinical documentation integrity principles
    • Medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, and chronic disease management
  • Experience conducting chart audits and medical record reviews.
  • Experience identifying documentation opportunities and coding accuracy concerns.
  • Demonstrated expertise in Medicare risk adjustment and HCC documentation requirements.
  • Strong understanding of ACOs, value-based reimbursement models, and population health strategies.
  • Ability to analyze clinical documentation and coding patterns across provider populations.
  • Excellent communication and provider education skills.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and critical-thinking ability.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating across multidisciplinary teams.

We'd Especially Like to Meet You If You Have

  • Clinical Documentation Integrity/Improvement (CDI) experience
  • Population health or value-based care experience
  • Medicare Advantage or risk-adjustment experience
  • Experience with CMS-HCC documentation and coding
  • Coding or clinical documentation auditing experience
  • Provider education experience
  • Experience with prospective and retrospective chart review
  • Experience caring for medically complex or chronically ill populations
  • A BSN
  • CPC, CRC, CDIP, CCDS, or another relevant documentation/coding credential

Preferred

  • Experience supporting:
    • Medicare Shared Savings Program (MSSP)
    • ACO REACH or successor value-based care models
    • Medicare Advantage risk adjustment programs
    • Population health management initiatives
  • Experience performing coding audits and compliance reviews.
  • Experience developing provider feedback and educational programs.
  • Experience with prospective and retrospective HCC review programs.
  • Familiarity with eClinicalWorks, HomeCare HomeBase, PCC, or other EHR platforms.
  • Knowledge of CMS documentation requirements and Medicare regulations.

Preferred Certifications

One or more of the following:

  • Certified Risk Adjustment Coder (CRC)
  • Certified Professional Coder (CPC)
  • Certified Professional Medical Auditor (CPMA)
  • Certified Documentation Expert Outpatient (CDEO)
  • Certified Documentation Integrity Practitioner (CDIP)
  • Certified Clinical Documentation Specialist (CCDS)
  • RHIA or RHIT
  • CCS or CCS-P

Clinical licensure (RN, LPN, PA, NP, etc.) is welcomed but not required.

The Kind of Person Who Will Thrive in This Role:

  • Value-based care focused. You understand how accurate documentation impacts quality performance, risk adjustment, compliance, and patient outcomes.
  • An HCC expert. You know how to identify documentation opportunities, validate coding accuracy, and ensure diagnoses are clinically supported and compliant.
  • Analytical. You enjoy reviewing records, identifying patterns, and translating findings into meaningful action.
  • Provider-centric. You can educate physicians and advanced practice providers in a collaborative, practical way that improves documentation without creating unnecessary burden.
  • Compliance-minded. You understand the difference between appropriate risk capture and unsupported coding.
  • Data-driven. You use audit findings and population trends to drive improvement and measure success.
  • Continuous-improvement oriented. You look beyond individual charts to improve processes, provider performance, and organizational results.

Work LocationThis is a full-time, 40-hour-per-week position with a flexible remote work arrangement.

  • Preference will be given to candidates based in or near Draper, Utah, and/or those residing within the Mountain Time Zone. Candidates located in other regions will be considered if they are able and willing to travel periodically to the Draper office and other Pennant locations as needed for meetings, provider education, audits, training, collaboration, and other business activities.
  • While this role may be performed remotely, regular availability during Mountain Time Zone business hours is strongly preferred to support effective collaboration with providers, operational leaders, and Pennant team members.
  • Periodic travel, including travel to the Draper, Utah office and affiliated operations, should be expected based on business needs.

Why This Role Matters

  • Great population health starts with understanding the patient accurately.
  • The documentation in the medical record informs how an organization understands disease burden, identifies care opportunities, measures outcomes, manages populations, and succeeds in value-based care.
  • In this position, your expertise in documentation integrity, coding, risk adjustment, and value-based care will help ensure that patient complexity is accurately captured and represented.
  • You'll help bridge the gap between clinical care, documentation, coding, and population health strategy by providing providers with practical guidance that improves documentation quality, strengthens compliance, and enhances Pennant's ability to serve its patient populations effectively.

The hourly range for this position is $38.00-$53.00 per hour. Actual hourly rate is dependent upon experience, qualifications, credentials, and demonstrated expertise in risk adjustment, value-based care, coding, and documentation integrity.

Why Join Us?

Something else that sets us apart from other companies is the quality of our most valuable resources – our people! We are dedicated to living out our culture as defined by our core values, “CAPLICO”:

  • Customer Second – We prioritize and support our team so they can deliver exceptional care.
  • Accountability – Own your work and outcomes.
  • Passion for Learning – Grow continuously with curiosity and culture.
  • Love One Another – Build authentic, respectful, and trusting relationships.
  • Intelligent Risk Taking – Innovate and challenge the status quo.
  • Celebrate – Recognize the small wins, they add up!
  • Ownership – Be the CEO of your role.

Additional Benefits:

  • True Work-Life balance – We believe in taking care of yourself before you take care of others!
  • Full benefits package (medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with match)
  • Paid time off, holiday pay, and professional development
  • Your voice matters! - Work with other passionate and high-achieving leaders who care deeply about patient outcomes and team success.

About Pennant Services

We support over 250 home health, hospice, senior living, and home care operations across 19 states. Our Service Center model empowers local leadership while providing centralized clinical, legal, HR, IT, and compliance support to help ensure high-quality care.


The employer for this position is stated in the job posting. The Pennant Group, Inc. is a holding company of independent operating subsidiaries that provide healthcare services through home health and hospice agencies and senior living communities located throughout the US. Each of these businesses is operated by a separate, independent operating subsidiary that has its own management, employees and assets. More information about The Pennant Group, Inc. is available at http://www.pennantgroup.com.

The AD, Advanced Analytics & Modeling (AAM) role will report to Director, AAM in AIDE and help translate priority business decisions into differentiated analytical capabilities, decision-ready evidence, and measurable business & patient impact. This role will lead the modeling capabilities (like KDA, PPM, Precision Health, etc,) and related business analytics to identify the factors influencing business performance and support strategic decision making. The role will partner with the business and cross-functional stakeholders to uncover growth opportunities, quantify key business drivers, generate actionable insights, and measure business impact.



The role will also collaborate seamlessly with the I&A and SPT partners – in HYD and EH, and will enable alignment of the core modeling capability ownership, roles and responsibilities, common quality expectations, and effective partnership model with different stakeholders.


Job Description

Associate Director, Advanced Analytics & Modeling

Location – Hyderabad #LI Hybrid

Major Accountabilities:

Advanced Analytics & Modeling Leadership Responsibilities

  • Support the establishment and evolution of the I&A Advanced Analytics & Modeling capability, including its roadmap, maturity agenda, investment priorities, and alignment with portfolio priorities, launches, evolving customer and patient needs, and broader I&A strategy.
  • Partner with AAM leadership to assess advanced analytics and ad hoc modeling needs across I&A pillars, prioritize demand, and translate business priorities into clear questions, analytical plans, and modeling agendas while challenging low-value or duplicative requests.
  • Determine where analytical and limited ad hoc modeling capabilities should be built, incubated, partnered, automated, reused, or retired based on business value, feasibility, differentiation, maturity, and scalability.
  • Deploy AIDE AAM expertise to test, learn, and develop reusable analytical approaches, promoting model reuse, consistency, technical standards, interpretability, human oversight, and responsible use.
  • Support KDA and related capability development from problem definition through analysis, insight generation, recommendations, and implementation, including early descriptive and contextual analytics.
  • Integrate brand and business context into KDA capabilities, support SPT in scaling reusable data science products, and translate complex analytical outputs into clear business storylines for I&A, senior leadership, and business stakeholders.

Integrated Partnership with SPT

  • Serve as the AAM point of contact in AIDE/HYD to the SPT Data Science organization for pre-aligned capabilities and initiatives requiring governed data, technical environments, reusable capabilities, productization, integration, deployment, or enterprise scale.
  • Partner with I&A and SPT to determine which use cases remain I&A-owned ad hoc analytics versus those transitioning to SPT-owned reusable products, recurring models, engines, or workflows.

Global US-Hyderabad Operating Model

  • Establish HYD as an integrated capability and delivery partner, engaged early in portfolio planning, business context, analytical design, execution, quality review, synthesis, and capability development.
  • Partner with EH leadership to align capability roadmaps, HYD capacity and expertise deployment, decision rights, work ownership, quality expectations, documentation, and talent priorities, while building HYD AAM capability to independently lead repeatable and increasingly complex analytical work with shared accountability for quality, interpretation, and decision impact.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Economics, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Operations Research, Engineering, Computer Science, Life Sciences, Business Analytics, or a related field required.
  • Master's degree or doctorate in a relevant quantitative discipline preferred.
  • 10+ years of leadership experience in advanced analytics, data science, decision science, commercial analytics, healthcare analytics, or a related quantitative field.
  • Proven success in defining and executing an Advanced Analytics strategy and capability roadmap across analytical domains.
  • Deep working and functional knowledge of statistical analysis, predictive analytics, and ML concepts.
  • Strong business acumen with experience supporting commercial, operational, or strategic decision making.
  • Experience leading senior capability owners, flexible expert teams, complex portfolios, and globally distributed analytics organizations.
  • Demonstrated experience applying advanced analytics to consequential commercial, patient, healthcare, launch, or enterprise decisions.
  • Experience in translating complex analyses into actionable business recommendations and executive-level narratives.
  • Experience establishing portfolio prioritization, capacity allocation, quality governance, and reusable capability models.
  • Strong track record partnering with senior business and technology leaders and translating complex analytics into strategic choices and measurable action.
  • Experience leading operating-model transformation, capability centralization or federation, and organizational change.

Leadership Skills:

  • Lead and deploy HYD talent across AAM priorities, therapeutic areas, and cross-portfolio initiatives, ensuring team members build differentiated technical depth through primary capability affiliation while developing breadth across adjacent domains.
  • Own KDA capability talent planning, including hiring, onboarding, goal setting, coaching, performance management, succession, career development, engagement, and retention, while building leadership depth through rotations, communities of practice, and T-shaped skill development.
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, constructive challenge, innovation, inclusion, continuous improvement, and accountability across Hyderabad and cross-functional teams.

Required Skills:

  • Strong expertise in Advanced Analytics & Modeling strategy, statistical analysis, predictive analytics, ML fundamentals, capability portfolio leadership, roadmap development, and investment prioritization.
  • Broad fluency across predictive modeling, patient analytics, driver analytics, causal inference, experimentation, IPMM, ROI, response curves, optimization, NLP, GenAI, and unstructured analytics, with sound judgment on method fit, evidence quality, validation, interpretability, uncertainty, model risk, and responsible AI.
  • Strong executive decision framing, business translation, stakeholder influence, conflict resolution, and portfolio trade-off management, with clear understanding of analytical versus technical ownership across analytics, modeling, products, platforms, and lifecycle management.
  • Proficiency in SQL, Excel, Python/Data IKU, large datasets, data preparation, and analytics workflows.

Preferred Experience and Skills:

  • Pharmaceutical, biotechnology, life sciences, healthcare, or another complex regulated industry.
  • Experience incubating emerging AI or unstructured-data capabilities and validating use cases before scale.
  • Experience establishing integrated operating models with global capability centers and AI, data, product, or platform organizations.

Location: Hyderabad NKC | Hybrid | 3 days a week in office is mandatory.

Direct Reports: 5 Senior associates along with cross-functional collaboration with 20+ associates.


Skills Desired

Artificial Intelligence (AI), Biostatistics, Business Value Creation, Change Management, Curious Mindset, Data Governance, Data Literacy, Data Quality, Data Science, Data Visualization, Deep Learning, Graph Algorithms, Learning Agility, Machine Learning (ML), Machine Learning Algorithms, Python (Programming Language), Stakeholder Engagement, Statistical Analysis, Time Series Analysis

Job Description

We have successfully supported the top 50 pharmaceutical companies and more than 750 biotechs, spanning 2,700 clinical trials across 100+ countries in the last 5 years.

• Produces project-specific status reports for management and/or clients on a regular basis.

In some cases an equivalency, consisting of a combination of appropriate education, training and/or directly related experience, will be considered sufficient for an individual to meet the requirements of the role.

Working Conditions and Environment:
• Work is performed in an office environment with exposure to electrical office equipment.

When you join Thermo Fisher Scientific, you become part of a global team that values passion, innovation, and a commitment to scientific excellence. You’ll work in an environment where collaboration and development are part of the everyday experience—and where your contributions truly make a difference.

Apply today to help us deliver tomorrow’s breakthroughs.

title: Rare Blood Disorders/Rare Hematology Thought Leader Liaison
description:
Job Title: Rare Blood Disorders/Rare Hematology Thought Leader Liaison (TLL)

  • Location: Remote, US

Geography: Ohio Valley

Travel: 60–80% travel expected

Job Type: Full Time

Reports To: Director, Thought Leader Liaisons

About the Job:

Sanofi focuses on developing specialty treatments for debilitating diseases that are often difficult to diagnose and treat, providing hope to patients and their families.

Sanofi has pioneered the development and delivery of transformative therapies for patients affected by rare and debilitating diseases for over 30 years. We accomplish our goals through world-class research, collaboration with the global patient community, and with the compassion and commitment of our employees. With a focus on rare diseases, oncology, immunology, and multiple sclerosis, we are dedicated to making a positive impact on the lives of the patients and families we serve. Sanofi's portfolio of transformative therapies, which are marketed in countries around the world, represent groundbreaking and life-saving advances in medicine.

At Sanofi, we are committed to the growth of our people, connected in purpose by career, life, and health. Learn more at .

The Rare Blood Disorders franchise is a patient-centric organization responsible for delivering the highest quality education and service regarding disease and treatment. The goal of the franchise is to penetrate existing and new markets to meet business goals by educating physicians and healthcare professionals on a portfolio of products while upholding the Company's mission and values.


Sanofi's Rare Blood Disorders/Rare Hematology Thought Leader Liaison (TLL) is a field-based, commercial role responsible for engaging Healthcare Professionals (HCPs) and Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) to strategically inform market development across the rare hematology portfolio of products. The TLL is expected to possess a high level of clinical and customer knowledge, have experience with both field and headquarters protocols and procedures, and possess the drive and spirit to engage with healthcare professionals to help build educational platforms, generate insights, and inform local and national brand strategies, supporting the commercial success of the portfolio. The portfolio focus is primarily on Systemic Mastocytosis (SM) and Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP).

The TLL will work closely, and within approved SOPs, with other field professionals including, but not limited to, Regional Business Directors, Area Business Managers, and Medical Science Liaisons, as well as home office-based colleagues in Marketing, Medical Affairs, Operations, and Market Access.

A core responsibility of this role is driving SM and ITP market development within the assigned region — identifying KOLs and fostering multi-disciplinary connections across specialists who treat and manage SM and ITP patients. The TLL serves as a strategic partner to cross-functional commercial and medical teams. The TLL helps to shape brand strategy through insight generation, KOL engagement, and regional market development initiatives across the full rare hematology portfolio.

Join the team transforming care for people with immune challenges, rare diseases, cancers, and neurological conditions. In Specialty Care, you'll help deliver breakthrough treatments that bring hope to patients with some of the highest unmet needs.

About Sanofi:

We’re an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives.

Main Responsibilities:

*All TLL interactions are on-label and consistent with commercial compliance, legal, and regulatory guidelines.*

A. KOL Development and Engagement

  • Work with cross-functional colleagues to coordinate function-specific activities aligned to business and customer needs
  • Identify, profile, and maintain long-term partnerships with KOLs and emerging leaders within the Hematology and Allergy/Immunology communities
  • Identify SM champions within the region
  • Engage in on-label conversations to gather insights on topics such as disease diagnosis and treatment, therapeutic options, and product positioning across SM and ITP.
  • Execute unique, on-label, and strategic HCP programming (e.g., disease state and product) as determined by brand needs
  • Serve as a single point of contact to resolve commercial KOL issues
  • Execute a customer-centric, needs-based approach with targeted KOLs
  • Plan and execute KOL engagements and executive encounters at local, regional, and national conferences, field visits, and other venues as directed
  • Be a voice for allergy/immunology and hematology/oncology KOLs within the organization, sharing insights with key stakeholders and cross-functional partners to inform brand strategy

B. SM and ITP Centers of Excellence and Market Development

  • Lead long-term market development efforts in assigned regions across the SM and ITP landscapes, focusing on high-potential centers and customers
  • Develop and execute customer engagement plans for KOLs within assigned regions, accountable for fostering KOL connections across multi-disciplinary specialists who treat and manage SM and ITP patients
  • Maintain understanding of regional market dynamics, including key opinion leaders, institutional accounts, and multi-disciplinary teams to advance SM and ITP patient care and partner with sales leadership and commercial field teams to align regional market development strategies
  • Develop and execute regional marketing initiatives (insight discovery, advisory boards, roundtables, etc.)
  • Support regional congress planning and execution, including KOL insight gathering engagement at priority conferences across hematology/oncology and allergy/immunology, in partnership with Medical, Sales Leadership, Commercial Operations, and Brand Marketing
  • Proactively meet with assigned centers and/or customers to solicit feedback and adjust strategies accordingly
  • Develop and continuously maintain a high level of clinical competence across SM, ITP, and aTTP

C. Market Insights and Collaboration

  • Capture, analyze, and share customer insights aligned with brand priorities across SM and ITP.
  • Work with targeted KOLs to obtain feedback on new and existing brand-related strategies and materials (all materials and programs will be approved by legal, compliance, and regulatory)
  • Capture and analyze competitive intelligence to help shape strategy and activities
  • Facilitate cross-functional planning, recruitment, and execution of regional and national advisory boards in partnership with HQ Marketing.
  • Identify, align, and recruit appropriate HCP/KOL consultants to meet the needs of marketing and achieve aligned KPIs for each project
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to inform account strategy and plans through treatment pathway discovery and insight generation to advance care in centers of excellence

D. Speaker Bureau Operations and Content

  • Assist with speaker bureau management, including identification and training/coaching of promotional speakers with approved slide decks and materials
  • Assist in the execution of speaker contracting when requested, including completion of annual budget plans, recommendations, and nominations
  • Coordinate and execute speaker training to ensure assigned speakers are competent, compliant, and up to date on new information
  • Attend HCP speaker programs to observe, coach, and remediate speakers when necessary to ensure optimal execution of content
  • Assist with new content creation and existing content updates and renewals
  • Serve as the single point of contact for a high-volume of speaker logistics/scheduling and work cross-functionally to ensure streamlined communication
  • Lead planning, execution, and pull-through of TLL-owned programs

About You:

Key Capabilities:

  • Strong communication, organization, and project management skills
  • Proven ability to work in a highly dynamic and fast-paced environment
  • Demonstrated ability to lead without formal authority and work in a highly collaborative environment
  • Excellent organizational, interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills
  • Passionate, confident, articulate, and comfortable in a team environment
  • Ability to successfully engage with top KOLs and other HCPs
  • Expertise in creating and executing customer account plans
  • Robust analytical and problem-solving skills; ability to identify and act on creative solutions
  • Ability to establish credibility, connect the dots, and align multiple stakeholders to pioneer the adoption of new products, methods, and technologies
  • Flexibility and ability to plan and adapt to changing market conditions
  • Motivated by patient focus, urgency, and personal commitment to high performance, results, and compliance
  • Possesses high integrity and exceptional work ethic

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree
  • A minimum of 5 years of work experience in one or more of the following: field sales, product marketing, or medical/clinical in the pharmaceutical/biotech space
  • Prior experience interacting with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs)
  • Ability to travel to meetings, trainings, and programs as necessary (60–80%)
  • Must have a valid driver's license
  • Must reside within the geographic area of the assigned territory, or within a reasonable distance as determined by leadership

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in Rare Diseases and/or Hematology
  • Allergy/Immunology and/or Hematology-Oncology background preferred
  • Experience in marketing or leading marketing projects
  • Academic center focus and KOL development experience
  • Experience working within or building multi-disciplinary treatment teams
  • Cross-functional commercial background (e.g., marketing, sales leadership)
  • Master's degree in a related field
  • Launch experience, including demonstrated success across multiple drug launches in applicable specialty markets
  • Previous experience working as a Thought Leader Liaison
  • KOL and/or speaker management experience
  • Project management and vendor management experience
  • Understanding of oral targeted therapies with a requisite diagnostic component and ability to navigate complex market access environments

Pursue Progress, Discover Extraordinary

Better is out there. Better medications, better outcomes, better science. But progress doesn't happen without people – people from different backgrounds, in different locations, doing different roles, all united by one thing: a desire to make miracles happen. So, let's be those people.

description:
Job Details

ChristianaCare is seeking a BC/BE Non-Invasive Clinical Cardiologist to join our Center for Heart & Vascular Health in Newark, Delaware.


Join our team at The Center for Heart and Vascular Health at ChristianaCare, consisting of 25 cardiologists and 16 advanced practice clinicians, in providing the highest-level care and treatments for cardiovascular diseases in the inpatient (Christiana Hospital, Wilmington Hospital and Union Hospital) and ambulatory settings. Our cardiologists participate in the full range of imaging studies both in our hospitals and in our outpatient diagnostic center. They will have the opportunity to work collaboratively with our primary care partners in the development of population health-based initiatives.


Position Highlights:

  • Progressive, innovative care in a busy clinical practice. The Center for Heart and Vascular Health at Christiana Hospital saw 1,800 chest pain admissions and performs over 3,000 cardiac catheterizations, 1,400 PCIs, 1,600 EP procedures and 880 cardiac surgical procedures annually. The Center also provides advanced heart failure services including placement and management of left-ventricular assist devices.
  • Opportunities to participate in teaching of Cardiology Fellows and house staff and engagement in clinical research. ChristianaCare is affiliated with the Sidney Kimmel Medical College at Thomas Jefferson University. In addition, the Center partners with the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania (HUP) for cardiac transplantation and transplant medicine services.
  • Collaborate with other members of the section of Cardiology that also includes diverse community-based practices.

Requirements

  • BE/BC in cardiology
  • Must have the ability to be licensed in the State of Delaware and meet credentialing requirements.

About ChristianaCare

ChristianaCare has earned continued Gold Seal of Approval™ by The Joint Commission for many years. As the largest healthcare provider in the state, ChristianaCare is committed to maintaining the highest standards of patient care while sustaining the well-being of its medical and dental staff members. In the past year, ChristianaCare received the AHA Gold award for heart failure, the AHA Platinum award for myocardial infarction care, the AACN Beacon Award for Excellence, and the Daisy Foundation Award for nursing excellence. ChristianaCare also operates a Comprehensive Stroke Center and a Level 1 trauma center providing care for a large number of patients with high clinical acuity. The cardiovascular program offers reasonable call, favorable benefits, teaching opportunities, research opportunities, and patient diversity.

ChristianaCare is one of the country’s largest and most dynamic health systems, centered on improving health outcomes, making high-quality care more accessible and lowering health care costs. ChristianaCare includes an extensive network of outpatient services, home health care, medical aid units, three hospitals (1,336 beds), a Level I trauma center and a Level III neonatal intensive care unit, a comprehensive stroke center and regional centers of excellence in heart and vascular care, cancer care and women’s health. ChristianaCare is a not-for-profit teaching health system with more than 260 residents and fellows. We are continually ranked by US News & World Report as a Best Hospital. With our unique, data-powered care coordination service and a focus on population health and value-based care, ChristianaCare is shaping the future of healthcare.

Living in and around Delaware offers varied and affordable housing options in DE, PA, MD, or NJ. Connected by Amtrak and I-95 this region is a hub for excellent restaurants, entertainment and sporting venues, cultural events and some of the nation’s best colleges and universities. Our location puts you within 1-3 hours of four international airports, major cities including Philadelphia, New York City and Washington, D.C., popular beach towns in MD, DE and NJ and popular ski resorts in PA and NY.

title: Undergraduate Research Assistantship - AI Chatbots
description:
Serve as an undergraduate research assistant on the project: Talking to the Machine: AI Chatbots and the Changing Landscape of Psychotherapy.

As AI chatbots are increasingly marketed and used for mental health support, questions arise about their therapeutic potential, their limitations, and their impact on access to care. This study aims to examine therapeutic use of chatbots, as well as whether interacting with an AI chatbot functions as a bridge that facilitates individuals’ access to human therapists, and whether it may inadvertently discourage or delay seeking care from trained clinicians.

The research assistant will:
• Attend weekly lab meetings, perform literature searches, development of study methodology, support of IRB proposal, participate in quantitative and qualitative data analyses, involvement in preparation of poster and/or paper for conference presentation.

• Must be Work Study eligible
• Time management
• Strong communication skills
• Basic knowledge of SPSS
