title: Senior Vice President of Manufacturing
location: 0PZ69 TULKOFF FOOD PRODUCTS LLC - BALTIMORE , MD 21224
description:
The Sr. Vice President of Manufacturing is a senior operating leader responsible for the safety, quality, productivity, and profitability of Tulkoff's manufacturing network. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this role provides strategic and operational leadership across Tulkoff's Cincinnati, Toronto, and Baltimore manufacturing facilities, working through a team of Site Directors to standardize best practices, drive continuous improvement, and scale capacity to meet growing customer demand. The Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) Manager also reports to this role, reflecting the SVP of Manufacturing's accountability for building and sustaining a strong safety culture across every site.

This is a highly visible, hands-on leadership role for an experienced manufacturing executive who can balance strategic, multi-site vision with the discipline to be on the plant floor solving problems alongside site teams. The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in food manufacturing operations, a track record of developing high-performing leaders, and a passion for building a world-class safety and quality culture.

Key Responsibilities

Manufacturing Strategy & Multi-Site Leadership

  • Set the strategic direction for Tulkoff's manufacturing network across Cincinnati, Toronto, and Baltimore, translating company growth and commercial goals into an integrated manufacturing plan.
  • Lead, coach, and hold accountable the three Site Directors, ensuring each facility operates against clear performance targets for safety, quality, delivery, and cost.
  • Standardize manufacturing processes, KPIs, and reporting cadences across sites while allowing for local flexibility where warranted by product mix or customer requirements.
  • Represent manufacturing on the senior leadership team, partnering with the COO and peer executives to shape company-wide strategy, capital investment, and network capacity planning.
  • Evaluate and lead network capacity decisions, including capital projects, line additions, automation investments, and potential new-site or expansion planning.

Environmental, Health & Safety

  • Own the overall safety performance and culture of the manufacturing network; provide direct leadership and support to the EHS Manager in developing and executing the EHS strategy.
  • Ensure all sites maintain compliance with applicable regulations, including OSHA requirements in the U.S. and equivalent occupational health and safety regulations in Canada, as well as environmental permitting and reporting obligations.
  • Champion a proactive, employee-driven safety culture, including behavior-based safety programs, incident investigation and root-cause analysis, and consistent corrective action follow-through.
  • Review leading and lagging safety indicators (e.g., near misses, TRIR, LTIR) across all sites and drive accountability for continuous improvement in safety outcomes.

Quality & Food Safety

  • Partner with Quality and Food Safety leadership to ensure every facility maintains and exceeds GFSI-benchmarked certification standards (e.g., SQF), HACCP plans, and customer/regulatory audit expectations.
  • Ensure Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs), sanitation programs, and food defense protocols are consistently followed across all shifts and sites.
  • Support root-cause investigation and corrective/preventive action (CAPA) for quality and food safety deviations, driving sites toward zero-defect performance.

Continuous Improvement & Operational Excellence

  • Deploy Lean, Six Sigma, and Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) principles to improve throughput, reduce waste, and lower total manufacturing cost across the network.
  • Establish a common operating system across sites, including standard work, visual management, tiered daily accountability meetings, and structured problem solving.
  • Lead or sponsor major process improvement and automation initiatives, tracking benefits realization against business case commitments.

Financial & Capital Management

  • Own the manufacturing network's operating budget, partnering with Finance and Site Directors to plan, monitor, and deliver against cost, labor, and productivity targets.
  • Develop and prioritize the capital expenditure plan across sites, ensuring investments are aligned to growth, reliability, safety, and quality priorities.
  • Identify and deliver cost-reduction and margin-improvement opportunities without compromising safety or quality.

Talent Development & People Leadership

  • Build a strong bench of manufacturing leadership talent, with particular focus on developing the Site Director team and their succession pipelines.
  • Foster a consistent, values-based culture across all sites that reinforces Tulkoff's commitment to customer focus, teamwork, and continuous development.
  • Lead workforce planning across the network, including labor strategy, staffing models, and (where applicable) union or labor relations matters.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner closely with Supply Chain, Procurement, R&D/Innovation, Sales, and Quality to ensure manufacturing capabilities align with new product launches, demand planning, and customer commitments.
  • Serve as an escalation point for cross-site operational issues, ensuring timely resolution and clear communication to the COO and broader leadership team.

title: Integrated Shift Supervisor - Night Shift
description:
Job Title: Integrated Shift Supervisor - Night Shift

Job Category: Information Technology

Time Type: Full time

Minimum Clearance Required to Start: TS/SCI with Polygraph

Employee Type: Regular

Percentage of Travel Required: None

Type of Travel: None

* * *

The Shift Supervisor is responsible for directing on-shift personnel and providing oversight and coordination across a multi-source service environment in support of the COMM Network Operations Center (NOC). This role ensures incidents are properly monitored, tracked, prioritized, and escalated according to established severity levels, particularly those impacting critical business functions. The Shift Supervisor is also responsible for maintaining situational awareness of operational conditions and communicating significant incidents, anomalies, and service impacts to appropriate leadership.

Given the proactive nature of the position, the Shift Supervisor must possess strong operational leadership experience, sound decision-making skills, and the ability to effectively direct resources supporting mission-critical operations in a fast-paced environment.

Work Schedule:

  • Panama Schedule (2 on, 2 off, 3 on, 2 off, 2 on, 3 off)
  • 12-hour shifts: 1800 - 0600

Position Responsibilities

  • Monitor and track service-impacting changes within the Enterprise infrastructure.
  • Work with Service Operations staff during the installation, upgrade, or decommissioning of infrastructure equipment and software to monitor and assess potential impacts to the Enterprise.
  • Monitor and analyze critical incident alerts related to outages or service degradations affecting the Enterprise using enterprise monitoring tools.
  • Assist with the development and maintenance of standard operating monitoring procedures.
  • Support Major Incident Severity Level calls, including establishing conference bridges, identifying appropriate service-line resources, and documenting timelines of events.
  • Monitor planned and unplanned service-impacting changes.
  • Assist with the preparation and distribution of Outage Notifications, Resolution Notifications, Advisory Notifications, Planned Outage Notifications, and associated updates.
  • Assist with SharePoint Outage Tracker entries and updates.
  • Assist with establishing conference bridges in support of Severity Level 1 and Severity Level 2 incidents and engage appropriate resources.
  • Archive the Daily Operations Report and Shift Change Log (Day Shift).
  • Perform trend analysis, incident reviews, recommendations, and service-status reporting through established reporting mechanisms, as requested.
  • Review the status of Critical Site Tickets and drive them to closure whenever possible.
  • Review the status of tickets experiencing prolonged resolution times or multiple transfers and drive them to closure whenever possible.
  • Provide Situational Awareness support to the customer, including updating reports, maintaining documentation and master station logs, monitoring chat rooms, and communicating ongoing operational impacts.
  • Leverage Enterprise Management tools and analytics to correlate service impacts, service availability, service capability, Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance, and other service-related trends.
  • Proactively monitor high-priority incidents affecting VIP personnel and mission-, business-, or enterprise-critical services.
  • Support the Government's Situational Awareness efforts regarding world, national, and local events (e.g., natural disasters, civil unrest, low-intensity conflicts, and acts of terrorism) and correlate potential impacts to Enterprise Operations Squadron-managed systems.
  • Provide operational coordination for network Event and Incident Management functions.
  • Prepare daily network availability briefings, charts, and reports for customer distribution to Government leadership.
  • Support the Government by performing daily ad hoc taskings as requested by the customer.
  • Generate Situational Awareness notifications through various messaging systems for customer distribution.
  • Provide technical assistance, when requested by the customer, in support of assigned duties.
  • Provide coordination, data collection, and support for the After-Action Report (AAR) process.
  • Integrate ITIL v3 best practices into existing documentation, recommend process improvements, and assist with maintaining governance documentation.
  • Demonstrate an understanding of network services and Carrier Ethernet technologies.
  • Collect incident information through customer interactions and self-service support tools.
  • Track incidents and requests from identification through resolution, ensuring a quality end-to-end customer experience.
  • Conduct initial assessment, triage, research, and resolution of basic incidents and service requests involving application software and infrastructure components.
  • Communicate status and progress updates in a timely manner.
  • Engage Service Desk personnel and other support resources to resolve incidents that exceed the scope of individual responsibility by routing issues to appropriate product-line, application, or system support specialists.
  • Execute responsibilities in accordance with established Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
  • Document resolutions and maintain self-help and staff knowledge bases.
  • Alert management to recurring issues, trends, and problem patterns.

Required Qualifications

  • Active TS/SCI clearance with Polygraph.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of recent and relevant experience coordinating and directing IT operations in a 24x7x365 operational environment.
  • Strong technical background and working knowledge of networking technologies.
  • Strong written communication skills.
  • Experience preparing presentations and executive-level reports.
  • Ability to review technical documentation and summarize complex information for executive-level audiences.

Required Certifications

  • Security+ or another DoD 8140 IAT-compliant certification.
  • Any ITIL 4 certification.

Desired Qualifications

  • Proficiency with word processing, spreadsheet, and desktop productivity applications.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Strong customer service skills and experience.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Proven ability to multitask, prioritize competing requirements, and maintain attention to detail in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent organizational skills.
  • Working knowledge of ServiceNow, Windows desktop environments, and other IT Service Management (ITSM) platforms.
  • Relevant certifications such as ITIL Service Operations, ITIL Service Operations Analysis, Cisco CCNA, Cisco CCNP, AWS Associate (or higher), VMware vSphere, or Microsoft Certified Solutions (MCS) certifications.

-

A culture of integrity.

At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation.

CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.

There are a host of factors that can influence final salary including, but not limited to, geographic location, Federal Government contract labor categories and contract wage rates, relevant prior work experience, specific skills and competencies, education, and certifications. Our broad and competitive mix of benefits options is designed to support and protect employees and their families. $70,800 - $148,600

title: Director of Thrift Store Operations (8882)
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

Manages and directs the Salvage/Thrift Stores in it’s work of reconditioning donated materials and merchandise into saleable form. Provides supervision and control of collecting and transporting donated materials, segregating, classifying, storing and dispensing of such materials and pricing. Provides maintenance of facilities and equipment and satisfies the transportation requirements of the organization.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: This job description should not be interpreted as all-inclusive. It is intended to identify the essential functions and requirements of this position. The incumbents may be requested to perform job-related responsibilities and tasks other than those stated in this job description.

Plans, schedules, supervises, coordinates, monitors, and evaluates the work performed by Thrift Store supervisors and their staff; trains and instructs staff in the proper methods and procedures for performing work; inspects work in progress and upon completion in order to ensure compliance with established policies and procedures; makes hiring and firing recommendations; conducts performance evaluations of supervisory personnel.

Prepares long range plans for the Salvage/Thrift Stores based on guidance received through the Officer(s)-In-Charge; develops and maintains improved conditions and procedures with the organization in general and within the department in order to meet workload requirements.

Prepares and provides information for the operations portion of the budget based on guidance and instruction received; utilizes the approved budget to govern the operations of the department.

Reviews and analyzes the performance continually to determine effectiveness and take corrective action where necessary; develops performance standards and keeps the Officer(s)-In-Charge informed of significant facts concerning department operations.

Maintains statistical information and records sufficient to maintain awareness of the productive capacity available and to make sales projects and assist in short and long range planning.

Performs public relations functions; seeks increased support from the general public and works to increase awareness and understanding of The Salvation Army; participates in public appearances in order to promote The Salvation Army; stimulates materials procurement through improved solicitation methods.

Receives, segregates, classifies, prices, stores or otherwise disposes of material received from contributors.

Supervises all transportation operations including pick-up of material, deliver to stores, transportation between stores, and all special transportation requirements.

Services and otherwise maintains transportation equipment; maintains all equipment, either directly with maintenance staff available, or through regular commercial facilities; makes alterations to premises as authorized by the Officer(s)-In-Charge(s)-In-Charge.

Receives salvage and scrap material; sorts and classifies the same according to type and market; prepares for sale into bales or lots; negotiates for sales and makes arrangements for shipping when necessary.

Maintains inventory records on all materials covering store shipments, etc.; compiles all production statistics and reports and maintains an organized filing system of the same.

Ensures that job descriptions for employees are current and applicable; schedules in-service training for department supervisors and employees.

Ensures knowledge, enforcement, documentation, and compliance with OSHA and wage and hour regulations.

Conducts transportation training and ensures that Corps requirements for Truck Drivers are met.

Collects and files daily production sheets; develops weekly and monthly production goals for each department in workshop including the store.

Develops and maintains plans for fire and other evacuation procedures; establishes and maintains systems for internal security.

Develops and maintains a comprehensive filing system (capital equipment, inventory, safety, production records, etc.)

OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES:

Attends The Salvation Army Advisory Board meetings when requested.

Furnishes Advisory Board with monthly reports.

Cooperates with the Advisory Board Committee.

Performs other related work as required.

MATERIALS AND EQUIPMENT:

General Office Equipment Trucks Fork Lift Bailer

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED:

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in a related field,

And

Two years progressively responsible supervisory experience in retail management or thrift store operations,

Or

Any equivalent combination of training and experience which provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities.

LICENSES AND CERTIFICATIONS:

Valid State Driver’s License

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

Knowledge of the principles and practices of production control, planning, scheduling, and budgeting as it relates to thrift store, transportation, and warehouse operations

Knowledge of the principles and practices of personnel supervision.

Knowledge of all aspects of shop operation and familiarity with modern shop equipment and processes in order to plan for the equipment additions and replacements that best serve the needs of the work performed.

Knowledge of materials handling equipment, including operations and maintenance requirements.

Knowledge of transportation equipment, its capabilities, and limitations, and dispatching including general practices.

Knowledge of both the construction and maintenance of plant equipment.

Ability to prepare accurate and complete statistical and sales records and reports.

Ability to develop, enforce, and improve standard operating procedures in order to maximize production and benefits of program operations.

Ability to train, motivate, and lead subordinate supervisory staff.

Ability to perform long range planning.

Ability to prepare operating budgets and to ensure expenditures are in compliance with budget restrictions.

Ability to negotiate prices in the sale of salvage.

Ability to build effective working relationships with businesses and other social service agencies in the community.

MENTAL AND PHYSICAL ABILITIES:

Ability to meet attendance requirements.

Ability to read, write, and communicate the English language.

Ability to perform public speaking.

Ability to perform mathematical computations.

Ability to perform frequent walking and/or standing, kneeling, or squatting relieved by lesser periods of sitting or operating a vehicle.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Work is performed in a normal office and thrift store environment where there are little or no physical discomforts associated with changes in weather.

Work is performed in a warehouse environment where there are physical discomforts associated with changes in weather or discomforts associated with noise, dust, dirt, and the like.

Work involves driving a vehicle where there may be physical discomforts associated with changes in weather such as rain, cold, snow, heat or discomforts associated with long distance trips or heavy traffic.

description:

title: Software Engineer — Engineering Systems, Continuous Integration

Snowflake is building the AI Data Cloud, enabling organizations around the world to mobilize data and develop applications at global scale. The Engineering Systems organization builds the tools, infrastructure, and platforms that help Snowflake engineers develop, test, and deliver high-quality software efficiently.

The Continuous Integration team is responsible for the systems that power builds, tests, validation, and developer workflows across Snowflake's engineering organization.   • Partner with engineers across Snowflake to understand CI needs and deliver solutions that are simple, scalable, and easy to operate.

  • Participate in design reviews, code reviews, testing, and production support.

  • Apply strong engineering judgment to improve system performance, reliability, security, and maintainability.

  • Help evolve CI practices, tooling, and operational processes as Snowflake grows.

Our Ideal Candidate

  • 3+ years of software engineering experience building production systems.

  • Experience designing and implementing reliable software services.

  • Proficiency in at least one programming language such as Java, C++, Python, or Go.

  • Familiarity with cloud-based development environments and distributed applications.

  • Experience with testing, debugging, monitoring, and operating production systems.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work through ambiguous technical challenges.

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to collaborate with engineers, product partners, and teams across the organization.

  • Knowledge of multi-tenant systems, reliability engineering, performance optimization, or security isolation.

  • Experience working with Kubernetes, containers, or public cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.

  • Experience supporting large-scale repositories, build pipelines, or engineering platforms.

  • Familiarity with observability tools and production metrics.

  • Experience contributing to technical design documents, postmortems, or root-cause analyses.

Why Engineering Systems at Snowflake?

  • Build infrastructure used by Snowflake engineers around the world.

  • Work on challenging distributed systems and developer productivity problems.

  • Help improve the speed, reliability, and quality of software delivery at Snowflake.

  • Collaborate with engineers across a multi-cloud data platform.

  • Join a team that values ownership, thoughtful engineering, and continuous improvement.

title: Tax - Tax Reporting Graduate Trainee - Leeds - September 2027
description:
Forvis Mazars is a leading global professional services network providing audit & assurance, tax, and advisory services. description:
MISSION:

The palletizer is responsible, according to process and procedure, for handling and monitoring quality of material that will be converted into finished product; finished product; packaging materials; and related scrap that results from converting and other associated processes.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Handle and move (e.g. pack, feed, palletize, aerate, bale) process specific material/product consistent with the assigned position, the machine speed, and customer and quality specifications.

OTHER REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, & ABILITIES:

  • Ability to use RF scanner for warehouse management system transactions as required for position.
  • Ability to operate a manual pallet jack and/or an electric pallet jack as required for position.

We are representing a fast-scaling technology company developing cutting-edge autonomous vehicle platforms. They are seeking a Staff Perception Software Engineer to lead the design and development of intelligent perception systems that power autonomy across complex, real-world environments.


This is a high-impact role where you’ll shape the algorithms and systems responsible for situational awareness, object detection, and environmental understanding for next-generation autonomous mobility.

Flexible across the U.S. with a preference for candidates near major tech hubs (Austin, San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle).

You’ll architect and optimize systems that fuse sensor data (LiDAR, camera, radar) and deliver real-time, accurate understanding of the surrounding environment to support safe autonomous decision-making.

title: Technical Product Manager, CPU Platform Ecosystem
description:
At NVIDIA, we're shaping the future of accelerated computing infrastructure — and we believe a CPU platform is only as strong as the ecosystem around it. This role sits at the heart of that ecosystem, bringing clarity to what must work, what is qualified, and what customers can count on when deploying NVIDIA data center CPUs alongside GPUs, networking, storage, DPUs, and third-party components. We're looking for someone who wants to lead a tangible product outcome: customers who can configure, deploy, and operate a fully supported platform with confidence!


The work is hands-on and technically grounded, spanning NVIDIA devices, third-party components, firmware, software stacks, and industry standards such as Arm ServerReady. We offer clear ownership, strong executive visibility, and the opportunity to build something that lasts — not just handle a checklist. If you're ready to make a real impact at the intersection of hardware, software, and ecosystem strategy, we'd love to hear from you!


What you'll be doing:

  • Defining the required platform ecosystem by product, customer use case, and launch phase. This includes specifying what is supported, qualified, planned, or out of scope. It also involves maintaining the qualification roadmap and approved-vendor list accordingly.
  • Heading enablement and qualification activities for NVIDIA GPUs on PCIe and a wide range of third-party devices: networking, storage, DPUs, accelerators, management controllers, and security components.
  • Drive cross-component dependencies involving BIOS/UEFI, BMC, firmware, drivers, operating systems, telemetry, and manageability — collaborating with component owners to address interoperability, performance, and lifecycle gaps.
  • Leading readiness against platform and ecosystem standards, including Arm ServerReady, with defined test coverage, entry/exit criteria, certification evidence, and reproducible qualification matrices.
  • Running ecosystem-readiness reviews passionate about gaps, exceptions, and decisions — not status collection — and producing concise launch-readiness and executive views of coverage and residual risk.
  • Coordinating execution across CPU platform, firmware, validation, GPU, networking, DPU, storage, OEM/ODM, component-vendor, and customer teams: owners, achievements, dependencies, and blocking issue paths for every committed ecosystem item.

What we need to see:

  • 6+ years in technical product management, platform engineering, systems engineering, validation, product management, or ecosystem enablement.
  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent experience.
  • Proven experience delivering server, silicon, embedded, or other complex hardware/software platforms to customers or production.
  • Experience with PCIe devices and server-platform dependencies including BIOS/UEFI, BMC, firmware, drivers, operating systems, and manageability.
  • Experience running component qualification, compatibility matrices, approved-vendor lists, certification programs, or release-readiness processes.
  • Proven track record to drive closure across many engineering and partner organizations without direct authority.
  • Technical presentation skills and disciplined management of configurations, evidence, issues, and risk.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience qualifying GPUs, accelerators, NICs, storage, DPUs, or other PCIe devices on server platforms.
  • Familiarity with Arm ServerReady, server firmware standards, Linux enablement, or platform certification programs.
  • Direct experience working with OEMs, ODMs, component vendors, or strategic data-center customers.
  • Evidence of building a qualification or ecosystem-readiness system that measurably reduced deployment risk or accelerated customer adoption.
  • Experience working with data center CPUs, accelerated-computing platforms, or deploying production servers.

title: Audit - Mid Market - Graduate - Nottingham - September 2027
description:
Forvis Mazars is a leading global professional services network providing audit & assurance, tax, and advisory services. See how businesses really work and make an impact from day one.
Audit is about more than numbers. It's about understanding organisations, building trust in financial information, and helping businesses, investors and communities make informed decisions. Enjoy working with numbers, analysing data and spotting trends.

A clear communicator who builds strong relationships.
Interested in technology, data analytics and AI in audit.
Adaptable, motivated and eager to learn.

title: Senior Engineering Consultant-AI Science
description:
When you join Verizon

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. At Verizon, we power and empower how people live, work and play by connecting them to what brings them joy. We do what we love — driving innovation, creativity, and impact in the world. Our V Team is a community of people who anticipate, lead, and believe that listening is where learning begins. In crisis and in celebration, we come together — lifting our communities and building trust in how we show up, everywhere & always. Want in? Join the #VTeamLife.

Position Summary

The Senior Engineer Consultant – AI Science serves as a technical leader and subject matter expert in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advanced analytics. In this hybrid consulting and engineering role, you will bridge the gap between complex business challenges and cutting-edge AI technologies. You will architect, build, and deploy production-grade AI solutions—including Generative AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and autonomous Agentic AI systems—to drive measurable business impact and transformation.

Key Responsibilities

1. Solution Architecture & Technical Strategy

  • Design scalable, enterprise-grade architecture for AI/ML systems, Generative AI models, and autonomous multi-agent frameworks (e.g., LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen).
  • Define standards for Model Context Protocol (MCP), RAG architectures, prompt engineering, and LLM fine-tuning/evaluation.
  • Assess technical feasibility, select model architectures, and define data pipelines for complex, structured, and unstructured datasets.

2. Hands-on AI Engineering & Implementation

  • Programmatically integrate state-of-the-art LLM APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini) into enterprise workflows.
  • Develop, train, and validate statistical models, optimization algorithms, and machine learning pipelines using Python, R, or C++.
  • Implement MLOps, AI observability, and tracing tools to monitor model drift, token usage efficiency, latency, and system performance in production.

3. Client Consulting & Stakeholder Management

  • Act as a trusted technical advisor to cross-functional leaders, product managers, and external clients.
  • Translate unstructured business problems into actionable mathematical and computational models.
  • Communicate complex technical concepts, model outputs, and risk assessments to both technical teams and non-technical business executives.

4. Mentorship & Best Practices

  • Champion enterprise AI safety, ethical AI, data governance, and secure coding practices.
  • Mentor junior AI engineers and data scientists on modern development workflows, including the effective leverage of AI coding assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor).

Qualifications & Skill Requirements

Technical Expertise

  • Languages & Frameworks: Fluent in Python, SQL, and Deep Learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow).
  • Generative AI & Agentic AI: Hands-on experience with orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, LangGraph), vector databases (Pinecone, Qdrant, Milvus), and agentic workflows.
  • Cloud & Infrastructure: Cloud AI platforms (AWS Bedrock/SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI, or Azure OpenAI/AI Foundry).
  • MLOps & Deployment: Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD for AI models, MLflow, and API integration (REST, gRPC).

Experience & Education

  • Education: Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.
  • Experience: 6+ years of relevant experience in software engineering, data science, or AI consulting, with a proven track record of shipping AI models into production environments.

Soft Skills & Consulting Competencies

  • Strong analytical reasoning and structured problem-solving abilities.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills for technical and business audiences.
  • Ability to work autonomously in ambiguity and manage multiple project streams simultaneously.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Model Context Protocol (MCP) and multi-agent orchestration frameworks.
  • Industry expertise in supply chain, finance, telecommunications, or operations research.
  • Contributions to open-source AI/ML libraries, technical publications, or patent filings.

Where you’ll be working

In this hybrid role, you'll have a defined work location that includes work from home and assigned office days set by your manager.

40

title: Tax - Tax Reporting Graduate Trainee - Birmingham - September 2027
description:
Forvis Mazars is a leading global professional services network providing audit & assurance, tax, and advisory services. Forvis Mazars in the UK spans 14 offices across the nation and has over 3,400 professionals, with 190 partners. We have a clear purpose and a shared commitment to shape a better future.

Kickstart your career by helping businesses understand, calculate and report their Tax responsibilities accurately. As a Graduate Tax Trainee, you’ll learn how Tax connects to financial performance, regulation and business decisions, while working with a diverse range of clients, studying towards a fully funded professional qualification and building the confidence to make a real impact from day one.

About our Team
Join our Corporate Tax Reporting team, supporting a diverse range of businesses from ambitious owner-managed companies to large multinational organisations. You'll help clients navigate complex tax requirements, changing legislation and an evolving business environment while developing valuable technical and commercial skills.


Hear from our trainee, Harvey: 'My journey as a school leaver apprentice has been eye-opening and an experience at Forvis Mazars that has enabled me to learn and grow confidently and gain invaluable knowledge within Corporate Tax. The combination of on the job learning, as well as studying for both an accounting and tax qualification, has led to my development increasing faster than I could of ever imagined when I first joined.' #LI-DNP’

• Enjoy working with numbers, analysing data, spotting patterns and solving problems with accuracy and attention to detail.
• Are curious about how businesses operate and how tax influences financial performance, reporting and decision-making.
• Can communicate clearly, build strong relationships and explain complex information in a practical, easy-to-understand way.

We know everyone’s circumstances are different. If exceptional circumstances have affected your academic results, we’ll consider the context you provide as part of your application.

• You’ll work on Tax Reporting, helping businesses understand, calculate and report their tax obligations accurately, meet tax requirements and clearly report tax in their financial statements.

You do not need to be a tax expert before you join. We’ll help you build your knowledge through professional study, practical client work and day-to-day support from your team.

Develop technical knowledge through funded ACA/CTA study, structured training and study leave. Build digital confidence by learning how tax technology, data and automation support modern client work.

Put your learning into practice through real client work and see how your contribution supports clear and valuable outcomes. title: Undergraduate Research Assistantship - Field Metabolic Rate
description:
Serve as an undergraduate research assistant on the project: Using tree-based models to predict field metabolic rate of birds.

Field metabolic rate (FMR) describes the energy use of free-living organisms for maintenance and other activities. FMR therefore represents the "pace of life" in ecology. Unlike standard or resting metabolic rates, FMR has been under-studied, mainly due to the methodological limitations during measurement of the energy expenditure of free-living animals in the field. The first goal of this project is to compile a comprehensive dataset of FMR of bird species at the individual level. The dataset will also include other biotic and abiotic variables that can affect FMR. The second goal of this project is to use ensemble tree models, a machine learning approach, to distill key factors that may influence the variation of FMR of birds. The FMR dataset can be used to improve our understanding of the relationship between energy use, functional traits, and environmental conditions.

The research assistant will:

  • Responsible to compile data of FMR and other variables from the literature
  • Will write dataset documentations following the data and metadata standards of Ecology, the flagship journal published by the Ecological Society of America.

* You must have Federal Work Study funding added to your awards BEFORE applying for this position. You are potentially eligible for Work Study if you are a US Citizen or permanent resident, have filed a FAFSA, are enrolled in at least 6 credits, and are in good academic standing.

This position requires the following:

  • Must be Work Study eligible
  • Need to have a minimum of 6 months of working experience with data compilation and management
  • Should have basic skills with R and subject knowledge in ecology

Instructions to find your Work Study eligibility status:

  • Log into your MyPacePortal and click on “Student Home” and then the “Financial Aid” box (middle of screen).
  • Once in Financial Aid, select the “Award Offer” tab and the correct Award Year.
  • Scroll down to “Options to Pay Net Cost” and take a screenshot of the funds that are allocated specifically to Work Study for the academic year. Make sure your name is captured in the screenshot, then upload the screenshot, and submit it along with your application.

* If these details are not available in the “Award Offer” section of your profile, you are NOT currently eligible for Work Study funding. If you are a US citizen or permanent resident, and you have filed a FAFSA, you can open a Help Desk ticket with Financial Aid to determine your Work Study eligibility.

Central Processing Technician at Intermountain Healthcare

description:

About the opportunity

What if you could focus on meaningful clinical work while continuing to learn alongside some of the most respected experts in your field?

At Cognitive & Behavioral Consultants (CBC), we are seeking an experienced ADHD/Autism Clinical Psychologist with at least five years of clinical experience and strong competency in both Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT).

Founded by internationally recognized experts in CBT and DBT, CBC is known for its commitment to evidence-based care, professional training, and clinical excellence. You'll join a collaborative team where your expertise is valued, professional growth is encouraged, and administrative support allows you to focus on what matters most: helping clients thrive.

Why join CBC?

  • Learn from leaders in the field: Collaborate with internationally recognized CBT and DBT experts and experienced clinicians.

  • Make a meaningful impact: Help individuals with ADHD, autism, and related concerns through personalized, evidence-based care.

What you'll do

  • Provide individual, group, family, and parent therapy tailored to client needs.

  • Conduct psychological assessments, diagnostic evaluations, and treatment planning for ADHD, autism, and related concerns.

  • Use CBT and DBT as core components of your clinical practice.

  • Monitor treatment progress and collaborate with families, schools, and other professionals when appropriate.

  • Maintain timely, accurate clinical documentation.

  • Participate in clinical consultation, team meetings, and professional development.

Required qualifications

  • Ph.D. or Psy.D. in Clinical Psychology or a related qualifying psychology discipline.

  • Current New York State psychologist licensure or eligibility for licensure.

  • At least five years of clinical experience.

  • Demonstrated clinical competency and experience applying both CBT and DBT in practice.

  • Competency in assessing, diagnosing, and treating ADHD, Autism Spectrum Disorder, and related concerns.

  • Strong communication, collaboration, and clinical judgment skills.

Additional experience in ACT, PCIT, psychological assessment, supervision, or professional training is a plus.

  • Clinical expectations: 24 professional service units per week over 47 weeks annually.

  • Health and financial benefits: Comprehensive insurance programs, retirement plan with up to 3.5% employer matching, life insurance, long-term disability benefits, and eligible FSA/HSA options.

  • Additional benefits: Employee Assistance Program, commuter benefits, voluntary pet insurance and legal benefits, and other supportive workplace policies.

About CBC

Founded in 2004, Cognitive & Behavioral Consultants (CBC) provides evidence-based psychological care to children, adolescents, adults, couples, and families. Through clinical services, professional training, and consultation, we are committed to advancing effective psychological treatment and helping individuals and families thrive.

Ready to take the next step?

If you're an experienced psychologist who is passionate about ADHD, autism, and evidence-based treatment, we'd love to hear from you.

Bring your expertise. Expand your impact. Grow with CBC.

title: Senior Clinical Pharmacology Trial Leader
description:
Salary Range:

£49,140.00 - £91,260.00


Job Description Summary

Role Type: Hybrid Working, #LI-Hybrid
Location: WestWorks, London, United Kingdom
Relocation Support: This role is based in London, United Kingdom. Novartis is unable to offer relocation support: please only apply if accessible.

What if your leadership could help turn first-in-human research into confident decisions about the medicines of tomorrow? As Senior Clinical Pharmacology Trial Leader, you will provide the scientific and operational leadership needed to deliver early clinical pharmacology studies from protocol development through to Clinical Study Report finalisation. Acting as the primary bridge between Novartis, internal study teams, investigators, and selected Contract Research Organisations, you will ensure that emerging pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and safety data are delivered to a high standard and translated into meaningful program decisions.

Working Arrangement: This hybrid role is based at WestWorks in London, with flexibility to work remotely for up to two days per week. Domestic and international travel may be required to support study oversight, investigator meetings, and study-team engagement.


Job Description

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead assigned first-in-human and clinical pharmacology studies from protocol development through Clinical Study Report finalisation.
  • Develop protocol synopses and protocols with medical, pharmacokinetic, biomarker, statistical, and other cross-functional partners.
  • Serve as the primary Novartis contact for Contract Research Organisations, providing direction, oversight, challenge, and issue resolution.
  • Lead cross-functional study teams, aligning internal contributors, investigators, vendors, and external partners around study objectives.
  • Oversee study start-up, conduct, and close-out, including deliverables, timelines, risks, milestones, and operational execution.
  • Lead ongoing review and interpretation of pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, safety, and other emerging clinical study data.
  • Prepare and lead dose-escalation meetings, ensuring timely availability of quality data to support informed decisions.
  • Lead study-level risk management and implement appropriate mitigation strategies throughout the trial lifecycle.
  • Contribute to Clinical Study Reports, regulatory documents, internal decision materials, publications, and program updates.
  • Manage study budgets and vendor strategies while sharing lessons learned and strengthening clinical trial delivery practices.

Essential Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Healthcare, or a related discipline.
  • Approximately six or more years of experience in clinical trial development, clinical pharmacology, or early clinical development.
  • Experience contributing to or leading first-in-human, clinical pharmacology, or other early-phase studies.
  • Strong experience in protocol development, early-phase study design, and interpretation of pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and safety data.
  • Experience delivering studies through Contract Research Organisations or other external clinical-research partners.
  • Strong clinical-trial leadership, operational project-management, planning, prioritisation, and organisational skills.
  • Ability to lead cross-functional teams, manage competing priorities, and influence internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to interpret, discuss, and represent clinical study data and support timely scientific and operational decisions.
  • Strong knowledge of Good Clinical Practice, International Council for Harmonisation standards, regulatory requirements, and high-quality clinical trial conduct.
  • Fluent written and spoken English.

Desirable Requirements

  • Advanced degree such as a Master of Science, Doctor of Philosophy, Doctor of Pharmacy, Doctor of Medicine, or equivalent.
  • Experience managing or leading multiple complex global clinical studies concurrently.
  • Working knowledge of clinical finance principles, study forecasting, and budget management.
  • Experience contributing to talent development, mentoring, onboarding, or capability building within study teams.

Benefits & Rewards

At Novartis, we’re committed to reimagining medicine together - and rewarding the people who make it happen.

The rewards of being part of our team go far beyond base pay and incentives. We also offer a variety of competitive benefits in kind to help you thrive personally and professionally, such as insurance plans, retirement plans, wellbeing resources and global recognition programs. Pay equity is a fundamental principle of our employment policy and reflects our commitment to create a diverse, equitable and inclusive environment that treats all employees with dignity and respect, as outlined in our Code of Ethics.

Novartis is committed to building an outstanding, inclusive work environment and diverse teams’ representative of the patients and communities we serve.

As an Operations Planner at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you will play a key role in translating customer and project requirements into an executable and optimized packaging schedule. The Operations Planner will also be developed as a potential successor to the Master Planner.


This position requires more than maintaining an established schedule. description:
Grow your career with us

You are on a journey to join an exciting Company and be part of our success story to improve lives by developing resources sustainably. Here we offer you an exciting and dynamic work environment and will equip you with the know-how that will stretch and enhance your career journey.

Responsibilities:

Purpose:
The Remote Sensing Data Quality Assurance Analyst ensures the accuracy, consistency, and reliability of LiDAR datasets used in geospatial analysis and decision-making. This role focuses on developing and applying Quality Analyses (QA)/Quality Check (QC) protocols to validate LiDAR point clouds, derived products, and metadata against project specifications and operational standards. The analyst works closely with data engineers, geospatial data analysts, field teams, and Geographic Information Systems specialists to detect and resolve data anomalies, document quality processes, and provide actionable insights that improve LiDAR workflows, modeling accuracy, and end-user confidence.

🛰️ Roles and Responsibilities:

Project Execution:

  • Data acquisition, coordination, quality assurance of the data before deploying to the production server.

  • Close coordination with potential customers, incorporating feedback and requisite deliverables.

Database Management:

  • Running QA tests (Density, Accuracy, Nomenclature, Landuse, Coverage) on all LiDAR data from different applications.

  • Root cause analysis and action plan in coordination with field customer and field crew to ensure IOP targets.

  • Data transfer and compilation in the storage server.

  • Deployment of data in the production server for all Forest Inventory, Microplanning, and Tree improvement applications.

  • Collaborate with other divisions to ensure data accuracy and reliability.

  • Continuous optimization of the dataset lifecycle policy, curation workflow.

  • Develop/build and manage spatial databases linking with other organizational database management systems and create channels for user interaction.

  • Support the development of processes for efficient & effective QA/QC of remote sensing data (LiDAR + Optical).

  • Day-to-day data curation activities, processing, tracking, validation, and resolution of data quality issues.

Coordinating & Reporting:

  • Manage subordinates effectively and ensure project progress.

  • Provide suggestions to the remote sensing manager for new ideas and implementations.

  • Provide routine reports and operational recommendations to the remote sensing manager regarding project progress and challenges faced.

  • Prepare technical reports or presentations on the results of developmental projects.

  • Develop standard operational procedures to guide the operational implementation of remote sensing workflows.

🎓 Qualifications:

  • Preferably, Masters in Computer Science, Geoinformation Science, or closely related discipline.

  • OR Bachelor Degree with some exposure in Data Science.

🌐 Experience:

  • Previous quality assessment experience preferably at a management level; proven track record of delivering quality solutions.

  • Proven experience with modern quality improvement tools – SPC, capability studies, root cause analysis (fishbone, why-why analysis etc.).

  • Experienced in geospatial data validation & calibration procedure, Automated quality control algorithms, quality metadata & documentation.

  • Experience in big data management with demonstrated skills in processing, automation, compilation/integration, and deployment in the processing/production server.

  • Knowledge about remote sensing, GIS technologies, software & tools and development of datasets & documentation of Earth science data.

  • Proficiency with interpreted data languages for Earth science data using either Python, MATLAB, R, IDL, JavaScript etc.

  • Six Sigma/LEAN processing certified preferred but not required.

  • Competency in project development & deployment strategy.

  • Building cross-functional relationships to collaborate with business stakeholders and internal stakeholders/customers.

  • Excellent communication, interpersonal and presentation skills. Able to relate technical information to all levels of the organization.

🔍 Specific Knowledge:

  • Awareness of market trends and innovations in UAV, Satellite & LiDAR technologies.

  • Proficient in statistical & spatial analytics for informed business decisions.

  • Understanding of remote sensing data structure and applications in various disciplines.

  • Knowledge of artificial intelligence, deep/machine learning methods applicable to remote sensing.

  • LiDAR & optical data structure, spatial database management & processing.

  • Compilation & integration of model scripts, geospatial applications.

  • Expert in geospatial data processing & automation using different programming languages as well as GIS applications.

title: Liquidity Optimization Intern
description:
Making a Difference

The State of Wisconsin Investment Board (SWIB), founded in 1951, is a premier global investment organization responsible for managing the more than $178 billion of assets of the fully funded Wisconsin Retirement System (WRS), the State Investment Fund and other state funds. Through SWIB’s effective and innovative investment management, WRS remains one of the only fully funded US public pensions. The WRS consistently ranks among the 10 largest public pension funds in the U.S. SWIB is recognized by the investment industry for our teamwork and innovation. SWIB pursues sophisticated global investment strategies across the asset and risk allocation spectrum. Providers across the investment ecosystem seek to partner with SWIB.

Serving more than 703,000 beneficiaries of the WRS, SWIB is a mission-driven organization focused on providing a strong financial future to those who committed their careers to public service. For public employees and the 1,607 Wisconsin employers who contribute on their behalf, we are a trusted partner. Our team innovates continuously to meet the challenges of an evolving investment landscape while growing and protecting the assets of the WRS.

SWIB provides a strong, steady economic pillar for the state of Wisconsin by growing the trust funds under its management, managing risk, and optimizing costs of the long term. We are a mission-driven organization and the participants we serve are our mission. By bringing a disciplined, prudent, and innovative approach to market opportunities, SWIB has been successful in generating required returns and maintaining the trust of the beneficiaries and stakeholders of the funds we oversee.
Home To Top Talent
Our high-performing staff is key to what makes us a premier investment manager. SWIB is committed to investing in talented professionals to implement our robust, sophisticated investment strategies and to keep the organization at the forefront of the investment industry. We encourage innovation and offer professional development opportunities to help staff sharpen and expand their skills. Approximately 61 percent of SWIB’s investment professionals are Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) charterholders.

Job Description:

About the Team

The Liquidity Management and Beta Implementation (LMBI) division of SWIB is tasked with managing the funds of the State’s money fund (State Investment Fund), centrally managing all our passive Beta allocations, arranging for all the leverage used as part of our asset allocation process, optimizing our use of collateral and trading in the public markets on behalf of all portfolios in SWIB.

Essential activities:

  • Manage the assets of the $24 billion State Investment Fund.
  • Manage all our index tracking passive Beta portfolios.
  • Arrange for all the leverage that are recommended by the board approved asset allocation process.
  • Manage our securities lending and borrowing activities.
  • Optimize the use of all collateral.
  • Execute trade globally.

The Ideal candidate:

  • Ability to work in Madison, WI for an approximate 10-week period beginning late May/early June 2027.
  • Is pursuing a career in quantitative asset management.
  • Is pursuing a graduate degree in quantitative finance, economics or related areas.
  • Has strong understanding of the math in optimization algorithms & the ability to program them.
  • Has some familiarity with market design/auction literature.
  • Demonstrates excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Is proficient in at least one statistical programming language, such as MATLAB, Python or R.
  • Enjoy working across functional teams toward a common goal.

title: Rhinology MSL - West
description:
Job title: Rhinology MSL - West

  • Location: Remote, US

About the job


The Medical Science Liaison (MSL) is a field-facing role that serves as a trusted scientific partner to key external experts, conducting frequent scientific exchanges to enhance understanding of Sanofi's products. The MSL executes stakeholder engagement plans to gather insights that inform medical strategies and future research, while staying current on therapeutic developments to identify research opportunities and support evidence generation.


This role involves recognizing and sharing insights about patient and healthcare provider needs, maintaining effective communication with internal stakeholders across Medical Affairs and Commercial Operations, and ensuring full compliance with company, industry, legal, and regulatory requirements through excellent governance and risk management.


Join the engine of Sanofi’s mission — where deep immunoscience meets bold, AI-powered research. In R&D, you’ll drive breakthroughs that could turn the impossible into possible for millions.

About Sanofi:


We’re an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world and are supported and enhanced through our diverse portfolio of medical device and diagnostic products. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives.

Main Responsibilities:


1. Scientific Engagement: Conduct one-on-one and group interactions with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) and healthcare stakeholders, sharing medical/scientific information about products and disease management within regulatory guidelines.

2. Stakeholder Mapping & Strategy: Identify, profile, and prioritize ~50 stakeholders using the Scientific Engagement Model; develop territory and individual engagement plans aligned with Medical Affairs strategy.

3. Relationship Building: Establish long-term peer relationships with KOLs, payers, and HCPs by demonstrating strong clinical knowledge and articulating the medical value of Sanofi products.

4. Congress & Event Presence: Attend scientific congresses, symposia, and organize educational meetings or advisory boards to establish Sanofi's medical presence in the field.

5. Medical Information Support: Respond to unsolicited requests for medical information on products and disease states; support speaker training for continued scientific education.

6. Insight Generation: Gather feedback from stakeholder interactions, critically evaluate published studies, and report insights that inform Sanofi's medical strategies, messages, and product development.

7. Internal Collaboration: Share scientific information and external insights with Medical Affairs, Commercial Operations, Regulatory, and other internal teams while ensuring compliance with company and regulatory policies.

8. Evidence Generation Support: Identify clinical trial sites, monitor disease epidemiology, support protocol development, and facilitate investigator-sponsored study (ISS) submissions through approved processes.

9. Healthcare Policy Awareness: Understand healthcare policies, guidelines, and clinical practices at local, state, and national levels as they relate to the therapeutic area.

10. Independent Operation & Compliance: Work remotely with minimal supervision, travel nationally/internationally as needed, and maintain strict regulatory boundaries between non-promotional medical activities and commercial operations.

About you


Basic Qualifications

title: Senior Consultant – Business Systems Analyst – Coupa
description:
Role Title: Senior Consultant – Business Systems Analyst – Coupa

Location: Chennai


We are one purpose-led global organisation. The enablers and innovators, ensuring that we can fulfil our mission to push the boundaries of science and discover and develop life-changing medicines. We take pride in working close to the cause, opening the locks to save lives, ultimately making a massive difference to the outside world.

AstraZeneca (AZ) is in a period of strong growth and our employees have a united purpose to make a difference to patients around the world who need both our medicines and the ongoing developments from our science. In this journey AZ must continue to work across borders and with partners and new colleagues in a fast and seamless way. The ambition, size and complexity of the organisation, coupled with the opportunities afforded by new technology, has led the Board to approve a large-scale transformation programme – Axial.

The Axial Programme will be powered by S/4HANA a new ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) system which will be implemented right across the organisation and will provide our business with standardised processes, enhanced financial management, common data and real time reporting, transforming the way we work through our entire supply chain - from bench to patient.

The new system will be used by more than 20,000 employees daily, is foundational to all AZ entities and is central to most core business processes. This is a once in a generation programme for AstraZeneca and will shape our ways of working globally for many years to come.

The Axial programme needs the best talent to work in it. Whether it’s the technical skills, business understanding or change leadership, we want to ensure we have the strongest team deployed throughout. We are striving to deliver a world class change programme that leaves all employees with a fuller understanding of their role in the end-to-end nature of our global company. This programme will provide AZ with a competitive edge, to the benefit of our employees, customers and patients.


What you’ll do

  • Business Analysis Leadership: Apply business analysis techniques and lead delivery within a global S/4HANA Finance transformation, ensuring solutions align with clear business objectives.
  • Finance Capability Design: Be responsible for the design of Finance capabilities, enable seamless delivery across releases, and lead solution remediation to protect process integrity and performance.
  • SAP Best Practice and Architecture: Ensure compliance with SAP best practices, maintain integrated architecture standards, and implement robust, compliant data designs that endure.
  • Planning and Risk Management: Assist in project planning, proactively handle risks and interdependencies, and keep delivery on time and on budget.
  • Delivery Methodologies: Organise and implement project activities using Agile or Waterfall approaches, including SAP Activate, selecting the right tool for the outcome.
  • Multi-functional Solution Design: Partner with the IT Design Team to produce solution designs that meet business and multi-functional requirements without fragmenting standards.
  • Global Process Alignment: Engage with Enterprise Process Owners to define IT solutions that align to standardised global processes and deliver consistent outcomes.
  • Finance Process Design and Integration: Lead Finance process design during global definition, ensuring deep integration with SAP solutions and related data objects.
  • Standards Development and Testing: Develop and test global standard solutions, and bring designs through governance forums and frameworks to ensure adoption and quality.
  • Product and Design Integration: Work with IT Business Analysts, Product Managers, and design experts to ensure global designs are coherent, scalable, and integrated.
  • Innovation with External Experts: Collaborate with partner SME to bring the best of technology and standard approaches into our solutions.
  • Strategic Design Forums: Participate in cross-functional design forums to align global designs with strategic business goals and system architecture.
  • Localisation within Standards: Address localisation needs during deployment while safeguarding global standardisation and maintainability.
  • Documentation and Enablement: Create clear solution designs, maintain high-quality project documentation, and deliver training on relevant tools and technologies.
  • Coupa Solution and Process Expertise: Apply hands-on Coupa experience to analyse, design, and support Coupa-enabled procurement and invoicing capabilities integrated with SAP S/4HANA.
  • P2P and Accounts Payable Process Leadership: Bring strong end-to-end business process understanding across Procure-to-Pay (P2P) and Accounts Payable (AP), including requisitioning, purchasing, goods receipt, invoicing, matching, approvals, and payment-related dependencies.
  • Coupa-to-SAP Data Mapping and Validation: Define, review, and validate Coupa versus SAP field mappings for master and transactional data; establish mapping rules, identify data gaps, reconcile interface outputs, and support defect resolution through SIT and UAT.

Essential for the Role

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field of study or equivalent experience
  • Experience applying business analysis tools, techniques, and concepts (e.g., requirements management, user-centered design, business process/product design) to deliver business change
  • Experience collaborating with business partners to identify and address process/product requirements and IT needs
  • Experience leading discussions, identifying and documenting business IT problem statements, business process/product design, and report requirements
  • Experience working with third-party suppliers/vendors and supplier solutions/products
  • Experience planning and handling resources and budgets within assigned areas
  • Demonstrable hands-on experience working with Coupa, including procurement and invoicing processes and integration touchpoints with SAP.
  • Strong functional understanding of end-to-end Procure-to-Pay (P2P) and Accounts Payable (AP) business processes, controls, and data flows.
  • Prior experience mapping Coupa fields to SAP fields for master and transactional data, with responsibility for data validation, reconciliation, interface testing, and defect analysis during SIT and UAT.

Desirable for the Role

  • Certification in business analysis practice (preferred)
  • Experience in advising business partners across one or more functional domains within the pharmaceutical industry;
  • Experience in effectively communicating with and influencing individuals at various levels (e.g., peers, managers, team members)
  • Experience working within a global matrix organization, including geographically dispersed teams and partners.

When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. title: Avionics Technician II, MQ-9 (Yuma, AZ)
description:
The USMC MQ-9 CLS Technician is a qualified and skilled aircraft electronics and/or Ground Control Station technician with experience in troubleshooting multiple electronics systems both aircraft and control stations. Work may be reviewed by supervisor for general compliance with accepted practices.


Essential Responsibilities:

  • Must maintain assigned UAS aircraft electrical generators, load banks, starters, relays, batteries, actuators, circuit breakers, switches, and aircraft instruments.
  • Must apply advanced technical knowledge to solve complex problems that typically cannot be solved solely by referencing manufacturers’ manuals or similar documents. Examples of such problems include determining the location and density of circuitry, evaluating electromagnetic radiation, isolating malfunctions, and incorporating engineering changes.
  • Work typically requires an understanding of the interrelationships of circuits, exercising independent judgment in performing such tasks as making circuit analyses, calculating wave forms, and tracing relationships in signal flow, using complex test instruments such as high frequency pulse generators, frequency synthesizers, distortion analyzers, and complex computer control equipment.
  • The CLS technician shall utilize excellent organizational skills in prioritizing workload to meet Daily Flight Schedule.
  • Required to make entries in aircraft logs and records, attend shift change maintenance meetings, and is responsible for providing guidance and technical expertise to lower-level technicians throughout all aircraft modifications and/or maintenance efforts.
  • Applies advanced technical knowledge to solve unusually complex problems that affect operational and maintenance capabilities.
  • Requires an advanced understanding of the interrelationships of circuits and associated systems.
  • Exercises independent judgment and leadership in performing assigned tasks in conjunction with designated direction from Production Staff and/or Avionic Leads.
  • Uses common and complex test instruments in the performance of assigned duties.
  • Must be able to sign off work in either NALCOMIS/OOMA or IMDS.
  • Must have knowledge and understanding of CNAFINST 4790.2 and/or DAFI 21-101.
  • Maintains, repairs, and installs various types of electronic equipment and related devices.
  • Applies advanced technical knowledge of electronics principles in determining malfunctions and applies skill in restoring equipment operations.
  • Performs all other duties as assigned.

  • Must have an active Secret US Government clearance with eligibility to obtain a Top-Secret clearance. Note: US Citizenship is required to obtain a Secret Clearance.

title: Builder
description:
At Curriculum Associates, we believe in the potential of every child and are changing the face of education technology with award-winning learning programs like i-Ready that serve a third of the nation’s K–8 students. For more than 50 years, our commitment to making classrooms better places, serving educators, and supporting accessible learning experiences for all students has driven the continuous improvement of our innovative programs. Our team of more than 2,500 employees is composed of lifelong learners who stand behind this mission, working tirelessly to serve the educational community with world-class programs and support every day.

aka: Engineer | Maker | Member of Technical Staff | Person who GSD


At Stile, we’re building awesome software that actually matters. We make educational tools used by millions of students and teachers for many hours in classrooms across Australia and the United States. Our tools make science and maths education joyful, challenging, and effective.

We’re a small team, but Stile is already used by 40% of Australian science students, with millions more joining both here and in the US over the next 18 months. This is a unique opportunity to have an outsized impact on the future of education.

We care about outcomes, not processes. If you love making pragmatic tradeoffs, carve through ambiguity, get excited about how AI can help you do more, and can’t help but fix all the problems you see around you, then you’ll love it here.

What you’ll do

You will own problems end-to-end: understanding the need, shaping the solution, building, shipping, observing, and evolving.

You’ll work:

  • Across the stack (because silos get in the way)

  • Closely with designers and educators (because context multiplies output)

  • With AI tools that actually save time (because you hate drudge work)

  • In fast cycles: build → ship → learn → repeat. Every day.

Who you are

You’re brilliant. You might have 20YoE or be fresh out of school, but you learn quickly, and impress everyone you’ve worked with.

You:

  • Fall in love with problems, not solutions

  • Ship an astonishing amount of impressive work

  • Rapidly learn new skills, technologies, problem domains, and ways of working

  • Can articulate a clear vision of what better looks like

  • Thrive on autonomy and feedback

  • Can’t resist the urge to make things unreasonably great rather than just good enough

  • Care about long term results: you want your work to matter

  • Lean into disagreements, fighting to stay in sync with your colleagues

  • Have strong opinions, loosely held: You love being convinced as much as you love convincing someone else

  • Give a damn. About your work, your colleagues, and especially about helping the next generation take a better shot at the future

What working here feels like

We’re a decade old, 70-ish person team (~20 engineers) in Melbourne. We run like a fast paced startup with the reach of a global enterprise. Engineers sit close to decisions, ideas get tried quickly, AI is used everywhere where it can make our work sharper, faster, or smarter.

You’ll get:

  • Brilliant colleagues

  • In person collaboration, 2–3 days a week in our Melbourne office

  • Flexibility, common sense, and autonomy

  • The power to ship to millions of students within hours

  • Rapid career growth

  • A high level of automation

  • Real ownership of important problems

  • An opportunity to meaningfully shape how students learn science and maths

Who we’re not looking for

Let’s be explicit to save everyone time:

  • If you want to work only in one area, this won’t work. We’re all full stack (with specialties).

  • If you want detailed requirements before writing code, you’ll struggle here.

  • If you like long planning cycles with rigid targets, this isn’t the place.

  • If you can’t make AI useful to you, then you won’t keep up.

  • If ownership stresses you out more than it energises you, you won’t enjoy it.

If that all sounds like a breath of fresh air, then come and talk to us!

How to apply

Click “Apply Now” and send us your resume and a cover letter addressed to Daniel Rogers-Pryor telling us about the project you’re most proud of, or the application of AI that you’re most excited to experiment with. One page max, please!

We don’t need a perfectly polished CV.

We need evidence that you build, ship, learn, and care.

Our commitments to you

  • Application review within 1-2 days

  • Coffee chat within 5 business days

  • Interview outcomes within 2 business days

  • Average time to hire in 26 days

title: Partnerships and Fundraising Associate
description:
Summary

The Partnerships & Fundraising Associate plays a vital role in sustaining TMA's mission by securing the financial resources necessary to provide free education, meals, materials, and staff salaries. Working closely with the Executive Director, this position focuses on cultivating a diverse and stable funding ecosystem. The incumbent will be responsible for identifying new sources of support, nurturing existing relationships, and ensuring that every contributor clearly understands the tangible impact of their generosity, thereby directly influencing student retention and educational quality.

Responsibilities

  • Assist the Executive Director in formulating the annual fundraising strategy by analyzing historical revenue data, donor patterns, and emerging opportunities across individual donations, sponsorships, corporate alliances, grants, events, and in-kind contributions.
  • Investigate and recommend new revenue streams, such as recurring donations, payroll deductions, diaspora networks, and community faith groups, to broaden the organization's financial foundation.
  • Monitor fundraising progress against established targets, promptly identifying any deficits or gaps to enable proactive leadership planning.
  • Identify and vet potential partners, including corporations with CSR initiatives, foundations, development agencies, embassies, and NGOs, preparing detailed prospect briefs for executive review.
  • Develop customized proposals, pitch presentations, and engagement materials, while supporting the Executive Director during pitch meetings and subsequent follow-ups.
  • Manage the administrative documentation for partnership agreements and Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs), ensuring all deliverables and deadlines are met by both parties.
  • Maintain a schedule of grant deadlines, drafting and submitting concept notes, budgets, and proposals in collaboration with the Programs and Finance teams.
  • Oversee grant compliance by tracking reporting dates and preparing timely narrative reports for funders.
  • Source and pursue in-kind opportunities, including educational supplies, food, uniforms, technology, venues, and professional services.
  • Help design recurring giving structures with defined tiers that clearly illustrate donor impact.
  • Facilitate the Executive Director's engagement with major individual donors by preparing briefing materials, tracking interactions, and organizing site visits and follow-up activities.
  • Plan and execute both digital and physical fundraising campaigns, such as crowdfunding and social media drives, aligned with key dates like the school term start, admission cycles, International Day of Education, Children's Day, and year-end giving.
  • Manage logistics for fundraising events, including donor visits and community outreach drives.
  • Evaluate campaign and event performance against costs and objectives, sharing insights and lessons learned with leadership.
  • Execute the agreed-upon stewardship strategy to ensure donors receive prompt acknowledgments, regular impact updates, and engagement opportunities like school tours and student narratives.
  • Monitor donor retention rates, re-engage lapsed supporters, and handle routine inquiries, escalating complex issues to the Executive Director as required.
  • Maintain a precise donor and partner database within the CRM, reconciling donation records with the Finance department.
  • Generate monthly and quarterly reports detailing funds raised, pipeline status, retention metrics, and target achievement.
  • Collaborate with Communications and Programs to produce impact reports, newsletters, case studies, and appeal materials, representing the organization at networking events when authorized.
  • Ensure all student stories, images, and data used in fundraising comply with TMA's consent and anonymity protocols, reporting any concerns immediately to the Child Protection Officer.
