title: Director, Compliance, AMLCO
description:
Director, Compliance, AMLCO – Sydney, Australia

​​The Director, AML Compliance, AMLCO (otherwise known as Money Laundering Reporting Officer or MLRO) serves as WUFSA's formally appointed Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Compliance Officer as mandated by and defined under the Australian AML/CTF regulatory framework.

The role is responsible for leading the Australian AML/CTF compliance function, overseeing and coordinating the implementation and ongoing effectiveness of WUFSA's AML/CTF Program, ensuring compliance with applicable AML/CTF legislative and regulatory requirements, and supporting the identification, assessment, monitoring and management of money laundering, terrorism financing, proliferation financing, sanctions and other financial crime risks across the business.

​The role provides strategic oversight, leadership and subject matter expertise of AML/CTF governance, risk assessment, monitoring, controls, training and regulatory compliance activities. The role is responsible for ensuring AML/CTF risk considerations are embedded into business decision-making, new products, services, delivery channels and strategic initiatives. The incumbent also provides independent challenge and oversight to ensure financial crime risks are appropriately identified, assessed, managed and escalated across the organisation.

​While primarily focused on the Australian AML/CTF regulatory framework, the role is expected to lead regional AML/CTF projects across APAC, providing subject matter expertise, guidance and coaching to AML/CTF Compliance Officers and MLROs across the region.

​Role Responsibilities

REGULATORY APPOINTMENT REQUIREMENTS:

This position is the designated AML/CTF Compliance Officer for WUFSA.

The AML/CTF Compliance Officer has direct access to the WUFSA Governing Body and may escalate material AML/CTF matters independently of operational management where required to fulfil regulatory obligations. The role is responsible for maintaining an effective AML/CTF governance framework and ensuring AML/CTF obligations are communicated, implemented and monitored across the organisation.

The position holder shall:

  • Serve as the nominated AML/CTF Compliance Officer for WUFSA.
  • Act as primary contact with AUSTRAC regarding AML/CTF matters.
  • Oversee and coordinate day-to-day compliance with AML/CTF legislation (comprises the Act, Rules and other applicable regulatory guidance and requirements), applicable sanctions obligations; WUFSA AML/CTF Program and WU global AML/CTF standards.
  • Oversee the effectiveness of AML/CTF governance, risk management, and compliance controls.
  • Escalate material AML/CTF risks, breaches and deficiencies to Senior Management and the Governing Body.
  • Provide periodic AML/CTF reporting to Senior Management and relevant governance forums.
  • Formally report AML/CTF compliance outcomes and program effectiveness to the Governing Body at least annually.
  • Maintain eligibility to perform the role throughout tenure.
  • Meet all competency, authority, and independence, and fit-and-proper requirements established under WUFSA's AML/CTF Program and associated governance framework.

AML/CTF Program Governance and Oversight

  • Own and oversee the WUFSA AML/CTF Program.
  • Maintain AML/CTF policies, procedures, controls and governance documentation.
  • Ensure AML/CTF frameworks remain aligned with legislative requirements and regulatory expectations.
  • Oversee implementation of AML/CTF controls across all designated services.
  • Ensure AML/CTF documentation remains fit for purpose and current.
  • Coordinate periodic reviews and updates of the AML/CTF Program.

Oversee remediation of compliance deficiencies, audit findings and regulatory issues.

AML/CTF Compliance Officer and MLRO Responsibilities

  • Perform statutory responsibilities of the AML/CTF Compliance Officer.
  • Act as the principal AML/CTF contact with AUSTRAC.
  • Ensure compliance with all AML/CTF reporting obligations, including Suspicious Matter Reports (SMRs), Threshold Transaction Reports (TTRs), International Funds Transfer Instructions (IFTIs) and other regulatory reporting requirements.
  • Oversee suspicious activity investigations, decision-making and escalation processes.
  • Oversee the effectiveness of Customer Identification Program (CIP), Customer Due Diligence (CDD), Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) and ongoing customer monitoring controls.
  • Ensure AML/CTF risk considerations are incorporated into new products, services, systems, delivery channels and material business change initiatives.
  • Oversee sanctions compliance controls and escalation of potential sanctions-related matters.
  • Ensure AML/CTF record-keeping obligations are maintained and periodically tested.
  • Oversee implementation and monitoring of remediation programs arising from audits, compliance reviews, regulatory examinations and issue management activities.
  • Maintain regulatory documentation, appointment records and compliance evidence.
  • Support regulatory examinations, inspections, enquiries and information requests.
  • Maintain awareness of emerging financial crime typologies, regulatory developments, sanctions risks and industry best practices.

Ensure the organisation's AML/CTF obligations are effectively communicated and understood across relevant business areas.

Financial Crime Risk Management

  • Oversee the effective design and execution of enterprise AML/CTF risk assessments including associated customer, product, channel and geographic risk assessments.
  • Ensure effective management of financial crime risks including money laundering, terrorism financing, proliferation financing, sanctions, and fraud, based on risk assessment outcomes and controls being implemented to manage the identified risks.
  • Ensure enhanced due diligence requirements are effectively implemented.
  • Review and appropriately challenge other business risk assessments as required.

Escalate material financial crime risks to senior management and governance forums.

Governance, Board Reporting and Regulatory Engagement

  • Prepare periodic AML/CTF compliance reporting for Senior Management, Governing Body and other governance forums. Retain ownership and control of AML/CTF Compliance Officer reports and recommendations provided to the Governing Body, ensuring material findings, risks and recommendations are communicated transparently and without inappropriate modification.
  • Provide formal AML/CTF Compliance Officer reporting to the Governing Body at least annually, including:

· Compliance with AML/CTF policies and procedures;

· Effectiveness of AML/CTF controls in managing ML/TF risks;

· Compliance with AML/CTF legislative and regulatory obligations;

· Material AML/CTF deficiencies, breaches and remediation activities.

  • Escalate material AML/CTF incidents, compliance breaches, significant control deficiencies, emerging regulatory concerns and material financial crime risks as required.
  • Present significant compliance issues, regulatory developments, financial crime trends, breaches and emerging risks to governance forums and senior stakeholders.
  • Oversee responses to internal / external audit, compliance review, independent evaluation and regulatory findings.
  • Monitor closure of audit, regulatory and review findings and ensure timely remediation of identified issues.
  • Maintain effective relationships with regulators, governance stakeholders and relevant internal control functions.
  • Provide strategic advice and independent challenge to support informed decision-making regarding AML/CTF and financial crime risk matters.

Ensure Senior Management and the Governing Body remain informed of the effectiveness of the AML/CTF Program and material financial crime risks.

Monitoring, Training and Program Enhancement

  • Oversee AML/CTF compliance monitoring activities.
  • Ensure AML/CTF training programs remain effective, current and risk based.
  • Promote and maintain a strong financial crime compliance culture throughout the organisation.
  • Coordinate independent review and evaluation of the AML/CTF Program at prescribed intervals.
  • Monitor remediation and closure of findings arising from independent reviews.
  • Report progress of remediation activities to Senior Management and the Governing Body.
  • Assess emerging regulatory developments and recommend enhancements to AML/CTF controls and governance arrangements.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives across financial crime compliance frameworks, systems and controls.

Support the development of AML/CTF capability, awareness and expertise across the organisation.

AML/CTF Governance, Appointment and Regulatory Oversight

  • Maintain ongoing eligibility and suitability as the appointed AML/CTF Compliance Officer and MLRO.
  • Support periodic Fit and Proper assessments and eligibility reviews.
  • Maintain records evidencing appointment, eligibility and ongoing suitability.
  • Ensure regulatory notifications relating to appointment, resignation, replacement or eligibility changes are completed within prescribed timeframes.
  • Escalate any matter affecting continued eligibility, suitability, independence or regulatory standing.
  • Ensure governance records relating to appointment remain current and available for review.

Western Union Competencies:

  • Customer Focus
    • Provides expert compliance support and guidance to business stakeholders while ensuring customer outcomes are balanced with regulatory obligations and risk management requirements.
  • Management & Planning
    • Develops, oversees and enhances compliance frameworks, governance structures, policies and risk management programs.
  • Business Expertise
    • Possesses extensive expertise in AML/CTF compliance, financial crime risk management, sanctions compliance and regulatory governance.
  • Leadership
    • Provides strategic compliance leadership, influences senior stakeholders and drives a culture of accountability, integrity and regulatory compliance.

Core Factors:

Functional Knowledge

  • Recognised subject matter expert in AML/CTF legislation, financial crime compliance, sanctions compliance, governance and regulatory engagement.
  • Applies deep technical expertise and judgement to oversee AML/CTF risk management frameworks and regulatory compliance obligations.
  • Possesses extensive knowledge of money laundering, terrorism financing, proliferation financing and sanctions risks relevant to financial services and payments industries.
  • Maintains awareness of emerging financial crime typologies, regulatory developments, industry trends and best practices.
  • Provides authoritative advice to Senior Management, governance forums and business stakeholders regarding AML/CTF obligations and financial crime risk management.
  • Exercises independent judgement in complex and high-risk regulatory and compliance matters.
  • Influences organisational strategy, governance and risk management outcomes through expert knowledge and thought leadership.

Area of Impact

  • Direct impact on WUFSA's regulatory compliance, financial crime risk profile, governance effectiveness and regulatory relationships.

Nature of Impact

  • Influences organizational compliance, risk management and regulatory outcomes through independent oversight and governance leadership.

Problem Solving

  • Exercises independent judgement and advanced analytical skills to address complex regulatory, governance and financial crime matters.

MANDATORY ELIGIBILITY AND APPOINTMENT REQUIREMENTS

The incumbent must be an Australian resident and satisfy the eligibility requirements for appointment as an AML/CTF Compliance Officer under applicable AML/CTF legislation.


Competence and Capability

The incumbent will demonstrate:

  • Advanced knowledge of AML/CTF legislation, regulatory requirements and industry guidance.
  • Strong understanding of money laundering, terrorism financing, proliferation financing and sanctions risks.
  • Ability to interpret and apply complex regulatory obligations and expectations.
  • Experience designing, implementing and overseeing AML/CTF compliance frameworks.
  • Experience engaging with regulators, governance forums, internal audit and external audit.
  • Capability to exercise independent judgement and risk-based decision-making.
  • Ability to effectively challenge business decisions where AML/CTF risks or compliance concerns exist.
  • Capability to oversee AML/CTF governance, compliance monitoring, reporting and risk management activities.

Authority

The incumbent will:

  • Hold a management-level position or equivalent authority within the organisation.
  • Possess sufficient standing and influence to drive compliance outcomes across the business.
  • Have unrestricted access to Senior Management and the Governing Body.
  • Maintain direct access to the Governing Body and appropriate governance forums for the purpose of escalating AML/CTF matters independently of operational management.
  • Have authority to independently escalate ML/TF risks, deficiencies, breaches and regulatory concerns.
  • Have authority to challenge business decisions where AML/CTF risks are not being appropriately addressed.
  • Have authority to directly engage and communicate with AUSTRAC and other relevant regulators regarding AML/CTF matters where required.
  • Have unrestricted access to governance committees and the Governing Body to discharge AML/CTF Compliance Officer responsibilities.
  • Have authority to request information, documentation and resources necessary to effectively discharge AML/CTF obligations.
  • Be empowered to recommend corrective actions, control enhancements and remediation initiatives to address identified AML/CTF risks and compliance deficiencies.

Independence

The incumbent will:

  • Operate independently and objectively in the performance of AML/CTF Compliance Officer responsibilities.
  • Remain free from undue operational influence or conflicts that may impair independent judgement.
  • Exercise independent judgement regarding AML/CTF risk management and compliance matters.
  • Escalate AML/CTF concerns without inappropriate influence or restriction.
  • Maintain sufficient independence to provide objective oversight, challenge and governance across the AML/CTF Program.

Access to Resources

The incumbent will have access to:

  • Appropriate staffing resources and subject matter expertise.
  • AML/CTF systems, technology and reporting tools.
  • Legal, compliance and risk management support functions.
  • External professional advice where necessary.
  • Information necessary to discharge responsibilities effectively.
  • Ongoing training and development necessary to maintain AML/CTF competency.
  • Appropriate organisational support, budget and resources to enable effective execution of AML/CTF responsibilities.

Ongoing Suitability

The incumbent will:

  • Maintain eligibility to perform the role throughout tenure.
  • Immediately disclose any matter that could impact ongoing suitability, independence or effectiveness in the role.
  • Continue to satisfy WUFSA's AML/CTF Compliance Officer eligibility and Fit and Proper requirements. Failure to maintain these requirements may result in the incumbent no longer being eligible to perform the role of AML/CTF Compliance Officer and MLRO.

FIT AND PROPER ASSESSMENT REQUIREMENTS

Ongoing Fit and Proper Obligations

The incumbent must immediately disclose any matter that may impact suitability including:

  • criminal investigations or proceedings;
  • regulatory investigations or actions;
  • disciplinary actions;
  • material conflicts of interest;
  • insolvency-related matters;
  • any circumstance that could affect integrity, competence, independence or suitability.

Fit and Proper assessments may include:

  • Criminal history screening.
  • Regulatory enforcement and disciplinary history reviews.
  • Employment and reference verification.
  • Verification of qualifications, certifications and professional memberships.
  • Adverse media screening.
  • Conflict of interest assessments.
  • Financial probity assessments where permitted under applicable laws.
  • Review of competency, performance and regulatory obligations associated with the role.

Conflicts of Interest

  • The incumbent must disclose any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest which may impair their independence, objectivity or ability to perform AML/CTF Compliance Officer responsibilities.
  • The incumbent must comply with WUFSA conflict management requirements and promptly notify relevant governance bodies of any material conflicts.

WUFSA may conduct periodic reassessments of the incumbent's Fit and Proper status. Continued appointment is contingent upon maintaining satisfactory Fit and Proper standing.


Role Requirements

  • Minimum 10 years' experience in AML/CTF Compliance, Financial Crime Compliance, Financial Crime Risk Management, Regulatory Compliance or related disciplines.
  • undefined
  • Minimum 5 years' experience in senior AML/CTF compliance leadership in Australia, for example this could be acting as the AMLCO or Deputy AMLCO in a similar sized organisation, a senior leader who runs a sizable financial crime risk function in a large organisation, or demonstrated experience in acting as, or supporting, an AMLCO within a regulated financial institution, payments provider, remittance business or financial services organisation.
  • undefined
  • Demonstrated experience engaging directly with regulators, boards, audit committees, executive leadership teams and governance forums.
  • undefined
  • Demonstrated experience designing, implementing and maintaining AML/CTF frameworks, risk assessments and financial crime control environments.

  • undefined
  • Bachelor's degree required in Law, Finance, Business, Risk Management, Accounting, Public Policy, or a related discipline. Advanced degree preferred.

    • Postgraduate qualifications in Compliance, Risk Management, Financial Crime or Law is highly desirable.
  • Professional certifications such as ACAMS certification, ICA Diploma or Advanced Certificate, ACFCS Certification, or other recognised AML/CTF; compliance or financial crime certifications will be highly regarded.

Additional Skills:

  • Advanced knowledge of AML/CTF, sanctions compliance, financial crime risk management, regulatory reporting, governance, controls, and audit/remediation frameworks.
  • Skilled in risk assessment, policy development, compliance monitoring, and pragmatic risk-based decision-making.

title: Project Manager, Permit & Communications Lead
description:
Title:

Project Manager, Permit & Communications Lead

KBR Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) provides holistic and value-added solutions across the entire asset life cycle. These include world-class licensed process technologies, differentiated advisory services, deep technical domain expertise, energy transition solutions, high-end design capabilities, and smart solutions to optimize planned and operating assets.


KBR is seeking a Permit & Communications Lead to provide overall leadership of the permitting, communications, and stakeholder engagement function for a multi-billion-dollar GMP manufacturing program in the Greater Richmond, VA area, serving as the Client's primary regulatory, governmental, and external stakeholder interface within the PMC team. As a senior pharmaceutical PMC/Owner's Representative role, this position is responsible for establishing permitting and communications governance, overseeing regulatory approvals and permit compliance, directing stakeholder and community engagement strategies, managing contractor performance within the assigned scope, and ensuring alignment between project objectives and external requirements. The Permit & Communications Lead provides strategic guidance to PMC leadership on permitting status, regulatory and stakeholder risks, communications priorities, mitigation strategies, and project readiness, while supporting successful project execution, GMP compliance, startup readiness, and long-term operational success.


Functional job responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

  • Lead the development and execution of permitting, regulatory engagement, stakeholder management, and communications strategies to support all phases of project delivery.
  • Serve as the primary interface between the Client, regulatory agencies, local authorities, community organizations, utility providers, and other external stakeholders.
  • Oversee the identification, tracking, submission, and approval of all required permits, licenses, environmental authorizations, and regulatory approvals necessary for project execution.
  • Establish and maintain permitting governance processes, schedules, and reporting systems to ensure timely approvals and compliance with project milestones.
  • Coordinate closely with engineering, environmental, construction, commissioning, and operations teams to ensure permitting requirements are integrated into project planning and execution.
  • Direct public relations, community outreach, and stakeholder engagement initiatives to foster positive relationships and maintain the project's social license to operate.
  • Manage communications consultants, permitting contractors, and external advisors to ensure consistent, effective, and compliant execution of project objectives.
  • Monitor regulatory developments, policy changes, and external factors that may impact project execution, and develop mitigation strategies to address emerging risks.
  • Lead the preparation and delivery of executive-level communications, presentations, stakeholder briefings, and regulatory submissions.
  • Develop and maintain stakeholder engagement plans, communications matrices, and issue management processes to ensure proactive and transparent communications.
  • Identify, assess, and manage permitting, regulatory, and stakeholder risks, implementing mitigation and recovery plans to minimize project impacts.
  • Support project leadership in development and execution of incident communications, issue management, and crisis communication strategies.
  • Collaborate with project controls and project management teams to ensure permitting activities, approvals, and stakeholder commitments are incorporated into the overall project schedule and execution strategy.
  • Coordinate permitting activities associated with GMP manufacturing facilities, laboratories, utilities, warehousing, and support infrastructure.
  • Support project readiness activities related to regulatory inspections and occupancy approvals.
  • Coordinate with Quality, Validation, and Operations teams regarding regulatory commitments.
  • Oversee environmental permitting and compliance activities including air permits, stormwater permits, wastewater permits, hazardous materials requirements, and agency reporting obligations.
  • Ensure permit conditions and environmental commitments are incorporated into project execution plans and contractor requirements.
  • Provide regular performance reporting and strategic recommendations to PMC and Client leadership regarding permitting status, regulatory compliance, stakeholder concerns, and communications effectiveness.
  • Promote a culture of safety, compliance, transparency, and accountability in all interactions with regulatory agencies, stakeholders, and project teams.

Required Education, Experience, & Skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Public Policy, Communications, Planning, Construction Management, or related discipline.
  • Minimum 10 years of experience supporting permitting, stakeholder engagement, environmental compliance, communications, or project management on major capital projects, including projects exceeding $500 million TIC.
  • Experience managing permitting, regulatory affairs, environmental compliance, stakeholder engagement, communications, or infrastructure delivery teams on major capital projects Strong knowledge of engineering governance, design management, and project delivery processes.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical decision-making and stakeholder alignment.
  • Strong leadership and stakeholder management capabilities.
  • Experience directing and evaluating performance of permitting consultants, communications consultants, stakeholder engagement firms, and regulatory support contractors, including review and approval of deliverables.

Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills:

  • Experience supporting pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or other GMP-regulated facilities.
  • Prior experience in an Owner’s Representative or PMC role for major capital projects in excess of $1B TIC.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license and/or PMP certification.
  • Experience supporting FDA inspections, commissioning, startup, and operational readiness activities.

title: Pest Control Technician
description:
Want to build a brighter, bolder future and cultivate your career? Join Ecolab’s team and help create a world in which we all thrive.

Our Pest Elimination team proudly serves our communities and customers by safeguarding public health, food safety and property from the damaging effects of pests. Focused exclusively on commercial pest solutions, we deliver science-based expertise and cutting-edge innovation to solve the industry’s most complex pest challenges. By partnering with our customers in these markets, you can be part of a team that helps protect facilities, employees, and brands at a time when it’s more important than ever.

Ecolab is seeking a Pest Control Technician Trainee to join our team in Northbrook, IL. As a Pest Control Technician Trainee, you’ll be at the forefront of protecting public health and commercial businesses by delivering science-based pest elimination solutions. Through our industry-leading training program, you’ll gain the skills and certifications needed to build a long-term career in service, sales, or management. This is your opportunity to grow your career while helping others thrive.

How You’ll Make an Impact:

  • Participate in a 5-week paid training program to learn pest detection, elimination, and prevention techniques
  • Establish effective working relationships with a variety of commercial customers, including those in the hospitality and foodservice industries
  • Partner with customers on best practices to identify and solve pest elimination needs
  • Maintain expertise in Ecolab’s product and service offerings to enhance service and sales
  • Use handheld computerized equipment to document structural, sanitation, and pest issues
  • Deliver timely, cost-effective, and high-quality service under close supervision
  • Obtain required pest control licensing and/or certification as mandated by state/local law

Position Details:

  • Location: Northbrook, IL
  • Territory: Northbrook, Glenview IL
  • Work Week & Shift: Sunday-Thursday; Overnight shift (9pm-5am); Full time
  • Travel Requirement: Eagan, MN for 1 week of training. You are responsible to have the proper documentation to fly such as a Real ID or other acceptable form of identification.

What’s Unique About This Role:

  • Work independently in a flexible, field-based environment
  • Help protect customer brands and public health through science-based solutions

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Two years of work or military experience
  • Position requires a current and valid Driver’s License with no restrictions
  • Availability to work overnight shifts and be on call during off-hours and weekends as needed
  • Due to the nature and hours of the work, must be 18 years of age or older
  • Position requires obtaining pest certification and/or business licensing pursuant to state/local law
  • Ecolab conducts a background check on all candidates who receive a job offer
  • Due to federal contract requirements, this position requires a drug test including THC for all candidates who receive a job offer
  • Immigration sponsorship is not available for this role

Physical Demands:

  • Position requires lifting, pushing, pulling, and carrying up to 50 pounds chest high
  • Position requires wearing and using a respirator
  • Position requires working in a variety of conditions including confined spaces, damp/dusty areas, and extreme temperatures
  • Position requires climbing ladders and performing physical tasks such as stooping, kneeling, crouching, reaching, and standing for extended periods
  • Position requires driving a company vehicle as required (ongoing motor vehicle record checks will be performed)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous customer service experience
  • Experience selling value-added products to existing customers
  • Previous pest elimination industry or route experience preferred

What’s in it for you:

  • Starting on Day 1: Access to our comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, matching 401K, company-paid pension, stock purchase plan, paid parental leave, select discounted childcare resources, and more!
  • The opportunity to take on some of the world’s most meaningful challenges, helping customers achieve clean water, safe food, and healthy environments
  • The ability to make an impact and shape your career with a company that is passionate about growth
  • The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives, and ideas to achieve our best

About Ecolab:

At Ecolab, we prioritize our talent-first philosophy by creating the most capable and diverse team to excel at our nearly three million customer sites. Building on a century of innovation, our 48,000 associates help deliver comprehensive science-based solutions, data-driven insights and world-class service to advance food safety, maintain clean and safe environments, and optimize water and energy use, and improve operational efficiencies and sustainability for customers in the food, healthcare, life sciences, hospitality and industrial markets in more than 170 countries around the world. Our solutions not only enhance operational efficiency but also contribute to sustainability and public health, making a positive impact on the world. We are committed to eliminating unnecessary complexities and embracing a beginner's mindset, continuously seeking new perspectives and innovative solutions to stay ahead in a rapidly changing world.

The total Compensation range for this position is $53,600-$80,300 which includes base pay and target incentive based on performance, per plan terms after completion of the comprehensive paid training program. Many factors are taken into consideration when determining compensation, such as experience, education, training, geography, etc. We comply with all minimum wage and overtime laws.

title: Rare Hematology Thought Leader Liaison
description:
Job Title: Rare Hematology Thought Leader Liaison

  • Location: US / Remote

Geography: Gulf Coast Region

Travel: 60–80% travel expected

Job Type: Full Time

About The Job:

Sanofi focuses on developing specialty treatments for debilitating diseases that are often difficult to diagnose and treat, providing hope to patients and their families.

Sanofi has pioneered the development and delivery of transformative therapies for patients affected by rare and debilitating diseases for over 30 years. We accomplish our goals through world-class research, collaboration with the global patient community, and with the compassion and commitment of our employees. With a focus on rare diseases, oncology, immunology, and multiple sclerosis, we are dedicated to making a positive impact on the lives of the patients and families we serve. Sanofi's portfolio of transformative therapies, which are marketed in countries around the world, represent groundbreaking and life-saving advances in medicine.

At Sanofi, we are committed to the growth of our people, connected in purpose by career, life, and health. Learn more at .

The Rare Blood Disorders franchise is a patient-centric organization responsible for delivering the highest quality education and service regarding disease and treatment. The goal of the franchise is to penetrate existing and new markets to meet business goals by educating physicians and healthcare professionals on a portfolio of products while upholding the Company's mission and values.

Sanofi's Rare Blood Disorders/Rare Hematology Thought Leader Liaison (TLL) is a field-based, commercial role responsible for engaging Healthcare Professionals (HCPs) and Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) to strategically inform market development across the rare hematology portfolio of products. The TLL is expected to possess a high level of clinical and customer knowledge, have experience with both field and headquarters protocols and procedures, and possess the drive and spirit to engage with healthcare professionals to help build educational platforms, generate insights, and inform local and national brand strategies, supporting the commercial success of the portfolio. The portfolio focus is primarily on Systemic Mastocytosis (SM) and Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP).

The TLL will work closely, and within approved SOPs, with other field professionals including, but not limited to, Regional Business Directors, Area Business Managers, and Medical Science Liaisons, as well as home office-based colleagues in Marketing, Medical Affairs, Operations, and Market Access.

A core responsibility of this role is driving SM and ITP market development within the assigned region — identifying KOLs and fostering multi-disciplinary connections across specialists who treat and manage SM and ITP patients. The TLL serves as a strategic partner to cross-functional commercial and medical teams. The TLL helps to shape brand strategy through insight generation, KOL engagement, and regional market development initiatives across the full rare hematology portfolio.

Join the team transforming care for people with immune challenges, rare diseases, cancers, and neurological conditions. In Specialty Care, you'll help deliver breakthrough treatments that bring hope to patients with some of the highest unmet needs.

About Sanofi:

We’re an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives.

Main Responsibilities:

A. KOL Development and Engagement:

  • Work with cross-functional colleagues to coordinate function-specific activities aligned to business and customer needs.
  • Identify, profile, and maintain long-term partnerships with KOLs and emerging leaders within the Hematology and Allergy/Immunology communities.
  • Identify SM champions within the region.
  • Engage in on-label conversations to gather insights on topics such as disease diagnosis and treatment, therapeutic options, and product positioning across SM and ITP.
  • Execute unique, on-label, and strategic HCP programming (e.g., disease state and product) as determined by brand needs.
  • Serve as a single point of contact to resolve commercial KOL issues.
  • Execute a customer-centric, needs-based approach with targeted KOLs.
  • Plan and execute KOL engagements and executive encounters at local, regional, and national conferences, field visits, and other venues as directed.
  • Be a voice for allergy/immunology and hematology/oncology KOLs within the organization, sharing insights with key stakeholders and cross-functional partners to inform brand strategy.

B. SM and ITP Centers of Excellence and Market Development:

  • Lead long-term market development efforts in assigned regions across the SM and ITP landscapes, focusing on high-potential centers and customers.
  • Develop and execute customer engagement plans for KOLs within assigned regions, accountable for fostering KOL connections across multi-disciplinary specialists who treat and manage SM and ITP patients.
  • Maintain understanding of regional market dynamics, including key opinion leaders, institutional accounts, and multi-disciplinary teams to advance SM and ITP patient care and partner with sales leadership and commercial field teams to align regional market development strategies.
  • Develop and execute regional marketing initiatives (insight discovery, advisory boards, roundtables, etc.).
  • Support regional congress planning and execution, including KOL insight gathering engagement at priority conferences across hematology/oncology and allergy/immunology, in partnership with Medical, Sales Leadership, Commercial Operations, and Brand Marketing.
  • Proactively meet with assigned centers and/or customers to solicit feedback and adjust strategies accordingly.
  • Develop and continuously maintain a high level of clinical competence across SM, ITP, and aTTP.

C. Market Insights and Collaboration:

  • Capture, analyze, and share customer insights aligned with brand priorities across SM and ITP.
  • Work with targeted KOLs to obtain feedback on new and existing brand-related strategies and materials (all materials and programs will be approved by legal, compliance, and regulatory).
  • Capture and analyze competitive intelligence to help shape strategy and activities.
  • Facilitate cross-functional planning, recruitment, and execution of regional and national advisory boards in partnership with HQ Marketing.
  • Identify, align, and recruit appropriate HCP/KOL consultants to meet the needs of marketing and achieve aligned KPIs for each project.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to inform account strategy and plans through treatment pathway discovery and insight generation to advance care in centers of excellence.

D. Speaker Bureau Operations and Content:

  • Assist with speaker bureau management, including identification and training/coaching of promotional speakers with approved slide decks and materials.
  • Assist in the execution of speaker contracting when requested, including completion of annual budget plans, recommendations, and nominations.
  • Coordinate and execute speaker training to ensure assigned speakers are competent, compliant, and up to date on new information.
  • Attend HCP speaker programs to observe, coach, and remediate speakers when necessary to ensure optimal execution of content.
  • Assist with new content creation and existing content updates and renewals
  • Serve as the single point of contact for a high-volume of speaker logistics/scheduling and work cross-functionally to ensure streamlined communication.
  • Lead planning, execution, and pull-through of TLL-owned programs.

About You:

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree.
  • A minimum of 5 years of work experience in one or more of the following: field sales, product marketing, or medical/clinical in the pharmaceutical, healthcare, biotech or other related life science industries
  • Prior experience interacting with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) and/or HCPs.
  • Ability to travel to meetings, trainings, and programs as necessary (60–80%).
  • Must have a valid driver's license.
  • Must reside within the geographic area of the assigned territory, or within a reasonable distance.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in Rare Diseases and/or Hematology.
  • Allergy/Immunology and/or Hematology-Oncology background preferred
  • Experience in marketing or leading marketing projects.
  • Academic center focus and KOL development experience.
  • Experience working within or building multi-disciplinary treatment teams.
  • Cross-functional commercial background (e.g., marketing, sales leadership)
  • Master's degree in a related field.
  • Launch experience, including demonstrated success across multiple drug launches in applicable specialty markets.
  • Previous experience working as a Thought Leader Liaison.
  • KOL and/or speaker management experience.
  • Strong communication, organization, and project management skills
  • Proven ability to work in a highly dynamic and fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead without formal authority and work in a highly collaborative environment.
  • Excellent organizational, interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Robust analytical and problem-solving skills; ability to identify and act on creative solutions.
  • Ability to establish credibility, connect the dots, and align multiple stakeholders to pioneer the adoption of new products, methods, and technologies.
  • Flexibility and ability to plan and adapt to changing market conditions.
  • Motivated by patient focus, urgency, and personal commitment to high performance, results, and compliance.
  • Possesses high integrity and exceptional work ethic.

Pursue Progress, Discover Extraordinary

Better is out there. Better medications, better outcomes, better science. But progress doesn't happen without people – people from different backgrounds, in different locations, doing different roles, all united by one thing: a desire to make miracles happen. So, let's be those people.

title: Manufacturing Technician, Staff
description:
Manufacturing Technician, Staff


We are looking for a Manufacturing Technician, Staff to join our team!


The Manufacturing Technician, Staff will perform advanced manufacturing, testing, inspection, troubleshooting, and production-support activities in accordance with established procedures, engineering requirements, quality standards, and applicable industry regulations. You will apply broad manufacturing knowledge to complex or non-routine production assignments of parts, components, subassemblies, and final assemblies.


Location: Round Rock, TX (onsite)


We Take Care of Our People:

Paid Time Off I 401K with Employer Match and Profit Sharing I Health and Wellness Benefits I Learning and Development Opportunities I Referral Program I Competitive Pay I Recognition I Employee Stock Purchase Plan I Inclusive & Supportive Culture

title: Principle Software Engineer (Scottsdale)
description:
Company Overview

AdviNOW Medical is transforming how healthcare is delivered by building AI-powered clinical decision support systems that improve diagnostic accuracy, reduce clinician burden, and increase patient safety. Our platform combines advanced reasoning, probabilistic models, and machine learning to support real-world medical decision-making at scale.

We are a product-driven startup tackling complex, high-impact problems in healthcare—and we’re looking for a Principal Engineer to help lead the technical evolution of our platform.

Job Summary

As a Principal Engineer at AdviNOW Medical, you will serve as a senior technical thought leader responsible for driving engineering standards and delivering scalable, AI-enabled healthcare software. This is a deeply hands-on role for someone who thrives in startup environments, owns problems end-to-end, and enjoys building systems that matter.

You will work closely with senior leadership, product, clinical experts, and engineering teams to shape both what we build and how we build it.

Hands-On Engineering

Data & AI Systems

  • Advanced understanding of RESTful APIs, async processing, and service-oriented architectures
  • Extensive experience with PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and ORM-based data modeling
  • Hands-on experience integrating AI/ML-powered features into real-world production systems
  • Strong grounding in software architecture patterns, testing strategies, and system scalability
  • Comfortable working in fast-moving startup environments with high ownership and ambiguity

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience with event-driven architectures, background jobs, or message queues
  • Prior experience helping scale an early-stage or growth-stage product
  • Exposure to probabilistic systems, Bayesian reasoning, or clinical decision support platforms

title: Principal Digital OCM Lead
description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections, where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

The Position

In Pharma Technical Operations (PT), we deliver life-saving medicines to patients worldwide. As our Principal Digital OCM Lead, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring that our strategic digital and data initiatives - ranging from digital site transformations and operations-wide data foundations to network automation and agile mindsets - take firm root across our global operational teams.

As a Principal Digital OCM Lead, you will join an elite, internal advisory and delivery team within PT Digital and Operational Excellence (PTE). Acting as an internal Behavioral OCM leader, you will serve as a high-impact catalyst for digital evolution across Pharma Technical Operations (PT). You will bridge strategic intent and operational reality, designing human-centric change strategies that minimize operational disruption, safeguard quality compliance, and foster long-term behavioral change.

Core Responsibilities:

  • Transformational Leadership: Partner closely with the broader PTE leadership team to embed robust Organizational Change Management (OCM) strategies for large-scale operations-wide transformations, post-merger integrations, digital shifts, and process restructurings.
  • Behavioral & Cultural Transformation: Apply modern change frameworks and behavioral insights (e.g., nudge management) to align workforce mindsets with strategic change, data-driven culture, psychological safety, and a mindset of continuous innovation.
  • Operational & Digital Change Execution: Design, drive, and scale change management frameworks for major PT digital initiatives (e.g., global data governance adoption, smart factory/Industry 4.0 rollouts, and digital shopfloor tools).
  • Stakeholder Alignment & Network Building: Act as a trusted advisor to site leaders, global process owners, shopfloor operators, and quality teams to build strong change networks and active sponsorship across the PT matrix.
  • Impact & Readiness Assessments: Conduct systematic change impact analyses, risk evaluations, and organizational readiness assessments across diverse global functions within PT. Leverage quantitative data and behavioral analytics to measure adoption velocity, identify adoption barriers, and iterate on change interventions.
  • Communication & Enablement: Establish tailored communication architectures and learning strategies that translate complex data and digital solutions into clear, engaging adoption journeys for end-users.
  • Methodology & Practice: Define, adopt, evolve, and implement standardized human-centric OCM methodologies, blueprints, and training assets across the global network, ensuring consistency in how digital change is navigated.
  • AI & Automation Enablement: Drive adoption strategies for AI-assisted tools, shopfloor automation, and operations-wide data models, helping teams transition from transactional execution to data-informed decision-making.


Who You Are

You are an architect of adoption, not just a communicator. You understand that digital transformation is 20% technology and 80% human behavior. You bring a pragmatic, empathetic approach to driving technology adoption across matrixed, multi-cultural teams.

Qualifications & Experience:

  • Behavioral Science Expertise: Demonstrated experience applying behavioral science principles (e.g., behavioral economics, nudge theory, habit formation loops) in a professional or operational context.
  • Education: University degree (Master’s or equivalent) in Business Administration, Organizational Psychology, Information Systems, Engineering, Life Sciences, or a related field.
  • Professional Experience: 10+ years driving organizational change management, digital transformation, or business adoption - ideally within pharmaceutical operations, manufacturing, biotech, or healthcare IT. Proven track record of supporting large-scale rollouts affecting multi-site global operational networks (e.g., 1,000+ end-users across multiple geographies).
  • Industry & Regulatory Understanding: Solid grasp of operational dynamics in technical, regulated environments. Experience driving change within validated environments without compromising strict GxP quality standards or operational compliance.
  • Change Methodologies: Proven expertise in established change management frameworks (e.g., Prosci, ADKAR, Kotter) combined with practical experience in Agile, Lean, or Design Thinking.
  • Leadership & Influence: Outstanding stakeholder management, empathy, and resilience, with a demonstrated ability to influence leaders and cross-functional teams without direct line authority.
  • Languages: Business-fluent English is required; Spanish is a strong asset given the Madrid location.
  • Behavioral Analytics & Digital Adoption: Experience utilizing digital adoption platforms (e.g., WalkMe, Pendo) or product analytics to track, measure, and optimize user interaction patterns within digital solutions.
  • Coaching & Change Leadership: Demonstrated ability to coach managers and local leadership teams in behavioral management techniques, empowering them to act as effective change agents and scale adoption impact.

Who We Are

At Roche, more than 100,000 people across 100 countries are pushing back the frontiers of healthcare. Working together, we’ve become one of the world’s leading research-focused healthcare groups. Our success is built on innovation, curiosity, and diversity.

What We Offer:

  • Impact for Patients: Direct contribution to optimizing the global manufacturing and supply chain operations that bring life-saving therapies to millions of patients.
  • High-Visibility Scope: Broad strategic influence across the global Pharma Technical Operations network.
  • Growth & Culture: An empowering environment that values psychological safety, flexible hybrid working models, continuous learning, and personal development.

title: Software Engineering SMTS / LMTS - AI Core (REMOTE)
description:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Engineering at Qualified


Engineering at Qualified is a high-ownership, high-velocity environment where engineers ship customer-facing product to real enterprises at scale. We're building at the frontier of AI + product: developing agentic software and

embedding AI directly into our platform, using modern toolchains and processes that help engineers move faster while staying focused on high-impact problem solving.


Following our acquisition by Salesforce, we continue to operate with the pace and ownership of a startup, backed by the distribution, resources, and long-term runway of a global enterprise. Engineers have true end-to-end ownership from idea to production: scoping, implementation, testing, deployment, monitoring, and iterative improvement based on real customer feedback.


You'll work alongside a high-talent-density team that cares deeply about craft, performance, reliability, and user experience, and that raises the bar through collaboration, code review, and strong engineering principles. You'll make architecture decisions, solve meaningful system design challenges, and see your work land quickly with customers, without layers of approvals slowing you down.


The Role


As an Engineer on the AI Core team, you'll operate as a technical leader who turns ambiguous, high-stakes AI problems into durable, high-quality systems, while raising the technical bar for the broader team. AI Core builds the retrieval systems and agent infrastructure that power how our AI agents find, trust, and use knowledge, and the developer tooling that lets engineers across the company ship production agents quickly and safely.


You'll lead significant initiatives end to end: faithful answering over a customer's own knowledge, retrieval that combines RAG and hybrid search, content lifecycle controls such as freshness, deduplication and source precedence, transcript processing, and the frameworks, registries, and evaluation tooling that make building a production agent a paved path. You'll partner closely with product, design, and engineering leadership to decide what we build, how we build it, and how we measure whether answers actually got better.


What You'll Do


Lead retrieval initiatives end to end: Design, build, and operate retrieval systems using RAG and hybrid search (lexical plus vector, reranking, filtering) so agents answer from the right content with the right amount of context. Own delivery from scope and design through launch, monitoring, and iteration.


Build developer tooling for production agents: Drive technical design for the frameworks and platform pieces our engineers use to build agents, including multi-agent orchestration, shared primitives for prompts, tools, tracing, and evaluation.


Own answer quality: Diagnose why answers are thin, wrong, or inconsistent by separating retrieval problems from generation problems (prompt, token budget, model choice). Set a quality bar we can test against, and lead the

work to reach it.


Design content and data models: Define how content from documents,

knowledge bases, and call transcripts is ingested, segmented, labeled, and retrieved, including the primitives behind freshness, dedupe, source

precedence, and internal versus external visibility.


Make AI changes safe to ship: Build evaluation, observability, and rollout

practices (offline evals, online monitoring, regression detection) so we can change prompts, models, and retrieval with confidence. Evaluate multiple

solution paths and know when to trust, redirect, or override model and agent output.


Set performance and scaling benchmarks across the platform we own:


Define and track targets for retrieval and indexing, LLM provider usage, and agent orchestration.


Own operational health: Ensure the reliability and performance of the systems your team owns. Participate in on-call, lead incident resolution for your area, and communicate clearly with the team and stakeholders during incidents.


Use agentic development to raise leverage: Use coding agents by default for implementation, testing, refactoring, and documentation while holding a high validation bar. Create reusable workflows, patterns, and tooling that raise the effectiveness of your team beyond your own output.


Partner across functions: Work with product, design, and engineering

leadership to shape roadmap, tradeoffs, and requirements, and to translate strategy into concrete execution plans.


Raise team effectiveness: Mentor engineers, give high-quality code review and technical guidance, and improve standards, tooling, and processes.


Who You Are


Proven experience shipping production AI or backend systems in a high ownership environment, with a recent focus on LLM-powered applications.


Expertise building retrieval systems using RAG and hybrid search, including chunking and indexing strategy, embeddings, vector and lexical search,

reranking, and measuring retrieval quality.


Expertise building developer tooling that lets developers build production agents, which can include frameworks for multi-agent orchestration, an agent and tool registry, and shared infrastructure for tracing and evaluation.

Experience owning platform initiatives from design through adoption,

across systems such as retrieval and indexing, LLM provider integrations, and agent orchestration, including driving adoption and evolving the platform as usage grows.


Demonstrated technical leadership: you lead significant projects, design solutions for non-trivial problems by weighing tradeoffs, and influence architecture and execution beyond your immediate workstream.


Strong track record delivering complex projects with multiple stakeholders, dependencies, or phases.


Strong backend engineering fundamentals and proficiency in languages such as Ruby on Rails, Python, JavaScript, or Go, with SQL and RDBMS experience (PostgreSQL preferred).


Hands-on experience with the AI application lifecycle: experiment setup, dataset curation, offline evaluation, error analysis, deployment, and online evaluation.


Comfortable operating in ambiguity and driving clarity: you can frame problems, propose solutions, and align others.


Strong communicator across functions, able to explain technical ideas to both technical and non-technical audiences and to translate complex concepts into business impact.


Ownership mindset and bias for action. You raise the bar for the team through mentoring, code review, and your own work.


Curious and continuously learning, with an agent-forward approach to how you build software.


Nice to Have


Experience with pgvector or other vector indexes, and with query performance at scale.


Experience with content ingestion from third-party systems (document stores, knowledge bases, CRM knowledge objects) and the lifecycle problems that follow: sync state, dedupe, source conflict.


Experience processing conversation or call transcripts, including handling PII and consent constraints.


Experience designing evaluation suites that score qualities such as thoroughness and faithfulness, not only correctness.


Experience with voice or real-time conversational agents.


Experience with enterprise SaaS (especially B2B marketing or sales tech) or Salesforce/CRM integrations.


Startup experience and rapid shipping.


Why Join Qualified


Foundational impact: Shape how our AI agents retrieve, reason, and answer, and the tooling every engineer here uses to build them.


Lead real initiatives: Own significant projects end to end, with scope and

influence that grow as you deliver. You'll own the platform as it scales, from retrieval to model providers to agent orchestration, and set the performance and reliability bar that grows with the company.


AI as a core product surface: Turn new AI capabilities into dependable

experiences that customers trust, with strong engineering around evaluation, observability, and iteration.


High bar, low bureaucracy: Work with a team that values craft and decisive execution, where strong ideas win and shipping is the default.


Room to grow: Take on larger technical and product scope over time: leading projects, influencing architecture, and leveling up quickly.


If you're excited to build retrieval systems and agent infrastructure at the intersection of AI and enterprise software, we'd love to hear from you.


Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

Accommodations

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this Accommodations Request Form.

Please note that Salesforce uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help our recruiters assess and evaluate candidates’ resumes and qualifications throughout the recruiting process. Humans will always make any candidate selection and hiring decisions. Please see our Candidate Privacy Statement for more information about how we use your personal data and your rights, including with regard to use of AI tools and opt out options.

  • Design and operationalize enhanced capabilities of Polarion and own the Polarion enhancement backlog and single request intake; consolidate, validate and prioritize requests with key users, process owners and project stakeholders.

  • Define and monitor relevant KPIs, including support demand, backlog, adoption and training; identify and address capability or compliance gaps.
  • Author and maintain procedures and work instructions related to Polarion and represent GDPD as Polarion subject-matter expert in internal and external audits.

  • Experience working with computerized systems in a regulated GxP or medical-device environment, with a strong understanding of quality, compliance and controlled change.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional networks and teams without direct line authority, manage competing priorities and drive decisions across organizational boundaries.

title: Principal Researcher, Program Evaluation (Grant-funded)
description:
Applications must be submitted no later than 11:59 p.m. CT on the day before the listed closing date.


Weekly Work Hours

40

Compensation Range

Staff Range N06

Salary Minimum

$68,840.00 Annually

FLSA

United States of America (Exempt)

Work Location

  • All positions are considered on-site roles.
  • After six months of employment, some positions may be eligible to apply for a hybrid work arrangement based on job responsibilities, operational needs, supervisor approval, and Dallas College policy.
  • Academic (Faculty) positions require an on-campus presence, even when teaching online courses, in accordance with state law.

Position Type

Staff

Position / Job Summary

The Center for Student Parent Success (CSPS) coordinates and expands services across Dallas College’s seven campuses to help student parents balance academic, family, and work responsibilities. The Principal Researcher leads the design, implementation, and evaluation of CSPS’s research agenda, using mixed-methods approaches to assess programs and guide data-informed decision-making. Reporting to the Executive Director of CSPS and collaborating with the Student Outcomes Lab at The Research Institute at Dallas College, this role produces the evidence base that informs institutional strategy, resource allocation, and program improvements to advance student parent success.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Lead the design and implementation of needs assessments and formative, summative, and outcome evaluations using established program evaluation frameworks (e.g., Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) systems).

  • Design and implement quantitative and qualitative data collection strategies and instruments, including surveys, evaluation rubrics, and interview and focus group protocols, and develop sampling approaches.

  • Apply quantitative methods to assess student outcomes using survey and college administrative data.

  • Conduct foundational research (e.g., literature reviews, data exploration, consultation with subject-matter experts) to inform evaluation design.

  • Collaborate with team members and stakeholders to evaluate student parents’ access to, utilization of, and satisfaction with CSPS programs and services, as well as related academic outcomes.

  • Synthesize research findings and translate results into actionable recommendations that inform Center strategy, policy, and resource allocation decisions.

  • Produce high-quality reports, memos, briefs, and presentations to communicate research findings to stakeholders and leadership.

  • Complete required Dallas College professional development and human subjects research training each academic year (minimum of 19 hours; people leaders complete an additional 16 hours of leadership development).

  • Performs other job duties as assigned.

The following duties are required for People Leader roles specifically:

  • Exercises discretion and decision-making authority in the recruitment, selection, hiring, coaching, development, and termination of staff, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and workforce planning strategies.

  • Drives high performance by administering the performance management process, setting clear expectations, conducting evaluations, and implementing initiatives that enhance employee engagement and retention.

Minimum and Preferred – Education, Experience, and/or Certifications

Minimum Qualifications for Role

  • Bachelor’s degree in social science or education with coursework in program evaluation, research design, qualitative and quantitative methodology, statistics, or related discipline

  • At least three (3) years of post-undergraduate/graduate experience conducting program evaluations in education or a related field, including survey design, data collection, and analysis, and qualitative research methods

  • Expertise in program evaluation and qualitative/quantitative research methods and analysis

  • Demonstrated experience in academic and research-focused writing

  • Official transcripts required

Preferred Qualifications for Role

  • Master’s degree in a social science discipline (e.g., Education, Sociology, Public Policy, Economics, Psychology)

Conditions of Employment

  • Valid driver’s license required

  • Subject to a criminal background check; some positions may require a fingerprint-based background check

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

We are looking for experience in the following areas:

  • Expertise in program evaluation and assessment

  • Expertise in qualitative research design, data collection, and analysis

  • Expertise in survey design, collection, and data analysis

  • Proficiency in descriptive and inferential quantitative analysis

  • Experience with data analysis software; familiarity with data visualization tools is a plus.

  • Exceptional written communication and report-writing skills for research and general audiences

  • Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Required

Work Condition Environment / Physical Requirements

Normal physical job functions performed within a standard office environment. Reasonable accommodation(s) may be made to individuals with physical challenges to perform the essential duties and responsibilities.

Applications Deadline

November 2, 2026

title: Principal Forward Deployed Engineer I, Frontier Engineering

  • Be the trusted technical partner to customer engineering leadership: Build durable, peer-level relationships with CTOs, VPs of Engineering, chief architects, and heads of data/AI at Snowflake’s most strategic accounts: lead architectural steering, technical reviews, and executive strategy alignment to help shape their AI roadmaps.

  • Drive Architecture & Technical Strategy Across High-Stakes Deployments: Own end-to-end technical execution and outcomes across Snowflake’s most complex, high-visibility AI engagements.

  • Stay hands-on: Write production code and working prototypes on the most critical parts of customer programs, and review designs and code to set the bar for how the team builds.

  • Own the AI quality bar: Lead how the team measures and improves AI quality, turning ambiguous customer goals into clear, testable evaluation standards.

  • Provide Technical Leadership & Mentorship: Mentor Senior and Staff engineers, raise engineering standards across the organization, and partner with cross-functional leads to drive complex technical initiatives.

  • Travel to Customer Sites: Spend at least 25% of your time onsite working with customers.

OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE:

  • 15+ years of software engineering experience, including at least 3 years building and shipping production AI/ML or agentic systems at enterprise scale.

  • Proven track record as a trusted technical advisor to CTOs and executive engineering leaders at large enterprises.

  • Strong systems mindset with exceptional technical communication skills across both deeply technical and executive audiences.

BONUS POINTS FOR THE FOLLOWING:

  • Experience shipping features into a commercial data or AI platform, based on customer requirements.

  • Active contributions to open-source AI frameworks, technical publications, or industry speaking engagements.

  • Familiarity with Cortex AI, Snowpark, or modern enterprise data infrastructure platforms.

WHY JOIN FRONTIER ENGINEERING AT SNOWFLAKE?

Frontier Engineering is where Snowflake’s AI platform meets reality. You’re not building demos, you’re shipping AI applications that run in some of the world’s most complex enterprise environments. You will work on hard problems with real stakes, alongside engineers who are deeply technical and customer-obsessed.

How do you want to make your impact?

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

title: AI & Data Use-Case Project Manager
description:
Job Title: AI & Data Use-Case Project Manager

Job Category: Project and Program Management

Time Type: Full time

Minimum Clearance Required to Start:

Employee Type: Regular

Percentage of Travel Required: Up to 10%

Type of Travel: Local

* * *

The Opportunity:
CACI is seeking an experienced AI & Data Use-Case Project Manager to support the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of the Inspector General (OIG). This role offers a unique opportunity to decide where artificial intelligence earns its place in federal oversight work, by connecting the people who do audits, investigations, and inspections with the AI pilots that could make that work faster and better.
As the AI & Data Use-Case Project Manager, you will work with the Chief Data Officer's analysts, OIG program offices, and Government Product Owners to find the workflow problems AI can solve, shape the strongest ideas into pilot candidates, and carry each pilot through to a decision the Government can act on. Candidate pilots include AI analysis of investigative hotline data, AI-assisted investigative queries, an eDiscovery supplement for large collections of files, and translation and transcription. You will write the case for each candidate, secure approval for the test data it needs, prepare the selection and go/no-go packages, and report what each pilot was worth. AI engineers build the pilots and a Scrum Master runs the delivery cadence; your job is to make sure the team builds the right things and that leaders can see the return. The position is primarily remote, with on-site work at DHS OIG headquarters in Washington, DC as requested, during core hours of 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM Eastern. Join us to help an oversight agency adopt AI deliberately, with evidence behind every step.

Responsibilities:
• Lead use-case discovery with the Chief Data Officer's analysts and OIG program offices, including audit, investigations, inspections, and counsel, to identify workflow pain points where AI or analytics could help, and maintain a prioritized pipeline of candidate uses
• Write the case for each pilot candidate, covering the user problem, expected benefit, data needed and its sensitivity, feasibility input from the AI engineers, and success criteria a Government Product Owner can verify
• Prepare pilot selection packages for Government decision, and coordinate reviews with OCIO, the Chief Data Officer, OIG cybersecurity and privacy staff, and program office leadership
• Request and track approval of the test data each pilot needs through Government data owners and the COR, recording where approved data may be held, who may use it, and for how long, in line with rules for SPII, Law Enforcement Sensitive, and FOUO information
• Define pilot success criteria with Government Product Owners and AI engineers, and keep each pilot's scope tied to those criteria from selection through go/no-go
• Prepare go/no-go decision packages from validation results, user testing, and cost, with a clear recommendation to move a pilot to sustainment, rework it, or stop
• Measure and report the value of each pilot, including time saved, quality of results, cost, and adoption, in a form OIG leadership can use for enterprise investment decisions
• Capture lessons learned and feed them into the next wave of candidates and into data platform priorities, so the data sets onboarded first are the ones the highest-value questions depend on
• Coordinate with the Scrum Master, AI engineers, UX researchers, and technical writer so discovery, build, testing, and documentation move in step, and maintain pilot risks, issues, and decisions
• Explain AI capabilities and limits in plain language to non-technical leaders and staff, and provide inputs to biweekly status briefings and monthly progress reports


Qualifications:
Required –

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant field + 10 years of experience in program or project management, business or data analysis, or technology portfolio management; equivalencies considered (Master's + 7 years; 16 years with no degree; AA + 12 years)
  • U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a DHS Public Trust (High Risk) fitness determination
  • Demonstrated experience leading discovery and requirements work with mission or business users, and turning their needs into prioritized, decision-ready proposals
  • Experience managing pilots, proofs of concept, or a portfolio of analytics, AI, or data initiatives through selection, evaluation, and go/no-go decisions, including defining success criteria and measuring benefits
  • Working knowledge of data governance and sensitive data handling (PII, SPII, Law Enforcement Sensitive) and of responsible AI practices such as output validation, human review, and documented limitations
  • Strong written and oral communication, including briefing senior Government leaders and writing decision documents for non-technical readers

Desired –

  • Experience in inspector general, audit, investigative, law enforcement, or other oversight environments
  • Familiarity with Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, Databricks, or comparable enterprise AI and data platforms, and with generative AI uses such as document analysis, search, transcription, and translation
  • PMP, PMI-CPMAI, or product ownership certification (CSPO or PSPO), and experience with Jira, Azure DevOps, or comparable tools
  • Experience building benefit or adoption measures and presenting them in dashboards such as Power BI





-

What You Can Expect:

A culture of integrity.

At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation.

An environment of trust.

CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.

Our employees value the flexibility at CACI that allows them to balance quality work and their personal lives. We offer competitive compensation, benefits and learning and development opportunities. title: GP/Health Screener
description:

Town: Glasgow Central

Full time / Part Time: Minimum 4+ sessions per week Monday, Tuesday, Friday available

Permanent: Salaried​

Salary: £10,400 basic sessional rate with the option to earn an extra £800/£1200 per session


We're looking for a talented GP to join our team onsite at HCA UK Primary Care Glasgow. We are the UK's largest private patient GP employer and this current vacancy is due to another exciting period of expansion!


The majority of our patients come through to us from our corporate clients; corporate sector professionals who are prioritising their health and who value a comprehensive, personalised approach. If you have a passion for "prevention rather than cure" and lifestyle medicine, this could be the role for you!


As a General Practitioner / Health Screener at HCA UK Primary Care, you'll provide Comprehensive primary care for an adult population who actively invest in their health; engaging with patients, exploring their medical history, addressing concerns and performing examinations. You'll also arrange investigations, provide guidance, prescribe, discuss medical options, treatments, and deliver expert advice.


With our advanced health screenings, you will have time to have those important lifestyle and coaching conversations and use extended appointment times to explore patients’ goals, support behaviour change, and develop actionable health plans.


You will also be expected to perform procedures such as taking bloods, smear tests and ECG's.


At HCA UK, you’ll have the time to care, the tools to succeed, and the flexibility to enjoy life outside of work with structured pre-booked appointments in office hours. Our GP appointments are 15 minutes and our health screens range from 30 minute up to 2 hours depending on the type of screening being undertaken.


What you'll bring:


  • GMC registered
  • Strong communication and IT skills.
  • A proactive, patient-first approach with a genuine interest in preventative and lifestyle medicine coaching.
  • Training provided on 'Advanced' Health Screening.
