Why HCA UK?


Originally founded over 50 years ago by Dr Thomas Frist, HCA has gone on to become one of the world’s leading healthcare providers. In the UK, we’re one of the largest providers of privately funded healthcare and have invested over £500 million in the latest treatments, technology, techniques, medication and facilities. Being part of a large multisite, established healthcare group we can offer you unrivalled opportunities for career progression through internal and external courses, as well as working conditions that prioritise both your mental and physical wellbeing.


We believe that by caring for our employees, we empower them to provide exceptional care for our patients. That’s why we offer a host of flexible benefits that reflect the invaluable contribution they make every day. As a GP / Health Screener you’ll be eligible for:


  • 25 days holiday each year (plus bank holidays) increasing with service, with option to buy or sell leave to suit you
  • Private Healthcare Insurance for treatment at our leading hospitals
  • Private pension contribution which increases with length of service
  • Season Ticket Loan and Cycle to Work scheme
  • Group Life Assurance from day one
  • Critical illness cover
  • Enhanced Maternity and Paternity pay
  • Corporate staff discount for all facilities including Maternity packages at The Portland
  • Comprehensive range of flexible health, protection and lifestyle benefits to suit you
  • Discounts with over 800 major retailers

Culture and values


At HCA UK we believe exceptional care starts with our people. We celebrate the unique perspectives and different experiences each of us bring as we know that when you feel seen, heard and supported you can be at your best for our patients, and each other.


Our mission is simple, above all else we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life, a clear statement that extends to both our patients and colleagues. To achieve this, we live and breathe four core values:

  • Unique and Individual: We recognise and value everyone as unique and individual
  • Kindness and compassion: We treat people with kindness and compassion
  • Honesty, integrity and fairness: - We act with absolute honesty, integrity and fairness
  • Loyalty, respect and dignity: We trust and treat one another as valued members of the HCA UK family with loyalty, respect and dignity

title: DevOps Engineer
description:
Xynotech is an IT consulting and software development company that helps organizations gain a competitive edge through agile digital solutions and enhanced user experiences. The company works with clients across industries, with a strong focus on start-ups seeking innovative technology and flexible pricing models. Xynotech operates distributed teams based in Pakistan and the United Kingdom and emphasizes hiring highly skilled professionals. Through its Offshore Development Team model, Xynotech provides dedicated, long-term development resources that integrate closely with clients’ existing teams. This approach allows organizations to expand their software capabilities while maintaining a secure, focused, and efficient development environment.

Role Description:

The DevOps Engineer role at Xynotech is a full-time, on-site position based in Karāchi. The DevOps Engineer will design, implement, and maintain infrastructure and deployment pipelines that support agile software development across distributed teams. Day-to-day responsibilities include managing Linux-based systems, configuring and optimizing CI pipelines, monitoring system performance, and ensuring reliable application releases. The role also involves collaborating with software developers, QA engineers, and project managers to improve build, test, and deployment workflows, as well as implementing Infrastructure as Code practices for scalable and repeatable environments. title: Regional Council Executive Minister
description:
East Central Ontario, Eastern Ontario Outaouais, Nakonha:ka Regional Councils

The United Church of Canada is seeking an individual to fill the role of Regional Executive Minister for East Central Ontario, Eastern Ontario Outaouais and Nakonha:ka Regional Councils on a permanent full-time basis (35 hours/week). This position represents a current, active vacancy within our organization.

All applications received through The United Church of Canada’s Applicant Tracking System (ATS) for all publicly advertised positions, AI might be used to support certain applicant evaluations however, all applications are manually reviewed by our hiring team to ensure a fair and thorough evaluation of all candidates. All decisions are made solely by the hiring team.

Position Purpose

The Regional Council Executive Minister serves as the chief executive leader of the assigned Regional Council(s), operating with delegated authority from the General Secretary. The RCEM provides strategic, pastoral, fiduciary, and governance leadership, ensuring that Regional Councils fulfill their responsibilities as Denominational Councils under The Manual.

This role balances governance integrity, mission vitality, organizational leadership, and faithful accompaniment of Communities of Faith. The RCEM serves as both a denominational leader and regional pastor, fostering strong relationships among Communities of Faith, Regional Councils, and the General Council.

The successful candidate will provide visionary leadership while ensuring accountability, sound stewardship, and alignment with the mission and priorities of The United Church of Canada.

Primary areas of responsibility:

1. Executive Leadership and Governance

  • Provide grounded, collaborative, trust based and visionary leadership to Regional Councils and sustains the strategic direction and momentum of the three Regional Councils.
  • Ensure compliance with The Manual, denominational policies, and applicable legislation.
  • Support Regional Council governance processes, including agenda planning, decision-making, and policy development.
  • Oversee property and pastoral relations processes, ensuring timely approvals, documentation, and compliance.
  • Provide leadership in organizational change, restructuring, transitions, and conflict situations.
  • Communicate and interpret denominational priorities, strategic directions, and policies across the Region(s).
  • Ensure sound governance and fiduciary oversight of Regional Council operations and resources.

2. Financial Leadership and Stewardship

  • Oversee the financial health and sustainability of the Region(s).
  • Monitor budgets, financial performance, and resource allocation.
  • Ensure responsible stewardship of assessments, designated funds, grants, and special project funding.
  • Approve major expenditures and monitor financial risks.
  • Ensure compliance with charitable, regulatory, and denominational requirements.
  • Promote transparency, accountability, and strategic financial planning.

3. People Leadership

  • Provide people-centered leadership to the regional staff team by setting clear expectations, maintaining open communication, providing timely and constructive feedback, supporting professional development, and coaching staff to achieve individual and shared goals.
  • Oversee recruitment, hiring, onboarding, performance management, and professional development.
  • Foster a healthy, collaborative, inclusive, and mission-aligned workplace culture.
  • Address employee relations matters in partnership with Human Resources and senior church leadership.
  • Ensure staffing structures effectively support regional mission priorities.

4. Relationship Building and Ministry Development

  • Support Communities of Faith through all stages of ministry, including formation, growth, transformation, amalgamation, closure, and legacy planning.
  • Encourage innovation and the development of new ministry expressions.
  • Provide oversight and guidance to incorporated ministries within the Region(s).
  • Build and maintain relationships with ecumenical, interfaith, regulatory, and denominational partners.
  • Support governance, accountability, and denominational alignment across the Regional Council.

5. Denominational Leadership

  • Participate in national leadership forums and denominational initiatives.
  • Collaborate with General Council Office teams and Regional Council leaders across the church in animating the church wide 2035 initiative.
  • Interpret and communicate decisions of the Denominational Council to Communities of Faith and ministry personnel.
  • Represent The United Church of Canada in public, media, and community settings.
  • Respond thoughtfully to emerging societal issues affecting Communities of Faith.

*** To request a copy of the full job description, please send an e-mail to Careers@united-church.ca with Regional Executive Minister EOORC on the subject.

Qualifications

  • Graduate degree in Theology, Divinity, or a related field (Master of Divinity or equivalent) from an accredited institution.
  • Graduate-level education in Public Administration, Nonprofit Management, Business Administration, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of relevant education and work experience.
  • Training or certification in governance, board relations, or executive leadership is considered an asset.
  • Advanced verbal communication skills in both French and English is a requirement;
  • Intermediate written communication skills in French are considered an asset;
  • Training in conflict resolution, mediation, or change management is considered an asset.
  • Minimum 5 to 7 years of progressive leadership experience in ministry, senior management, or a comparable role.
  • Active member of The United Church of Canada engaged in the life and ministry of the church.
  • Strong knowledge and understanding of Quebec culture and the Nakonha:ka region and communities, with the ability to effectively lead within the regions.
  • Demonstrated experience in financial management, budget development, and financial oversight.
  • Experience leading teams, managing organizational change, and working within complex governance environments.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of the doctrine, polity, governance structures, and policies of The United Church of Canada.
  • Strong theological understanding and the ability to communicate effectively in worship, public settings, and media environments.
  • Excellent leadership, relationship-building, facilitation, and decision-making abilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate complex issues with sound judgment, discretion, and integrity.
  • Experience in conflict management, organizational development, and strategic planning.
  • Commitment to reconciliation, intercultural ministry, equity, diversity, inclusion, and bilingual engagement.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Dynamics, Zoom, and other digital collaboration tools.
  • A strong commitment to the vision, mission, and values of The United Church of Canada.
  • Integrity, authenticity, and a pastoral heart.
  • Strategic thinking combined with practical execution.
  • Adaptability and resilience in times of change.
  • Creativity, initiative, and sound judgment.
  • Respect for inclusion and diversity, with strong intercultural competency and the ability to collaborate effectively across diverse communities and perspectives;
  • Passion for ministry, discipleship, and faithful leadership.

Working Conditions

The United Church of Canada has adopted a hybrid workplace model, providing flexibility for this position, working both off-site and from the Regional Council Office. The incumbent will be provided, for work purposes, use of secure devices and must be available by email, phone, teams or zoom during regular office hours Monday to Friday. Sitting and viewing a computer screen for long periods, keyboarding/using assistive devices or software, intermittent physical activity including sitting, standing and being on the phone for long periods of time will be required. Occasional additional hours may be required and travel, with the approval of the supervisor, will be required at times.

Equity, Diversity, and Accessibility

The United Church of Canada is committed to creating an inclusive and accessible workplace. We welcome applications from individuals who reflect the diversity of our church and communities.

In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act and applicable human rights legislation, reasonable accommodations will be provided throughout the recruitment and employment process for candidates with disabilities or other human rights-related needs. If you are contacted regarding a job opportunity, please advise us of your accommodation needs at that time.

Compensation

The target hiring range for this position is $123,271 to $140,493. with the ability to progress to a maximum of $164,362. This is based on category 12 on our2027 salary scale. Placement on the salary range will be based on factors such as internal equity, candidate experience skills and qualifications relevant to the role. Pension and group benefit plans coverage and annual vacation round out this compensation package.

Closing Date for Applications: November 5, 2026

title: QA Team Leader
description:

  • Record mixing errors and any adjustments made to batches
  • Record all checks and tests and file for future reference
  • Critical control points are being monitored, verified and recorded

  • Audit raw materials for adherence to specifications.

OTHER DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Fill in for QA Supervisor.

title: Senior Systems Engineer
description:
Southern New Hampshire University is a team of innovators. World changers. Individuals who believe in progress with purpose. Since 1932, our people-centered strategy has defined us — and helped us grow a team that now serves over 180,000 learners worldwide.

Our mission to transform lives is made possible by talented people who bring diverse industry experience, backgrounds and skills to the university. And today, we're ready to expand our reach. All we need is you.

Make an impact — from near or far

At SNHU, you'll have the option to work remotely in the following states: Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, Wisconsin and Wyoming.

We ask that our remote employees have access to a reliable internet connection and a dedicated, properly equipped workspace that is free of distractions. Employees must reside in, and work from, one of the above approved states.

The opportunity

The Senior Systems Engineer will work closely with application teams, business stakeholders, vendors, and other IT teams to troubleshoot complex problems, implement solutions, improve system processes, and ensure reliable data exchange across the University's technology ecosystem. You will focus on Southern New Hampshire University's Student Information System (Ellucian Banner), working in collaboration with our CRM, Learning Management System, and other platforms to ensure the best experience for our students and business partners. The position requires strong technical problem-solving skills, the ability to understand complex interconnected systems, and the judgment to balance immediate production needs with longer-term technical improvements. You will report to the Senior Director of SIS Platform and Development. #LI-Remote


What you'll do:

  • Provide advanced production support for the Student Information System (SIS) and related enterprise applications, including troubleshooting complex application, database, integration, and data issues.
  • Serve as a technical subject matter expert for the SIS and the broader ecosystem of applications and services that support University operations.
  • Maintain, and troubleshoot integrations between the SIS and other institutional systems using APIs, web services, middleware, database interfaces, and other integration technologies.
  • Analyze complex technical issues across multiple systems and identify root causes.
  • Work closely with application developers, database administrators, infrastructure teams, functional teams, and business stakeholders to resolve issues and deliver technical solutions.
  • Monitor system performance, reliability, and data flows and proactively identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, system diagrams, support procedures, and operational standards.
  • Participate in system upgrades, enhancements, implementations, and other technology initiatives, including requirements analysis, technical design, testing, deployment, and post-production support.
  • Collaborate with software vendors and external partners to troubleshoot issues, evaluate solutions, and coordinate technical activities.
  • Participate in incident response, problem management, and change management activities for critical systems.
  • Identify opportunities to automate manual processes and improve operational efficiency.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to other members of the IT organization.
  • Contribute to architectural discussions and help establish sustainable, scalable, and supportable solutions across the University's technology ecosystem.
  • Maintain awareness of higher education technology trends, vendor roadmaps, and emerging technologies relevant to the University's systems and integrations.

What we're looking for:

  • 4+ years of experience supporting enterprise applications, systems, integrations, or related technology environments.
  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, or related field. Equivalent experience in lieu of degree acceptable
  • Demonstrated experience troubleshooting complex production systems and resolving issues across multiple technology layers.
  • Strong experience with relational databases and SQL.
  • Experience working with APIs, web services, data integrations, and enterprise application interfaces.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to understand complex systems and trace issues across applications, databases, integrations, and infrastructure.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently, prioritize competing demands, and take ownership of complex technical problems.

We believe real innovation comes from inclusion - where different experiences, perspectives and talents are celebrated. So if you're wondering whether SNHU is right for you, take the leap and apply. You might be just the person we're looking for.


If you have a disability and require a reasonable accommodation to fully engage in any part of the application or hiring process, please complete the Accommodation Request form or contact us at 603-626-9447. A member from the Employee Accommodation Support Center will be in contact with you within two business days to discuss your request.


Compensation


The annual pay range for this position is $96,954.00 - $155,153.00. Actual offer will be based on skills, qualifications, experience and internal equity, in addition to relevant business considerations. We expect this position to be hired in the following target hiring range $107,132.00 - $144,945.00.

Exceptional benefits (because you’re exceptional)

You’re the whole package. Your benefits should be, too. As a full-time employee at SNHU, you’ll get:

  • High-quality, low-deductible medical insurance

  • Low to no-cost dental and vision plans

  • 5 weeks of paid time off (plus almost a dozen paid holidays)

  • Employer-funded retirement

  • Free tuition program

  • Parental leave

  • Mental health and wellbeing resources

title: Data Scientist, Global Smaller Companies Equities
description:
As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco.

Job Description

We have an outstanding benefits package which includes:

  • Company-provided healthcare
  • A competitive annual leave allowance
  • Flexible working options, including hybrid working arrangements
  • Generous pension provisions
  • Income protection
  • Health and wellness benefits
  • Volunteering days
  • Enhanced parental leave
  • Life insurance

Your role:

Working closely with Portfolio Managers and Analysts, the successful candidate will build tools, engineer datasets and apply scripting and machine learning techniques to embed data-driven research across the team’s investment process.


Show Us What You've Built - Application requirement:

We believe the best evidence of technical ability is seeing what you've created. As part of your application, please share at least one project that you have personally designed and built. This could be a machine learning model, data pipeline, research platform, analytics application, automation workflow, web application or another technical product.


Please include:

  • The problem or opportunity you addressed
  • The technologies, frameworks and data sources used
  • The specific elements you personally designed and implemented
  • The outcome or impact achieved
  • A GitHub repository, live demo, portfolio, or supporting documentation where possible

Applications that do not include a project submission will not progress to review.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, build and maintain automated tools and workflows that support the team's investment research process, reducing manual effort and improving efficiency across sectors and geographies
  • Work alongside the fundamental analyst team to combine data science techniques with fundamental stock research on the watchlist and existing holdings
  • Engineer and manage large datasets from vendor and proprietary sources (e.g. FactSet, Bloomberg, Morningstar, Compustat, Worldscope, DataStream) to support screening, idea generation and portfolio construction
  • Proactively seek out and apply new scripting, AI and machine learning techniques to identify patterns, surface original insights and research small companies at scale
  • Support the maintenance and evolution of financial models, ensuring data feeds, calculations and outputs are robust, reproducible and scalable
  • Partner with technology, data and risk teams to translate research needs into practical, well-engineered solutions, including in cloud-based environments
  • Clearly communicate quantitative research, tools and methodologies to Portfolio Managers, Analysts, CPMs and other stakeholders in a way that is accessible to both technical and non-technical audiences

What you can bring:

  • Educated to degree level or equivalent in a subject such as Statistics, Financial Engineering, Mathematics or Computer/Data Science or similar. CFA or IMC would be advantageous
  • Python, R, SQL or other languages used to engineer large datasets
  • Experience applying scripting, automation and AI techniques to enhance research or workflows
  • Fundamental understanding of core machine learning concepts
  • No direct experience of equity markets is necessary, but a genuine knowledge of, and willingness to learn about investing and financial markets is valued

Before applying: Please ensure you have included a project example. This role assesses technical capability through work you have personally created.

Disability Confident Scheme

Applicants who opt in to the Disability Confident Scheme and meet the criteria for the role will be offered an interview. We are committed to providing an inclusive recruitment process for all candidates who make an application. By opting-in to this scheme, applicants will be disclosing that they have a disability solely for the purpose of the Disability Confident Scheme.


The Disability Confident Scheme only guarantees an interview – it does not automatically mean that applicants interviewed will gain employment with Invesco at that time.


To apply through the Disability Confident Scheme, you’ll need to firstly ensure you have applied for the role via our external careers page. Following this, you’ll need to email us at emea-talentacquisition@invesco.comconfirming your wish to opt-in, alongside your contact details and the title of the role you wish to apply for.

Full Time / Part Time

Full time

Worker Type

Employee

Job Exempt (Yes / No)

No

Workplace Model


Pursuant to Invesco’s Workplace Policy, employees are expected to comply with the firm’s most current workplace model, which as of October 1, 2025, includes spending at least four full days each week working in the role's advertised office. This reflects our belief that spending time together in the office helps us build stronger relationships, collaborate more easily, and support each other’s growth and development.

If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you! We want all of our candidates to shine during the application and selection process, so if you need any adjustments to be made, please send an e-mail to emea-talentacquisition@invesco.com. Please include your name, the job you are interested in, and the type of adjustment you need (for example; breaks during your interview, remote interviews, additional time for assessments or other required adjustments)

We promote a working environment that welcomes everyone and creates inclusive teams, celebrates difference and encourages everyone to be themselves at work.

Our commitment to the community and environmental, social and governance investing:
We partner with charitable organisations globally to make an impact in the communities where we live and work. Our people are encouraged to support the charities they feel most passionate about. We are also committed to environmental, social and governance (ESG) investing. We serve our clients in this space as a trusted partner both on specific responsible investment product strategies as well as part of our commitment to deliver a superior investment experience.

Recruitment Agencies:
Invesco has an in-house recruitment team, which focuses on sourcing great candidates directly. Invesco will not accept unsolicited resumes from agency or search firm recruiters. Fees will not be paid in the event a candidate submitted by a recruiter without an agreement in place is hired. When we do use agencies, we have a PSL in place, so please do not contact hiring managers directly.

Regulatory:
This position may fall in-scope of one or multiple regimes/directives.

title: Director of Health & Wellness (Senior Living)
description:
About Discovery Management Group

Discovery Management Group leads one of the nation’s most purpose-driven and people-centered senior living organizations, managing and enhancing senior living communities across the United States. With a focus on operational excellence, lifestyle personalization, and culture-driven leadership, we proudly serve residents and families with more than 15,000 units nationwide and growing.

As part of one of the largest senior living families in the U.S., our communities have earned Great Place to Work® certifications from 2022–2027. At Discovery Management Group, purpose guides our work, culture fuels our success, and growth defines our future. We continually aspire and invest in learning and development opportunities that support our team members’ professional growth, ensuring every team member has the tools to build a meaningful and rewarding career.

Discover Your Purpose with Us at St. Andrew's Village!

As Director of Health & Wellness, you’ll play an essential role in enriching the lives of seniors, creating meaningful connections, and making a difference every single day.

Your Role:

As the Director of Health & Wellness, your role includes overseeing the clinical and care services for our community. You’ll lead a team of licensed nurses, care managers, and support staff to ensure residents receive exceptional care and service in accordance with state, federal, and organizational standards. Through leadership, communication, and compassion, you will foster a culture of clinical excellence and resident-centered care.

Position Highlights:

  • Status: FULL TIME
  • Schedule: Monday through Friday 8am-5pm. Flexible leadership schedule with MOD coverage, on-call responsibilities, and operational flexibility required based on community needs, including occasional evenings, weekends, and emergency support as needed.
  • Location: 13801 East Yale Avenue, Aurora, CO 80014
  • Rate of Pay: $85k - $95k Annually + 10% Annual Bonus Performance
  • Travel: 10%-20%

What You’ll Do:

Clinical Leadership & Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local regulations, as well as company policies and ownership standards
  • Oversee assessments, service plans, and resident health documentation in accordance with state requirements
  • Monitor clinical outcomes, implement corrective action, and lead quality improvement initiatives
  • Partner with the Executive Director and department heads to align resident health and safety goals with community operations
  • Maintain open communication with residents and families regarding changes in care or health status

Resident Care & Services

  • Lead the clinical team in providing exceptional care, including wellness checks, medication management, and service plan updates
  • Ensure resident service plans are accurate and updated to reflect current health status
  • Partner with physicians, pharmacy consultants, and allied providers to ensure continuity of care
  • Support education and engagement of residents and families in the care process

Team Leadership & Development

  • Hire, train, schedule, and supervise nurses, care managers, and other clinical team members
  • Provide ongoing coaching, feedback, and professional development opportunities for staff
  • Foster teamwork, accountability, and a culture of compassion and service excellence
  • Ensure adequate staffing levels, competency training, and clinical supplies to meet resident needs

Qualifications & Requirements:

  • Registered Nurse (RN) or Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) license in good standing in the current state required
  • ALR Administrator Certification is required
  • Minimum of one (1) year of nursing leadership experience; senior living experience preferred
  • BLS Certification required
  • Strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate, develop, and manage a clinical team
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving abilities
  • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and electronic health record systems
  • Participation in on-call and Manager on Duty (MOD) coverage required

Why Join Us

Discovery Senior Living Earned Coveted Great Place to Work Certification for 2025-2027!

A large part of what makes Discovery different from other companies in this industry is our willingness to embrace change. At Discovery Senior Living, we are constantly challenging how we are doing things to ensure the lifestyle we are offering our residents is absolutely the greatest value proposition in the marketplace. It’s just as important to us that the environment and culture for our team members are constantly refreshed. In addition, embracing and even encouraging change brings a never-ending supply of new energy to our business and our culture. That energy translates to other far-reaching positive impacts on our residents as well as our team members.

Find out what makes working at Discovery unique in the world of senior living. Discover Your Purpose!

Our Culture & Values

So often, what brings people together is deeply rooted in who we are and what we stand for. And at Discovery Senior Living, we’re unified by certain, core values, which we call our “Pillars of Excellence.” They make up the fabric of our company, and include TEAMWORK, INTEGRITY, PERFORMANCE, ACCOUNTABILITY, COMPASSION, HARD WORK and CREATIVITY.

Individually, they are our virtues, and together, they make up a roadmap which helps us foster innovation and success.

Benefits You’ll Enjoy

For eligible employees, we offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes competitive pay, medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, paid time off and holidays, a 401(k) with employer match, paid training and career growth opportunities, wellness-related benefits, and additional support through our Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

Equal Opportunity Employer

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all team members. EOE D/V

A Note to Applicants

This job description outlines the general nature and level of responsibilities for this role and is not an exhaustive list of all duties. Qualified individuals with disabilities, as defined by the ADA, must be able to perform the essential job functions with or without reasonable accommodation, as determined on a case-by-case basis.

Agency Policy

We do not accept unsolicited resumes from staffing agencies. Please refrain from contacting hiring managers directly.

Employment Scam Warning

We only post jobs on our official careers site and accept applications through that platform. We do not conduct interviews via text or social media or ask for personal or banking information.

Regulatory Compliance & Background Screening

Discovery Senior Living complies with all applicable federal, state, and local employment laws and regulatory requirements governing hiring practices, background screening, and workforce eligibility. Employment may be contingent upon successful completion of state-mandated and/or federally required background screenings, which may include criminal history checks, fingerprint-based screening, Level 2 background screening, registry verification, and other screenings required for healthcare and senior living roles with direct or indirect resident access.

Certain positions may be subject to additional requirements under federal programs, including CMS, Medicare, and Medicaid regulations, as well as state-specific licensing or regulatory agencies. Screening requirements vary by role and jurisdiction, and candidates must meet all applicable standards as a condition of employment. These measures support regulatory compliance and help maintain a safe, secure environment for residents, families, and team members.

Employment in Florida is contingent upon completion of a Level 2 background screening in accordance with Florida AHCA requirements. Applicants will be required to complete fingerprinting and background screening through the AHCA Clearinghouse. For more information, please visit: .

title: Audit - Mid Market - Graduate - Manchester - September 2027
description:
Forvis Mazars is a leading global professional services network providing audit & assurance, tax, and advisory services. Forvis Mazars in the UK spans 14 offices across the nation and has over 3,400 professionals, with 190 partners. We have a clear purpose and a shared commitment to shape a better future.

See how businesses really work and make an impact from day one.
Audit is about more than numbers. It's about understanding organisations, building trust in financial information, and helping businesses, investors and communities make informed decisions. You'll work with a diverse range of clients, gain insight into different industries, and develop skills that will benefit you throughout your career.
At Forvis Mazars, you'll work towards a professional qualification, learn from experienced professionals, and gain hands-on experience using the latest technology and data-driven tools. With real responsibility, continuous learning, and exposure to a variety of businesses, Audit offers an exciting foundation for a successful career.
Ready to challenge yourself, accelerate your development, and discover how businesses really work? Start your career in Audit with Forvis Mazars and make a difference from day one.

About our team:
Join our Mid-Market Audit team, working with a diverse portfolio of privately owned businesses, from ambitious start-ups to large international groups. You'll gain exposure to a wide range of industries, helping businesses achieve their goals while developing valuable technical, commercial and client-facing skills.

Hear from our graduate trainee Max:
“I've really enjoyed the combination of on the job learning and studying. There is a great network of people from dedicated learning and development teams to my people manager and buddy to support with the transition from university'
#LI-DNP

To apply for our Graduate Programme, you’ll need:

  • GCSE Maths and English Language at Grade 4/C (or equivalent qualifications).
  • Achieved a minimum of 112 UCAS tariff points from your top three A Levels, BTECs, Scottish Highers/Advanced Highers, or other recognised Level 3 qualifications.
  • Achieved or predicted a 2:1 degree classification (or equivalent).


We know everyone’s circumstances are different. If exceptional circumstances have affected your academic results, we’ll consider the context you provide as part of your application.

Does this sound like you?

Enjoy working with numbers, analysing data and spotting trends.
Curious about business, financial performance and risk.
A clear communicator who builds strong relationships.
Interested in technology, data analytics and AI in audit.
Adaptable, motivated and eager to learn.
Ready to study towards a professional qualification alongside your role.


What you'll work on:
Support audit engagements by testing financial information and reviewing evidence to help ensure financial statements are accurate and compliant.
Analyse financial data to understand how businesses operate, identify risks and highlight key findings.
Use audit technology, AI-powered tools and data analytics to interpret large volumes of data, identify trends, enhance insights and improve audit quality.
Research accounting and auditing standards and help apply them to client situations in a practical way.
Work closely with clients and colleagues, gathering information, responding to queries and contributing to meetings and reports.
Collaborate with specialists across Audit, Tax and Advisory teams to gain a broader understanding of client challenges and solutions.
Take on increasing responsibility as you develop, building technical expertise, managing your workload and strengthening client relationships.

Your development and benefits:
You don't need prior audit experience before you join. We'll help you build your knowledge through professional study, hands-on client work and ongoing support from your team.

Develop your technical expertise through funded ACA study, structured training and dedicated study leave.
Build digital skills by learning how technology, data analytics and automation are transforming the audit profession.
Learn in a supportive environment with access to a buddy, mentor and experienced colleagues who will help you succeed.
Apply your learning to real client work, gaining practical experience from day one and seeing the impact of your contribution.
Benefit from a balanced approach to study and client work, with regular check-ins, coaching and guidance throughout your programme.

If you're curious, analytical and ready to keep learning, Audit offers the opportunity to develop sought-after skills, work with a diverse range of clients and build your confidence in a career that helps businesses grow, manage risk and maintain trust in financial reporting.

At Forvis Mazars diversity, equity and inclusion are central to our values. We value our people's unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experience, and know this diversity create better outcomes for our clients. We seek to attract, develop, and retain the best talent, inclusive of sex, ethnicity, disability, socio-economic background, sexual orientation, gender identity, nationality, and faith. We select candidates based on skills, knowledge, qualifications, and experience and aim to support all our team members to reach their potential. At Forvis Mazars, we promote an environment in which you can grow your skills, belong to a team that values your ideas, and make an impact that matters.

title: Digital Innovation Intern

title: 2027 Intern - Community Development
description:
Company

Federal Reserve Bank of DallasWe are dedicated to serving the public by promoting a strong financial system and a healthy economy for all. These efforts take a team of dedicated individuals doing many different jobs. Together we’re creating a workplace where talented people can thrive, and we welcome your unique background and perspective to help present the best possible solutions for our partners.

Location: #LI-Onsite. If you need assistance or a reasonable accommodation, please notify your Talent Acquisition Consultant.


ABOUT THE DALLAS FED:


At the Dallas Fed we serve the public by partnering with communities and businesses, promoting jobs and stable prices, and keeping your money safe and available. We welcome different perspectives, ideas, and experiences. As part of the nation’s central bank, we are committed to improving the economy and our communities. Are you ready to make a difference?

Learn more about the Dallas Fed: .

ABOUT THE INTERNSHIP PROGRAM:


The Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas Internship Program is a prestigious, cohort-based experience that attracts top talent from across the country for paid, full-time summer internships spanning majors and functional areas – from economic research and finance to Cash Services, IT, and beyond. While interns take on a specific functional role for the summer with meaningful work and opportunities to grow, the program offers much more than a single assignment. Dedicated staff mentors help launch your career, and curated cohort programming provides broad exposure to central banking, direct access to senior leaders and industry experts, and dedicated learning and development opportunities. As part of the Federal Reserve System, you'll also build a professional network of peers that spans the nation. The program runs approximately for 10-12 weeks, beginning in mid-to-late May and concluding in August. For this specific position, you will be located in the Dallas office.

Learn more about our internship program: .


ABOUT YOUR TEAM:


This intern will support the Community Development unit of the Dallas Fed’s Community Engagement and Development Department, the team that builds deep, strategic partnerships with community and business leaders to help shape our understanding of the economy. Community Development is responsible for programs and research focused on advancing economic outcomes for low- and moderate-income people and places in the Eleventh Federal Reserve District.


WHAT YOU’LL DO:


  • Support the implementation of targeted Community Development initiatives such as Advance Together, Digital Access, the Texas Impact Capital Alliance and Texas CDFI Coalition
  • Contribute to the planning and execution of outreach meetings and programs
  • Assist the Community Development research team on articles and outreach as needed

WHAT YOU BRING:

  • Undergraduate or graduate coursework focusing community development, public administration, urban planning/urban studies, economics, statistics, or related field
  • Strong communication, qualitative research, writing, and analytical skills
  • Experience or academic interest in community development, public policy or municipal research and practice is a plus

OUR BENEFITS:


  • Professional development opportunities
  • Broader networking opportunities across District
  • Downtown location with free parking
  • 24/7 on-site fitness center (Dallas & Houston Offices)
  • On-site café and coffee shop

WORK HOURS:


Monday – Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. (40 hours/ week). Some additional hours may be required.

NOTES:

Participation in our internship program is a valuable learning opportunity and does not guarantee future employment.

title: Youth Development Director
location: Liberty County/ Armed Services YMCA - Hinesville, GA 31313
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:

The Youth Development Director is responsible for the development, implementation and administration of high-quality After School Care, Child watch, Summer Day Camp, and sports and teen programs for the branch. In addition, responsibilities may include other youth development programs, family activities, special events and participation in the Community Impact Campaign for the association.

**Specific programs may vary slightly, depending upon availability, staffing, and programming at individual branch.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  1. Manages, directs and coordinates the school age childcare and day camp programs for assigned location(s). Also manages and builds teen programs and activities for locations with adolescent age participants. Ensures high quality programs and establishes new program activities. Expands programs within the community in accordance with strategic and operating plans.

  2. Recruits, hires, trains, develops, schedules and directs personnel and volunteers as needed. Reviews and evaluates staff performance. Develops strategies to motivate staff and achieve goals.

  3. Develops, manages and controls budgets related to the position. Ensures program operates within budget and that program fees are collected. Supports and budgets for healthy eating through coaching, mentoring, and monitoring menu quality.

  4. Assures compliance with state and local regulations as they relate to program areas. Ensures that YMCA program standards are met and safety procedures followed. Maintains proper documentation for Bright from the Start, the State of Georgia’s Licensing division (I.e. CACFP Food Program, Licensing, CAPS, daily attendance records, transportation and medication logs.

  5. Develops and implements sports programs for youth and adults including basketball, baseball, soccer, martial arts, and other related competitive team sports deemed beneficial to the community and YMCA participants.

  6. Plans, implements and supervises special activities for teens. Expands, directs, and supervises teen classes and programs that meet YMCA community objectives.

  7. Provides for upkeep of assigned program facilities and equipment and ensures the physical environment supports healthy living.

  8. Develops and maintains relationships with state childcare licensing agency, school administration, parent groups and other organizations and agencies related to assigned programs. Responds to all agency, parent and community inquiries and complaints in a timely manner.

  9. Provides staff leadership for annual fund-raising campaign and committees as assigned.

  10. Maintains proper records and department files. Reviews payments, receipts, late fees, immunization forms and registrations for all participants.

  11. Organizes special events for parents. Assists in YMCA fund raising activities.

  12. Assists with Program Committee meetings.

  13. Assists in the marketing and distribution of program information.

  14. Compiles program statistics. Monitors and evaluates the effectiveness of and participation in program.

  15. Preventing incidents of child abuse, identifying incidents of child abuse and reacting properly in the event they occur.

  16. Assist in the overall retention and satisfaction of YMCA members through appropriate customer service

  17. Assist in the annual Community Impact Campaign for the YMCA of Coastal Georgia

  18. Maintain a positive and cheerful attitude with staff, parents and children

  19. Performs all other duties as assigned.

This organization has zero tolerance for abuse and will not tolerate the mistreatment or abuse of consumers in its programs. Any mistreatment or abuse by an employee or volunteer will result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or volunteer service and cooperation with law enforcement. This organization takes every allegation of abuse or misconduct seriously and will fully cooperate with the authorities to investigate all cases of alleged abuse or misconduct. Employees and volunteers shall cooperate with any external investigation by outside authorities or internal investigation conducted by the organization or persons given investigative authority by the organization. An employee or volunteer’s failure to cooperate with an investigation will result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or dismissal from the organization.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:

The Youth Development Director is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of direct reports. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning assigning and directing work; appraising performance; reward and discipline employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Sufficient strength, agility and mobility to perform essential functions of position and to safely supervise children’s activities.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and smell. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move

up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIORNMENT
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to outside weather conditions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

title: Tax - Tax Transfer Pricing School Leaver Apprenticeship  - London - September 2027
description:
Forvis Mazars is a leading global professional services network providing audit & assurance, tax, and advisory services. Forvis Mazars in the UK spans 14 offices across the nation and has over 3,400 professionals, with 190 partners. We have a clear purpose and a shared commitment to shape a better future.

Kickstart your career by helping businesses understand, calculate and report their Tax responsibilities accurately. As a School Leaver Apprentice, you’ll learn how Tax connects to financial performance, regulation and business decisions, while working with a diverse range of clients, studying towards a fully funded professional qualification and building the confidence to make a real impact from day one.

About your Team
As businesses operate across an increasingly global economy, transfer pricing plays an important role in supporting international growth and compliance. Join our friendly and multicultural team to work with a wide range of clients, develop specialist expertise and build a rewarding career in an area that combines tax, economics and business strategy.

Hear from our trainee, Lauren: 'Joining Forvis Mazars as a school leaver has been such an amazing opportunity. I have expanded my network, boosted my confidence, and learnt so much in only a year! Everyone has been so supportive and helpful along my journey so far. I’m excited for my future progress and career at Forvis Mazars' #LI-DNI’

Does this sound like you?
• Do you enjoy learning new things, asking questions and understanding how businesses operate across different countries?
• Can you analyse information, think critically and use your judgement to find practical solutions?
• Are you interested in using new technologies, and data to work smarter and help deliver better outcomes for clients?
• Can you manage your time effectively, take responsibility for your work and follow through on your commitments?
• Do you enjoy building relationships, working as part of a team and learning from people with different perspectives and experiences?
• Are you resilient, open-minded and comfortable embracing new challenges in a fast-moving business environment?
• Are you motivated to continuously develop your skills, knowledge and professional confidence throughout your career?

To apply for our School Leaver Apprenticeship, you’ll need
• GCSE Maths and English Language at Grade 4/C (or equivalent qualifications).

• Achieved or predicted a minimum of 112 UCAS tariff points from your top three A Levels, BTECs, Scottish Highers/Advanced Highers, or other recognised Level 3 qualifications.


We know everyone’s circumstances are different. If exceptional circumstances have affected your academic results, we’ll consider the context you provide as part of your application.

What you'll work on
• No two days are the same. You'll work with businesses of all sizes, from entrepreneurial companies to global organisations, gaining exposure to international business, finance and tax.
• Supporting multinational businesses to understand the tax impact of their international operations.
• Attending client meetings and helping gather information about how businesses operate across different countries.
• Analysing financial and business data to help provide insights and recommendations to clients.
• Assisting with reports and documentation that help clients comply with UK and international tax regulations.
• Using the latest digital tools, technology and AI-powered solutions to help streamline processes, analyse information and deliver value to clients.
• Collaborating with colleagues across Tax, Audit and Advisory teams in the UK and around the world
• Developing project management skills by helping to coordinate client work and deliver projects on time.
• Building relationships with clients and colleagues while developing your commercial and professional skills.

Your development and benefits
You do not need to be a tax expert before you join. We’ll help you build your knowledge through professional study, practical client work and day-to-day support from your team.

Develop technical knowledge through funded ATT/CTA study, structured training and study leave.

Learn in a supportive team, with access to a buddy, mentor and colleagues who will help you settle in. Put your learning into practice through real client work and see how your contribution supports clear and valuable outcomes. You will benefit from balanced study and client work with structured support, regular check-ins and practical guidance.

Build digital confidence by learning how tax technology, data and automation support modern client work.

Want to understand how global businesses work? Transfer Pricing gives you the opportunity to work with internationally recognised organisations, solve real business challenges, and build valuable skills in business, data, technology and communication from day one. You'll gain professional qualifications, work alongside experts and use innovative technologies to help clients navigate an increasingly connected world.

At Forvis Mazars diversity, equity and inclusion are central to our values. We value our people's unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experience, and know this diversity create better outcomes for our clients. We seek to attract, develop, and retain the best talent, inclusive of sex, ethnicity, disability, socio-economic background, sexual orientation, gender identity, nationality, and faith. We select candidates based on skills, knowledge, qualifications, and experience and aim to support all our team members to reach their potential. At Forvis Mazars, we promote an environment in which you can grow your skills, belong to a team that values your ideas, and make an impact that matters.

title: Product Manager Wealth Management
description:
About Our Company


We’re a diversified financial services leader with more than $1.5 trillion in assets under management, administration and advisement as of year-end 2024. Our team of 22,000 people across 19 countries, serves more than 3.5 million individual, small business and institutional clients. We are a longstanding leader in financial planning and advice, a global asset manager and an insurer. Our unwavering focus on our clients and strong financial foundation connects each of our unique businesses – Ameriprise Financial, Columbia Threadneedle Investments and RiverSource Insurance and Annuities. Here, we foster meaningful careers, invest in the future, and make a difference for clients, institutions and communities around the world.

Job Description

The Product Manager role, within the Wealth Management Solutions – Product and Platform Solutions Development team, will primarily serve as a subject matter expert supporting the development of the end-to-end advisor and client experience across the advisory platform. This role will also ensure the maintenance of a healthy compliance environment by completing regular reviews of policies, procedures, and reports.

Key Responsibilities

  • Act as a business lead/subject matter expert on medium to large projects; responsible for providing direction from products perspective and working across the organization to drive projects forward.
  • Ensure the maintenance of a healthy compliance environment by completing regular reviews of policies, procedures, and reports and identifying change; lead resolution of complex and non-routine advisor/client issues with internal/external partners.
  • Provide research and analysis (quantitative and qualitative) from multiples sources and make recommendations to support business needs (e.g., product adds, platform changes, etc.).
  • Protect and increase the revenue earned across the advisory platform by developing and enhancing new programs and features that support firm ROA.
  • Lead investment product efforts that support increases in advisor acquisition, broadens advisor usage and grows clients.
  • Tracks industry trends for continual advancement and competitiveness.
  • Lead successful transitions of product development to successful product management processes and procedures.



Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience
  • 5+ years financial services experience
  • Excellent strategic and analytical skills to solve complex problems and identify new product solutions
  • Knowledge and experience working with Ameriprise product suite
  • Strong understanding of compliance and regulatory environment
  • Proven organizational skills, including managing multiple tasks simultaneously
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Attention to detail, accuracy, and high level of personal accountability
  • Active Series 7 or the ability to obtain within 120 days



Preferred Qualifications

  • Project Management experience

We are a client-centric, relationship-based business. Working together, in-person, is foundational to how we achieve results. By fostering a culture of face-to-face collaboration, idea sharing, productivity and personal connection, we deliver for our stakeholders — clients, advisors, employees and shareholders. Our employees work in the office at least four (4) days per week, with flexibility to work from home one (1) day per week. Some roles may require additional in-office time or different in-office expectations, and specific requirements will be discussed during the hiring process.


Base Pay Salary

The estimated base salary for this role is $81,700 - $112,300 / year. We have a pay-for-performance compensation philosophy. Your initial total compensation may vary based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and geographical work location. title: Head of Fixed Income Trading
description:
CMC Markets is seeking an experienced and commercially driven Head of Fixed Income Trading to establish, build and lead a new Fixed Income trading business.


This is a senior leadership role with end-to-end responsibility for developing the Fixed Income franchise, including strategy, trading, technology, team build-out, risk management and commercial development.


The successful candidate will define the proposition and lead its implementation, working closely with Treasury, Risk, Operations, Technology and Account Executives to create a scalable and commercially successful Fixed Income business.


This is a unique opportunity to build a new Fixed Income business within CMC Markets and to have significant influence over its strategy, structure and development.


The Head of Fixed Income Trading will have the mandate to build the franchise from the ground up and establish a scalable platform capable of delivering sustainable growth and long-term commercial value.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Define and execute the strategy for CMC Markets' Fixed Income trading business, including product scope, market coverage, liquidity model and client proposition.
  • Lead the build-out of the trading desk, with responsibility for trading, pricing, execution, liquidity and inventory management.
  • Establish an appropriate risk management framework in partnership with Risk and Treasury, ensuring market, liquidity and counterparty risks are effectively managed.
  • Define the technology and infrastructure requirements for the business, working with Technology and Operations to implement scalable front-to-back trading capabilities.
  • Recruit, develop and lead the Fixed Income team as the business grows.
  • Develop and manage relationships with liquidity providers, counterparties, execution venues and other key market participants.
  • Partner with Account Executives and commercial teams to develop the client franchise, support key client relationships and drive trading volumes and revenue.
  • Work closely with Treasury on funding, liquidity and balance-sheet requirements and with Operations on robust trade and settlement processes.
  • Partner with Compliance, Legal and Risk to ensure the business operates within appropriate regulatory and governance frameworks.
  • Take ownership of the commercial performance of the Fixed Income franchise and identify opportunities for its continued development and expansion.

KEY SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • The successful candidate will be an established Fixed Income trading professional with significant experience in institutional markets and the credibility to build and lead a new business at Executive Director level.
  • You will bring deep knowledge of Fixed Income markets, pricing, liquidity, execution and risk management, together with a strong understanding of the technology and infrastructure required to support a modern trading operation.
  • The individual should have a demonstrable commercial track record, strong relationships across the Fixed Income market and experience working with institutional or professional clients. Previous experience building or materially expanding a trading desk or business would be highly advantageous.
  • The role requires an entrepreneurial, hands-on and commercially focused leader who can combine strategic thinking with practical execution. The successful candidate will be comfortable operating across trading, technology, risk, operations and client development and will have the leadership skills required to build a high-performing team and a sustainable Fixed Income franchise

CMC Markets is an equal opportunities employer and positively encourages applications from suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of gender, sexual orientation, marital or civil partner status, gender reassignment, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief, disability or age

title: Director, Advanced Analytics & Modeling
description:
Job Description Summary

The Director, AMM, is accountable for the Advanced Analytics & Modeling strategy, organization and portfolio, including strategic directions, capability evolution, capacity allocation, cross-capability orchestration, analytical quality, US delivery, and decision impact.

The role holds established capability leaders accountable for differentiated roadmaps and outcomes and directly incubates AI & Unstructured Intelligence until sustained demand, maturity, and scale support a different LT model.

This role DOES NOT own the broader enterprise analytics strategy, enterprise analytics governance, technology architecture, analytics platforms, production engineering, or technical lifecycle management.

The Director aligns the Advanced Analytics & Modeling Strategy with broader I&A priorities and partners with Analytics Strategy & Governance, and SPT leaders through explicit decision rights and connected portfolio governance.


Job Description

Director, Advanced Analytics & Modeling

Location – Hyderabad #LI Hybrid

Major Accountabilities:

Advanced Analytics & Modeling Strategy & Capability Evolution

  • Define and continuously evolve the Advanced Analytics & Modeling (AAM) strategy, portfolio roadmap, capability maturity agenda, and investment priorities, ensuring alignment with portfolio priorities, launches, evolving customer and patient needs, and the broader I&A capability direction.
  • Establish and manage priorities across Precision Health, Key Drivers & Action Planning Analytics, Integrated Promotion Mix Modeling & Resource Optimization, and AI & Unstructured Intelligence, ensuring focus on the highest-value opportunities.
  • Guide decisions on where advanced analytics capabilities should be built, incubated, partnered, scaled, automated, or retired based on business value, differentiation, feasibility, reuse potential, and maturity.

Portfolio Prioritization, Capacity & Delivery

  • Establish transparent intake, prioritization, service levels, and portfolio governance across launch, brand, therapeutic-area, functional, and enterprise demand, ensuring Hyderabad capacity is allocated to the highest-value work with explicit trade-offs when demand exceeds capacity.
  • Balance near-term decision support with sustained capability development, reusable methods, and cross-portfolio learning, while assigning one accountable analytical leader for cross-capability engagements to ensure integrated workplans, contributions, recommendations, and outcome measures.

Capability Portfolio Leadership & Analytical Excellence

  • Establish shared expectations for analytical rigor, fit-for-purpose methods, validation, interpretability, reproducibility, documentation, peer challenge, privacy, compliance, and responsible AI across advanced analytics and modelling work.
  • Resolve priorities, dependencies, quality issues, and capability seams spanning predictive analytics, patient opportunity modeling, key drivers, causal measurement, IPMM, optimization, and emerging AI methods, while promoting reuse and consistency and preserving capability-specific technical standards with appropriate adaptation to business context.

Emerging Capability: AI & Unstructured Intelligence

  • Establish the Advanced Analytics strategy, roadmap, use-case priorities, capability boundaries, and investment thesis for AI & Unstructured Intelligence, with a focus on high-value applications such as call-note and text analytics, NLP, GenAI, unstructured signal detection, evidence synthesis, summarization, and knowledge acceleration.
  • Deploy AAM HYD expertise to test, learn, and build reusable analytical approaches while ensuring human oversight, interpretability, and responsible use.

Business Partnership & Decision Impact

  • Translate strategic priorities into clear business questions and analytical agendas, challenging low-value, duplicative, or poorly framed demand.
  • Convert analytical findings into implications, choices, recommendations, learning agendas, and measurable actions, advancing decision support through appropriate predictive, diagnostic, causal, experimental, optimization, and AI-enabled methods.

Integrated Partnership with SPT

  • Serve as the Advanced Analytics & Modeling (AAM) point of contact in AIDE/HYD to the SPT organization for initiatives requiring governed data, technical environments, reusable capabilities, productization, deployment support, ModelOps, or enterprise scale.
  • Ensure AAM owns its strategy, portfolio, use-case framing, analytical requirements, fit-for-purpose methodology, ad hoc model development, validation, interpretation, recommendations, acceptance, and impact measurement, while partnering with the I&A EH leader and SPT to determine which use cases remain I&A-owned analytics versus those transitioning to SPT-owned products, recurring models, engines, or workflows.
  • Enable portfolio-level ownership of feasibility, reuse, capacity, investment, dependencies, and lifecycle issues within the AAM remit, escalating broader enterprise issues through appropriate governance.

Global US-Hyderabad Operating Model

  • Establish HYD as an integrated capability and delivery partner, engaged early in portfolio planning, business context, analytical design, execution, quality review, synthesis, and capability development.
  • Partner with Hyderabad leadership to align capability roadmaps, capacity, expertise, decision rights, work ownership, quality expectations, documentation, and talent priorities, matching ownership to capability maturity, technical expertise, proximity needs, and business value rather than location-based handoffs.
  • Build HYD capability to independently lead repeatable and increasingly complex analytical work while maintaining shared accountability for quality, interpretation, and decision impact.

Minimum Requirements

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Economics, Econometrics, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Operations Research, Engineering, Computer Science, Life Sciences, Public Health, Business Analytics, or a related field required or Master's degree or doctorate in a relevant quantitative discipline preferred.
  • 12+ years of leadership experience in advanced analytics, data science, decision science, commercial analytics, healthcare analytics, or a related quantitative field.
  • Proven success defining and executing an Advanced Analytics strategy and capability roadmap across analytical domains.
  • Experience leading senior capability owners, flexible expert teams, complex portfolios, and globally distributed analytics organizations.
  • Demonstrated experience applying advanced analytics to consequential commercial, patient, healthcare, launch, or enterprise decisions.
  • Experience establishing portfolio prioritization, capacity allocation, quality governance, and reusable capability models.
  • Strong track record partnering with senior business and technology leaders and translating complex analytics into strategic choices and measurable action.
  • Experience leading operating-model transformation, capability centralization or federation, and organizational change.

Leadership skills

  • Lead and deploy HYD Associate Directors and high-performing teams across capability priorities, launches, therapeutic areas, and cross-portfolio initiatives, ensuring effective alignment of expertise to business needs.
  • Build strong talent and leadership depth by managing hiring, onboarding, objectives, coaching, performance, succession, career development, engagement, retention, rotations, communities of practice, and T-shaped skill development.
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, constructive challenge, innovation, inclusion, continuous improvement, and accountability, while supporting I&A and AIDE leadership on talent priorities, capability planning, organizational operations, and site-level initiatives.

Success Measurements

  • Priority launch, brand, functional, and portfolio decisions are improved through timely, rigorous, and actionable Advanced Analytics, with Precision Health, Key Drivers, IPMM, and AI & Unstructured Intelligence delivering against clear roadmaps, quality standards, ownership boundaries, validated value, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Portfolio priorities, capacity, and trade-offs are transparent, reducing low-value or duplicative work while reusable methods, assets, and quality practices improve consistency, speed, scalability, and cross-therapeutic-area learning.
  • HYD, AAM, and SPT operate with clear ownership, effective deployment, timely lifecycle decisions, strong handoffs, growing capability, sustainable utilization, and shared value realization, reinforcing senior stakeholder confidence in analytical rigor, recommendations, role clarity, and decision impact.

Required Skills

  • Leadership in Advanced Analytics & Modeling strategy, capability portfolio management, roadmap development, and investment prioritization.
  • Broad fluency across predictive modelling, patient analytics, driver analytics, causal inference, experimentation, IPMM, ROI, response curves, optimization, NLP, GenAI, and unstructured analytics, with strong judgment on method fit, evidence quality, validation, interpretability, uncertainty, model risk, and responsible AI.
  • Strong executive decision framing, business translation, stakeholder influence, conflict resolution, and portfolio trade-off management, with clear understanding of analytical versus technical ownership across analytics, modelling, products, platforms, and lifecycle management.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, life sciences, healthcare, or another complex regulated industry, with exposure to product lifecycle, launches, customer and patient analytics, promotional investment, and healthcare delivery.
  • Experience incubating emerging AI or unstructured-data capabilities, validating use cases before scale, and establishing integrated operating models with global capability centers and AI, data, product, or platform organizations.
  • Strong healthcare and pharmaceutical commercial acumen across customer, patient, access, field, and investment decisions.
  • Expertise in AI-enabled analytics, NLP, GenAI, unstructured-data methods, experimentation, simulation, and optimization, with familiarity in product management, agile delivery, analytical productization, ModelOps, and business-to-technology translation.
  • Strong executive storytelling, strategic facilitation, organizational design, and transformation leadership skills.

Location: Hyderabad NKC | Hybrid | 3 days a week in office is mandatory.

Direct Reports: 5 - 10 Direct Reportees

Team size: Team of 30+ Associates


Skills Desired

Artificial Intelligence (AI), Business Value Creation, Change Management, Curious Mindset, Data Governance, Data Literacy, Data Quality, Data Science, Data Visualization, Deep Learning, Learning Agility, Machine Learning (ML), Machine Learning Algorithms, Mentorship, Stakeholder Engagement, Statistical Analysis, Time Series Analysis
