title: Director/Team Lead, Oncology Field Access & Reimbursement - East Region
description:
ROLE SUMMARY

Pfizer Commercial Oncology is introducing the world to the next era of cancer care. With a growing portfolio of novel therapies, industry-leading R&D, and a goal of delivering eight breakthroughs by 2030 across major cancer types, we're translating cutting-edge science into market-shaping impact. Here, you'll partner with exceptional colleagues across scientific, medical, and manufacturing teams, backed by advanced digital and AI-enabled infrastructure and the authority to accelerate medicines from discovery to delivery. Guided by our values of courage, excellence, equity, and joy, you'll have the opportunity to stretch your skills and build a career that evolves with you—across teams, roles, and the Pfizer enterprise. Join us to make history — for patients, for their families, for the future.


The Director/Team Lead, Oncology Field Access & Reimbursement – East Region is responsible for leading and coaching the Oncology Field Reimbursement Directors (FRDs) within the East region, with a key focus on executing a patient first approach to impact the patient access journey across the region. This individual will report directly to the Senior Director, National Oncology Field Access and Reimbursement Lead, and will be responsible for all Oncology products including oral oncolytics, IV and injectables, and copromotes. This individual will ensure regional alignment with the strategic vision of Pfizer Oncology's overarching access and reimbursement strategies and within the parameters of the organization's compliance expectations/guidelines. This role will also help lead the team’s transformation to a proactive, data-led engagement model to identify accounts’ educational needs.


ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES

Performance

  • Lead the regional execution of field Access & Reimbursement strategies and tactics and provide insights to Pfizer leadership across Oncology, Pfizer Patient Services, Chief Marketing Office, and other cross-functional partners
  • Review selected KPI metrics along with market and access trends to assess regional performance and provide necessary FRD coaching to adjust tactics, execution and/or strategy
  • Design and implement regional adoption of signal-based case prioritization, and support the region's transition towards measurement via compliant KPIs
  • Collaborate with FRDs and other leaders to appropriately manage budget and assign allocations and resources
  • Prioritize Oncology state societies and manage membership to ensure connectivity to reimbursement professionals
  • Manage FRDs' engagement in cross-functional account teams, at Medicare Administrative Carriers and with accounts

Leadership

  • Collaborate with the Oncology Field Access and Reimbursement Leadership team to develop strategy, align on change management approaches, and guide implementation. Share successes, best practices and experiences
  • Lead and set clear accountability with FRDs for execution of regional strategies and goals
  • Provide leadership, coaching, and development of FRD capabilities and the management of operational standards, evaluation of performance and ensuring compliance
  • Champion Pfizer’s Values and ensure behaviors are modeled by all colleagues within region

People and Culture

  • Optimize Regional Field Access & Reimbursement support through deployment, alignment, and vacancy management
  • Coach FRDs and provide colleague development, manage recruiting and hiring, talent and performance management
  • Lead and be accountable for the Region's PX-related processes to include, but not limited to: consistency in interviewing and hiring practices, Annual Goal Setting and Year-End Process (e.g. Team Performance and Year End Reviews), Annual Compensation Process (i.e. Merit, and LTI)
  • Lead and ensure a compliant culture within the region regarding all Pfizer policies, procedures and relevant regulations

Market/Customer/Cross-Functional Team

  • Actively partner with cross- functional team, as needed and in compliance with Pfizer policies, to optimize appropriate patient support

description:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That’s the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Job Category

Underwriting

Compensation Overview

The hourly salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual hourly rate for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$25.00 - $26.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Are you curious by nature? Do you enjoy managing relationships and employing your critical thinking skills? Underwriters perform a critical function of evaluating the acceptability of risk and determining appropriate pricing of insurance products. The Underwriting Apprenticeship Program provides students with the amazing opportunity to gain exposure to this critical function at Travelers.

The semester long program provides qualified students with an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand insurance underwriting experience, receive valuable on-the-job training and learn more about the property & casualty insurance industry from industry professionals.

It is a potential pathway to our 12 month Underwriting Professional Development Program. The intent of this position is to provide students the ability to apply to our 2024 Underwriting Apprenticeship opportunities which start in January. Applications outside of this audience will not be considered at this time. However, for summer internship opportunities, we encourage anyone to apply to our current 2024 Underwriting Professional Development Program Internship roles in various locations.

What Will You Do?

  • Within your assigned business unit, each apprentice will be given a designated coach and be expected to:
  • Complete core assignments and training modules geared toward insurance and underwriting principles.
  • Participate and complete self-paced professional development courses in time management, presentation skills and other key areas.
  • Complete challenging and meaningful project work over the course of this program at the discretion of your manager. You may work independently or with other interns and will be asked to present your findings to local leadership. Sample projects include a territorial risk assessment to determine profitability and underwriting opportunities as well as a business process analysis to determine underwriting gaps.
  • Learn about other areas at Travelers such as Risk Control, Claims, and related Corporate functions. Interns may also engage in Agency visits with Account Executives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Because the Underwriting Apprenticeship Program is itself complex and dynamic, we welcome applicants that have a variety of majors, backgrounds, and experiences. We are most interested in students who are serious about entering the insurance industry and who are excited about the prospect of making underwriting their future career choice.
  • Preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above.

description:

Job Category

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Description


Salesforce is hiring Senior Forward Deployed Engineers — the Technical Builders, responsible for deciding that leads who design, build, and deploy the most complex agentic AI solutions directly inside enterprise customer environments. You'll lead technical delivery on your team, mentor the next wave of engineers, and set the engineering standards that define how agentic AI gets deployed at scale. Partnering closely with a Deployment Strategist (Strategic Builder - a customer-facing advisor who shapes AI strategy and drives adoption), you'll own outcomes end-to-end, from architecture decision to production. Your passion for well-crafted software that solves real problems will be supported by best-in-class AI tools and a team of talented builders around you.


The Senior Builder Experience

  • Technical Ownership: Partner with a Deployment Strategist to own customer outcomes end-to-end. You're the senior technical authority in the room, ensuring deliverables meet the highest engineering standards, whether it was generated by an AI tool by a colleague or written by you directly.
  • AI-Supported Engineering: Cursor, Claude, and Salesforce coding products like Vibes are embedded in your daily workflow. The conventions and patterns you develop tend to propagate through the team because other Builders look to your work as reference.
  • Roadmap Influence: Your field experience routes directly to Product and Engineering. The gaps you hit and the edge cases you encounter in real life customer environments become the features they ship. Senior Forward Deployed Engineers are the most credible voice in agentic AIproduct evolution.
  • Continuous Innovation: You're expected to stay at the forefront — piloting emerging AI tools, experimenting with new models and frameworks, and sharing what you learn with your team and customers.

What You'll Actually Be Building

  • Own end-to-end build and deployment of agentic AI solutions for Salesforce's most strategic customers — from architecture decisions through production handoff.
  • Design and ship agentic systems on the Agentforce platform: agent logic, tool calls, multi-agent orchestration, deterministic guardrails, and the integration patterns that hold up in enterprise environments. Your reference implementations become the basis for how other Builders approach similar problems.
  • Own the data lifecycle: model design, processing pipelines, and data readiness for AI applications across Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake, Databricks, and customer-specific platforms.
  • Resolve the technical blockers that other engineers can't — data integration failures, model deployment issues, orchestration breakdowns, performance regressions. These problems are routed to you because of your track record of solving them.
  • Build and maintain agent performance dashboards and customer KPI reporting to track deployment health and business outcomes across engagements.
  • Develop proofs-of-concept and MVPs quickly, with the judgment to know which decisions can be deferred and which need to be right the first time.
  • Codify what you learn. The patterns, reusable assets, and internal frameworks that come out of your real customer work become the playbooks the rest of the org draws from.
  • Mentor other Engineers through code reviews, pair sessions, and shared work. Most of your influence on developing engineers happens inside the same codebases you're building in.
  • Provide technical depth on at-risk or strategically critical deployments when senior engineering judgment is needed.
  • Surface field insights directly to Product and Engineering. The gaps and edge cases you encounter in real customer environments are some of the most valuable inputs to the Agentforce roadmap.
  • Partner with the Deployment Strategist on your team to translate complex customer business challenges into agentic solutions that actually ship.

You're Our Senior Forward Deployed Engineer If…

  • You have 6+ years of software engineering or technical delivery experience, with proven end-to-end ownership of scalable production systems in enterprise AI, cloud, or SaaS environments.
  • You have a degree in Computer Science or a related field
  • You're an expert in at least one of Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or Apex, and conversant in the others.
  • You've integrated LLMs into production, used frameworks like LangChain or LlamaIndex, and applied prompt engineering and responsible AI practices in real customer contexts.
  • You have deep experience in data modeling, processing, and analytics, with demonstrable proficiency across platforms like Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake, or Databricks.
  • You bring deep Salesforce platform expertise: Agentforce, Apex, LWC, Flows, and Salesforce APIs.
  • You have an entrepreneurial, get-things-done mindset focused on fast, impactful delivery — and the judgment to know when "fast" is the wrong call.
  • You've mentored technical talent and created reusable assets — frameworks, playbooks, internal tooling.
  • You communicate clearly and credibly with engineering peers, customer architects, and executive stakeholders.
  • You actively tinker with the evolving AI/data landscape — piloting new tools, experimenting with new models, and staying genuinely curious about what's coming next.
  • You're excited to travel ~25% of the time, embedded with customer engineers.
  • You have a Bachelor's in Computer Science or related field.
  • You are fluent in Spanish and English

About the Role
The Life Sciences Program Executive (PE) is a senior, executive-facing individual contributor (IC) within the Global Life Sciences Acceleration Hub at Salesforce. As an IC, Program Executives hold no direct reports, and yet expertly lead large numbers of our most senior talent across our most complex Life Sciences customer engagements: multi-workstream transformations, strategic accounts, and enterprise implementations where the margin for error is narrow and the consequences of failure are visible at the C-suite.
The PE is fully allocated to a single flagship Life Sciences transformation program or a set of strategic accounts. They own the end-to-end program P&L, lead the Salesforce project team, run the steering committee, manage the executive customer relationship, manage scope, govern the budget, and surface risk before it becomes an escalation. The ideal candidate brings a deep background in Life Sciences (pharma, biotech, medtech, or related sectors) combined with IT or management consulting delivery experience, leveraging that industry credibility as a strategic advisor to customers, partners, and internal teams across Salesforce.
Life Sciences Program Executives sit at the helm of AI and Agentforce transformations that accelerate drug commercialization, streamline field engagement, and modernize clinical and commercial operations through intelligent, autonomous agents. They lead cross-functional teams deploying digital workforces that bridge the gap between complex Life Sciences data and actionable business outcomes, driving the next frontier of Life Sciences innovation.
Their success is defined by what they deliver, what they prevent, and the customer confidence they command.

Your Impact
* AI and agentic delivery are embedded in how you work: you actively leverage AI tooling and agentic workflows to optimize how your program teams deliver. You reduce manual overhead, accelerate insight, and model the productivity gains Life Sciences customers are investing in Salesforce to achieve.
* Engagement success is well-defined and honored: you create the program strategy, management approach, governance, and guide the customer at the executive and program level to align on objectives, outcomes, and KPIs.
* Customer outcomes are owned with clear accountability: you are the executive-facing delivery contact for your engagement and are responsible for communications with the client and within Salesforce up to the CxO level regarding expectations, performance, governance, and issue escalation and resolution. You earn trust through consistently accurate forecasting, honest risk communication, and follow-through.
* The delivery team performs at a higher level because you're in it: you effectively lead, inspire, and uplift Salesforce Professional Services team members, coaching them to perform at a higher level while contributing to the internal processes, artifacts, and methodologies that raise the floor for service delivery across our most strategic Life Sciences accounts. What you learn and implement travels.

* Value delivered translates into real adoption and consumption: you drive the transformational changes, especially around AI and agentic capabilities, needed to achieve customers' objectives, informed by deep Life Sciences industry and product expertise. You align IT strategy, governance, processes, and stakeholder decisions to ensure adoption and consumption directly deliver measurable customer impact.
* Risk is managed before it manages you: you anticipate, mitigate, and manage risk to Salesforce and the customer, taking decisive program action to address risk profiles. You raise signals with a recommended path, not just a problem statement. Surfacing a risk is success; being surprised by one is not.
* White space becomes pipeline and internal alignment sustains it: you proactively build and expand business relationships which enable Salesforce to support, transform and win business that delivers mutual value, working hand in hand with Sales, Success, Technology and Product, and Support to drive customer adoption initiatives and maintain alignment as One Salesforce.

* 12+ years of professional services or consulting delivery experience, with direct accountability for program execution across financials, risk, scope, and customer outcomes
* Demonstrated track record leading large, complex programs ($10M+) with measurable outcomes
* 5+ years of direct Life Sciences industry experience (pharma, biotech, medtech, or related sectors) sufficient to engage credibly at the executive level on commercial, regulatory, and operational priorities
* 5+ years leading large, cross-functional delivery teams across multiple geographies and workstreams, including third-party system integrators, without positional authority

* Proven ability to lead steering committee and executive-level customer relationships, including difficult data-driven conversations around budget, resources, timelines, and outcomes
* Outstanding executive presence and communication skills, verbal and written, with the ability to tailor messaging across technical, commercial, and regulatory audiences
* Must be able to operate as a fully billable IC

* Deep knowledge of Life Sciences commercial operations: field engagement, HCP engagement, territory management, sampling, MSL workflows, compliance controls, and data-driven customer insights

description:
Job Description

When you work at NXP Semiconductors you become part of a dynamic company. We have an informal culture, a can-do mentality and we learn from each other every day. This combination contributes to the success of our organization, our teams, and our people.

WHO ARE WE ?

You will be a part of a diverse and experienced team of 8 Local People Partners (formerly HR managers) supporting corporate headquarters, business lines, R&D organizations and a factory. Next to that we have about 37 NL-based HR professionals in recruitment, rewards, legal, HR systems, HR analytics, administration and payroll, plus another ~300 HR colleagues worldwide.

YOUR PROFILE

You are an enrolled Bachelor or Master student in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Psychology, or a related field.

  • You are analytical, curious, and able to translate insights into practical recommendations.
  • You are self-driven and take ownership of your work.
  • You have excellent communication and organizational skills.
  • You are fluent in English and Dutch.

Research question:

This research explores how the adoption of Artificial Intelligence is reshaping the role of Local People Partners. The study will examine the impact of AI on HR processes, required competencies, decision-making, and the future strategic positioning of local people partners within NXP.


Possible research question: How will the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) transform the role, responsibilities, competencies, and strategic contribution of Local People Partners within NXP?

The research may include topics such as the augmentation of HR activities, the changing skill set of HR professionals, the impact of AI on employee experience and talent management, and the ethical and governance considerations associated with AI-driven HR practices. The outcome of the study should provide practical insights and recommendations for the HR function preparing for an AI-enabled future.

DURATION

The duration of the internship will be a minimum of 4-6 months.

Job Description

This role is designed for an experienced and forward-thinking regulatory project manager who thrives in a fast-paced, innovative environment and can seamlessly integrate strategic thinking with operational execution across all stages of product development, registration, and post-marketing.


As a key member of the Global Regulatory Science team, you will partner strategically with Global Regulatory Leads to shape and execute comprehensive regulatory strategies for the U.S. and ex-U.S. markets. You will lead the development and execution of proactive global regulatory plans that articulate clear milestones, surface risks and opportunities, and support timely, informed regulatory decision-making.


This is a highly visible, cross-functional role requiring strong leadership, agility, and strategic foresight. You will be accountable for driving regulatory excellence by aligning cross-functional stakeholders, managing complex timelines, and anticipating challenges to enable successful delivery of regulatory milestones that support the clients' mission to bring transformative mRNA medicines to patients worldwide.


In close partnership with Global Regulatory Leads, you will also play a key role in facilitating Global Regulatory Subteam (GRST) meetings and subteam forums, ensuring effective meeting structure, clear agendas, documented decisions and actions, timely follow-up, and strong meeting hygiene consistent with project management best practices. This includes helping teams operate with clarity, accountability, and a high-performance mindset through disciplined planning, communication, and execution.

Here’s What You’ll Do

  • Partner strategically with Global Regulatory Leads to shape and execute forward-looking, globally aligned regulatory plans across all stages of development and post-marketing.
  • Translate regulatory strategy into integrated, actionable plans with clear milestones, critical paths, risks, and opportunities to support effective planning and decision-making.
  • Lead the execution of regulatory plans, ensuring alignment between day-to-day operations and broader strategic objectives across global programs.
  • Identify and propose innovative regulatory pathways and planning scenarios that align with global regulatory expectations and business objectives.
  • Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams and senior leadership to drive clarity, alignment, and accountability for regulatory deliverables, timelines, and interdependencies.
  • Facilitate Global Regulatory Subteam (GRST) meetings and other routine and ad hoc project review forums, ensuring meetings are purpose-driven, well-structured, and focused on decision-making, risk mitigation, and regulatory execution.
  • Apply project management best practices for meeting management and hygiene, including developing and distributing agendas in advance, defining objectives and discussion topics, maintaining action logs, documenting key decisions and next steps, tracking follow-up items to closure, and ensuring materials are stored and communicated appropriately.
  • Partner with Global Regulatory Leads and cross-functional stakeholders to maintain effective GRST governance, meeting cadence, stakeholder alignment, and communication flow across global and regional teams.
  • Anticipate and troubleshoot complex regulatory project and operational challenges, implementing scalable solutions that strengthen team effectiveness, process efficiency, and submission readiness.
  • Prepare and deliver strategic dashboards, reports, and scenario plans to senior stakeholders, translating regulatory progress and risks into actionable business insights.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table

  • BA/BS degree in a scientific, engineering, or healthcare discipline required; advanced degree (MS, PharmD, PhD) and/or PMP certification strongly preferred.
  • Minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or related life sciences industry, with at least 5 years in regulatory or regulatory program management.

title: Software Engineering- Mulesoft, MTS/SMTS
description:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

About the Role


We are looking for a forward-thinking Software Engineer to own, administer, and scale our MuleSoft integrations across our Finance systems landscape, supporting mission-critical business processes. In this role, you will serve as the primary process expert for your service area, keeping enterprise APIs running smoothly while working closely with developers, business stakeholders, and cross-functional teams to support end-to-end Salesforce business processes.

Beyond core administration, you will drive operational efficiency by analyzing support trends, identifying enhancements, and actively redesigning workflows by integrating AI agents alongside human support engineers. If you are agile, adaptable, and bridge the gap between enterprise integrations, platform reliability, and modern AI automation, this is your play.


Key Responsibilities


MuleSoft Platform & Finance Systems Administration

  • Core Administration: Lead day-to-day administration, configuration, scaling, and proactive monitoring of MuleSoft integrations supporting core Finance and enterprise systems across CloudHub 2.0 and Runtime Fabric.
  • Environment & Security Governance: Manage runtime configurations, secrets, environment variables, TLS certificates, and OAuth security while maintaining strict segregation of duties.
  • Lifecycle Operations: Execute application restarts, runtime upgrades, capacity scaling, and configuration updates with minimal system downtime.


Application Support, Maintenance & Trend Analysis

  • Production & Incident Support: Resolve technical and functional system issues across enterprise applications, analyzing logs, alerts, metrics, and transaction traces to intercept failures early.
  • Proactive Improvement: Perform trend analysis on recurring support tickets to identify root causes and implement system enhancements that reduce overall support volume.
  • Salesforce & Ecosystem Alignment: Serve as a primary process expert collaborating with developers, QA, infrastructure teams, and business stakeholders to support end-to-end Salesforce workflows and deploy new functionality.


AI-Driven Workflow & Process Automation

  • Agentic Workflows: Design and implement intelligent support systems where AI agents collaborate alongside human support engineers to resolve incidents faster.
  • Process Transformation: Identify manual, repetitive IT and business processes across the organization and transform them into streamlined, automated workflows.
  • Automation Health: Continuously monitor existing automations, troubleshoot pipeline failures, and optimize system performance.

Release, Change Management & Governance

  • Deployment Pipelines: Oversee sandbox environments, UAT testing, and production releases using established CI/CD best practices.
  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Align major releases, enhancements, and platform upgrades across business stakeholders and development teams.
  • Documentation: Maintain comprehensive, audit-ready technical documentation for system configurations, integrations, and business processes.

What You Bring


  • MuleSoft Mastery: 4+ years of hands-on administration and implementation experience using the Anypoint Platform (Runtime Manager, CloudHub/CloudHub 2.0, API Manager, Exchange, and Mule Runtime).
  • Enterprise & Finance Ecosystem Connectivity: Proven experience supporting integrations connecting Salesforce, Workday, SAP Concur, Coupa, relational databases, SFTP, REST/SOAP APIs, and messaging queues.
  • Technical Depth: Solid grasp of SOA patterns, API security standards, TLS/certificates, CI/CD toolchains, and log analysis tools.
  • Agility & Innovation Mindset: A proactive problem-solver comfortable managing multiple competing priorities, experimenting with new tools, and embracing AI-driven workflows.
  • Communication & Collaboration: Strong verbal and written communication skills with a track record of collaborating effectively with developers, QA, and business partners.

Required Skills


  • A demonstrated, genuine AI-first approach to engineering — using AI to move faster, build fluency across the stack, and contribute well beyond your core specialty.
  • Experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Cursor, etc.) in development workflows.
  • Advanced prompt engineering skills and the ability to write precise, structured prompts and cultivate the system context that makes AI outputs reliable, secure, and production-ready.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this Accommodations Request Form.

Humans will always make any candidate selection and hiring decisions. Please see our Candidate Privacy Statement for more information about how we use your personal data and your rights, including with regard to use of AI tools and opt out options.

title: Tax - Tax Dispute Resolutions Graduate Trainee - Leeds - September 2027
description:
Forvis Mazars is a leading global professional services network providing audit & assurance, tax, and advisory services. Forvis Mazars in the UK spans 14 offices across the nation and has over 3,400 professionals, with 190 partners. We have a clear purpose and a shared commitment to shape a better future.

Kickstart your career by helping businesses understand, calculate and report their Tax responsibilities accurately. As a Graduate Tax Trainee, you’ll learn how Tax connects to financial performance, regulation and business decisions, while working with a diverse range of clients, studying towards a fully funded professional qualification and building the confidence to make a real impact from day one.

About our Team
Join our Tax Dispute Resolution team and help businesses and individuals navigate complex tax challenges. In this role, you'll help clients resolve complex issues with HMRC, develop strong problem-solving skills, and gain hands-on experience across a wide range of taxes while studying towards a professional qualification.


Hear from our trainee, Millie: 'Ever since my first day, everyone has been approachable, supportive and understanding, and there are plenty of opportunities to get involved in a wide variety of work, which makes it a great environment to learn and develop.' #LI-DNP’


Does this sound like you?
• Do you enjoy asking questions, investigating problems, and finding solutions?
• Are you curious about how businesses work and keen to learn something new every day?
• Do you like using technology and AI tools to work smarter, analyse information, and find answers more efficiently?
• Are you comfortable learning new digital tools and adapting to new ways of working?
• Do you enjoy working with people and building strong relationships?

• Are you organised, reliable, and able to manage different priorities?
• Do you take pride in producing high-quality work and seeing things through to completion?
• Are you confident communicating your ideas, whether in writing or in conversation?
• Do you want to gain a professional qualification while building a rewarding career?

To apply for our Graduate Programme, you’ll need:
• GCSE Maths and English Language at Grade 4/C (or equivalent qualifications).

• Achieved a minimum of 112 UCAS tariff points from your top three A Levels, BTECs, Scottish Highers/Advanced Highers, or other recognised Level 3 qualifications. Achieved or predicted a 2:1 degree classification (or equivalent).


We know everyone’s circumstances are different. If exceptional circumstances have affected your academic results, we’ll consider the context you provide as part of your application.

What you'll work on
• From your first day, you'll be involved in real client work, including:
• Helping clients respond to HMRC enquiries and investigations by gathering information, reviewing evidence, and supporting case strategies.
• Researching complex tax issues and turning technical legislation into clear, practical advice for clients.
• Drafting client communications including letters, reports, and responses to HMRC.
• Supporting real tax dispute cases across areas such as Income Tax, Corporation Tax, VAT, PAYE, and National Insurance.
• Attending client meetings and calls to understand challenges, build relationships, and see how advice is delivered in practice.
• Working with specialists across Tax, Audit, and Advisory to solve problems and deliver the best outcomes for clients.
• Building professional qualifications and technical expertise while applying what you learn to real client situations from day one.

Your development and benefits
You do not need to be a tax expert before you join. We’ll help you build your knowledge through professional study, practical client work and day-to-day support from your team.

Develop technical knowledge through funded ATT/CTA study, structured training and study leave.

Learn in a supportive team, with access to a buddy, mentor and colleagues who will help you settle in. Put your learning into practice through real client work and see how your contribution supports clear and valuable outcomes. You will benefit from balanced study and client work with structured support, regular check-ins and practical guidance.

Build digital confidence by learning how tax technology, data and automation support modern client work.

Whether you're already interested in tax or simply enjoy solving problems and learning new things, we'd love to hear from you. Bring your curiosity, ambition, and unique perspective to our Tax Dispute Resolution team and start building a career where you can grow, belong, and make an impact.

At Forvis Mazars diversity, equity and inclusion are central to our values. We value our people's unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experience, and know this diversity create better outcomes for our clients. We seek to attract, develop, and retain the best talent, inclusive of sex, ethnicity, disability, socio-economic background, sexual orientation, gender identity, nationality, and faith. We select candidates based on skills, knowledge, qualifications, and experience and aim to support all our team members to reach their potential. At Forvis Mazars, we promote an environment in which you can grow your skills, belong to a team that values your ideas, and make an impact that matters.

title: Undergraduate Research Assistantship - High School Fed Challenge
description:
Serve as an undergraduate research assistant on the project: From the Fed Challenge to the Economics Pipeline: How High School Economics Competitions Shape Students’ Educational and Career Interests.

This project will examine the experiences of high school students and teachers who participate in the Federal Reserve’s High School Fed Challenge. Although Fed Challenge is a well-established and highly respected program, relatively little research has examined its broader impact on participating students. The study will survey students and teachers to explore how participation may affect students’ interest in economics and finance, academic development, teamwork and communication skills, college aspirations, and educational and career choices. The project will also examine whether programs such as Fed Challenge can help introduce a broader and more diverse group of students to economics and pathways into the profession.

The research assistant will:

  • Identify high schools and teachers who have participated in High School Fed Challenge and compile publicly available contact information
  • Assist with developing the student and teacher surveys in Qualtrics
  • Complete CITI training and assist with the IRB process
  • Assist with survey distribution and data collection
  • Clean, organize, and analyze the survey data
  • Help interpret and present the research findings
  • The student will gain hands-on experience with the full research process, from study design and data collection through analysis and presentation of results

* You must have Federal Work Study funding added to your awards BEFORE applying for this position. You are potentially eligible for Work Study if you are a US Citizen or permanent resident, have filed a FAFSA, are enrolled in at least 6 credits, and are in good academic standing.

This position requires the following:

  • Must be Work Study eligible
  • An interest in economics, economic education, public policy, education, or applied social science research
  • Should be organized, dependable, attentive to detail, and comfortable working independently after receiving guidance
  • Prior experience with R or another statistical program is desirable but not required
  • Familiarity with Excel or Google Sheets would be helpful
  • No previous experience with Qualtrics, IRB procedures, or CITI training is required, as learning these tools and procedures will be an important part of the research experience

Instructions to find your Work Study eligibility status:

  • Log into your MyPacePortal and click on “Student Home” and then the “Financial Aid” box (middle of screen).
  • Once in Financial Aid, select the “Award Offer” tab and the correct Award Year.
  • Scroll down to “Options to Pay Net Cost” and take a screenshot of the funds that are allocated specifically to Work Study for the academic year. Make sure your name is captured in the screenshot, then upload the screenshot, and submit it along with your application.

* If these details are not available in the “Award Offer” section of your profile, you are NOT currently eligible for Work Study funding. If you are a US citizen or permanent resident, and you have filed a FAFSA, you can open a Help Desk ticket with Financial Aid to determine your Work Study eligibility.

title: Director of State Government Relations
description:
Centerstone is among the nation’s leading nonprofit behavioral health systems with thousands of employees dedicated to delivering care that changes people’s lives. A dynamic, well-established organization, we offer rewarding opportunities to serve all ages in a variety of settings. Come talk to us about joining the Centerstone team!


JOB DESCRIPTION:

Position Summary

The Director of State Government Relations leads Centerstone's state legislative and regulatory strategy in support of the organization’s mission to deliver care that changes lives. Serving as Centerstone’s primary government relations leader in the state, the Director manages relationships with policymakers, contract lobbyists, advocacy organizations, and internal leaders to advance key policy priorities.

This role is ideal for a highly experienced government relations professional who understands the state’s political, legislative, regulatory, and healthcare landscape and can translate complex policy developments into clear organizational strategies. The Director will also provide strategic legislative support to other states within the Centerstone system, representing up to 20% of the role’s responsibilities.

Candidates must live within a one-hour commute from the Indiana State Capitol. The position requires frequent travel to the State Capitol during the legislative session, occasional travel throughout the state, and periodic out-of-state travel.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Lead the development and execution of a comprehensive state government relations strategy aligned with organizational priorities.
  • Manage the policy and legislative agenda and activities for key state markets.
  • Serve as an advisor to market CEOs and executive teams on state legislative and regulatory matters, including risks and opportunities.
  • Provide strategic policy updates and briefings to the Board of Directors and executive leadership.
  • Serve as the primary liaison to state government officials, associations, and other external stakeholders.
  • Engage with elected officials and staff, state agencies and state associations to influence healthcare policy.
  • Develop and implement tailored, state-specific government affairs strategies that reflect the unique political, regulatory, and healthcare landscapes.
  • Oversee lobbying efforts and manage relationships with external consultants and advocacy partners.
  • Anticipate and respond to emerging policy trends that impact healthcare delivery, behavioral health, substance use, and FQHC operations.
  • Monitor, research, and analyze legislative and regulatory developments; assess their impact on organizational operations and communicate findings to relevant internal audiences.
  • Represent the organization at the state capitol, including a strong in-person presence during the legislative session.
  • Collaborate with regional and clinical leaders to align legislative strategies with local priorities and stakeholder interests.
  • Represent the System in coalitions, workgroups, and public forums to advocate for policy positions that support the System’s mission and goals.
  • Leads in drafting comments for state and/or federal regulatory RFIs.
  • Leads in identifying and developing content for Centerstone’s communication platforms.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This position does not have supervisory responsibilities.


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Deep understanding of federal/state/local government structures, legislative, and political processes; including a robust understanding of the landscape as well as key decision makers within the state.
  • Impeccable ability to exercise judgment and diplomacy among a wide variety of public and internal audiences.
  • Ability to work with diverse constituencies including business leaders, public officials, community representatives, consumers, and trade associations.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills.
  • Strong collaboration and consensus building skills, ability to cultivate buy-in at all levels of the System.
  • Strong interpersonal and negotiation skills.
  • Well-respected executive presence with strong presentation and facilitation skills.
  • Ability to set priorities and manage projects autonomously, completing them on time and on budget.
  • Proactive, independent self-starter with ability to multi-task and effectively juggle competing priorities.

Minimum Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in policy related field. Master’s degree preferred.

Experience

  • Minimum of 10 years' government relations/state policy experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree preferred; Experience within the healthcare industry preferred, however, other types of government relations/policy/advocacy experience will be considered.

Physical and Work Environment Requirements

Work is performed in an office, clinical, residential, and/or community-based environment depending on role and assignment. The position may involve routine use of office, clinical, or electronic systems and equipment. Duties may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, and working at a computer. Work hours may include evenings, weekends, holidays, or extended shifts based on program needs. This position is classified as sedentary work. Sedentary work involves exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects. title: Postdoctoral Associate/Research Scientist - Duguma Lab
description:
The Donald Danforth Plant Science Center seeks a highly motivated Postdoctoral Associate or Research Scientist to join the HeatSmart Cassava project, focused on improving photosynthetic performance and resilience of cassava under heat and combined heat–drought stress through genetic engineering and genome editing.

The successful candidate will conduct research integrating plant stress physiology, photosynthesis, molecular biology, genome editing, and gene expression analysis to develop climate-resilient cassava varieties. This position will report to Dr. Getu Duguma and Dr. Nigel Taylor and collaborate with national and international research partners.

Responsibilities:

  • Design and conduct experiments evaluating physiological and photosynthetic responses to heat and drought stress.
  • Apply molecular biology, genetic engineering, and CRISPR-based genome editing approaches to improve cassava stress tolerance.
  • Perform molecular and functional characterization of genetically engineered and gene-edited plants.
  • Analyze experimental data, prepare manuscripts, and contribute to scientific publications and project reports.
  • Independently design, coordinate, and execute research activities with minimal supervision.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary research teams to achieve project milestones.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities:

  • Demonstrated experience in molecular biology and plant physiology research.
  • Strong publication record in peer-reviewed scientific journals.
  • Proven ability to independently design, execute, and manage research projects with minimal supervision.
  • Excellent analytical, organizational, communication, and teamwork skills.

  • Live the Danforth Center values: Collaboration, Diversity & Inclusion, Innovation, Integrity & Respect, Environmental Sustainability, and Stewardship

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in plant stress physiology, particularly heat and drought responses.
  • Expertise in photosynthesis and physiological measurements.
  • Experience with CRISPR/Cas genome editing, plant genetic transformation, and molecular characterization of edited plants.
  • Experience in bioinformatics, particularly RNA-seq and differential gene expression analysis (preferred but not required).

title: Site Supervisor
description:
Overview:

We’re a trusted multi-site ophthalmology practice rooted in compassion, collaboration, and patient-centered care. Our team is made up of dedicated caregivers and respected physicians who are known in our community not just for clinical excellence, but for the way we treat our patients.

We’re looking for someone who shares the values that make Levenson Eye Associates unique – a professional who shows up with integrity, is prepared for teamwork, and a respectful and compassionate attitude towards our patients and every member of our team.

If you’re ready to make a meaningful impact and grow alongside a team that truly cares, we’d love for you to apply and take the next step with us!

Position Summary:
The Site Supervisor is responsible for the day-to-day oversight of front desk and medical records operations. This position provides leadership and operational direction to ensure consistent, efficient, and patient-centered workflows across all assigned sites.

The Site Supervisor oversees patient access functions including registration, scheduling, check-in/check-out, insurance verification, prior authorizations, and medical records management. This role is responsible for establishing and maintaining standardized processes, developing and implementing policies and procedures, monitoring staff performance, and ensuring compliance with organizational and regulatory requirements.

The Site Supervisor works closely with the Practice Administrator, physicians, clinical teams, billing, benefits verification/eligibility, and other departments to identify operational challenges, resolve escalated issues, and continuously improve the patient experience and overall practice efficiency.

Schedule: Clinic hours vary between 7:00am to 5:00pm, Monday through Friday, 8-hour shifts.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Provide direct supervision and operational leadership to front desk and medical records staff across 3 locations.
  • Train, coach, and evaluate staff in accordance with organizational standards and performance expectations.
  • Establish clear performance expectations and hold staff accountable for productivity, accuracy, professionalism, and adherence to company policies.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain standardized Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for patient access and medical records workflows.
  • Monitor staffing needs across assigned locations and make recommendations regarding coverage, scheduling, and resource allocation.
  • Manage employee schedules, timekeeping, attendance, and time-off requests within the payroll system.
  • Conduct regular staff meetings and provide ongoing training and professional development.
  • Foster a professional, collaborative, and patient-focused work environment.
  • Address employee performance concerns, workplace issues, and policy violations in partnership with the Practice Administrator and Human Resources, as appropriate.
  • Identify trends, workflow deficiencies, and opportunities for process improvement across assigned locations.
  • Standardize front desk and medical records processes to promote consistency, efficiency, and accountability across all practices.
  • Collaborate with billing, benefits verification, eligibility, clinical, and administrative teams to reduce registration, insurance, and documentation-related errors.
  • Assist the Practice Administrator with monitoring and managing patient satisfaction surveys through the Satisfied Patient Dashboard.
  • Participate in management meetings and contribute to organizational planning and operational improvement initiatives.
  • Assist with the implementation of new systems, processes, policies, and organizational initiatives.
  • Serve as an operational resource for assigned locations and provide coverage or support when unexpected staffing or workflow needs arise.

Front Desk & Patient Access Operations:

  • Oversee patient registration, check-in/check-out, scheduling, appointment management, and related front desk workflows.
  • Ensure patient demographic, insurance, and registration information is accurate, complete, and maintained according to organizational standards.
  • Oversee timely and accurate insurance verification, eligibility, and prior authorization processes.
  • Monitor patient access workflows to identify inefficiencies, errors, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Establish and maintain customer service standards that promote a positive and professional patient experience.
  • Monitor patient feedback and address service concerns appropriately.
  • Respond to and resolve escalated patient complaints involving scheduling, registration, front desk interactions, or other patient access concerns.
  • Ensure front desk processes are consistently followed across all assigned locations.

Medical Records Management:

  • Oversee the daily operations of the medical records function across assigned locations.
  • Ensure the appropriate handling, storage, scanning, organization, retrieval, and release of medical records.
  • Maintain compliance with HIPAA, organizational privacy policies, and applicable requirements governing Protected Health Information (PHI).
  • Ensure medical records requests are processed accurately and within established timeframes.
  • Implement and monitor record retention, storage, and destruction procedures in accordance with applicable legal and organizational requirements.
  • Collaborate with clinical, billing, and administrative teams to ensure timely access to accurate and complete patient documentation.
  • Identify and address medical records workflow issues that may affect patient care, billing, compliance, or operational efficiency.

title: Infant Feeding Prep Floater PRN
description:
Job Description:

Performs a variety of tasks related to the preparation and delivery of human milk, pasteurized donor human milk, and infant/pediatric formulas and transfer of patient feeding order information. Technicians will greet and interact with internal and external IFPR customers. Technicians must adhere to all food safety/sanitation regulation and standards established by the hospital and regulatory agencies. The technician is responsible for the safe and effective operation of equipment needed to prepare infant/pediatric feedings and maintain sanitation in the preparation room. Processes human milk, pasteurized donor human milk, and formula orders and maintain temperature records. Performs required quality assurance monitoring activities.

Work Schedule & Minimum Requirements

  • Floater Position to complete shifts at two Intermountain Health facilities

  • PRN, on call as needed

  • Pay Rage: Based on experience ($19.50 - $26.48)

  • Availability Needed: Sunday-Saturday 7:30am-9:00pm

  • Shifts Assigned: variable shifts assigned for Morning, Afternoon & Evening

  • Required Scheduling: Weekend and holiday coverage rotations

  • Required: High school diploma or General Education Development (GED), Food Handlers Permit, & One-year experience working with a hospital culinary program, diet office, or in a medical field


This position will be required to complete shifts at the following Intermountain Health locations:

  • Intermountain Health Primary Children's Hospital (Salt Lake City area)

  • Intermountain Health Primary Children's Lehi Hospital (Lehi)


Essential Job Duties

  • Maintains friendly and helpful attitude toward customers (internal and external) and coworkers.
  • Prepares, portions, and delivers patient feedings per feeding order, recipes, or registered dietitian nutritionist (RDN) instruction.
  • Maintains patient feeding orders via computer system and accurately prepares feeding orders that are not available as a ready-to-feed formula.
  • Transcribes feeding order information to prepare feeding labels.
  • Reports discrepancies in feeding orders to manager or RDN.
  • Communicates with manager, patient care areas, and RDNs regarding issues or problems with feeding orders, human milk/pasteurized donor human milk/formula storage, or administration of feedings.
  • Communicates with parents who are dropping off, storing, and/or picking up expressed human milk to ensure proper labeling and storing of expressed human milk.
  • Communicates with parents, nurses, lactation consultants, dietitians, and colleagues to receive and clarify daily diet orders and ensures accurate preparation and labeling of human milk/pasteurized donor human milk feedings.
  • Completes necessary paperwork for accurate billing and tracking of pasteurized donor human milk and infant formulas.
  • Complies with daily records and updates computerized patient profiles regarding infant/pediatric feeding orders, including allergy information.
  • Follow processes, as established, for quality assurance monitors.
  • Sets up assigned workstation.
  • Maintains an adequate inventory of IFPR supplies.
  • Unpacks, labels, and stores fortifiers, formula, and supplies in their designated storage area; rotates supplies using first-in, first-out (FIFO) method.
  • Covers, labels, and dates formula requiring refrigeration according to Infant Feeding Preparation Room policy.
  • Maintains a sanitary and safe environment by following departmental and infection prevention policies; reports unsafe conditions and accidents to manager.
  • Uses correct technique to measure solids and liquids.
  • Maintains a clean and orderly workspace, ensuring that department standards are met and that all sanitary activities are conducted in accordance with federal, state, and local health regulations.
  • Maintains clean equipment and cleans small wares in dishwasher; records dish machine temperatures per procedure.
  • Records refrigerator and freezer temperatures on appropriate log daily in designated pantries and work areas.
  • Removes damaged formula cans and outdated formula stock from inventory and disposes per facility guidelines.
  • Adheres to Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) guidelines; maintains temperature logs of prepared feedings for quality assurance.
  • Adheres to uniform policy established in area; no artificial nails are allowed; nails must be kept short, clean and unpolished.
  • Assist in training other staff in feeding preparation and proper handling techniques as needed.
  • Attends mandatory meetings and in-service education programs as scheduled by the department and facility.
  • Treats all information and data with the scope of the position with appropriate confidentiality and security. Complies with Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPPA) regulations.
  • Adheres to all established systems and training programs to provide a safe working environment.Complies with all Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulation and other local, state, and federal regulations.
  • Recognizes and adopts activates appropriate to the specific needs of the patient population and demonstrates knowledge of specific issues directly related to age of the patient population.
  • Maintains compliance with standards of operation; maintains all records and reports necessary to comply with government and accrediting agency standards, regulation, and codes.
  • Performs additional duties as assigned.

Physical Requirement

  • Ongoing need for employee to see and read information, recipes, and labels.
  • Frequent interactions with patient parents and colleagues that require caregiver to verbally communicate as well as hear and understand spoken information, needs, and issues accurately.
  • Expected to lift and utilize full range of movement. Will also bend to retrieve, lift, and carry supplies and equipment. Typically includes items of varying weights, up to 50 lb.

Wednesday-Saturday 10:30 PM – 8:00 AM

The pay range for this position is $34.00–$38.00 per hour for employees hired in the Santa Cruz, CA area. The pay range provided in this job posting represents the typical range or starting rate for candidates hired within the bay area region. Candidates hired in other California locations may have different starting salaries based on cost of living and market data variations. Factors that may be used to determine your actual starting salary include your education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, the market data for your work location, and internal comparisons to other employees in similar roles.

✨ Make a Meaningful Impact

Aspiranet, one of California’s leading nonprofit organizations supporting children, youth, and families, is seeking a compassionate and skilled Licensed Vocational Nurse to join our Crisis Stabilization Unit (CSU) team in Santa Cruz.

This position plays a vital role in providing high-quality medical and behavioral care to youth in crisis. If you’re passionate about supporting the emotional and physical well-being of young people and thrive in a collaborative, mission-driven environment, we invite you to join our team and make a lasting impact.

❤️ About Aspiranet

Founded in 1975, Aspiranet is a mission-driven organization dedicated to helping families thrive. We provide a continuum of care across California through six service divisions: Foster and Adoption, Transitional Aged Youth, Residential, Intensive Home-Based Services, Behavioral Health, and Family and Community. Every role at Aspiranet contributes to something greater: building a future where every child is loved, every family supported, and every individual equipped to succeed.

📝️ Position Summary

The Licensed Vocational Nurse provides compassionate care and clinical oversight to youth placed in Aspiranet’s Crisis Stabilization Unit (CSU).

This role is responsible for assessing clients, administering medication, monitoring medical needs, and supporting individualized treatment plans. The Licensed Vocational Nurse collaborates closely with multidisciplinary treatment teams, supports health and wellness education, and ensures compliance with health, safety, and infection control standards.

🔍 Key Responsibilities

Client Care & Supervision

  • Provide direct care and supervision to youth at the Crisis Stabilization Unit.
  • Administer medications and monitor for side effects or changes in client condition.
  • Coordinate clients’ medical, physical, and dental needs, including referrals and linkages to community providers.
  • Deliver health screening, education, and counseling focused on prevention, wellness, and mental health.
  • Provide daily living assistance and supportive behavioral interventions to clients.

Medical & Clinical Support

  • Consult with physicians and pharmacists regarding client medication needs.
  • Manage prescription call-ins and medication documentation.
  • Oversee and implement communicable disease and infection control policies.
  • Provide training to staff on health and safety protocols.
  • Participate in treatment planning meetings and multidisciplinary care coordination.

Documentation & Communication

  • Accurately document interventions, medical issues, progress, and behavioral observations.
  • Communicate effectively with treatment team members, supervisors, and client families.
  • Attend required staff meetings, trainings, and clinical consultations.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

✅ Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:

  • Graduate of an accredited School of Nursing or Medical Assistant program.
  • Current Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN) or Psychiatric Technician certification.
  • Minimum of one year of professional nursing or medical assistant experience.
  • CPR/BLR and First Aid certification
  • Minimum of two years’ experience working with children, adolescents, and families with emotional or behavioral challenges.
  • Mental health background and experience working with youth or adolescents preferred.
  • Experience in an inpatient, residential, or clinical setting strongly desired.
  • Must be at least 21 years of age.
  • Strong knowledge of crisis assessment, trauma-informed care, and safety planning.
  • Meets all state-required employment conditions, including:
    • DOJ fingerprint and Child Abuse Index clearance
    • TB/Health physical
    • Valid CA Driver’s License, acceptable driving record, and proof of insurance

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Proficiency in English (reading, writing, speaking, and comprehension).
  • Ability to work independently while seeking guidance when necessary.
  • Knowledge of federal, state, and local regulations related to CSU operations and Medicaid/EPSDT.
  • Familiarity with the DSM-V and psychotropic medications.
  • Understanding of substance abuse issues and mental health care.
  • Strong writing and documentation skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word and standard office software.
  • Excellent time management, multitasking, and organizational abilities.
  • Ability to establish and maintain professional boundaries with clients and staff.

💻 Work Environment & Schedule

  • This position operates within a Crisis Stabilization Unit (CSU) clinical environment in Santa Cruz, CA.
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • May require occasional travel for training or collaboration with partner agencies.

❤️ Why Aspiranet?

  • Competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits package, and a 403(b) retirement plan with employer matching.
  • Access to the free Aspiranet Employee Perks Program. Enjoy exclusive discounts on entertainment, travel, wellness, pet care, gym memberships, theme parks, and more
  • Flexible paid time off including 11 paid holidays, 10 vacation days, 10 sick leave days, two diversity days, and paid birthday time off.
  • Access to our employee assistance program including 24/7 crisis line; up to 6 counseling sessions per issue.
  • Training opportunities are available to support your ongoing development and career aspirations.
  • Collaborate in a supportive, inclusive, and mission-aligned culture.
  • Opportunity to lead meaningful initiatives that support employee wellbeing.

title: OCONUS - All Source Analyst - (Mid-Level)
description:
Your Impact:


The Counterintelligence Operational Support Team provides Counterintelligence (CI) analysis services that includes the fusing intelligence and collecting of raw data from multiple sources and varying classifications to identify threats, trends, structures, and locations of Foreign Intelligence Entities (FIE). This includes the dissemination of time-sensitive and non-time-sensitive Force Protection (FP) threat information and assessments to supported Commanders including six (6) Air Force Central (AFCENT) forward deployed units within the CENTCOM AOR and one (1) CONUS based unit.


Responsibilities:


  • Conduct analysis using intelligence and information from multiple sources to assess, interpret, forecast, and explain a range of national security issues and developments that are regional or functional in nature. Provides all-source analytic support to collections, operations, investigations, and other defense intelligence analytic requirements.
  • Review CI2MS activities for unit COINEs, Investigations, and source documentation.
  • Provide assistance to AFOSICOINEs and other investigations, supporting the identification, exploiting, and neutralizing of criminal, terrorist and intelligence threats in multiple domains to protect the designated vital interests.
  • Ensure products are compliant with ICD and AFOSI standards and uploaded to appropriate databases.
  • Maintain knowledge of host nation intelligence and security organizations.
  • Maintain knowledge of third country intelligence services that pose a threat to DAF resources and the organization’s personnel, and maintain knowledge of the capabilities of state sponsored, transnational, international or regional terrorist groups and their surrogates that threaten DAF security.
  • Review and provide analyst comments for CRs and IIRs. Disseminate raw and finished intelligence products to interested agencies
  • Prepare comprehensive foreign intelligence and terrorism informational or analytical products.
  • Fuse intelligence and raw data from multiple sources in varying classifications to identify threats, trends, structures of terrorist cells, their location, plotting attack information (such as fire-points, impact sites, timeline, etc.)
  • Perform collection management duties by evaluating field reports involving terrorist group organizational structures and their involved interrelationships among other organizations and state-sponsored groups targeting the DAF/DoD.
  • Assist in the development of target packages to mitigate threats to 24 EFIS, subordinate units, and USAF/DoD personnel and resources in the USCENTCOM/AFCENT AOR.
  • Prepare briefings that describe the nature, scope, specific identification, and possible impact of coordination and cooperation prevalent among hostile groups.
  • Coordinate and maintain liaison relationships with military and national level agencies.
  • Travel and provide onsite and offsite support to other CONUS and OCONUS locations in the CENTCOM AOR as requested.

Minimum Requirements (Knowledge, Skills, Abilities):


  • Must be a U.S. citizen.
  • Must have a Top-Secret Clearance and be eligible SCI level Clearance at time of hire.
  • Six (6) years of all-source analytical experience utilizing HUMINT, SIGINT, IMINT, or OSINT.
  • One (1) year comprehensive analytical support to counterintelligence, counterterrorism, and/or HUMINT operations, ending within the last three (3) years.
  • One (1 year) comprehensive analytical or operational experience to operations involving DOD National Defense Strategy priority countries including Russia, China, or Iran.
  • Six (6) years of experience in the development of intelligence analysis products.
  • Strong writing skills and being capable of effectively operating as a member of a combined/joint intelligence team required. Strong briefing skills and being capable of effective communication in the accomplishment of collection management reporting and requirements required.
  • Experience and working knowledge of the following programs and systems within the last three (3) years: Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Access); Analyst Notebook; SIPR/JWICS Access; M3 - Multi Media Messenger (Or other message handling system such as TAC/Tripwire, Palantir, etc.) ; SOMM - Source Operations Management Module; Proton - JWICS Access Required (or other similar such database such as ROCKSTAR, Voltron, etc.); Intellink; CIDNE - Combined Information Data network Exchange; CIA WIRE; HOT-R (Or CHROME – Counterintelligence and Human Intelligence Requirements, Reporting, and Operations Management Environment); NCTC Online - National Counter Terrorism Center Online; J2 DCP Portal (CJCS Portal) on JWICS.
  • Maintain current passport and visa requirements and maintain the ability to be world-wide deployable to include medical clearances.

Clearance Required:


  • TS/SCI

Minimum Education:


  • High School Diploma.

Minimum Years of Experience:


  • Six (6) years of all-source analytical experience utilizing HUMINT, SIGINT, IMINT, or OSINT.
  • One (1) year comprehensive analytical support to counterintelligence, counterterrorism, and/or HUMINT operations, ending within the last three (3) years.
  • One (1 year) comprehensive analytical or operational experience to operations involving DOD National Defense Strategy priority countries including Russia, China, or Iran.
  • Six (6) years of experience in the development of intelligence analysis products.

Preferred:


  • Desired Education: Bachelor’s degree in international affairs, national security studies, Arabic studies, international business, international terrorism, trends and analysis, intelligence/counterintelligence or other related fields;
  • Desired Experience: Southwest Asian regional expertise.
  • Knowledge ofAFOSII2MS and/or CI2MS is desirable.

Job Description

Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. (NYSE: TMO) is the world leader in serving science, with revenues of more than $20 billion and approximately 65,000 employees globally. Through our premier brands – Thermo Scientific, Applied Biosystems, Invitrogen, Fisher Scientific and Unity Lab Services – we offer an unmatched combination of innovative technologies, purchasing convenience and comprehensive services

The Position

We are seeking a Lead DevOps Engineer to design, implement, and maintain robust CI/CD pipelines and automation frameworks supporting software development and delivery processes. This role focuses on enabling efficient, reliable, and scalable build and release workflows, particularly within C#/.NET environments.

You will work in a collaborative, cross-functional environment, partnering with development, QA, test automation, and infrastructure teams to streamline software delivery, improve system reliability, and support continuous improvement initiatives across the organization.

Key responsibilities include, but are not exclusively:

  • Design, develop, and maintain CI/CD pipelines using tools such as Jenkins and GitLab to support automated build, test, and deployment processes
  • Support and optimize C#/.NET/Angular build and deployment workflows, including management of NuGet packages
  • Implement and maintain version control strategies using Git, including branching and merging approaches aligned with release processes
  • Manage release activities, including maintaining stabilization branches and ensuring smooth release cycles
  • Develop and maintain automation scripts using Python and PowerShell to improve operational efficiency
  • Design and support containerized environments using Docker and Kubernetes for scalable application deployment
  • Implement advanced deployment strategies such as Blue-Green deployments to ensure minimal downtime and risk
  • Ensure integration of static code analysis tools (e.g., SonarQube, TICS) and multiple automated test suites within CI pipelines
  • Maintain end-to-end pipeline flow, from environment provisioning and build execution to artifact storage and archival
  • Collaborate with development, QA, and test automation teams to translate requirements into technical solutions and pipeline designs
  • Work closely with shared infrastructure teams (e.g., SETI, Toolchain teams) to align infrastructure standards and best practices
  • Contribute to and maintain documentation using Confluence, ensuring knowledge sharing and transparency across teams
  • Utilize Jira for backlog tracking, sprint planning, and progress monitoring within Agile frameworks
  • Actively participate in Scrum, Kanban, and scaled Agile (ART) environments, contributing to continuous delivery practices
  • Collaborate with cross-ART teams (e.g., CI/CD and Test Automation teams) to align on shared tools, frameworks, and codebases
  • Leading and mentoring junior DevOps resources within the team.
  • Apply strong analytical and problem-solving skills to troubleshoot complex issues and improve system performance and reliability

Requirements:

The ideal candidate for this position thrives in a complex technical environment and is passionate about automation, continuous integration, and delivering high-quality software solutions.

  • University degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline
  • Strong hands-on experience with CI/CD tools such as Jenkins and GitLab, including designing and maintaining automation pipelines
  • 8+ years of Strong Experience in supporting C#/.NET/Angular build and deployment processes
  • Solid knowledge of package management, especially NuGet
  • Strong experience with Git and modern branching strategies
  • Experience in release management, including maintaining stabilization branches and coordinating releases
  • Hands-on scripting and automation experience using Python and/or PowerShell
  • Proven experience with containerization technologies such as Docker and orchestration platforms like Kubernetes
  • Experience in implementing modern deployment strategies such as Blue-Green deployments
  • Strong understanding of VMware infrastructure and security best practices
  • Experience in integrating static code analysis tools (e.g., SonarQube, TICS) into CI/CD pipelines
  • Experience in integrating and managing multiple automated test suites within CI pipelines
  • Understanding of end-to-end pipeline processes, from environment setup to artifact management and archival
  • Hands-on experience with Jira for backlog management and sprint tracking
  • Experience in working within Agile frameworks such as Scrum and Kanban
  • Familiarity with Agile Release Trains (ART) and scaled Agile environments
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to troubleshoot complex issues
  • Proven ability to deliver solutions in complex technical environments
  • Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively with development, QA, test automation, and infrastructure teams
  • Experience collaborating with shared infrastructure teams (e.g., SETI, Toolchain teams) and cross-ART teams
  • Optimize infrastructure resource utilization to ensure high performance, scalability, and cost efficiency.
  • Monitor and identify performance bottlenecks and implement improvements.
  • Fluent in English (B2 level or higher)
  • Eligible for travel if required

title: Bike Patrol Officer
description:
General Definition: The Bike Patrol Officer is responsible for maintaining a safe and secure environment for guests, employees, and property through active patrol, observation, and rapid response to incidents. This role carries the additional responsibility of lawfully carrying and maintaining a firearm, exercising sound judgment, and responding to high-risk situations in accordance with training, company policy, and applicable laws.

Essential Job Functions:

  • Carry a firearm in accordance with company policy, state regulations, and training requirements, maintaining readiness and secure control at all times.
  • Exercise sound judgment and restraint when responding to high-risk or volatile situations, using force only as authorized and appropriate.
  • Conduct vehicle patrols of assigned areas, including parking lots and exterior property, as required.
  • Protect designated individuals and sensitive or restricted areas from harassment, physical harm, vandalism, or unauthorized access.

  • Conduct continuous patrols of the casino, adjacent buildings, and exterior areas, maintaining a visible security presence and identifying hazards, suspicious activity, and security breaches.
  • Provide guest assistance, including directions and escorts, and regularly escort employees in money-handling positions.
  • Observe, assess, and report incidents accurately and without delay, escalating concerns through appropriate channels.
  • Prepare clear, timely, and detailed incident, accident, and activity reports.
  • Enforce internal security policies and procedures consistently and professionally.
