title: Director, Commercial Data Strategy & Enablement
description:
Job Description

Company Overview


Vertex is a global biotechnology company that invests in scientific innovation to create transformative medicines for people with serious diseases. We are driven by a commitment to patients, scientific excellence, and an inclusive culture where talented people can do their best work. Our teams collaborate across disciplines to translate data, insights, and technology into meaningful business outcomes and improved patient experiences.


Role Summary


The Director, Commercial Data Strategy & Enablement will lead the strategy, governance, and enablement of commercial data assets, platforms, and capabilities across the organization. This role will partner closely with Commercial, Digital & Technology, Data & Analytics, Finance, Market Access, Patient Support, and external vendors to ensure high-quality, trusted, and accessible data supports strategic decision-making.


The successful candidate will define and execute a scalable commercial data roadmap; establish standards for data quality, governance, and adoption; and enable business teams to turn data into actionable insights. This leader will combine strong commercial acumen, data strategy expertise, and change-management capabilities to advance a data-driven culture across Vertex’s commercial organization.


Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and lead the enterprise commercial data strategy, aligning data investments and priorities with commercial objectives, brand strategies, and patient-focused outcomes.
  • Define a multi-year roadmap for commercial data capabilities, including data acquisition, integration, governance, analytics enablement, self-service access, and performance measurement.
  • Partner with Commercial leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to identify critical business questions, prioritize use cases, and translate needs into scalable data solutions.
  • Establish and oversee commercial data governance practices, including data ownership, stewardship, data quality standards, metadata management, privacy, access controls, and issue-resolution processes.
  • Lead initiatives to improve the availability, consistency, usability, and reliability of commercial data across domains such as customer, healthcare provider, payer, specialty pharmacy, patient services, field engagement, sales, and marketing.
  • Collaborate with Digital & Technology and Data & Analytics teams to design and implement modern data architecture, data products, reporting environments, and analytics capabilities.
  • Enable adoption of commercial data and analytics tools by developing training, communications, playbooks, and operating models that support business users and data stewards.
  • Establish key performance indicators to measure data quality, platform adoption, business value realization, operational efficiency, and maturity of data capabilities.
  • Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to senior leaders, clearly communicating data strategy, risks, opportunities, and recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Lead, develop, and mentor a high-performing team of data strategy, governance, and enablement professionals.
  • Manage relationships with external data providers, technology partners, and consulting firms, including vendor selection, performance management, and contract-related collaboration.
  • Ensure commercial data practices align with applicable privacy, compliance, security, and pharmaceutical industry requirements.
  • Drive continuous improvement by monitoring evolving data, analytics, artificial intelligence, and commercial technology trends.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, analytics, data science, information systems, life sciences, or a related field.
  • Typically 10+ years of progressive experience in commercial data strategy, data management, analytics, digital transformation, or related disciplines.
  • Significant experience supporting commercial functions within the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, healthcare, life sciences, or similarly regulated industry.
  • Demonstrated success developing and executing data strategies that improve decision-making, operational effectiveness, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Experience leading cross-functional, enterprise-scale data governance, data quality, and data enablement initiatives.
  • Strong understanding of commercial data domains, including sales, marketing, customer relationship management, market access, payer, patient support, and third-party healthcare data.
  • Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, build alignment across functions, and manage competing priorities in a complex organization.
  • Experience leading and developing teams, including direct reports and/or matrixed teams.
  • Excellent communication, executive presentation, strategic problem-solving, and change-management skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in a hybrid or on-site environment and collaborate with teams across locations.

Technical Skills Required

  • Commercial data strategy and roadmap development
  • Data governance, stewardship, and operating-model design
  • Data quality management, profiling, monitoring, and remediation
  • Master data management and reference data management
  • Data catalog, metadata management, and data lineage concepts
  • Data architecture, data integration, and data product principles
  • Cloud-based data and analytics platforms
  • Business intelligence, dashboarding, and self-service analytics tools
  • Customer relationship management and commercial engagement platforms
  • Commercial data sources, including sales, claims, prescription, payer, provider, and patient-support data
  • Data privacy, security, access management, and compliance controls
  • KPI definition, performance measurement, and value realization
  • Agile delivery methodologies and product-management practices

Preferred Skills

  • Advanced degree in business administration, data science, analytics, information systems, or a related discipline.
  • Experience with pharmaceutical commercial platforms and data ecosystems, such as CRM, omnichannel engagement, field force effectiveness, market research, and real-world data solutions.
  • Experience with modern cloud data technologies, including data warehouses, lakehouses, APIs, and data integration tools.
  • Familiarity with data visualization and analytics tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or similar platforms.
  • Knowledge of SQL, Python, or other analytical programming languages.
  • Experience enabling artificial intelligence or machine learning use cases within commercial operations.
  • Certifications in data management, cloud technologies, product management, project management, or agile methodologies.
  • Experience supporting product launches, indication expansions, or global commercial data transformation programs.

At Vertex, we embrace continuous learning and encourage employees to stay informed on advances in AI, technology, automation, and industry trends. We seek talent who bring an external perspective, demonstrate curiosity and sound judgment, and thoughtfully adopt new capabilities that improve decision-making, drive innovation, increase efficiency, and help deliver better outcomes for patients.

Pay Range:

$192,000 - $288,000

Disclosure Statement:

The range provided is based on what we believe is a reasonable estimate for the base salary pay range for this job at the time of posting. description:

General Summary:

The Director, Innovation and Business Transformation leads the execution across multiple highly complex and interconnected technology-enabled transformation initiatives within Medical Writing Science (MWS). The role translates established transformation priorities into a coordinated slate of initiatives, integrates business, solution, implementation, and adoption approaches, and aligns MWS leaders with enterprise technology partners. title: Associate Director, Forecasting
description:
Job Description Summary

The Associate Director (AD), Forecasting will lead development and communication of high-quality, assumption-driven commercial forecasts and value assessments to support decision making across pipeline assets, BD&L opportunities and Established Medicines portfolio. The role will partner cross-functionally to ensure alignment on key inputs, drive forecast governance and documentation standards, and enable leadership with insights on performance drivers, upside/downside, and investment trade-offs. The role brings strong commercial judgment, analytical rigor, and project management capabilities to translate market dynamics, strategic choices, and evidentiary uncertainty into transparent forecast narratives, risks, and scenarios.


Job Description

Associate Director, Forecasting

Location – Hyderabad #LI Hybrid

Major Accountabilities:

  • Develop and maintain transparent, assumption-driven forecasts for Established Medicines and select pipeline/launch assets, applying appropriate methodologies, challenging assumptions, and documenting key inputs from analogs, epidemiology, patient flows, competitive intelligence, and cross-functional partners.
  • Quantify the impact of market dynamics and internal events such as LOE, pricing, contracting, indication expansion, label changes, and supply constraints through scenarios, sensitivities, and risk/opportunity assessments; track forecast-to-actuals, identify variance drivers, and refresh models as needed.
  • Support pipeline, launch, and BD&L deliverables through timely forecast updates, market sizing, revenue modeling, due diligence support, clear narratives, and alignment on key assumptions, uncertainties, and value drivers.
  • Drive standardization, simplification, and automation of forecasting processes, models, templates, data pipelines, and dashboards to improve scalability, transparency, speed, and decision support, using advanced analytics where appropriate.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing HYD forecasting capability team with clear accountability, decision rights, and performance expectations, while partnering with the US GM organization, US Finance, I&A pillars, and AIDE leadership on capability priorities, talent, operations, and site-level initiatives.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Minimum 10 years of experience in pharmaceutical forecasting, data analytics, or sales operations, preferably in branded, pipeline, marketed, Specialty, or Rare Disease products, with strong knowledge of the US pharmaceutical commercial model, market dynamics, and analytics ecosystem.
  • Undergraduate degree in Business or STEM required, with deep expertise in forecasting and analytics, including pharmaceutical datasets such as Rx and APLD, ROI/financial modeling, statistical analysis, and data-driven decision support.
  • Strong ability to partner cross-functionally, build consensus, communicate uncertainty, and explain insights from aggregate business trends to modeling mechanics for diverse stakeholders, including senior leadership.
  • Proven self-starter with high standards, innovative thinking, strong analytical, interpersonal, communication, project management, and change management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Strong organizational agility, political awareness, and ability to navigate complex environments to get things done, with excellent PowerPoint and Excel skills.

Preferred Skills:

  • Preferred to have master’s degree in data analytics, data science, or finance workstreams
  • Experience operating through a large-scale organizational transformation or operating model redesign
  • Experience across multiple enterprise analytics organizations and experience in establishing capabilities in GCCs
  • Breadth in experience in forecasting techniques, projects and managing stakeholder constraints across different brand portfolios and market
  • Fluent English, other languages desirable.

Location: Hyderabad NKC | Hybrid | 3 days a week in office is mandatory.

Direct Reports: 3-5 Internal Associates + team of External Associates.


Skills Desired

Change Agility, Cross-Functional Collaboration, Customer Engagement, Customer Experience (CX), Customer Insights, Data Analytics, Data Strategies, Digital Marketing, Marketing Strategies, Market Research, Media Campaigns, Product Marketing, Stakeholder Engagement, Stakeholder Management, Team Leadership, Waterfall Model

title: PeriOp Inventory Coordinator II
description:
Job Description:

This position is accountable for coordinating all inventory activities for assigned dept, facility or clinical program. This may include replenishment, picking, staging, delivery, put away, special orders and substitutions. It may include managing PAR levels, Binning, Cycle Counts, Bill Only and Inventory Relief activities. This position is often a direct liaison between a department or clinical program and other Supply Chain Teams. In addition, it is also considered a "Lead" or subject matter expert who takes on more complex or demanding responsibilities with little supervision.

Schedule: Sunday - Thursday

Hours: Full-time 40 hours

* Some holidays


Essentials:

  • Coordinates inventory management activity to ensure the needs of the facility or assigned clinical program are being met. Works in cross functional teams to meet customer needs in a timely and efficient manner.

  • Performs inventory control on both stock and non-stock items (e.g., sets par levels, identifies and adjusts to trends) for assigned inventory. Keeps supplies binned and organized. Acts as liaison with Field Logistics Management and clinical program.

  • Orders and delivers supplies for assigned department or clinical program using standard operating procedures, appropriate technology, and suppliers. Manages Consignment or Vendor Managed Inventory according to SCO (SOP's).

  • Accountable for replenishment activity in assigned locations or clinical program using established SCO Standard Operating Procedures (SOP's). Ensures temperature sensitive products are stored properly and are delivered according to manufacturer and Intermountain guidelines.

  • Ensures required documentation related to shipping & receiving, delivery, and tissue tracking are completed according to policy and procedures.

  • Communicates information concerning supply levels, new products, standardization, back orders, and product implementation to the relevant stakeholders or clinical program staff.

  • Coordinates the MMIS system ensuring distribution, inventory, receiving, departmental files, and reports are managed in accordance with Auditing, Accounting, and other regulatory agency requirements.

  • Adheres to established cycle count and inventory relief (SOP’s). Understands and applies Supply Chain (SOP’s), Reports and Tools.

Skills:

  • PeriOp logistics Management
  • Medical Supply Distribution
  • Supply Chain Processes
  • Warehouse Inventory Management
  • Warehouse Management System (WMS)
  • Excellent Team Player
  • Continuous Improvement (CI)
  • Communication between multiple teams

Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience working with PeriOp/Inventory.
  • Experience with prioritizing multiple tasks, organizing teams with multiple levels of caregivers, and meeting deadlines.
  • History of inventory control such as cycle counts and physical inventory.
  • Demonstrated examples of strong cross functional teamwork.

description:
Senior Design Manager, Men’s Tops & Bottoms Apparel

Now that you’ve found the job description, what’s next?

At The North Face we dare to lead the world forward through Exploration. We were born to Explore, Disrupt and to Lead. We were born to Love Wild Places and to Spark Curiosity. We believe that exploration is a mindset, both on the mountain and off the mountain, and it infuses everything we do. As a community of explorers, we stay curious about new ideas, places, and people.

So, before we get to the job details, take a minute to learn a little more about us, our values and our culture. If you can see yourself working side-by-side with a team of adventure-loving people, The North Face just may be the place for you.

To learn more about our values and our culture, visit The North Face Careers or The North Face.

What will you do?

A day in the life of a Senior Design Manager, Men’s Tops & Bottoms Apparel at The North Face looks a little like this.

  • You will lead and elevate the design expression for Men’s Tops & Bottoms, creating best-in-class product with a high level of aesthetic competence and a strong point of view. You are a highly influential member of the design team who balances strong creativity with the ability to deliver, setting direction and driving design decisions across the category.
  • You will lead seasonal research and insights, concepts, design direction, presentation tools and key design deliverables for the category, ensuring the work connects brand vision with consumer and business needs.
  • You will drive and inspire design ideas across the team, with a focus on craftsmanship and excellence. You are highly experienced in presenting design work to senior audiences in a compelling and persuasive way and are comfortable giving clear, objective and constructive feedback.
  • You will provide creative direction, mentorship and guidance to designers, helping elevate individual capabilities as well as the overall quality and consistency of the team’s design output.
  • You will bring a highly advanced understanding of brand aesthetic and DNA, materials and technologies, fit and silhouette, translating these into relevant and distinctive product that supports consumer and business needs.
  • You will bring a strong understanding of the needs of outdoor apparel, combined with an elevated taste level and strong knowledge of the competitive landscape, using those insights to identify opportunities and push the category forward.
  • You will partner closely with Merchandising, Product, Development and other cross-functional partners, influencing decisions and ensuring the creative vision is maintained from concept through commercialization.

What do you need to succeed?

We all have unique skills that we bring to work and celebrate every day. For this role, there are foundational skills you’ll need to succeed and excel. While formal education in a related field is great to have, we are most interested in your experience, professional achievements and demonstrated design leadership.

The foundational skills you will need in this position are:

  • 10+ years of experience in athletic / outdoor / sportswear / men’s apparel design, with strong expertise relevant to Men’s Tops & Bottoms.
  • Demonstrated experience providing creative direction, mentoring designers and elevating design output across a team or category.
  • Exceptional product acumen with comprehensive knowledge of apparel product development processes, including design, development, sourcing and manufacturing.
  • Advanced knowledge and understanding of apparel construction, with strong flat sketching and illustration expertise.
  • Understanding of, and ideally active participation in, some of the activities / sports you are designing for.
  • Advanced hands-on experience with Adobe Creative Suite and CAD software. 3D software and AI image-generation experience (Clo / Browzwear / Vizcom / Midjourney) is a plus but not required.
  • Comprehensive knowledge and experience creating high-quality, detailed tech packs.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of cost engineering and the ability to design to cost while maintaining the integrity of the creative vision.
  • Advanced experience in fitting, with a strong understanding of category silhouette needs for sport and an elevated sense of aesthetic.
  • Strong experience developing performance materials, trims and color palettes.
  • Exceptional presentation and storytelling skills, with the ability to influence and build alignment around a creative vision.
  • Strong communication and influencing skills across design, cross-functional partners, vendors and senior stakeholders.
  • Comprehensive understanding of product cycles, key milestones and core deadlines, with the ability to drive the team toward successful execution.
  • Growth mindset, curiosity and enthusiasm for learning new tools, exploring new approaches and solving complex design challenges.

At The North Face, we know you expect as much from us as we do from you. That is why we make a commitment to support and grow our people. We offer extensive development and growth opportunities for your current and future positions, a competitive compensation package, and a strong benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, and 401(k).

As a Production Technician I, you will manufacture, assemble, and package Bioprocess Containers in a cleanroom environment. You will safely carry out the production process by closely following the Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), Work Instruction Documents (WID), blueprints, and drawings as they relate to assembly, material handling, equipment operation, and finished goods packaging. Production Technician I’s will work through the site Technician Training Program.

  • Perform production-related duties, including operating equipment, assembling boxes, and packaging and preparing finished products for shipment.

  • Ensure products meet quality standards by collaborating with other stations and departments to address quality errors.
  • Maintain accurate documentation as the task is being performed.
  • Participate in Practical Process Improvements (PPI) activities.
  • Work effectively to consistently meet goals as an individual and as part of a team.
  • Focus on personal development through timely completion of training.
  • Adhere to schedule to meet department and site goals while maintaining focus on quality of work.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned to support business and operational needs.

Education & Experience:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • No previous work experience required.
  • Preferred Experience: Previous work experience in a cGMP environment, manufacturing, operations, production, or warehouse.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities:

  • Competency in using computers, Microsoft Office products, and inventory management systems.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Attention to detail and problem-solving abilities.
  • Read and understand written materials, including words, pictures, and numbers.
  • Accurate counting, sorting, calculating, and measuring using tools like calculators and tape measures.
  • Ability to understand chemical safety, including interpreting labels and Safety Data Sheets (SDS).

Physical Requirements and Work Environment:

  • Adherence to all Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and Safety Standards.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment up to 12 hours a day with additional overtime as required.
  • This role involves getting in the cleanroom frequently, which is a temperature controlled environment. Cleanrooms do not allow hair products, jewelry, makeup, nail polish, acrylic nails, perfume/cologne, piercings, lip balm, lotion, chewing gum, etc.
  • Some degree of Personal Protective Equipment is required including safety-toed boots (ASTM F2413-24), high visibility gear, safety glasses, cleanroom suit, hair/beard coverings, gloves, lab coat, ear plugs, etc.

The Coral Springs Family Health and Surgery Center provides patients with convenient access to the same world-class care provided at Cleveland Clinic's regional hospitals. This state-of-the-art facility specializes in primary care, outpatient surgery, imaging and more. As a caregiver on our team, you will experience endless support and appreciation while building a rewarding career with one of the most respected healthcare organizations in the world.

As OR Service Assistant I, you will play a vital role in supporting surgical operations by assisting with patient transport and preparing the Operating Room. You will be responsible for setting up and operating specialized equipment as needed, while coordinating the necessary supplies and instruments for service-specific surgical cases. In this role, you will also manage the tracking of loaned and borrowed equipment and supplies, ensuring everything is available, functional and ready to meet the needs of the surgical team.

A caregiver in this role works days from 7:00 a.m. – 5:30 p.m.

A caregiver who excels in this role will:

  • Assist in transporting patients and setting up the OR.
  • Maintain and operate surgical instrument sets and special equipment in the OR.
  • Maintain storage areas in the OR.
  • Coordinate equipment and supplies for service specific surgical cases.
  • Monitor and track the loaning/lending of supplies and equipment.
  • Ensure proper sterile conditions and clean used instruments after surgery.
  • Order supplies, stock, run labs and transport blood and materials.
  • Assist in transporting patients and room turnover.
  • Ensure service specific supply expiration dates are checked monthly.
  • Coordinate and document equipment repairs and loaner return.
  • Work as a liaison to educate staff in the proper use and functioning of equipment.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum qualifications for the ideal future caregiver include:

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Basic Life Support (BLS) certification through American Heart Association (AHA) or American Red Cross

Preferred qualifications for the ideal future caregiver include:

  • Sterile processing certification
  • One year of patient-care experience in a hospital setting

  • Requires full range of body motion to include handling and lifting patients, manual and finger dexterity and eye-hand coordination.
  • Requires standing and walking for extensive periods of time.

title: Security Officer
location: Intermountain Health St Vincent Regional Hospital
description:
Job Description:

The Security Officer provides a safe environment for patients, visitors, employees, and volunteers, typically in an office or ambulatory clinic setting. This position is responsible to monitor visitor or patient activity, monitor the premises in and around the facility , enforce policy, provide assistance and direction, respond to emergencies, and to provide protection for employees, visitors, and Intermountain property.

Essential Functions

  • Operates and monitors security technology systems, including surveillance cameras, access control systems, and alarm systems. Ensures proper functioning and maintenance of security equipment.
  • De-escalation: Security officers use verbal and non-verbal strategies to calm individuals and resolve conflicts peacefully, minimizing the need for physical force.
  • Dealing with Violent Patients: They intervene to protect the safety of everyone involved when patients act aggressively or violently, including using physical restraints when necessary.
  • Regulatory Compliance: Ensuring compliance with regulations such as HIPAA when reporting crimes or incidents, disclosing only the minimum necessary information to law enforcement.
  • Bomb Threat/Suspicious Package Responses: Trained to respond to bomb threats and suspicious packages, following protocols to ensure the safety of the facility.
  • Participation in Drills: Engaging in exercises like infant abduction and active shooter scenarios to prepare staff for real-life situations.
  • Conducting Searches: Performing respectful and safe searches of patients and searching for narcotics, ensuring compliance with legal requirements.
  • Safety Inspections: Conducting inspections of walking surfaces, fire extinguishers, and overall facility safety to mitigate risks.
  • Parking Enforcement: Enforcing parking regulations to ensure safety and accessibility, focusing on enhancing the patient experience.
  • Investigations: Collaborating with HR and law enforcement to conduct investigations, following protocols for disclosing patient information, and ensuring facility safety.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Current Driver’s License (if applicable for the role).
  • Current Basic Life Certification (BLS) for healthcare providers or willing to obtain within 90 days of hire.
  • At least 21 years of age.
  • If located in the State of Montana Security Guard Licensure is required within 120 days of hire.

Preferred Qualifications

  • One-year previous law enforcement, corrections, public safety, military police or security experience.

Physical Requirements

  • Ongoing need for employee to see and read information, labels, monitors, identify equipment and supplies, and be able to assess customer needs.
  • Frequent interactions with customers require employees to communicate as well as understand spoken information, alarms, needs, and issues quickly and accurately.
  • Manual dexterity of hands and fingers to manipulate complex and delicate equipment with precision and accuracy.
  • Expected to lift and utilize full range of movement to transport, pull, and push equipment. Will also work on hands and knees and bend to set-up, troubleshoot, lift, and carry supplies and equipment. Typically includes items of varying weights, up to and including heavy items.
  • For roles requiring driving: Expected to drive a vehicle which requires sitting, seeing and reading signs, traffic signals, and other vehicles.

title: Senior Communications & Visual Design Lead
description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections, where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

At Roche, we are committed to delivering life-changing therapies to patients by scaling cutting-edge digital and data solutions. As a Senior Communications & Visual Design Lead, you are the creative bridge between complex digital transformations and the global organization. You will own the visual identity, storytelling, and communication strategy for our digital initiatives, ensuring our impact is clearly communicated to stakeholders at all levels in Pharma Technical Operations. In this role, you will translate intricate technical roadmaps and data milestones into compelling visual narratives, professional presentations, and engagement campaigns that drive awareness and adoption across the global Pharma Technical Operations (PT) network.

Core Responsibilities

  • Communications Strategy: Develop and execute comprehensive internal communication plans that articulate the vision, progress, and value of digital and data transformation initiatives.
  • Visual Storytelling & Layout: Design and produce high-impact visual content, including executive slide decks, digital assets, infographics, and project collateral, ensuring a consistent and professional aesthetic.
  • Content Creation: Draft, edit, and curate engaging content for various channels, including newsletters, digital signage, Intranet platforms, and team updates.
  • Brand & Identity Management: Maintain and evolve the visual branding for the Digital & Data portfolio, ensuring all outputs align with Roche corporate identity standards.
  • Stakeholder Engagement Support: Partner with the leadership "triad" (Program, OCM, and Digital Leads) to prepare communication materials for town halls, leadership forums, and site-level engagement sessions.
  • Digital Channel Management: Manage and optimize the digital presence of the Digital & Data team on internal platforms, ensuring information is up-to-date, accessible, and user-friendly.
  • Executive Presentation Support: Collaborate directly with senior leadership to design complex data visualizations and performance dashboards that communicate strategic impact to non-technical audiences.
  • Feedback & Metrics: Track communication effectiveness through engagement metrics, gathering feedback to continuously refine our messaging and visual strategy.

Who You Are

You are a creative, detail-oriented professional with a passion for visual communication and storytelling. You possess a unique ability to simplify complex, technical information into intuitive, aesthetically pleasing, and highly effective communications. You thrive in a fast-paced environment where you can partner with technical experts to "show, not just tell" the story of digital transformation. You are highly collaborative, possess impeccable editorial judgment, and understand the importance of tailoring messaging to diverse audiences in a global, matrixed organization.

Qualifications & Expertise:

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Graphic Design, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related field.
  • Professional Experience: Minimum requirements include:
    • 5+ years of experience in corporate communications, internal engagement, or visual design within a complex or multinational corporate environment.
    • Proven experience supporting digital transformation or change management programs is highly desirable.
  • Design & Tool Literacy: Expert proficiency in presentation design (PowerPoint master templates), creative design software (Adobe Creative Cloud, Figma), and information design tools. Experience leveraging AI-assisted workflows for rapid design ideation is an asset.
  • Communication Mastery: Exceptional writing and editing skills, with the ability to convey strategic priorities clearly and concisely to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Project Management: Ability to manage multiple workstreams and design requests under tight deadlines, maintaining high attention to detail and quality standards.
  • Stakeholder Presence: Demonstrated experience working closely with senior leadership and managing sensitive or highly visible project communications.


Who We Are

At Roche, more than 100,000 people across 100 countries are pushing back the frontiers of healthcare. Working together, we’ve become one of the world’s leading research-focused healthcare groups. Our success is built on innovation, curiosity, and diversity.

What We Offer:

  • Impact for Patients: Direct contribution to communicating the global manufacturing and supply chain operations that bring life-saving therapies to millions of patients.
  • Creative Scope: Broad influence over the visual identity and narrative of a high-priority global digital transformation.

Growth & Culture: An empowering environment that values psychological safety, flexible hybrid working models, continuous learning, and personal development.


Who we are

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.


Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Loan Kit Coordinator
description:
Materials Loan Kit Coordinator

The Princess Grace Hospital, London
Full time, 37.5 hours per week
Monday – Friday (8:00am – 4:00pm or 9:00am – 5:00pm)
Permanent
£28,860 per annum plus excellent benefits

We’re looking for a Materials Loan Kit Coordinator to join our Supply Chain team based at The Princess Grace Hospital. This team plays a critical role in supporting surgical services by managing the end-to-end loan kit process for theatre procedures. Loan kits provide essential prostheses, instruments and consumables required for patient surgeries, ensuring clinical teams have access to specialist equipment exactly when it is needed. Working closely with Theatres, Sterile Services, Purchasing, Accounts Payable and external suppliers, the team helps maintain the highest standards of patient care and operational efficiency.

As a Loan Kit Coordinator, you'll be responsible for coordinating the full lifecycle of surgical loan kits, from booking and ordering through to receipt, reconciliation and return. You'll work with theatre teams to ensure the correct kits are available for upcoming procedures, investigate discrepancies, manage supplier relationships and support the accurate processing of documentation and purchase orders. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working in a fast-paced theatre environment and wants to play a visible role in supporting life-changing surgical care. Your attention to detail and ability to build strong relationships will help ensure procedures run smoothly and patients receive the highest quality care.

Above all else, we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life. It’s this guiding vision that influences everything we do at HCA UK. From the CEO to the colleagues on the floor we all have a part to play in delivering exceptional care to our patients. Other’s may think this is just a role in Supply Chain, but to us, you’ll be part of a wider team with a unique sense of purpose, one that helps improve lives on a daily basis.

What you’ll do:

  • Coordinate the end-to-end management of loan kits required for surgical procedures, ensuring kits are available and delivered on time.
  • Review theatre bookings daily and liaise with clinical teams and suppliers to arrange appropriate equipment and prostheses for upcoming cases.
  • Receive, inspect and reconcile incoming loan kits, investigating discrepancies and coordinating resolutions with suppliers and clinical stakeholders.
  • Process purchase orders, requisitions and supporting documentation to ensure the timely payment of suppliers and accurate charging of used items.
  • Support the management of consignment stock, high-value inventory checks and reporting of loan kit activity and exceptions.

What you’ll bring:

  • Experience working within a theatre or surgical hospital environment.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to build relationships across clinical and non-clinical teams.
  • Strong customer service skills and a proactive, solutions-focused approach.
  • Good organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Computer literacy including Microsoft Word and Excel, alongside strong attention to detail.

Why HCA UK?

Originally founded over 50 years ago by Dr Thomas Frist, HCA has gone on to become one of the world’s leading healthcare providers. In the UK, we’re one of the largest providers of privately funded healthcare and have invested over £500 million in the latest treatments, technology, techniques, medication and facilities. Being part of a large multisite, established healthcare group we can offer you unrivalled opportunities for career progression through internal and external courses, as well as working conditions that prioritise both your mental and physical wellbeing.

By caring for our employees, we empower them to provide exceptional care for our patients. That’s why we offer a host of flexible benefits that reflect the invaluable contribution they make every day. As a Loan Kit Coordinator, you’ll be eligible for:

  • 25 days holiday each year (plus bank holidays) increasing with service, with option to buy or sell leave to suit you
  • Private Healthcare Insurance for treatment at our leading hospitals
  • Private pension contribution which increases with length of service
  • Season Ticket Loan and Cycle to Work scheme
  • Group Life Assurance from day one
  • Critical illness cover
  • Enhanced Maternity and Paternity pay
  • Corporate staff discount for all facilities including Maternity packages at The Portland
  • Comprehensive range of flexible health, protection and lifestyle benefits to suit you

description:
Job Title

Mechatronics & Robotics Technician

Job Description Summary

Job Description

At C&W Services, we live by the belief that Better Never Settles. We're dedicated to creating a positive impact globally, and we're looking for talented individuals to join our team.

C&W Services provides compelling benefits, including:

  • Weekly Pay
  • Comprehensive Benefits that start on your first day
  • Training, Development, and Advancement Opportunities
  • A Clean and Cutting-Edge Facility
  • A Safety-First Culture

About the Role

As a Mechatronics & Robotics Technician, you will use your skills to support the Operations Maintenance Team repairing and maintaining material handling equipment and pneumatic systems throughout the building. You will have the opportunity to install, maintain and repair automated packaging and distribution equipment.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Safety: Promote a safe working environment by following all safety procedures.
  • Maintenance: Complete preventative maintenance routines with proper documentation. Troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems related to all Material Handling Equipment (MHE) which includes belts, motors, photo-eyes, relays, and more.
  • Monitoring: Create, assign, and close out work order with data including labor hours, equipment maintenance, and parts used. Track and store department inventory.
  • Support: Mentor junior technicians to grow in their roles.
  • Communication: Maintain positive working relationships across all of the Operations facility.

Basic Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • 2+ years of experience in the repair of material handling equipment (MHE) or automated conveyor systems and controls.
  • 2+ years of experience conducting predictive and preventative maintenance procedures.
  • 1+ years of blueprint and electrical schematic reading.
  • 1+ years of knowledge with electrical and electronic principles.
  • Experience with a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS).
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Project, with the ability to create and manage documents effectively.
  • Ability to work flexible schedules/shifts.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Associates or higher degree from a vocational school or college with a focus on Mechanical or Electrical field.
  • Experience with Material Handling Equipment (MHE) safety standards accordance with Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and Safety standards.
  • Experience with robotic operation and maintenance.
  • Able to troubleshoot basic input and output functions.

Physical Demands:

  • Must have ability to reach overhead, kneel, squat, climb steps/ladders, use an aerial lift, and frequently lift a maximum of 50 lbs. of equipment.
  • Ability to perform tasks wearing appropriate or required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), which may include but is not limited to hard hat, face mask, face shield, and composite toe shoes.
  • Regularly required to crouch or bend and reach to install/move equipment.
  • Involves movement between departments, floors, and properties to facilitate work, averaging 6 to 12 miles per day.
  • Work in a warehouse environment with fluctuating temperatures.
  • Regularly required to type on a computer for 1-2 hours per day.

Why C&W Services?

We're a global company with over 400 offices in 60 countries. We're proud of our diverse family of employees and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We're recognized by the Human Rights Foundation as a Best Place to Work for LGBTQI+ individuals and are dedicated to continuing to build a culture of inclusion and respect.

What’s Next?

Ready to take the next steps in your career? Apply today and be part of a team that is making a difference!

title: Audit - Mid Market - Graduate - Glasgow - September 2027
description:
Forvis Mazars is a leading global professional services network providing audit & assurance, tax, and advisory services. Forvis Mazars in the UK spans 14 offices across the nation and has over 3,400 professionals, with 190 partners. We have a clear purpose and a shared commitment to shape a better future.

See how businesses really work and make an impact from day one.
Audit is about more than numbers. It's about understanding organisations, building trust in financial information, and helping businesses, investors and communities make informed decisions. You'll work with a diverse range of clients, gain insight into different industries, and develop skills that will benefit you throughout your career.
At Forvis Mazars, you'll work towards a professional qualification, learn from experienced professionals, and gain hands-on experience using the latest technology and data-driven tools. With real responsibility, continuous learning, and exposure to a variety of businesses, Audit offers an exciting foundation for a successful career.
Ready to challenge yourself, accelerate your development, and discover how businesses really work? Start your career in Audit with Forvis Mazars and make a difference from day one.

Join our Mid-Market Audit team, working with a diverse portfolio of privately owned businesses, from ambitious start-ups to large international groups. You'll gain exposure to a wide range of industries, helping businesses achieve their goals while developing valuable technical, commercial and client-facing skills.

Hear from our graduate trainee Max:

#LI-DNP

To apply for our Graduate Programme, you’ll need:

  • GCSE Maths and English Language at Grade 4/C (or equivalent qualifications).
  • Achieved a minimum of 112 UCAS tariff points from your top three A Levels, BTECs, Scottish Highers/Advanced Highers, or other recognised Level 3 qualifications.
  • Achieved or predicted a 2:1 degree classification (or equivalent).


We know everyone’s circumstances are different. If exceptional circumstances have affected your academic results, we’ll consider the context you provide as part of your application.

Does this sound like you?

Enjoy working with numbers, analysing data and spotting trends.
Curious about business, financial performance and risk.
A clear communicator who builds strong relationships.
Interested in technology, data analytics and AI in audit.
Adaptable, motivated and eager to learn.
Ready to study towards a professional qualification alongside your role.


What you'll work on:
Support audit engagements by testing financial information and reviewing evidence to help ensure financial statements are accurate and compliant.
Analyse financial data to understand how businesses operate, identify risks and highlight key findings.
Use audit technology, AI-powered tools and data analytics to interpret large volumes of data, identify trends, enhance insights and improve audit quality.
Research accounting and auditing standards and help apply them to client situations in a practical way.
Work closely with clients and colleagues, gathering information, responding to queries and contributing to meetings and reports.
Collaborate with specialists across Audit, Tax and Advisory teams to gain a broader understanding of client challenges and solutions.
Take on increasing responsibility as you develop, building technical expertise, managing your workload and strengthening client relationships.

Your development and benefits:
You don't need prior audit experience before you join. We'll help you build your knowledge through professional study, hands-on client work and ongoing support from your team.

Develop your technical expertise through funded ACA study, structured training and dedicated study leave.
Build digital skills by learning how technology, data analytics and automation are transforming the audit profession.
Learn in a supportive environment with access to a buddy, mentor and experienced colleagues who will help you succeed.
Apply your learning to real client work, gaining practical experience from day one and seeing the impact of your contribution.
Benefit from a balanced approach to study and client work, with regular check-ins, coaching and guidance throughout your programme.

If you're curious, analytical and ready to keep learning, Audit offers the opportunity to develop sought-after skills, work with a diverse range of clients and build your confidence in a career that helps businesses grow, manage risk and maintain trust in financial reporting.

At Forvis Mazars diversity, equity and inclusion are central to our values. We value our people's unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experience, and know this diversity create better outcomes for our clients. We seek to attract, develop, and retain the best talent, inclusive of sex, ethnicity, disability, socio-economic background, sexual orientation, gender identity, nationality, and faith. We select candidates based on skills, knowledge, qualifications, and experience and aim to support all our team members to reach their potential. At Forvis Mazars, we promote an environment in which you can grow your skills, belong to a team that values your ideas, and make an impact that matters.

title: Instrumentation & Controls Technician
description:
Do you envision a workplace where every team member works together to create an amazing workplace experience? Do you want to be part of a dedicated group of professionals who consistently deliver excellence to reach our common goal of a best in class working environment? If you have a positive can-do attitude and a drive for success, Amentum is looking for you! We are seeking an Instrumentation & Controls Tech V team member for our client site in Groton, CT. The successful candidate will have outstanding calibration and maintenance skills and will be committed to working with others to deliver best in class, unparalleled excellence in customer service and satisfaction.


Typical work schedule is 5 8-hour days M-F, days and hours vary based on business demand.


As the Instrumentation & Controls Technician, your daily duties for this role will include:

• Acting as the subject-matter expert in responding to work orders, troubleshooting, and providing calibration service on the production equipment.

• Effectively communicating with the site management team and the end user.

• Identifying and correcting any safety-related issues.

• Performing independent equipment evaluations to identify potential equipment failures.

• Performing General Maintenance of equipment.

• Utilizing software such as DeltaV, AMS, and Valve link to commission and troubleshoot equipment.

• Maintaining and calibrating all instrumentation associated with Water Discharge.

• Maintaining and repairing emissions monitoring and water treatment equipment to ensure all state and federal regulations are met.

• Utilizing strong mechanical and electrical skills to complete assignments.

• Operating various measuring, diagnostic, and testing instruments to help provide energy efficiency solutions.

• Operating a variety of equipment such as hand tools, laptop computers, and diagnostic hardware to perform work.

• Utilizing CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System) to track, schedule, calibrate, and maintain records for process equipment.

• Complying with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).

• Analyzing and resolving work problems or assisting workers in solving work problems.

• Developing and monitoring work assignments for other technicians and coaches.

• Responding and providing service and feedback to the customer on all work orders while assuring compliance to codes, regulations, and industry standards.

• Creating and modifying site operation procedures for equipment and recommending measures to improve maintenance methods and equipment performance.

• Providing regular reports to senior management regarding throughput, performance, issues, and projects.

• Performing other duties as assigned by Management or Lead.

As the Instrumentation & Controls Technician, you will be expected to:

• Work in a team environment with a one team mentality; be friendly, respectful, empathetic, and professional to teammates and clients.

• Value and respect employee authenticity and demonstrate cultural awareness to create a memorable experience and a respectful workplace.

• Balance workload and multiple tasks while focusing on attention to detail and prioritizing assignments.

• Take initiative to resolve issues that arise and solve problems independently; shift priorities as needed or requested by management and remain flexible.


Minimum Requirements

• High school diploma or demonstrated equivalent.

• Six years of experience as an instrumentation and controls technician role including operating and maintaining steam driven turbines for power generation in a pharmaceutical, chemical, industrial, or related laboratory environment, or demonstrated equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Knowledge of Industrial Boiler Operation inclusive of any pressure, temperature, and flow monitoring equipment.

• Knowledge of Steam Turbine Operation working speeds, pressures, and safety protocols with steam driven turbines in a power plant/distribution center.

• Knowledge of Gas Turbine Operations.

• Knowledge of interrelationship between digital controls systems and field instrumentation.

• Knowledge of maintenance and operation of remotely operating valve inclusive of actuator, positioner, and valve itself.

• Ability to maintain monitoring equipment associated with ancillary systems.

• Understanding of process automation and integrated relationship with automated steam and water systems.

• Ability to obtain a security access badge at our client’s location.

• Ability to work overtime, holidays, weekends, and alternative work schedules.

• Ability to obtain an appropriate driver's license issued by the State Department of Motor Vehicles, as requested.

• Must be a United States citizen or permanent resident.

• This position does not include sponsorship for United States work authorization.


Some physical/special requirements include:

• Regularly lift to 50 lbs

• Regularly climb ladders, steps, and scaffolding

• Repetitive motions: bend, stoop, squat, kneel, stretch, reach, wrist movement

• Walk or ride bicycle extensively throughout the plant during shift

• Work at an accelerated pace in emergency conditions

• Ability to differentiate colors pertaining to wire color-coding

• Wear steel toe safety shoes, safety glasses, gloves, hard hats, and other Personal Protective Equipment as needed.

• Cope with demands (stressors) that are associated with the job and/or the work environment.


Preferred Qualifications

• Associate Degree or Technical School Certificate for Instrumentation and/or Electronics.

• ISA level 1 Certification.

• Experience with digital controls systems, PLCs, etc.

• CT E2 or higher license.

• Experience working with Reliability Engineers to determine Root Cause Failure Analysis and discuss vibration findings.

• Hands-on experience with the operation, repair and maintenance of Honeywell, Siemens, and Delta-V control equipment devices.

• Experience working in semiconductor facilities or chemical or pharmaceutical production or research faculties.

• Experience in calibration and repair on instrument transmitters including Pressure, Pressure Differential, Vacuum, Temperature, RH, CO2, Speed, Flow, and Level.

title: Project Manager, Project & Development Services
description:
Job Title

Project Manager, Project & Development Services

Job Description Summary

Provides professional project management experience to designated projects and assignments at a client site, campus, and facilities. Interacts with client representatives onsite, receives direction and coordinates with the property or facility management team. Monitors and coordinates the execution of the various services and processes relating to client contracted agreements for project management and tenant improvements. Works in collaboration with the assigned account manager, building or facility management team, clients, owners and others.

Job Description


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Prepare agendas, develop and maintain master project budgets and timelines as required for each project and project phase to ensure overall project objectives and client needs are met.
  • Keep building management apprised of progress at all times.
  • Prepare and coordinate project reports and drawing reviews for clients, property/facility management team, and project team (as applicable) at conceptual, schematic, design development and construction phases of project.
  • Assist in the selection, contracting process and oversight of consultants and construction teams as necessary for each project.
  • Review requisitions, change orders and other invoices associated with the project and confer with client and property management on costs and impacts.
  • Support the marketing of services to clients as requested.
  • Adhere to corporate, building, and client policies and procedures.
  • Cooperate with other building/facility personnel to achieve goals and objectives as to quality, service, cost and profit.
  • Report to immediate supervisor major problems and findings and results achieved with recommendations.
  • Advise and obtain the necessary approvals from the appropriate members of management of potential organizational changes, actions that might require additional commitments, and the need for expenditures in excess of approved budget.
  • Adhere to government laws and regulations and established rulings of government authorities, including building codes, safety regulations, etc.
  • Maintain high qualitative and quantitative standards of work performance.
  • Strive constantly to improve skill and work knowledge; keep up to date in the field of specialization.

KEY COMPETENCIES

1. Client Focus

2. Communication Proficiency (oral and written)

3. Relationship Management

4. Leadership

5. Multi-Tasking

6. Technical Proficiency

7. Consultation

8. Organization Skills

9. Time Management


IMPORTANT EDUCATION

  • B.S. Degree in Engineering, Architecture


IMPORTANT EXPERIENCE

title: Anesthesia Tech
description:
Job Description

Job Title: Anesthesia Tech
Department: OR
Location: Rochester General Hospital
Hours Per Week: 20
Schedule: 8 hour shifts between 6a-5:30a, Monday-Friday. Weekend on-call requirement.


SUMMARY:
As an Anesthesia Tech, your excellent attention to detail and commitment to quality control helps you to manage anesthesia equipment and supplies, while assisting with daily functions of the Anesthesia Department.


RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Equipment Management. Maintain all anesthesia equipment; manage quality control by recognizing malfunctioning equipment and taking necessary action; perform minor equipment repairs and preventive maintenance
  • Procedure Assistance. Prepare anesthesia equipment and supplies for use; calibrate and check equipment accurately before each use; assist with procedures as assigned; stock anesthesia carts with extremely high-risk medications (may handle meds, sharps and syringes); maintain a clean, safe and adequately supplied workroom
  • Maintains Ideal Working Operations. Contribute to maintenance of supply inventory, ensure there are adequate levels of available supplies and complete monthly pharmacy inspections.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • None.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • H.S. diploma preferred
  • Previous anesthesia experience preferred

EDUCATION:

LICENSES / CERTIFICATIONS:

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Heavy - Clinical - Heavy clinical roles require continual lifting of more than 50 lbs., pushing and pulling patients or equipment, and working in physically awkward or restrictive positions. Staff must maintain balance and coordination in confined, uneven, or emergent care settings while performing both fine and gross motor tasks. High sensory acuity is needed to recognize patient cues and environmental alerts. Emotional and cognitive demands are significant due to urgent decision-making, managing distressed patients, and functioning effectively in high-pressure clinical situations. Environmental exposures commonly include infectious agents, biohazards, noise, and chemicals. Employees may be required to complete mask-fit testing, TB screening, and participate in extended or on-call shifts.

For disease specific care programs refer to the program specific requirements of the department for further specifications on experience and educational expectations, including continuing education requirements.

Any physical requirements reported by a prospective employee and/or employee’s physician or delegate will be considered for accommodations.

Rochester

14621

Does this sound like you?

Enjoy working with numbers, analysing data and spotting trends.
Curious about business, financial performance and risk.
A clear communicator who builds strong relationships.

Adaptable, motivated and eager to learn.

Standard (Mon-Fri)

Office

Pharma Services |Viral Vectors | 5 Commerce Drive, Plainville, MA |100% Onsite Days

How will you make an impact?

This role makes an impact by leading and owning manufacturing investigations; utilizing root cause analysis tools, as required, to identify root causes and contributing factors; supporting and developing consistent manufacturing/quality standards and processes for Deviations and CAPAs in Quality Systems; and conducting complex document revisions and/or document management, including batch production records and manufacturing procedures.

title: Advisor Relations Lead
description:
When you join Verizon

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. At Verizon, we power and empower how people live, work and play by connecting them to what brings them joy. We do what we love — driving innovation, creativity, and impact in the world. Our V Team is a community of people who anticipate, lead, and believe that listening is where learning begins. In crisis and in celebration, we come together — lifting our communities and building trust in how we show up, everywhere & always. Want in? Join the #VTeamLife.

When you Join Verizon:

Verizon is one of the world’s leading providers of technology and communications services, transforming the way we connect across the globe. We’re a diverse network of people driven by our shared ambition to shape a better future. Here, we have the ability to learn and grow at the speed of technology, and the space to create within every role. Together, we are moving the world forward – and you can too. Dream it. Build it. Do it here.


What you’ll be doing:

Focusing on top-tier customer sourcing advisors, vertical influencers, and strategic consulting channels across the Verizon Business ecosystem, you will lead and own the end-to-end Advisor Relations strategy—driving market differentiation, shaping early-stage opportunities, and expanding our large-deal pipeline.


You will serve as a strategic bridge across advisor relations, field sales, marketing, and technical teams—shifting market perception of Verizon from a "pure connectivity provider" to a leading digital transformation and Managed Network Services (MNS) partner. Moving beyond traditional reactive RFP responses, you will build proactive, sole-source engagements with advisors, positioning Verizon early in deal planning cycles to ensure high-margin wins.


Your key responsibilities will include:

  • End-to-End Strategy Ownership & Leadership: Lead, build, and execute the holistic Verizon Business Advisor Relations strategy. This includes establishing channel governance, defining tiering and coverage models for advisory firms, tracking channel performance metrics (invitation rates, win rates, sourced pipeline), and setting the strategic narrative to position Verizon as a preferred transformation partner across the global advisory ecosystem.
  • Proactive Deal Growth & Sole-Source Engagement: Drive proactive growth initiatives directly with key advisors to unlock sole-sourced, uncompetitive opportunities ($10M+ to $25M+ TCV) well ahead of formal RFP cycles. Engage advisors during client discovery phases to co-create transformation roadmaps and position Verizon as the default solution partner before specifications are locked.
  • Strategic Advisor & Vertical Domain Mapping: Systematically map, align, and build deep executive relationships with key sourcing advisors and non-network Vertical Domain Leaders (Manufacturing, Healthcare, Finance, Public Sector) across top-tier advisory firms.
  • Early Deal Shaping & Margin Protection: Partner directly with Field Sales during deal pursuits to influence RFP framing, align solutions with advisor frameworks, provide strategic pursuit coaching, and protect commercial margins early in the sales lifecycle.
  • Technical-to-Commercial Translation: Translate complex technical architectures (SD-WAN, SASE, NaaS, MNS) into compelling commercial and financial value propositions aligned with client CTO and CFO business outcomes.
  • Competitive Counter-Strategy & Market Perception: Defend and grow market share against competitor investments through regular executive briefings, capability workshops, and joint value-proposition sessions that highlight Verizon’s unique MNS value proposition.
  • Unified Messaging & Go-To-Market Alignment: Align advisor relations activities with Verizon’s Analyst Relations, Sales Enablement, and Account-Based Marketing (ABM) teams to drive unified messaging, elevate thought leadership across the advisory community, and maximize channel leverage.

What we’re looking for:

You are a senior-level strategic leader with proven experience owning cross-functional GTM strategies and building trusted relationships at all levels of leadership. You excel at verbal and written communication, comfortably bridging conversations between technical architects, field sales teams, and C-suite decision-makers. You are an innovative, outside-in thinker who transforms advisor insights into actionable business strategy, sole-sourced deal flow, and sustained revenue growth.

You’ll need to have:

  • Bachelor’s degree or 10 or more years of relevant work experience.
  • Experience leading advisor relations or strategic partner strategy, with a proven track record of driving sole-sourced, proactive deal growth ($10M+ to $25M+ TCV).
  • Demonstrated experience mapping and building strategic relationships across tier-1 sourcing advisory firms and vertical domain leaders (e.g., Manufacturing, Healthcare, Finance, Public Sector).
  • Ability to structure and articulate complex technology platforms (SD-WAN, SASE, NaaS, MNS) into high-impact commercial and financial models for C-level executives (CTO/CFO).
  • Experience aligning advisor channels with marketing, analyst relations, and sales enablement programs.
  • Willingness to travel.

Even better if you have one or more of the following:

  • Master’s degree or MBA.
  • Background working directly within or partnering closely with tier-1 management consulting or sourcing advisory organizations (e.g., ISG, Avasant, Wavestone, Everest Group).
  • Proven success developing channel governance, advisor coverage models, and performance tracking frameworks.
  • Strong experience coaching internal deal teams, senior leadership, and subject matter experts on advisor pursuit strategy and competitive RFP framing.

Where you’ll be working

In this hybrid role, you'll have a defined work location that includes working from home and a minimum of three days per week in the office, which will be set by your manager. Employees are responsible for maintaining compliance with hybrid work policies.

Scheduled Weekly Hours

40

Equal Employment Opportunity

Verizon is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to veteran status, disability or other legally protected characteristics.

Benefits and Compensation

Our benefits are designed to help you move forward in your career, and in areas of your life outside of Verizon. From health and wellness benefit options including: medical, dental, vision, short and long term disability, basic life insurance, supplemental life insurance, AD&D insurance, identity theft protection, pet insurance and group home & auto insurance. We also offer a matched 401(k) savings plan, up to 8 company paid holidays per year and up to 6 personal days per year, paid parental leave, adoption assistance and tuition assistance, plus other incentives, we’ve got you covered with our award-winning total rewards package. Depending on the role, employees have the opportunity to receive compensation in the form of premium pay such as overtime, shift differential, holiday pay, allowances, etc. Newly hired employees receive up to 15 days of vacation per year, which grows with additional service. For part-timers, your coverage will vary as you may be eligible for some of these benefits depending on your individual circumstances.

The salary will vary depending on your location and confirmed job-related skills and experience. This is an incentive based position with the potential to earn more. For part-time roles, your compensation will be adjusted to reflect your hours.

title: Packing and Crating Specialist
description:

Ensures compliance with Performance Work Statement (PWS) and Amentum ISO 9001 Quality Management System (QMS).

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Loads/offloads all 463L pallets, containers and trucks in a timely manner.

  • Inventories and inspects all incoming freight for damage prior to acceptance. Reports discrepancies to supervisor.

  • May use automated computer systems and programs to process and document all freight.

  • Operates and positions Material Handling Equipment (MHE), wide body loaders and cranes to load/offload trucks, containers and pallets in accordance with prescribed procedures.

  • Maintain publications, forms, and files required for traffic management and air terminal operations, as required.

title: Property Adjuster Specialist - Field CAT Claims
description:
Why USAA?

At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.

The Opportunity

As a dedicated Property Adjuster Specialist, you will work within defined guidelines and framework, investigate, evaluate, negotiate, and settle complex property insurance claims. You will confirm/analyze coverage, recognize liability exposure and negotiate equitable settlement in compliance with all state regulatory requirements. You will recognize and empathize with members' life events, as appropriate.


The dedicated catastrophe team supports members affected by severe weather events. Property Adjuster Specialist focus on using technology and desk adjusting for a virtual first approach to inspections and claims handling. USAA also provides a company vehicle to physically inspect losses within your locally assigned territory. Field Adjusters may travel outside of their local territory to respond to claims in other regions when needed. This hourly, non-exempt position is eligible for paid overtime.


The is a local field-based role in Fort Worth, TX. Candidates who are able to work in the South of Fort Worth area are encouraged to apply.


What you'll do:

  • Proactively manages assigned claims caseload comprised of complex damages that require commensurate knowledge and understanding of claims coverage including potential legal liability.
  • Partners with vendors and internal business partners to facilitate complex claims resolution. May also involve external regulatory coordination to ensure appropriate documentation and compliance.
  • Investigates claim damages by conducting research from various sources, including the insured, third parties, and external resources.
  • May identify and resolve potential discrepancies and identifies subrogation potential resulting from unusual characteristics.
  • Identifies coverage concerns, reviews prior loss history, determines and creates Special Investigation Unit (SIU) referrals, when appropriate. Determines coverage through analyzing information involving complex policy terms and contingencies.
  • Determines and negotiates complex claims settlement within authority limits. Develops recommendations and collaborates with management for determining settlement amounts outside of authority limits and accurately manages claims outcomes.
  • Maintains accurate, thorough, and current claim file documentation throughout the claims process.
  • Advance knowledge of estimating technology platforms and virtual inspection tools.
  • Utilizes platforms and tools to prepare claims estimates to manage complex property insurance claims.
  • Supports workload surges and catastrophe (CAT) response operations as needed, including mandatory on-call dates and potential evening, weekend, and/or holiday work outside normal work hours.
  • May be assigned CAT deployment travel with minimal notice during designated CATs.
  • Works various types of claims, including ones of higher complexity, and may be assigned additional work outside normal duties as needed.
  • Works independently solving complex problems with minimal guidance; acts as a resource for colleagues with less experience.
  • Adjusts complex claims with attorney involvement.
  • Recognizes and addresses jurisdictional challenges such as applicable legislation and construction considerations.
  • May require travel to resolve claims, attend training, and conduct in-person inspections.
  • Ensures risks associated with business activities are effectively identified, measured, monitored, and controlled in accordance with risk and compliance policies and procedures.



What you have:

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalency Diploma.
  • 2 years of relevant property claims adjusting experience of moderate complexity losses that includes writing estimates, involving dwelling and structural damages.
  • Advanced knowledge of estimating losses using Xactimate or similar tools and platforms.
  • Proficient knowledge of residential construction.
  • Proficient knowledge of property claims contracts and interpretation of case law and state laws and regulations.
  • Proficient negotiation, investigation, communication, and conflict resolution skills.
  • Proven investigatory, analytical, prioritizing, multi-tasking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to travel 50-75% of the year (local & non-local) and/or work catastrophe duty when needed.
  • Acquisition and maintenance of insurance adjuster license within 90 days and 3 attempts.
  • Successful completion of a job-related assessment may be required.

What sets you apart:


  • Experience on a Property Catastrophe team handling field claims (i.e. wind, hail, hurricane, flooding)
  • Experience adjusting large loss complex property claims caused by catastrophic events
