title: Calibration Technician
location: AMP The Woodlands Corporate Office - The Woodlands, TX 77380
description:
Calibration Technician

Job Description

Department: Quality

Job Status: Full-Time

FLSA Status: Salary, Non-Exempt

Reports To: QMS Manager

Location: The Woodlands, Texas

Amount of Travel Required: 25%

Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 8 a.m. - 5 p.m.

Positions Supervised: N/A

AIP Level: 7

POSITION SUMMARY: The Calibration Technician is responsible for maintaining the integrity of the company’s calibration program within the Digital Quality Management System (QMS). This role owns the calibration register for quality critical instruments used in vertically integrated electric pressure pumping services, which includes gas conditioning equipment, aeroderivative turbines and reciprocating engines for generating power, and pressure pumping equipment (blender, pumps, etc.).

Working under the direction of the QMS Manager, the Calibration Technician ensures that all Testing, Measuring, Monitoring, and Detection Equipment (TMMDE) is identified, controlled, calibrated, labeled, and documented in accordance with company procedures, customer requirements, and applicable standards. This role is critical in ensuring measurement accuracy, reducing risk of equipment related nonconformances, and supporting safe, reliable field operations.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: (The following duties and responsibilities are all essential job functions, as defined by the ADA, except for those that begin with the word "may")

  • Maintains the calibration register within the Digital QMS, ensuring all applicable devices are entered, current, and traceable.
  • Identifies and registers new measurement and test equipment used in operations (e.g., pressure transducers, flowmeters, torque wrenches, electronic measuring devices such as cable meggers, AVRs, multimeters, temperature probes, and other gauges).
  • Schedules, tracks, and coordinates calibration activities for inhouse and third party (external) calibration services, ensuring calibrations are performed on time.
  • Ensure third party calibration service providers are qualified to perform the calibration per OEM or industry standards.
  • Reviews calibration certificates for completeness, accuracy, and compliance (e.g., traceability, as found/as left data, ranges, tolerances, environmental conditions).
  • Uploads and maintains calibration certificates, records, and documentation in the Digital QMS, ensuring they are correctly linked to each device in the register.
  • Ensures all calibrated devices are properly labeled/stickered with calibration status, due date, and unique identification.
  • Monitors upcoming calibration due dates and proactively communicates with stakeholders (Quality, Operations, Maintenance, Field Leadership) to minimize downtime and avoid use of out of calibration equipment.
  • Initiates and documents nonconformance records within the QMS if devices are found out of tolerance, used beyond their calibration date, or otherwise non compliant.
  • Assists in root cause investigations related to measurement or instrumentation issues that may impact product/service quality or safety.
  • Works closely with field and maintenance personnel to ensure appropriate storage, handling, and use of calibrated equipment to maintain accuracy and prevent damage.
  • Performs visual checks and basic functional checks on measuring and test equipment before and after calibration as applicable.
  • May perform in house verification or basic calibration tasks, as qualified and authorized, using approved standards and procedures.
  • Generates and distributes periodic calibration reports and metrics (e.g., on time calibration rate, overdue items, out of tolerance findings) to the QMS Manager and Quality leadership.
  • Supports audits (internal, customer, and third party) by providing calibration records, demonstrating QMS functionality, and explaining calibration control processes.
  • Recommends improvements to calibration processes, intervals, and device selection to enhance reliability and reduce nonconformances.
  • Assists with training or orientation of operations and maintenance personnel on calibration requirements and proper handling of measurement devices.
  • Performs other duties as assigned to assist with successful operations and business continuity.

At AstraZeneca, Finance does more than report performance—it helps shape the choices that advance science and deliver life-changing medicines. Join a business that values bold thinking, recognizes impact, and invests in long-term careers.

title: Leadership Rotation Associate
description:
POSITION OVERVIEW

Schuyler Line Navigation Company is looking for driven, curious associates in to join our Leadership Rotation Program (LRP) - a 12-month structured development track built to grow our bench of future company leaders.

This isn't a shadowing program. As an Associate – Leadership Rotation (LRA), you'll take on real, accountable work across four core functions of our business, build genuine cross-functional fluency in the maritime industry, and graduate the program ready for a possible permanent placement on the team.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Over 360 days, you'll rotate through four departments, spending 90 days in each:

Finance: Get hands-on with AP/AR, general accounting, invoicing, and budgeting - building the numbers-based view of the business that grounds everything else you'll do as an Associate – Leadership Rotation (LRA),

HSQE / Technical: Dig into our Safety Management System, regulatory compliance, and technical/maintenance planning.

Operations: Own pieces of voyage planning, crewing coordination, vessel scheduling, and port operations as an Associate – Leadership Rotation (LRA),

Commercial: Get exposure to chartering, client relationships, freight negotiation, and market analysis.

In each rotation, you'll set goals with your supervisor, take ownership of real deliverables, and keep a rotation logbook to track your growth.

As an Associate – Leadership Rotation (LRA), you won't be figuring this out alone:

You'll experience structured check-ins with HR every 45 days, plus formal close-out reviews at the end of each rotation

There will be warm handoffs between supervisors at every transition, so you're never starting from zero

You'll be paired with a senior Executive Mentor - someone outside your direct chain - for independent monthly career coaching throughout the year.

There is a defined path forward - the program culminates in a possible permanent placement conversation around day 360.

QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree required.

Experience with Office 365 (Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel) preferred.

Able to successfully pass a post-offer background check.

Able to demonstrate exceptional attention to detail

Able to solve problems proactively.

Able to work discreetly and professionally with confidential and sensitive information.

Able to be adaptable and effective in fast-paced, growing environments

Able to demonstrate a collaborative, team-first mindset with a positive, solution-focused approach.

The selected candidate must possess access to a reliable form of transportation with the ability to work in the office during standard business hours Monday – Thursday, with a one-hour lunch, unless an alternate schedule is approved. This includes the option to work from home on Fridays during standard business hours with a one-hour lunch, unless an alternate schedule is approved. This position is expected to perform work outside and beyond normal working hours during times of critical deadlines, projects, or when there are time-sensitive duties.

COMPANY OVERVIEW

Headquartered in West Palm Beach, FL, Schuyler Line Navigation Company (SLNC) is a U.S.-flagged maritime transportation and logistics provider specializing in commercial and government cargo services.

With a commitment to operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and financial discipline, SLNC ensures secure and efficient transportation solutions for defense, energy, and commercial customers. We operate in some of the most remote and austere environments globally, offering door-to-door logistics solutions tailored to our customers' needs.

SLNC offers competitive pay, an exceptional culture and a generous benefits package.

By applying to this position, you consent to your application materials being processed through Indeed Talent Scout, Indeed Smart Sourcing, and associated AI/LLM tools as part of our application process.

Schuyler Line Navigation Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Applicants must be currently authorized to work for any employer in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

Forvis Mazars in the UK spans 14 offices across the nation and has over 3,400 professionals, with 190 partners. We have a clear purpose and a shared commitment to shape a better future.

See how businesses really work and make an impact from day one.
Audit is about more than numbers. It's about understanding organisations, building trust in financial information, and helping businesses, investors and communities make informed decisions. You'll work with a diverse range of clients, gain insight into different industries, and develop skills that will benefit you throughout your career.
At Forvis Mazars, you'll work towards a professional qualification, learn from experienced professionals, and gain hands-on experience using the latest technology and data-driven tools. With real responsibility, continuous learning, and exposure to a variety of businesses, Audit offers an exciting foundation for a successful career. Ready to challenge yourself, accelerate your development, and discover how businesses really work? Start your career in Audit with Forvis Mazars and make a difference from day one.

About our team:
Join our Mid-Market Audit team, working with a diverse portfolio of privately owned businesses, from ambitious start-ups to large international groups. You'll gain exposure to a wide range of industries, helping businesses achieve their goals while developing valuable technical, commercial and client-facing skills.

Hear from our graduate trainee Max:
“I've really enjoyed the combination of on the job learning and studying. There is a great network of people from dedicated learning and development teams to my people manager and buddy to support with the transition from university'
#LI-DNP


To apply for our School Leaver Apprenticeship, you’ll need:

  • GCSE Maths and English Language at Grade 4/C (or equivalent qualifications).
  • Achieved or predicted a minimum of 112 UCAS tariff points from your top three A Levels, BTECs, Scottish Highers/Advanced Highers, or other recognised Level 3 qualifications.

We know everyone’s circumstances are different. If exceptional circumstances have affected your academic results, we’ll consider the context you provide as part of your application.

Does this sound like you?

Enjoy working with numbers, analysing data and spotting trends.
Curious about business, financial performance and risk.
A clear communicator who builds strong relationships.
Interested in technology, data analytics and AI in audit.
Adaptable, motivated and eager to learn.
Ready to study towards a professional qualification alongside your role.


What you'll work on:
Support audit engagements by testing financial information and reviewing evidence to help ensure financial statements are accurate and compliant.
Analyse financial data to understand how businesses operate, identify risks and highlight key findings.
Use audit technology, AI-powered tools and data analytics to interpret large volumes of data, identify trends, enhance insights and improve audit quality.
Research accounting and auditing standards and help apply them to client situations in a practical way.
Work closely with clients and colleagues, gathering information, responding to queries and contributing to meetings and reports.
Collaborate with specialists across Audit, Tax and Advisory teams to gain a broader understanding of client challenges and solutions.
Take on increasing responsibility as you develop, building technical expertise, managing your workload and strengthening client relationships.

Your development and benefits:
You don't need prior audit experience before you join. We'll help you build your knowledge through professional study, hands-on client work and ongoing support from your team.

Develop your technical expertise through funded ACA study, structured training and dedicated study leave.
Build digital skills by learning how technology, data analytics and automation are transforming the audit profession.
Learn in a supportive environment with access to a buddy, mentor and experienced colleagues who will help you succeed.
Apply your learning to real client work, gaining practical experience from day one and seeing the impact of your contribution.
Benefit from a balanced approach to study and client work, with regular check-ins, coaching and guidance throughout your programme.

If you're curious, analytical and ready to keep learning, Audit offers the opportunity to develop sought-after skills, work with a diverse range of clients and build your confidence in a career that helps businesses grow, manage risk and maintain trust in financial reporting.

title: 2027 Intern - Strategic Risk Management
description:
Company

Federal Reserve Bank of DallasWe are dedicated to serving the public by promoting a strong financial system and a healthy economy for all. These efforts take a team of dedicated individuals doing many different jobs. Together we’re creating a workplace where talented people can thrive, and we welcome your unique background and perspective to help present the best possible solutions for our partners.

Location: #LI-Onsite. If you need assistance or a reasonable accommodation, please notify your Talent Acquisition Consultant.

ABOUT THE DALLAS FED:


At the Dallas Fed we serve the public by partnering with communities and businesses, promoting jobs and stable prices, and keeping your money safe and available. We welcome different perspectives, ideas, and experiences. As part of the nation’s central bank, we are committed to improving the economy and our communities. Are you ready to make a difference?

Learn more about the Dallas Fed: .

ABOUT THE INTERNSHIP PROGRAM:


The Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas Internship Program is a prestigious, cohort-based experience that attracts top talent from across the country for paid, full-time summer internships spanning majors and functional areas – from economic research and finance to Cash Services, IT, and beyond. While interns take on a specific functional role for the summer with meaningful work and opportunities to grow, the program offers much more than a single assignment. Dedicated staff mentors help launch your career, and curated cohort programming provides broad exposure to central banking, direct access to senior leaders and industry experts, and dedicated learning and development opportunities. As part of the Federal Reserve System, you'll also build a professional network of peers that spans the nation. The program runs approximately for 10-12 weeks, beginning in mid-to-late May and concluding in August. For this specific position, you will be located in the Dallas office.

Learn more about our internship program: .


ABOUT YOUR TEAM:


The Strategic Risk Management (SRM) team consists of two main functions – Internal Controls and Enterprise Risk Management (ERM). Internal Controls performs quarterly testing on controls that have a direct impact to our financial statements to ensure they are free from any material misstatement. Enterprise Risk Management aids in effectively managing risks to our mission critical operations which includes collaborating with business areas to identify, assess, monitor, and report on organizational risk as well as serve in an advisory capacity to senior leaders and the Bank’s Risk Management Committee (RMC).


WHAT YOU’LL DO:


  • Gain knowledge and basic understanding of above-mentioned teams and their general processes
  • Support the Internal Controls team by performing controls testing of various business areas
  • Support the ERM team by researching topics in preparation of RMC or other advisory group meetings
  • Support teams in creating or updating materials and documentation and recommending improvements as requested

WHAT YOU BRING:

  • Junior or Senior student majoring in Accounting, Finance, Risk, Business or related field
  • Proficient in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, SharePoint
  • Excellent analytical and communication skills, both verbal and written
  • Equivalent education and/or experience may be substituted for any of the above requirements

OUR BENEFITS:


  • Professional development opportunities
  • Broader networking opportunities across District
  • Downtown location with free parking
  • 24/7 on-site fitness center (Dallas & Houston Offices)
  • On-site café and coffee shop

WORK HOURS:


Monday – Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. (40 hours/ week). Some additional hours may be required.

NOTES:

Participation in our internship program is a valuable learning opportunity and does not guarantee future employment.

Applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S and the role is not available for sponsorship.


If you need special accommodation during your interview process, please notify your Talent Acquisition Consultant.

Please submit applications by Friday, October 23rd.

title: AI/ML for Biology Scientist
description:
Job Description Summary

Diseases of Aging & Regenerative Medicine (DARe)

DARe is seeking a talented AI/ML for Biology Scientist to advance the discovery of transformative therapies for diseases of aging. The role will integrate human genetics, longitudinal health data, multi-omics, imaging and functional biology with modern machine learning to uncover human disease mechanisms and identify, prioritize and validate therapeutic targets for diseases of aging with a focus on neurogenerative and cardiovascular diseases.


Job Description


Internal Job Title: Senior Expert I/II Data Science

Position Location: San Diego, CA Hybrid

About the Role:

Aging is the biggest risk factor for chronic diseases. The new AI for biology scientist will advance DARe’s mission to discover novel transformative therapies for diseases of aging by integrating at scale human pathobiology, experimental science and machine learning.

The role will develop, evaluate and apply machine-learning approaches across human genetics, longitudinal EHR cohorts, high resolution multi-omics technologies, cellular imaging and functional data to uncover disease mechanisms and drive therapeutic target identification, prioritization and validation. The successful candidate will combine strong biological insight with expertise in modern machine learning, including representation learning, multimodal methods, biological foundation models and reproducible model-development workflows.

Working in a global, multidisciplinary environment, the new team member will partner with biologists, disease experts and data scientists to shape experimental strategies, build scalable analytical workflows and translate complex biomedical data into testable hypotheses and actionable evidence for drug discovery.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Partner closely with experimental scientists to understand biological questions and design data-driven approaches to answer them.
  • Apply expertise in computational biology, human genetics, machine learning and AI approaches to support target identification, prioritization and validation for disease of aging.
  • Contribute to the design of large-scale experiments and data-generation strategies across genetics, multi-omics, imaging and functional biology.
  • Integrate diverse biological datasets to uncover disease mechanisms and generate therapeutic hypotheses.
  • Help establish reproducible and scalable computational workflows and analytical approaches that accelerate discovery across DARe.

Essential Requirements:

  • PhD in Computational Biology, Human Genetics, Bioinformatics, Data Science, Machine Learning, Systems Biology or a related quantitative discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience applying computational and ML approaches to biomedical research, translational science or drug discovery.
  • Hands on experience with modeling and analyzing diverse biomedical data types including genetic, single cell, perturbation datasets, spatial transcriptomics, and cellular imaging.
  • Experience evaluating, adapting, and applying biological foundation models to biomedical research, particularly RNA, DNA, single-cell, or spatial data.
  • Experience with Model deployment (MLops) and agentic frameworks Strong programming skills in Python and R and proficient in working in modern data-science environments and developing reproducible workflows.
  • Experience integrating complex biological datasets and translate into actionable insights.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with experimental scientists.
  • Demonstrated curiosity, learning agility and willingness to work across disciplines.

Desirable Requirements:

  • Strong experience in human genetics, including GWAS, rare variant analysis, Mendelian randomization, colocalization or fine mapping.
  • RWE experience including longitudinal human cohorts, EHRs and disease progression modelling.
  • Familiarity with biomedical knowledge graphs, representation learning or multimodal learning.
  • Familiarity with biomedical ontologies, FAIR data principles and data harmonization.
  • Experience with biological aging clocks.

Compensation & Benefits:


The salary for this position is expected to range between $126,000 and $234,000 USD annually for Senior Expert I, Data Science, and $138,600 and $257,400 USD annually for Senior Expert II, Data Science. The final salary offered is determined based on factors like, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience, and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. Novartis may change the published salary range based on company and market factors.


Your compensation will include a performance-based cash incentive and, depending on the level of the role, eligibility to be considered for annual equity awards.


US-based eligible employees will receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, life and disability benefits, a 401(k) with company contribution and match, and a variety of other benefits. In addition, employees are eligible for a generous time off package including vacation, personal days, holidays and other leaves.


To learn more about the culture, rewards and benefits we offer our people click here.

We do not discriminate in recruitment, hiring, training, promotion or other employment practices for reasons of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital or veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.


Accessibility and reasonable accommodations

Please include the job requisition number in your message.

title: Administration Supervisor
description:
Job Title: Administration Supervisor
Location: London Canary Wharf
Full time: 37.5 hours per week
Permanent: Monday to Friday onsite
Salary: £33k to £36k per annum

We’re looking for an Administration Supervisor to join our HCA UK Team based on a client site in Canary Wharf. You will be responsible and accountable for the management of any logistical tasks and the Front of House (FOH) team within the onsite client clinic.


You will be required to travel to Glasgow quarterly (travel and accommodation will be paid)


You will ensure strong relationships with the HCA Primary Care FOH and administrative management teams, to deliver an effective, consistent service to the client.

This is an interesting and exciting role where you will also collaborate with the client account management team and onsite clinical team to deliver a high-quality patient journey.

You will report to the Practice Manager and be trained to deputise for them when required. We are looking for applicants who want to learn and grow and who have career aspirations. Are you ambitious? This could be just the role for you!


Above all else, we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life. It’s this guiding vision that influences everything we do at HCA UK. From the CEO to the colleagues on the floor we all have a part to play in delivering exceptional care to our patients. Other’s may think this is just a role in (team), but to us, you’ll be part of a wider team with a unique sense of purpose, one that helps improve lives on a daily basis.

What you’ll do:

  • Deliver excellent customer service and ensure the front of house department fulfils this objective
  • Ensure the department adheres to all patient safety standard operating procedures and codes of conduct in line with GDPR and HCA policies.
  • Be visible, accessible, and approachable to staff, patients and vendors
  • Perform as a professional role model, driving high standards, mentoring and developing the team.
  • Carry out all reasonable tasks as required by Operational Services Manager

What you’ll bring:

  • Expertise in dealing with complaints both face to face and over the telephone, professionally and with empathy
  • Ability to manage two Senior Receptionists
  • Ambition to learn and grow in your role
  • Ability to work in a high-level corporate environment and work face to face with our client, listening to their requirements and actioning
  • Knowledge of health and safety, safeguarding and GDPR
  • Minimum of 2 years experience in front of house or admin
  • Approachable demeanour
  • Able to work as part of a team

Why HCA UK?

Originally founded over 50 years ago by Dr Thomas Frist, HCA has gone on to become one of the world’s leading healthcare providers. In the UK, we’re one of the largest providers of privately funded healthcare and have invested over £500 million in the latest treatments, technology, techniques, medication and facilities. Being part of a large multisite, established healthcare group we can offer you unrivalled opportunities for career progression through internal and external courses, as well as working conditions that prioritise both your mental and physical wellbeing.

By caring for our employees, we empower them to provide exceptional care for our patients. That’s why we offer a host of flexible benefits that reflect the invaluable contribution they make every day. As a (job title) you’ll be eligible for:

  • 25 days holiday each year (plus bank holidays) increasing with service, with option to buy or sell leave to suit you
  • Private Healthcare Insurance for treatment at our leading hospitals
  • Private pension contribution which increases with length of service
  • Season Ticket Loan and Cycle to Work scheme
  • Group Life Assurance from day one
  • Critical illness cover
  • Enhanced Maternity and Paternity pay
  • Corporate staff discount for all facilities including Maternity packages at The Portland
  • Comprehensive range of flexible health, protection and lifestyle benefits to suit you
  • Discounts with over 800 major retailers

Culture and values


At HCA UK we believe exceptional care starts with our people. We celebrate the unique perspectives and different experiences each of us bring as we know that when you feel seen, heard and supported you can be at your best for our patients, and each other.

Our mission is simple, above all else we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life, a clear statement that extends to both our patients and colleagues. To achieve this, we live and breathe four core values:

Installing, splicing, testing, repairing and maintaining the technology that keeps millions of customers connected. Be part of a team that makes a profound impact every single day by ensuring that our fiber-optic network performs reliably. Because here, better matters.

You know telecommunications construction and are anxious to put your knowledge and skills to work on Verizon’s network. You like to be busy and well-organized to stay on top of things. You know that the whole team needs to work together to win—and you take pride in a job well done.

title: Network Compliance & Risk Administrator
location: Reliance Rx Specialty Pharmacy Management, LLC
description:
FIND YOUR FUTURE

We're excited about the potential people bring to our organization. You can grow your career here while enjoying first-class perks, benefits and a culture that fosters growth, innovation and collaboration.

Overview

The Network Compliance and Risk Administrator shall be responsible for the overall execution, administration and monitoring of the compliance program as it relates to technical risk/cybersecurity, data governance and integrity, and data related law and regulation compliance to necessitate companywide adherence. The Network Compliance and Risk Administrator shall support various contract and regulatory activities and ensure the organization’s technical systems, processes and data handling comply with laws, regulations, and industry standards. They will report to the Deputy Counsel-Regulatory Compliance Manager and under their direction will be the liaison between Reliance Rx business units, the parent company Information Risk Office, related departments and applicable outside vendors or regulatory bodies related to these compliance matters.

They will conduct regulatory research and analysis as it relates to proposed, pending or effective laws, rules, and regulations impactful to Reliance Rx cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, data governance and integrity, information privacy and security, and interoperability. They will assess and implement appropriate industry standard cybersecurity frameworks and related processes to ensure adequate hardening and protection of the Reliance Rx environment. The position will work closely with the Reliance Rx Leadership Team to ensure leadership is appraised of and in compliance with regulations governing Reliance Rx programs, as well as work closely with the pharmacy team and internal audit to ensure compliance with relevant regulations.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required. An additional four (4) years of experience will be considered in lieu of degree.
  • Four (4) years of experience in compliance, quality assurance, auditing, or data governance/process management within a regulated environment required. Healthcare or pharmacy-related experience preferred.
  • Experience with data security, encryption, data masking, DLP technologies, data discovery and classification tools, and data privacy, including cloud access security broker (CASB) solutions.
  • Experience in framework and architecture of cloud and multi-tenant environments, including AWS.
  • Industry recognized certification within the domain of information security, information technology and privacy (e.g., CISSP, GIAC, CISM, CIPT, CIPP/US, etc.) preferred.
  • Understanding of healthcare privacy program core elements as it relates to regulatory oversight, monitoring requirements and data security measures (HITRUST, NIST, ITIL, HIPAA, HITECH, etc.)
  • Advanced experience with Microsoft Office applications and ability to learn new software applications.
  • Excellent research skills and ability to exercise independent judgement to determine which changes in regulatory landscape should be presented in collateral and training.
  • Excellent analytical skills, ability to analyze components of legislation and implement and draft necessary policies and procedures based upon regulatory requirements.
  • Excellent composition and drafting skills, with emphasis on various compliance/regulatory documents and correspondence.
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, and excellent interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively build and maintain relationships with both internal and external stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in performing necessary research and preparing substantive work which requires knowledge of compliance concepts, with emphasis on HIPAA/HITECH.
  • Possess initiative, creativity, project management and organizational abilities.
  • Proven examples of displaying the Reliance values: Collaborative, Accessible, Results-Oriented, Empowering, Supportive.

Essential Accountabilities

  • Research state and federal statutes and regulations concerning data privacy and handling such as, but not limited to state privacy laws, HIPAA/HITECH, DSCSA, PCI DSS; and monitor and track for any changes or updates.
  • Research and maintain an understanding of the compliance obligations of our team, including, but not limited to: HIPAA/HITECH, data privacy and security, cybersecurity industry practices, cloud environment protection, and artificial intelligence, and shall provide recommendations to Reliance Rx leadership to communicate, as appropriate.
  • Monitor emerging artificial intelligence laws, regulations, and industry guidance; assess organizational use of AI technologies for compliance with applicable regulatory, privacy, security, and governance requirements.
  • Research and present appropriate cybersecurity certifications to Reliance Rx leadership, and where implemented initiate and maintain such certifications and the requirements.
  • Support tracking and monitoring of contractual technical risk maintenance and compliance processes to ensure adherence with key contract terms and conditions.
  • Facilitate coordination with parent Information Risk Office, and other relevant departments as needed during negotiation and review of Reliance Rx contracts containing technical compliance, HIPAA/HITECH, and related security terms.
  • Support RFP requests and other contractually required cybersecurity assessments and questionnaires.
  • Coordinate and support third-party security risk assessments, including vendor due diligence reviews, cybersecurity questionnaires, and remediation tracking.
  • Support the development, implementation, communication, and continuous improvement of Reliance Rx's technical compliance, privacy, cybersecurity, and information security programs in collaboration with parent company Compliance and Information Risk teams.
  • Manage technical compliance policies, procedures, standards, and related governance processes, including regulatory review, updates, documentation, and organizational communication.
  • Develop and maintain cybersecurity risk management processes, including security assessments, incident response planning, risk tracking, vulnerability management, and remediation oversight.
  • Monitor and report on technical compliance, cybersecurity, privacy, and security metrics, key risk indicators, regulatory requirements, and program effectiveness.
  • Coordinate technical compliance training, security awareness initiatives, onboarding, annual education, attestations, and assessments for associates.
  • Oversee the identification, investigation, escalation, reporting, and remediation of technical compliance, privacy, and security incidents, including corrective action plans.
  • Collaborate with business, operational, and technical teams to establish and monitor data governance, data protection, access management, retention, and security controls.
  • Coordinate cybersecurity testing and monitoring activities, including vulnerability assessments, penetration testing, phishing simulations, endpoint monitoring, and risk reviews, ensuring timely remediation and leadership reporting.
  • Serve as the primary liaison between Reliance Rx and parent Compliance and Information Risk functions for technical compliance, privacy, security, audits, investigations, assessments, and regulatory inquiries.
  • Facilitate compliance committee activities, risk exception reviews, security governance processes, and related reporting requirements.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for associate technical compliance, privacy, and security inquiries, concerns, and reporting.
  • Promote organizational awareness of technical compliance, privacy, and cybersecurity requirements through ongoing communication, education, and engagement initiatives.

This is a hybrid position with onsite attendance required at our Williamsville location.

Immigration or work visa sponsorship will not be provided for this position

Hiring Compensation Range: $70,000 - $90,000 annually

Compensation may vary based on factors including but not limited to skills, education, location and experience.


In addition to base compensation, associates may be eligible for a scorecard incentive, full range of benefits and generous paid time off. The base salary range is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

Position Type

Staff

Make an Impact at Dallas College

Dallas College is seeking a passionate and detail-oriented Compliance Specialist to help ensure an inclusive, accessible, and equitable learning environment for all students. In this role, you will serve as a key resource for disability compliance, accessibility services, and age discrimination complaint processes, helping students and employees navigate complex situations with professionalism, empathy, and integrity.

As a trusted partner across the college, you will collaborate with stakeholders throughout the organization to promote compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, and other applicable regulations. Your work will directly support Dallas College's mission of transforming lives and strengthening communities through education.


What You'll Do

  • Serve as a primary resource for escalated student accommodation concerns and disability-related compliance matters.
  • Partner with Accessibility Services to support equitable access and ensure compliance with ADA and Section 504 requirements.
  • Build strong working relationships with teams across the college, including Accessibility Services, Human Resources, Student Rights and Responsibilities, and Academic Compliance.
  • Review policies, procedures, and practices related to student accommodations and recommend enhancements to align with legal requirements and best practices.
  • Develop and manage the intake process for age discrimination claims and collaborate with Human Resources on case resolution and process improvements.
  • Deliver training and educational programs that promote awareness of disability inclusion, accessibility, and compliance requirements.
  • Analyze accommodation and complaint data to identify trends, recommend improvements, and enhance the student and employee experience.
  • Conduct quarterly and annual reviews of escalated complaints and provide recommendations to strengthen programs and services.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality when handling sensitive student and employee information.
  • Support initiatives, committees, or student organizations that promote accessibility, disability awareness, and inclusive practices across the college.

What You'll Bring

  • Knowledge of ADA, Section 504, accessibility practices, and compliance principles within education, human resources, or related environments.
  • Strong problem-solving, conflict resolution, and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to interpret regulations, policies, and procedures and apply them to complex situations.
  • Experience analyzing data and identifying opportunities for continuous improvement.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, including the ability to train and educate diverse audiences.
  • Commitment to fostering equity, inclusion, and student success.






Position / Job Summary

The Compliance Specialist applies current regulations and best practices in the resolution of escalated compliance complaints and coordinated services for students with disabilities and accessibility needs, as defined under the 1990 Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Section 504 of the l973 Rehabilitation Act for Dallas College. The Compliance Specialist serves as the primary liaison with Accessibility Services, the primary intake of Age Discrimination in Employment Act claims, state and federal regulations and as a resource to Dallas College campuses. This role plays a vital part in advancing the college’s commitment to transforming lives and communities through higher education by maintaining equity and compliance.


Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Facilitates resolution between the institution and students with escalated Accessibility Services accommodation issues and ADA and Section 504 compliance programs.
  • Establishes and maintains collegial and programmatic relationships with Accessibility Services, Student Rights and Responsibilities, Academic Compliance and Human Resources.
  • Reviews and make recommendations, as required, on published policies, procedures and protocols on student accommodation, ensuring policies are consistent with legal mandates related to disability in higher education settings.
  • Provides training, professional development, and serves as a resource to all campus constituencies regarding sensitivity to disabilities and emerging trends in accommodation rights and services.
  • Develop, implement and maintain intake process of age discrimination claims and collaborate with Human Resources to identify process improvement and resolution opportunities.
  • Collects, analyzes, and uses data on accommodation requests and best practices to inform and improve services to support student success.
  • Collaborates with Accessibility Services to review and analyze data, identify trends, and recommend modifications to practices and protocols that improve student-centered practice.
  • Conducts quarterly and end-of-year evaluation of escalated complaints to assess the areas of concern and provide improvement recommendations.
  • Assures the highest level of confidentiality for all service providers, which reflects the privacy rights of all students registered with Accessibility Services and employees.
  • May serve as advisor to student organizations which promote institution-wide understanding of disability issues.
  • Required Dallas College Professional Development Hours per Academic Year.
  • All employees are required to complete a minimum of 19 hours.
  • People leaders are required an additional 16 hours of leadership development.
  • Perform other duties not listed as assigned.

  • Drive high performance by administering the performance management process timely, setting clear expectations, conducting performance evaluations, and implementing initiatives that enhance employee engagement, motivation, and retention.

  • Four (4) years of professional and supervisory experience in Education, Higher Education, Human Resources, Compliance or Vocational Rehabilitation

title: Theatre Practitioner - Recovery

Theatre Practitioner – Recovery
Location: London, The Princess Grace Hospital
Hours: Full time, 37.5 hours per week

On-call: Approximately 3 days per month and 1 in 6 weekends

We’re looking for a Theatre Practitioner – Recovery to join our Theatre team at The Princess Grace Hospital in London. This is an opportunity to be part of a highly specialised surgical environment where clinical excellence, innovation and compassionate care come together. With eight theatres across two floors, including three dedicated robotic surgery theatres and two recovery suites, the hospital delivers a broad range of complex procedures across specialties including spinal, orthopaedic and robotic surgery. Working alongside leading consultants and multidisciplinary teams, you’ll have access to advanced technology and the support needed to develop your skills within one of the UK’s most respected private hospitals.


As a Theatre Practitioner – Recovery within our Theatre department, you’ll play a key role in supporting patients through one of the most critical stages of their surgical journey. Our recovery team provides expert post anaesthetic care, ensuring every patient is closely monitored and supported following surgery. Working in a fast paced and collaborative environment, you’ll assess, monitor and respond to patients’ clinical needs while partnering closely with anaesthetists, surgeons and theatre colleagues. Exposure to a varied and complex caseload, combined with the latest surgical techniques and technologies, provides excellent opportunities to further develop your recovery and perioperative expertise.


At HCA UK we care about what you care about. We care that you want to deliver the very best care. We care that you want a career you can be proud of. We care that you want working conditions that support your health and wellbeing. Let us care for you and your career, the same way you do for others.


What you’ll do:

  • Deliver safe and effective post operative care for patients recovering from anaesthesia and surgery
  • Monitor, assess and respond appropriately to changes in patient condition during the recovery phase
  • Work collaboratively with anaesthetists, surgeons and theatre teams to ensure seamless patient care
  • Maintain accurate clinical documentation and support compliance with clinical governance standards
  • Contribute to the smooth running of recovery services while promoting a positive and supportive team culture

What you’ll bring:

  • Current NMC or HCPC registration
  • Previous experience working within a theatre recovery environment
  • Strong knowledge of post anaesthetic care, airway management and patient monitoring
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills
  • A commitment to delivering outstanding patient care within a fast paced clinical setting

Why HCA UK?

Originally founded over 50 years ago by Dr Thomas Frist, HCA has gone on to become one of the world’s leading healthcare providers. In the UK, we’re one of the largest providers of privately funded healthcare and have invested over £500 million in the latest treatments, technology, techniques, medication and facilities. Being part of a large multisite, established healthcare group we can offer you unrivalled opportunities for career progression through internal and external courses, as well as working conditions that prioritise both your mental and physical wellbeing.

We believe that by caring for our colleagues, we empower them to provide exceptional care for our patients. That’s why we offer a host of flexible benefits that reflect the invaluable contribution they make every day. As a Theatre Practitioner – Recovery, Theatre Department you’ll be eligible for:


  • 25 days holiday each year (plus bank holidays) increasing with service, with option to buy or sell leave to suit you
  • Private Healthcare Insurance for treatment at our leading hospitals
  • Private pension contribution which increases with length of service
  • Season Ticket Loan and Cycle to Work scheme
  • Group Life Assurance from day one
  • Critical illness cover
  • Enhanced Maternity and Paternity pay
  • Corporate staff discount for all facilities including Maternity packages at The Portland
  • Comprehensive range of flexible health, protection and lifestyle benefits to suit you
  • Discounts with over 800 major retailers

Culture and values

At HCA UK we believe exceptional care starts with our people. We celebrate the unique perspectives and different experiences each of us bring as we know that when you feel seen, heard and supported you can be at your best for our patients, and each other. Our mission is simple, above all else we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life, a clear statement that extends to both our patients and colleagues. To achieve this, we live and breathe four core values:

  • Unique and Individual: We recognise and value everyone as unique and individual
  • Kindness and compassion: We treat people with kindness and compassion
  • Honesty, integrity and fairness: We act with absolute honesty, integrity and fairness
  • Loyalty, respect and dignity: We trust and treat one another as valued members of the HCA UK family with loyalty, respect and dignity

Reasonable adjustments

We believe everyone should feel comfortable to bring their full self to work and be afforded the same opportunities. As a Disability Confident committed organisation, we’re happy to discuss flexible working arrangements to suit your needs as well as offer reasonable adjustments throughout our recruitment process, and in the workplace, to anyone that needs them.

title: Lead Data Scientist, Operations Research
description:
The Lead Data Scientist, Operations Research leads optimization, forecasting and decision modeling for Sensata's operations, starting with Supply Chain and extending to Procurement and Engineering. The role turns complex problems in inventory, planning, scheduling and cost into production models that change how planners, buyers and engineers make decisions. It also sets the data science standards for operations AI use cases. The role also supports enterprise data science needs as priorities arise.

General Responsibilities
• Oversees developing innovative product solutions to continuously drive value for the customer
• Leads development project teams by defining data needs
• Advises on insights to customer challenges
• Identify valuable data sources and efficient collection processes
• Analyze large data sets to discover trends and value driven insights
• Leads predictive models and algorithms
• Oversees development processes and tools to analyze model performance and data accuracy
• Communicate complex findings and ideas using data visualization techniques

Experience / Qualifications
• A university degree required (i.e. Bachelors degree) or equivalent relevant work experience.
• Must be a team player able to work in a fast-paced environment with demonstrated ability to handle multiple competing tasks and demands
• Strong communication skills; oral, written and presentation
• Strong organization, planning and time management skills to achieve results
• Strong personal and professional ethical values and integrity
• Holds self-accountable to achieving goals and standards
• Proficient in Microsoft Office programs (Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel)
• Strong interpersonal & collaboration skills to work effectively with all levels of the organization including suppliers and/or external customers

Additional Responsibilities:

  • Lead data science modeling and approach for variety operations use cases, incl. Supply Chain, from framing the problem through production and adoption.
  • Build optimization models for inventory policy, multi-echelon safety stock, item segmentation, capacity and production planning, and lab/test scheduling.
  • Build demand forecasting and signal-reliability models for noisy customer and EDI demand.
  • Develop should-cost and spend analytics to support Procurement decisions.
  • Design empirical tests to evaluate vendor and planning-platform models, and hold vendors to agreed performance thresholds.
  • Set standards for modeling, validation and backtesting. Define retraining and monitoring requirements with the AI Platform/MLOps team.
  • Work directly with planners, buyers and business leaders so models are adopted and improve inventory, service and cost.
  • Give technical direction and mentoring to data scientists and AI engineers working on operations use cases.

Additional Qualifications:

  • 7+ years building optimization, ML and statistical models for operational problems, with models deployed and in sustained use.
  • Deep operations research expertise: linear and mixed-integer programming, constrained optimization, inventory theory, scheduling and simulation.
  • Hands-on experience with optimization solvers and frameworks (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX, OR-Tools, Pyomo).
  • Strong time-series forecasting skills, including hierarchical and probabilistic methods and rigorous backtesting.
  • Strong Python and SQL; comfortable working with raw ERP, EDI and manufacturing data.
  • Experience in manufacturing, automotive, industrial or distribution supply chains strongly preferred.
  • Able to challenge and influence senior leaders and vendors with evidence.
  • Master's or PhD in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Statistics, Applied Mathematics or a related field preferred.

title: Surgical Tech, Family Birth Center (4706)
location: Trinity Health Hospital Campus & Medical District - Minot, ND 58701
description:
Position Summary:

The Family Birth Center, Surgical Technician provides direct support during obstetric surgical procedures, including cesarean sections, while also assisting with daily operational tasks within the Labor & Delivery unit. This dual role includes maintaining sterile techniques during surgeries, preparing and organizing surgical instruments, stocking supplies, and performing clerical support tasks to help ensure efficient workflow and patient safety. The role ensures proper handling of equipment and supplies, contributes to infection prevention practices, and supports accurate count procedures and documentation in accordance with established surgical protocols. Working closely with nurses, physicians, and other members of the care team, the Surgical Technician plays an important role in maintaining a well-coordinated surgical environment focused on safe, high-quality patient care. As part of a collaborative Labor & Delivery team, this role relies on clear communication, mutual support, and shared accountability to help maintain smooth surgical operations, while contributing to an organized unit environment that supports optimal patient outcomes and dependable departmental workflow.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Prepare and maintain sterile surgical fields for labor and delivery procedures.
  • Select, assemble, and organize surgical instruments and supplies according to physician preference and procedure requirements.
  • Assist surgeons and nurses during operative deliveries by passing instruments and maintaining aseptic techniques.
  • Ensure proper cleaning, sterilization, and storage of instruments post-procedure.
  • Respond promptly to emergency situations in the labor and delivery unit.
  • Stock and maintain inventory of supplies and equipment in patient rooms and surgical suites.
  • Perform clerical tasks such as chart preparation, order entry, and documentation support.
  • Transport patients, specimens, and equipment as needed.
  • Assist nursing staff with patient care tasks.
  • Maintain cleanliness and readiness of labor and delivery rooms.

description:

Job Description

This is a site based role at our global headquarters in Foster City, CA. We do offer a hybrid environment with three days onsite (Tues-Thurs) and two optional work from home days.


Core Responsibilities
Champions the development and adoption of data collection, analysis, and visualization within the group
Drives organizational maturity along the “data journey”; from raw data, to information, to insights, to action and results
Develops and owns the knowledge management system(s) to enable efficient storage, retrieval, and analysis of key data
Sets “best practice” related to data governance; responsible for the stewardship of data accuracy and validation of data provided by the organization
Supports data-driven business planning and review processes within the organization
Undertakes Operations Research projects to identify opportunities to optimize performance and minimize cost / risk
Publishes analyses, reports and dashboards to provide an objective view of performance and risk
Quantifies and reports gains from projects identified / implemented

Risk Management
Ensures compliance with data governance standards
Develops internal processes to ensure rigorous and systematic data curation
Quantifies and communicate risks associated with routine and non-routine business operations
Escalates issues related to data accuracy and compliance as necessary

Financial
Manages, in partnership with Finance, the annual business planning cycle (LE process) for operational and capital expenditures within the organization
Performs in-depth analyses to identify cost optimization opportunities and formulate recommendations to realize efficiencies
Establishes and develops financial benchmarks for projects and operations

Business Partnering
Partners cross-functionally to develop leading indicators that allow visibility into performance and risk
Works proactively with internal partners as well as external vendors to drive the adoption of KPI’s and metrics in day to day work
Continuous Improvement
Infuses external knowledge and expertise to adopt new methods of analyzing and presenting data
Creates training plans and materials, and conducts workshops on analytical tools and initiatives to increase knowledge within the team


Knowledge & Skills
Must have extensive experience with data analysis and business performance reporting
Must be highly analytical and comfortable working on complex problems in a variety of situations where analysis is required
Proficient at collecting, analyzing and visualizing data. Familiar with tools such as R, Python, and Tableau that promote effective and evidence based managerial decision-making
Able to develop schemes, systems, and programs for continuous improvement
Proficient at planning and scheduling own and direct reports activities to accomplish objectives and goals
Experience dealing with multiple budgets across a variety of currencies
Excellent written and interpersonal skills.
Effective communicator; experienced and proficient at presenting to various groups and levels
Experience with people management supported by a proven track record in managing change


Education & Experience
Relevant university degree in a technical or business field such as computer science, statistics, data management, engineering, business or finance
12 years progressive experience in a technical field with Bachelors or 10+ Years with Masters level of education
Advanced analytical skills; experience managing complex business problems and able to simplify ambiguous data sets to glean meaningful insights
Strong financial acumen; experience developing and monitoring large budgets and expenditures in multiple currencies
Extensive experience in business performance reporting and optimization with a track record in creating and improving processes and systems
Ability to build effective working relationships across functions and to be a change agent and influence without authority
Knowledge and experience of working within the Pharmaceutical, or a highly regulated, sector
Excellent report writing and presentation skills
Excellent interpersonal, leadership and conflict resolution skills

title: Technical Product Owner – System & Data Integration
description:

The Position

About the Role
As a Technical Product Owner (TPO), you hold technical, architectural, and operational ownership of assigned modules within the Data Computation Platform (DCP). Bridging high-level platform vision and hands-on software execution, you translate business requirements into robust technical designs, direct engineering backlogs, and drive fast, reliable digital solution delivery. Depending on your assigned module, your work will range from open-source analytics to GxP-validated applications, partnering with validation specialists when compliance applies.


Key Accountabilities
● Define and execute the technical vision, architecture, database schemas, and
release roadmaps for assigned platform modules.
● Translate business and analytics requirements into actionable technical user stories and manage sprint backlogs using Scrum or SAFe.
● Lead module technical design, microservice architecture, containerization
(Docker/Kubernetes), and API integrations with industrial data sources (e.g., AVEVA PI, LIMS, MES).
● Oversee CI/CD release pipelines, system health, and level-3 technical support
escalations.
● Act as the primary technical contact for Computerized System Validation (CSV) teams on regulated modules to align test cases, supply specifications, and streamline compliant deployments.
● Collaborate closely with peers across the team and contribute technical support across modules when needed.


Required Skills & Experience
● Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field.

● 5+ years of experience in software engineering, technical product ownership, or solution architecture.
● Strong software development background in languages such as Python, R, C#, or modern JS frameworks (Vue/Angular).
● Proven experience with microservices, RESTful APIs, relational data modeling, and containerization frameworks.
● Practical familiarity with pharmaceutical GxP regulations, 21 CFR Part 11, Data Integrity, or CSV workflows.
● Demonstrated success directing engineering teams and managing technical
backlogs in Agile environments.
● Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.


Nice-to-Have
● Practical integration experience with manufacturing execution systems, SCADA, or AVEVA PI.
● Hands-on experience automating test execution within modern CI/CD deployment pipelines

A healthier future drives us to innovate.   • Policy and Procedure

title: Undergraduate Research Assistantship - The American Girl magazine
description:
Serve as an undergraduate research assistant on the project: Defining American Girlhood Through American Girl Magazine’s Invitations to the Past.

The American Girl magazine, initially produced by The Pleasant Company and later published by Mattel, ran from 1992-2019. In its first seven years, the magazine included a one-page section called "Imagine," which featured a historical painting accompanied by a narrative snapshot of a historical moment in American history. Pleasant Company is most well-known for its American Girl historical characters and dolls. However, the magazine also included many opportunities to explore the American past. In “Imagine,” where each column begins with “Imagine you…,” girl readers are invited to insert themselves into the past. This research project explores what the brand sought to communicate to girls about American history, gender, social class, and race. This analysis is situated in the brand’s history; it was in this era that the brand released its first African American Doll and first Latina doll and began to publicly consider how to address issues such as colonialism and racism as well as drew upon the popular girl power narrative.

The research assistant will:

  • Gather and summarize peer reviewed sources as well as identify content to support thematic development

* You must have Federal Work Study funding added to your awards BEFORE applying for this position. You are potentially eligible for Work Study if you are a US Citizen or permanent resident, have filed a FAFSA, are enrolled in at least 6 credits, and are in good academic standing.

This position requires the following:

  • Must be Work Study eligible
  • Must be interested in art history, American history, visual arts and/or girls' media
  • Must be able to locate, evaluate, and synthesize peer-reviewed sources (e.g., journal articles, exhibition catalogues, scholarly books) and be familiar with academic databases
  • Must have strong written communication, attention to detail, ability to organize information, ability to meet deadlines and work independently with minimal supervision, and willingness to work with librarians to find sources

Instructions to find your Work Study eligibility status:

  • Log into your MyPacePortal and click on “Student Home” and then the “Financial Aid” box (middle of screen).
  • Once in Financial Aid, select the “Award Offer” tab and the correct Award Year.
  • Scroll down to “Options to Pay Net Cost” and take a screenshot of the funds that are allocated specifically to Work Study for the academic year. Make sure your name is captured in the screenshot, then upload the screenshot, and submit it along with your application.

* If these details are not available in the “Award Offer” section of your profile, you are NOT currently eligible for Work Study funding. If you are a US citizen or permanent resident, and you have filed a FAFSA, you can open a Help Desk ticket with Financial Aid to determine your Work Study eligibility.

  • Audit WMS records against physical product attributes to ensure complete traceability and compliance with quality standards

We are seeking an experienced Data Engineer to design, build, and support enterprise-scale data platforms and data integration solutions within Microsoft Azure environments.

This role is suited to a hands-on data professional with strong experience across data engineering, data warehousing, cloud-based analytics platforms, and modern data architectures. You will work closely with business stakeholders, solution architects, analysts, and development teams to deliver high-quality, trusted, and scalable data solutions that support reporting, analytics, and business decision-making.

You will play a key role in designing and optimising data pipelines, improving data quality, implementing governance controls, and driving best practices across the data ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and maintain scalable and reliable data pipelines and ETL/ELT processes.
  • Build and support Azure-based data platforms and enterprise data solutions.
  • Develop data integration frameworks to ingest, transform, and deliver data from multiple source systems.
  • Implement and support solutions using Azure Data Factory (ADF), Azure Databricks, Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS), Azure Synapse Analytics, and Azure SQL.
  • Design and optimise data warehouse and lakehouse architectures.
  • Develop data transformation logic using Python, PySpark, and SQL.
  • Create and maintain reusable data engineering frameworks, pipelines, and automation processes.
  • Perform data modelling activities to support reporting, analytics, and operational requirements.
  • Manage large-scale structured and unstructured datasets across cloud platforms.
  • Monitor, troubleshoot, and optimise data pipelines to ensure performance, reliability, and scalability.
  • Conduct root cause analysis and resolve complex data-related issues.
  • Implement data validation, reconciliation, and quality assurance processes.
  • Develop monitoring and alerting mechanisms to proactively identify data issues.
  • Support data migration and modernisation initiatives.
  • Collaborate with business and technical stakeholders to gather and analyse requirements.
  • Translate business requirements into scalable technical solutions and data models.
  • Implement and maintain data governance, security, and compliance controls.
  • Ensure adherence to enterprise standards, privacy requirements, and data management policies.
  • Produce technical documentation, data dictionaries, solution designs, and operational runbooks.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and cloud data platform best practices.
  • Work within Agile delivery teams and participate in sprint planning, stand-ups, reviews, and retrospectives.

What You'll Need

  • Minimum 5 years' experience in Data Engineering, Data Warehousing, or a related data-focused role.
  • Demonstrated experience designing, developing, and maintaining scalable data pipelines and integration solutions.
  • Strong hands-on experience with the Microsoft Azure Data Platform, including:
    • Azure Data Factory (ADF)
    • Azure Databricks
    • Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS)
    • Azure Synapse Analytics
    • Azure SQL
  • Strong experience with SQL development, performance tuning, database optimisation, and query troubleshooting.
  • Proven experience in data modelling for enterprise data platforms and analytics solutions.
  • Strong understanding of ETL/ELT methodologies and modern cloud-based data architectures.
  • Experience developing solutions using Python, PySpark, and/or Scala.
  • Experience managing data quality, validation, monitoring, reconciliation, and issue resolution processes.
  • Strong understanding of data governance, security, privacy, and compliance requirements.
  • Experience working with large and complex datasets in enterprise environments.
  • Ability to produce high-quality technical documentation and solution designs.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • Experience working within Agile and cross-functional delivery teams.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience designing modern cloud-native data platforms and lakehouse architectures.
  • Knowledge of data governance frameworks, master data management, and metadata management practices.
  • Experience with DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure-as-code practices.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience supporting enterprise reporting, analytics, and business intelligence initiatives.
  • Exposure to government, regulated, or highly secure environments is highly regarded.

Why Join Us?

  • Deliver large-scale Azure data and analytics transformation programs.
  • Work with leading cloud technologies including Azure Databricks, Synapse Analytics, and Data Factory.
  • Partner with architects, data specialists, and business leaders on strategic initiatives.
  • Contribute to modern data platform, governance, and analytics uplift programs.
  • Join a consulting culture focused on innovation, technical excellence, and continuous improvement.
  • Access exciting projects across government and enterprise organisations throughout Australia and New Zealand.

title: Emo Nite - Design Intern
description:
Job Summary:

WHO ARE YOU?

Do you have a deep-rooted love for emo, pop-punk, and alternative music? Are you a creative thinker with a passion for fostering community and delivering unforgettable experiences? If so, you might be just the person we're looking for! We're in search of a driven, innovative individual who shares our dedication to celebrating the emo scene and promoting authentic self-expression. Sound like you? Keep reading...


WHO ARE WE?

Emo Nite has become a cultural phenomenon, uniting fans of emo, pop-punk, and alternative music in a series of unforgettable events. What started as a single party in a dive bar in East L.A. and has since blossomed into a recurring celebration in over 50 cities across the United States. Our events bring together music lovers, artists, and pop culture icons, creating a space for nostalgia, discovery, and community-building.


Emo Nite has come a long way since that first party in 2014, hosting full-day festivals and curating performances at major events like Coachella, Lollapalooza, Bonnaroo, and Firefly. Alongside our events, we've launched successful clothing collaborations with well-known brands, solidifying our presence as a driving force pushing the emo and alternative culture scene forward.


At Emo Nite, we believe in the power of music to bring people together and create lasting connections. Join our team and help us continue to evolve and expand, making the scene more inclusive and vibrant than ever before.


THE ROLE

Emo Nite is looking for a highly motivated and proactive intern to join the design team in Calabasas, CA. This position will be a hands-on experience in an exciting, fast-paced, setting. This is not a remote position.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Templatizing tour materials (for example refreshing/changing dates, guest artists, announces, etc)
  • Resizing existing materials for specific markets/needs
  • Preparing materials for print
  • Organizing still/video files for distribution to clients/partners/reps
  • Sourcing stock footage, images and fonts from media libraries as needed
  • Assist onsite at Emo Nite events where needed
  • Assist with other duties as assigned

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Knowledge and interest in music industry, emo music, and Emo Nite’s brand preferred
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build relationships across departments and functions
  • Strong time management skills
  • Strong technical skills in Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace
  • Strong technical skills in Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator.
  • Experience in Adobe After Effects and Premiere is a plus.
  • Knowledgeable about current design trends, fonts, color palettes and layouts preferred
  • Eager to learn about and experiment with new technologies and techniques



WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Must be able to tolerate loud noise levels & busy environments in dynamic work locations
  • May work in drastic temperature climates while on site at events
  • Must be willing to travel to work during holidays, evening and weekend hours, as required, to meet deadlines

Applicants for employment in the U.S. must possess work authorization, which does not require sponsorship by Emo Nite for a visa.
