title: Vice President, AI Innovation & Partnerships
description:
Position Purpose: Leads Centene's AI innovation and strategic technology partnerships function, providing enterprise technical leadership for the highest-value AI use cases and shaping partner platforms/harnesses evolve to meet Centene's needs. Works directly with business, data, engineering, security, and governance leaders to manage complex opportunities where AI can materially improve outcomes, redesign workflows, or create new enterprise capabilities. Accountable for translating those opportunities into executable technical strategies, reference architectures, prototypes, and scaled solutions that combine Centene data and context with foundation models, agents, tools, and vendor platforms. Serves as the senior technical counterpart to business partners, influencing product roadmaps, defining joint development priorities, and ensuring vendor harnesses remain interoperable, extensible, observable, and aligned to Centene's AI control plane and enterprise architecture. Advises executive leadership on emerging AI capabilities, technical tradeoffs, partnership strategy, and where Centene should build, buy, partner, or co-develop.


AI Innovation and High-Value Use Case Leadership

  • Sets the enterprise agenda for data context and AI innovation, focusing resources on high-value use cases where advanced AI can materially improve member outcomes, operating performance, or medical cost management.
  • Partners with executive business and technology leaders to frame complex problems, test whether AI is the right solution, and translate priority opportunities into clear technical hypotheses, target workflows, and measurable outcomes.
  • Leads multidisciplinary teams through discovery, rapid prototyping, technical validation, and production architecture, balancing speed of learning with security, reliability, governance, and long-term maintainability.

Vendor Harness Strategy and Partnerships

  • Owns the technical strategy for Centene's use of vendor AI harnesses, defining the capabilities these platforms must provide and how they should integrate with Centene's data, context, identity, security, model, and observability services.
  • Serves as the senior technical counterpart to strategic AI vendors, shaping joint roadmaps, co-development priorities, platform extensions, and commitments required to support Centene's highest-value use cases.
  • Evaluates emerging vendor capabilities through technical diligence, architecture reviews, prototypes, and competitive testing, separating demonstrated capability from product claims and recommending where Centene should build, buy, partner, or co-develop.
  • Drives the evolution of vendor harnesses toward open, composable, and portable patterns, including support for multiple models, reusable agents and tools, enterprise context, standard protocols and APIs, evaluation, tracing, cost attribution, and lifecycle controls.
  • Partners with Procurement, Legal, Security, Enterprise Architecture, and AI Governance to ensure strategic agreements support technical interoperability, responsible AI, data protection, auditability, roadmap influence, and protection of Centene intellectual property and context.

Architecture, Engineering, and Scaled Adoption

  • Defines how priority AI solutions use Centene's AI control plane, agentic framework, AI Gateway, enterprise context layer, trusted data products, and existing engineering platforms.
  • Establishes technical quality standards for prototypes and production solutions, including evaluation, testing, security, reliability, observability, model and prompt change management, and operational ownership.
  • Works with platform and engineering leaders to identify gaps exposed by priority use cases and convert those needs into platform roadmap priorities.
  • Ensures innovation efforts transition into durable products with clear ownership, support models, adoption plans, performance measures, and value tracking rather than remaining disconnected pilots.
  • Maintains a disciplined view of the external AI market, identifies capabilities with strategic relevance to Centene, and runs focused experiments to determine when emerging technology is ready for enterprise use.

Executive and Team Leadership

  • Advises senior leadership on AI technology trends, architecture choices, vendor dependencies, investment priorities, and the practical implications of rapidly changing model and platform capabilities.
  • Represents Centene in strategic technology partnerships and external forums, strengthening relationships with leading AI companies, startups, research organizations, and industry partners while bringing relevant learning back into the enterprise.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
  • Comply with all policies and standards.

Education/Experience:

  • Requires a Bachelor's degree,12+ years of related experience, including significant leadership experience in artificial intelligence, machine learning, enterprise architecture, technology strategy, product innovation, software engineering, cloud platforms, data and analytics, or a related discipline.
  • Or equivalent experience acquired through accomplishments of applicable knowledge, duties, scope and skill reflective of the level of this position.
  • 10+ years experience leading enterprise technology initiatives, AI/ML solutions, software engineering, cloud platforms, data and analytics, enterprise architecture, or technology strategy, including executive-level leadership responsibilities required.
  • Demonstrated experience translating complex business opportunities into scalable technical solutions through AI, automation, advanced analytics, and emerging technologies preferred.
  • Experience working within healthcare, managed care, or other highly regulated industries, including implementation of secure, compliant, and scalable AI solution preferred.

Pay Range: $207,000.00 - $392,100.00 per year

At Centene, we connect people to the care they need to live healthier lives — and the work you do here makes that impact real every day. You’ll take on meaningful challenges that directly support individuals, families, and communities, building your skills while making healthcare more accessible and effective. It’s work with a purpose you can see, backed by a team committed to improving lives well beyond the workday.

Centene offers a comprehensive benefits package including: competitive pay, health insurance, 401K and stock purchase plans, tuition reimbursement, paid time off plus holidays, and a flexible approach to work with remote, hybrid, field or office work schedules. Actual pay will be adjusted based on an individual's skills, experience, education, and other job-related factors permitted by law, including full-time or part-time status. Total compensation may also include additional forms of incentives. Benefits may be subject to program eligibility.

Centene is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, and values the ways in which we are different. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other characteristic protected by applicable law.


Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered in accordance with the LA County Ordinance and the California Fair Chance Act

title: Planer proizvodnje
description:
Job descriptions may display in multiple languages based on your language selection.

What we offer:

At Magna, you can expect an engaging and dynamic environment where you can help to develop industry-leading automotive technologies. We invest in our employees, providing them with the support and resources they need to succeed. As a member of our global team, you can expect exciting, varied responsibilities as well as a wide range of development prospects. Because we believe that your career path should be as unique as you are.

Group Summary:

As an engineering and manufacturing partner, Magna’s Complete Vehicle group helps traditional OEMs and new entrants to bring their automotive visions to life. At Magna, you will work in an innovative, international and dynamic team, always pursuing the goal of delivering high-quality products. We work in a diverse environment with global development opportunities. Together with our employees we constantly strive to create a better world of mobility.

Job Responsibilities:

Namen delovnega mesta:


Zagotavljanje kakovostnega digitalnega načrtovanja in vizualizacije za proizvodne, logistične in infrastrukturne projekte z integracijo 2D/3D načrtov, BIM-modelov, podatkov laserskega skeniranja in podatkov o dejanskem stanju objektov. Delovno mesto podpira učinkovito koordinacijo projektov ter prispeva k nenehnemu izboljševanju standardov in metodologij na področju Factory Planning in BIM.


Ključne naloge in odgovornosti:


• Priprava in posodabljanje 2D in 3D postavitev za proizvodne in infrastrukturne projekte.

• Razvoj načrtovalskih konceptov za proizvodne objekte, logistična območja in stavbe.

• Integracija in koordinacija strokovnih modelov.

• Izvajanje preverjanja kolizij (clash detection) in kontrole kakovosti podatkov.

• Uporaba podatkov laserskega skeniranja in podatkov o obstoječem stanju za potrebe načrtovanja.

• Priprava dokumentacije za interno usklajevanje in postopke pridobivanja soglasij oziroma dovoljenj pri pristojnih organih.

• Vizualizacija variant načrtovanja in napredka projektov.

• Vzdrževanje in nadaljnji razvoj digitalnih podatkov o dejanskem stanju objektov in naprav.

• Sodelovanje pri nadaljnjem razvoju metod in standardov na področju Factory Planning in BIM.


Zahtevana izobrazba

• Zaključena tehnična izobrazba (srednja, višješolska ali visokošolska) s področja: gradbeništva, strojništva, arhitekture, ali primerljive tehnične smeri.


Delovne izkušnje

• Najmanj 3 leta ustreznih delovnih izkušenj na področju: Factory Planning, BIM, 2D/3D načrtovanja postavitev, ali primerljivega tehničnega načrtovanja.

• Izkušnje z modeli izvedbe projektov Design-Build in EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction).


Strokovna znanja

• Osnovne izkušnje pri načrtovanju industrijskih, infrastrukturnih ali visokogradbenih projektov.

• Izkušnje z CAD sistemi, predvsem: AutoCAD, Revit.

• Poznavanje BIM, načrtovanja tovarn in proizvodnih procesov.

• Izkušnje z laserskim skeniranjem.

• Izkušnje iz avtomobilske industrije.


Druge kompetence

• Zelo dobro poznavanje programov Microsoft Office: Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook.

• Poznavanje: Autodesk Revit, Navisworks, Forma (Autodesk Construction Cloud).


Osebne kompetence

• Podjetniški način razmišljanja.

• Visoka stopnja samoiniciativnosti, samomotivacije in odločnosti.

• Strukturiran in k rešitvam usmerjen način dela.


Potovanja

• Službena potovanja po potrebi.


Jezikovna znanja

• Angleški jezik (tekoče)

• Nemški jezik (osnovno)


Naša ponudba:

• edinstvena korporativna kultura, za katero sta značilna kolegialnost in timski duh,

• mednarodno in raznoliko okolje ter politika odprtih vrat

• dolgoročna perspektiva v mednarodnem podjetju,

• zanimiva in raznolika paleta nalog,

• možnosti osebnega in profesionalnega razvoja,


Delovno okolje:

title: PRODUCTION CONTROL SUPERVISOR
description:

The Production Control Supervisor is a hands-on position responsible for leading the day-to-day
activities of the Production Control team while directly performing production planning and
scheduling. This position oversees the execution of production planning activities and coordinates
customer demand, manufacturing capacity, material availability, inventory, and production
priorities to maintain executable production schedules and meet customer delivery requirements.

coordinates closely with cross-functional teams to communicate priorities and proactively resolve
issues affecting production flow and customer commitments.

activities.

availability and inventory levels, and identify shortages. Coordinate with relevant teams
across the organization to maintain production flow and resolve delivery issues.

including work orders, production priorities, inventory transactions, and system updates,
ensuring accurate and timely information.

title: Software Architect, Scheduling
description:
Join us as we work to create a thriving ecosystem that delivers accessible, high-quality, and sustainable healthcare for all.

Role Summary:

The Software Architect leads architecture strategy for complex software and AI systems in a healthcare environment. This role is based in Austin, TX and follows a hybrid work model. The architect will define target-state architecture, guide multi-quarter modernization plans, and help engineering teams deliver scalable, reliable, and compliant platform capabilities. This position reports to the Executive Director, Scheduling.

Team Summary:

We are seeking a Director-level Architect to define and drive architecture strategy for complex software and AI systems in a healthcare environment, with a strong emphasis on Scheduling platform modernization and cross-zone platform influence.


This role sits at the intersection of software engineering, systems architecture, and applied AI. The architect will establish target-state architecture, incremental migration plans, shared principles, and technical standards across engineering teams prioritizing platform-level solutions over zone-specific duplication.


The ideal candidate brings deep experience designing large-scale distributed systems, leading large modernization programs, and operationalizing AI capabilities in production with strong attention to reliability, performance, security, maintainability, cost, and compliance.

This is an individual-contributor role with no direct reports. Its leverage comes from technical credibility and influence across organizations, not from positional authority.

This position is based in Austin, TX, and reports to the Executive Director, Scheduling.

Essential Job Responsibilities:

  • Develop target-state architecture and multi-quarter migration roadmaps for complex platform capabilities across multiple teams.
  • Define architecture principles, technical standards, reference patterns, and decision records that guide engineering execution.
  • Design scalable, reliable, and performant distributed systems with measurable outcomes tied to service-level objectives (SLOs), benchmarks, and operational results.
  • Establish observability, incident response, runbook, and capacity planning practices that improve system health and operational readiness.
  • Evaluate event-driven and workflow orchestration approaches, including failure modes, resiliency patterns, and interoperability across consuming teams.
  • Partner with engineering, product, security, and operations leaders to influence platform direction and modernization priorities without direct authority.
  • Review application, data, and integration designs to ensure alignment with architecture standards, compliance requirements, and long-term platform goals.
  • Guide technical tradeoff discussions and decision-making across teams, balancing delivery speed, maintainability, cost, and risk.
  • Apply AI experience to architect, evaluate, and govern production AI capabilities, including orchestration, tool-calling patterns, context and state handling, monitoring, and model risk controls.
  • Use current hands-on technical depth in infrastructure as code, container platforms, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), and Java or a comparable modern language to prototype, review, and refine solutions.

Additional Job Responsibilities:

  • Support modernization planning for shared platform services and common capabilities.
  • Contribute to architecture review forums and design governance processes.
  • Help define integration standards, versioning approaches, and contract management practices.
  • Participate in incident reviews and help translate findings into architecture improvements.
  • Mentor engineers and architects through design feedback and technical discussion.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend where they should or should not be applied.
  • Collaborate on long-range planning for platform investments and technical debt reduction.
  • Assist in defining security, privacy, auditability, and access-control patterns for regulated systems.

Expected Education & Experience:

  • Typically requires 10+ years of software engineering experience, including at least 5 years of architecture ownership across multiple teams.
  • Demonstrated experience leading architecture strategy for complex, distributed software systems.
  • Proven success creating target-state architectures and multi-quarter migration plans with measurable delivery outcomes.
  • Experience defining and operationalizing architecture principles, standards, reference patterns, and architecture decision records.
  • Strong background in system design for scalability, reliability, performance, and operational excellence.
  • Deep knowledge of observability and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) practices, including SLOs, alerting, incident management, and post-mortems.
  • Experience with event-driven architectures, API design, contract versioning, and workflow orchestration.
  • Hands-on experience with infrastructure as code, container platforms, CI/CD pipelines, and Java or a comparable modern language.
  • Experience designing or governing AI-enabled systems in production, including orchestration, monitoring, and model risk considerations.
  • Experience building systems in regulated environments with attention to compliance, consent, data governance, auditability, and access control.
  • Strong communication and influencing skills with the ability to drive adoption across teams and functions

Expected Compensation

$216,000 - $368,000

The base salary range shown reflects the full range for this role from minimum to maximum. At athenahealth, base pay depends on multiple factors, including job-related experience, relevant knowledge and skills, how your qualifications compare to others in similar roles, and geographical market rates. Base pay is only one part of our competitive Total Rewards package - depending on role eligibility, we offer both short and long-term incentives by way of an annual discretionary bonus plan, variable compensation plan, and equity plans.

title: Global Project Head, Vaccines RnD
description:
Job title: Global Project Head, Vaccines RnD

  • Location: Waltham, MA

About the Job

As a Global Project Head within R&D Vaccines, you will serve as the strategic leader and driving force behind the development and execution of integrated strategies and development plans for New Vaccines (NV) projects from Gate M2 through the end of development. This pivotal role places you at the intersection of science, strategy, and leadership, where you will orchestrate cross-functional collaboration to bring life-saving vaccines to patients worldwide. In this position, you will lead Global Project Teams (GPT) and sub-teams in close cooperation with R&D and non-R&D function heads, ensuring seamless alignment across all development activities. You will be accountable for project risk management and will serve as the primary communicator to governance committees, providing strategic insights and recommendations that shape project direction. Your leadership will extend beyond internal teams as you serve as a key member of the Franchise Steering Team and Brand Team, contributing to broader strategic decisions.


As the ambassador for your project both internally and externally, you will build and maintain relationships with stakeholders across the organization and with external partners, including NGOs, partner companies, academic institutions, and joint ventures. Your ability to align diverse stakeholders, navigate complex organizational dynamics, and champion project objectives will be critical to success. This role offers the opportunity to make a lasting impact on global health while leading some of the most innovative vaccine development initiatives in the industry.


Join the team protecting half a billion lives every year with next-gen science, mRNA innovation, and AI driven breakthroughs. In Vaccines, you’ll help advance prevention on a global scale - and shape the future of immunization.

About Sanofi

We're an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people's lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system — and innovative pipeline — enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people's lives.

Main Responsibilities

Product Development Strategy & Execution

  • Contributes to creation and implementation of high-level product development strategies including Target Product/Vaccine Profile (TPP/TVP)
  • Hold full accountability for developing and executing project strategy from Gate M2 through licensure and life cycle management, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and patient needs
  • Drive strategic decision-making that balances scientific innovation, commercial viability, and patient impact
  • Ensure project deliverables meet timelines, quality standards and regulatory requirements across all markets

Team Leadership

  • Structure and lead the Global Project Team, fostering a collaborative, high-performance culture
  • Set clear objectives, provide constructive feedback, and hold team members accountable for deliverables
  • Mentor and develop team members, building capabilities across the organization
  • Create an inclusive environment where diverse perspectives are valued and leveraged

Resource Management

  • Supervise project activities and resolve resource utilization issues across functions
  • Optimize allocation of budget, personnel, and materials to maximize project efficiency
  • Partner with functional leaders to secure necessary resources and capabilities Make data-driven decisions regarding resource prioritization and trade-offs

Strategic Planning

  • Translate TPP into comprehensive scope, objectives, and actionable plans
  • Ensure alignment across Integrated Early Global Plan (IEGP), Integrated Strategic Commercial Plan (iSCP), Clinical Development Plan (CDP), Technical Strategy Document (TSD), and Global Regulatory Plan and Strategy (GRPS)
  • Anticipate future needs and proactively adapt strategies to changing landscapes
  • Drive innovation in development approaches and methodologies

Stakeholder Management

  • Manage relationships with internal and external stakeholders at the executive level
  • Build consensus among diverse stakeholder groups with competing priorities
  • Navigate complex organizational dynamics to advance project objectives
  • Represent the project in high-level strategic discussions and governance forums

Communication

  • Champion project objectives, progress, and risk mitigation strategies across all organizational levels
  • Present to senior leadership, governance committees, and external partners with clarity and impact
  • Ensure transparent, timely communication of project status, challenges, and opportunities
  • Tailor messaging to diverse audiences, from scientific experts to business leaders

Alliance Management

  • Manage strategic relationships with NGOs, partner companies, academic groups, and joint ventures
  • Negotiate and oversee collaboration agreements that advance project goals
  • Ensure alignment between internal objectives and external partner expectations
  • Leverage external partnerships to access capabilities, expertise, and resources

Franchise Strategy

  • Contribute to the development of a unified R&D vision and strategic roadmap for the franchise
  • Integrate project strategy with broader portfolio and franchise objectives
  • Identify opportunities for synergies across projects and therapeutic areas
  • Participate in long-term strategic planning and portfolio optimization

About You

Required Qualifications

  • Masters of Science degree in scientific-related field of study. PhD, MD, or PharmD is preferred.
  • 7+ years of experience in drug development, preferably in vaccines/infectious disease.

Skills & Competencies

  • Proven ability to lead international, cross-functional teams toward common goals
  • Skilled in building trust and fostering collaboration across diverse teams and cultures
  • Talent for inspiring and motivating others to achieve excellence
  • Ability to navigate ambiguity and drive clarity in complex situations
  • Exceptional presentation skills, capable of distilling complex information into compelling narratives
  • Strong negotiation skills and ability to build consensus among stakeholders with different perspectives
  • Commercial awareness and understanding of market dynamics
  • Adaptable and resilient in the face of challenges and changing priorities
  • Intellectually curious with commitment to continuous learning
  • Passion for improving patient lives and advancing global health

Why Choose Us

  • Bring the miracles of science to life alongside a supportive, future-focused team.
  • Discover endless opportunities to grow your talent and drive your career, whether it’s through a promotion or lateral move, at home or internationally.
  • Enjoy a thoughtful, well-crafted rewards package that recognizes your contribution and amplifies your impact.
  • Take good care of yourself and your family, with a wide range of health and wellbeing benefits including high-quality healthcare, prevention and wellness program
  • Work at the forefront of AI-driven research, smart manufacturing, and groundbreaking mRNA platforms that are redefining the future of immunology.
  • Help protect half a billion people every year, contributing to one of the largest global vaccination efforts in healthcare.
  • Develop your career with access to mentoring, international mobility programs, and opportunities to grow across four continents.

title: System Debug Lead Engineer
description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced System Debug Lead Engineer to join our team. This individual will play a critical role in root cause analysis and resolution of complex issues across our server and data center platforms, involving electrical, mechanical, thermal, and firmware components. The ideal candidate brings a multidisciplinary approach to system-level problem-solving and thrives in a dynamic, collaborative environment.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Lead cross-functional debug of critical system-level issues across hardware (electrical, mechanical, thermal) and firmware domains

  • Perform hands-on root cause analysis of failures observed during system validation, production, or in-field operation

  • Collaborate with electrical engineers, mechanical engineers, thermal engineers, firmware developers, and manufacturing teams to develop and validate fixes

  • Develop and implement detailed tests and experiments to identify and recreate intricate issues

  • Develop tools, scripts, and automation to accelerate debug workflows

  • Provide technical guidance and mentoring to cross-functional teams

  • Document debug procedures, findings, and mitigation plans clearly and concisely

  • Drive corrective and preventive action processes with suppliers and internal teams

What we need to see:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related fields (or equivalent experience)

  • 10+ years of experience in system-level debug in data center/server or similar hardware platforms

  • Deep understanding of system architecture including CPUs, memory, high-speed I/Os, power delivery, thermal management, and firmware

  • Proven experience in debugging electrical issues (e.g., signal integrity, power integrity), thermal issues (e.g., airflow, cooling design), and firmware anomalies (e.g., BIOS/UEFI, BMC)

  • Proficiency in tools such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and firmware debug equipment/utilities

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work across fields and teams

  • Experience working with contract manufacturers and suppliers is a plus

NVIDIA offers competitive salaries and benefits. We have experienced and talented individuals. Our engineering teams are growing quickly due to outstanding growth. If you're a creative engineer passionate about technology, we welcome your application!

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 168,000 USD - 258,750 USD for Level 4, and 200,000 USD - 322,000 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

title: FSP Local CTM Saudi Arabia
description:

Job Description

Join Us as a Clinical Trial Manager, managing studies locally in Saudi Arabia for one of our clients.

Make an Impact at the Forefront of Innovation
The Clinical Trial Manager is accountable for achieving the final clinical deliverable (usually clean data from evaluable patients as specified in the study protocol) within the time period specified in the contract with the customer. The Clinical Trial Manager interprets data on project issues and makes good business decisions with support from experienced team members or line manager. Works to ensure that all clinical deliverables meet the customer's time/quality/cost expectations. Maintains profitability by ensuring clinical activity is conducted within contract scope, through efficient management of the clinical team. The position involves working on projects of low to moderate complexity and as part of a team of CTMs.


What You'll Do:
• Manage all clinical operational and quality aspects of allocated studies, of low to moderate complexity, in compliance with ICH GCP. In accordance to project specific requirements, may assume Clinical Study Manager (CSM) responsibilities on small and/or less complex projects.
• Develop clinical tools (e.g. Monitoring Plan, Monitoring Guidelines) in conjunction with the Data Quality Plan. Contribute to the development of the Master Action Plan (MAP) for providing clinical related documents. Ensure timely set up, organization, content and quality of the relevant sections of the Trial Master File (local and central). May participate in the design and development of CRFs, CRF guidelines, patient informed consent templates and other protocol specific documents as required. Collaborate with the project manager to prepare, organize, and present at client meetings, including bid defense and hand-off meetings.
• Collaborate with the clinical team and other departments as needed to meet deliverables of the project. Regularly communicate with the team and lead team meetings to ensure that timelines, resources, interactions, and quality are maintained. Responsible for the implementation and training of standardized clinical monitoring processes within the study and according to corporate standard policies. Responsible for the timely archiving of documents and study materials for the department.
• Ensure achievement of the final clinical deliverable within the contractual time period specified by preparing and monitoring clinical activity timelines and metrics, providing status updates to the project manager, regularly reviewing projects using tracking and management tools, implementing recovery actions, reviewing monitoring visit reports, and managing CRF collection and query resolution. Continuously monitor or co-monitors clinical trials to assess performance and ensure contractual obligations are met. In smaller regions, may routinely conduct Accompanied Field Visits (AFVs) and be accountable for project financials.

  • Technical & Digital Literacy: Solid grasp of operations-wide data architecture, AI/ML operational applications, digital adoption platforms (e.g., WalkMe, Pendo), and shopfloor automation.
  • Methodology Mastery: Proven expertise combining Lean/Six Sigma principles with Agile, SAFe, Design Thinking, and Organizational Change Management (e.g., Prosci) frameworks.
  • Stakeholder Influence: Exceptional executive communication skills, with a track record of challenging senior leadership, navigating cross-functional resistance, and translating complex technical concepts into clear business cases.

Value & ROI Accountability: Demonstrated capability in defining, modeling, and delivering concrete financial and operational value (e.g., EBITDA impact, yield increase, COGS reduction) via digital & data solutions.

title: Operations & Learning Specialist
description:
Based in St. Louis, Core & Main is a leader in advancing reliable infrastructure™ with local service, nationwide®. As a specialty distributor with a focus on water, wastewater, storm drainage and fire protection products and related services, Core & Main provides solutions to municipalities, private water companies and professional contractors across municipal, non-residential and residential end markets, nationwide. With over 370 locations across the U.S., the company provides its customers local expertise backed by a national supply chain. Core & Main’s 5,700 associates are committed to helping their communities thrive with safe and reliable infrastructure. Visit coreandmain.com to learn more.

Position Summary

The Operations & Training Specialist serves as a field-based resource responsible for supporting associate onboarding, training, development, and operational excellence initiatives across an assigned territory. This role partners closely with branch leadership, regional leadership, and the Learning & Organizational Development team to drive consistency in operational processes, support systems adoption, and enhance associate effectiveness.


The incumbent works directly alongside associates and managers within branch locations, providing hands-on coaching, onboarding support, process training, and operational development to ensure alignment with company standards and best practices.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience with Core & Main, ideally in a sales focused or supporting role.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) and collaboration platforms (Teams/SharePoint).
  • Ability to identify potential problems and develop effective solutions without immediate direction or supervision.
  • Ability to manage deadlines, multi-task and operate in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to work cohesively with all stakeholders and trainees.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a learning & development, sales enablement, branch, talent development, or a related training role.

Environmental Job Requirements

Makes decisions under conditions of uncertainty, sometimes with incomplete information, that produce effective end results.

title: Assistant Executive Director
location: 412 - Heritage Elm Grove - Elm Grove, WI 53122
description:
Assistant Executive Director

Heritage Senior Living Elm Grove

Lead With Purpose. Support Your Team. Help Make Our Community Feel Like Home.

Are you a senior living professional ready to take the next step in your leadership career?

Heritage Senior Living is seeking an organized, compassionate, and motivated Assistant Director to help lead the day-to-day operations of our community.

Working alongside the Executive Director, you'll have the opportunity to make an impact across nearly every area of community operations—from resident experience and employee leadership to regulatory compliance, staffing, marketing, and financial administration.

This is an excellent opportunity for an emerging senior living leader who wants to broaden their operational experience and continue developing toward future Executive Director leadership opportunities.

What You’ll Do

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Assistant Director helps oversee community operations and works collaboratively with clinical, life enrichment, culinary, housekeeping, marketing, and other departments to provide an exceptional experience for residents, families, employees, and visitors.

Support Community Operations

  • Partner with the Executive Director in the overall day-to-day operation of the community.

  • Help coordinate operations across clinical, life enrichment, culinary, housekeeping, marketing, and other departments.

  • Serve as a visible and approachable leader for residents, families, employees, and visitors.

  • Help identify operational concerns and develop practical solutions.

  • Assist with maintaining a safe, organized, welcoming, and well-operated community.

  • Step in to provide leadership and operational support when the Executive Director is unavailable or as assigned.

  • Help ensure community policies, procedures, and operational standards are consistently followed.

Lead & Develop Employees

  • Participate in recruiting, interviewing, hiring, onboarding, training, supervision, and development of employees.

  • Assist with supervising caregivers/CNAs, housekeepers, and other assigned team members.

  • Help develop employee schedules based on resident and operational needs.

  • Provide employees with coaching, feedback, and direction.

  • Assist with performance management and corrective action when appropriate.

  • Coordinate and manage the employee performance appraisal process as assigned.

  • Conduct or participate in staff meetings, in-service education, and new-hire orientation.

  • Promote accountability, teamwork, communication, and a positive workplace culture.

  • Help ensure staffing levels support resident needs and quality service.

Support Resident & Family Experience

  • Build positive relationships with residents and families.

  • Meet with prospective residents and families to help determine whether community services can appropriately meet their needs.

  • Help ensure required resident information and documentation are completed prior to move-in.

  • Partner with the Director of Nursing and Executive Director to support systems for resident care, wellness, and life enrichment.

  • Maintain awareness of community healthcare resources that may support resident needs.

  • Visit with residents throughout the community, including during meals.

  • Respond to resident and family questions or concerns promptly and professionally.

  • Promote a resident-centered environment that respects dignity, independence, choice, and quality of life.

Maintain Regulatory & Operational Compliance

  • Assist with regulatory compliance for applicable Independent Living, RCAC, and CBRF operations.

  • Maintain working knowledge of applicable Wisconsin senior living requirements.

  • Assist with workplace safety and compliance responsibilities, including OSHA, workers' compensation, and applicable safety documentation.

  • Maintain organized records related to inspections, certifications, licensing, renewals, and surveys.

  • Immediately notify appropriate leadership when regulatory or inspecting organizations arrive at the community.

  • Assist with preparing for inspections, surveys, and other regulatory reviews.

  • Help identify compliance concerns and ensure appropriate follow-up.

Support Marketing & Community Growth

  • Support community sales and marketing efforts.

  • Respond to prospective resident and family inquiries professionally and promptly.

  • Conduct or assist with community tours.

  • Complete appropriate follow-up with prospective residents and families.

  • Assist with community outreach and relationship-building efforts.

  • Partner with leadership to promote consistent marketing activities and a positive community reputation.

  • Help create an exceptional first impression for prospective residents and families.

Support Administrative & Financial Operations

  • Assist with employee payroll processing and ensure required information is submitted accurately and timely.

  • Help monitor department and community spending according to established budgets.

  • Assist with purchase orders and purchasing processes.

  • Maintain accurate and organized administrative documentation.

  • Support reporting and other administrative responsibilities as assigned by the Executive Director.

Champion Customer Service

  • Help establish and reinforce high customer-service expectations throughout the community.

  • Model professional, compassionate, and responsive interactions with residents, families, employees, and visitors.

  • Help ensure common areas remain clean, organized, presentable, and welcoming.

  • Pay attention to details that contribute to the resident experience, including dining atmosphere and overall community presentation.

  • Encourage employees across departments to take ownership of the resident and family experience.

What We’re Looking For

The Assistant Director needs to be someone who can see the entire community—not just one department.

We're looking for a leader who can move comfortably from an employee conversation to a resident concern, a family meeting, a regulatory question, a community tour, or an operational challenge.

You may be a great fit if you:

  • Have senior living or assisted living experience and are ready for broader leadership responsibility.

  • Enjoy developing employees and building strong teams.

  • Understand the importance of regulatory compliance and accurate documentation.

  • Have high expectations for customer service and resident satisfaction.

  • Are comfortable interacting with residents, families, employees, and prospective residents.

  • Can manage multiple priorities without losing sight of important details.

  • Are confident addressing performance concerns and resolving conflict.

  • Use sound judgment and remain professional when handling challenging situations.

  • Are comfortable making decisions and working independently when needed.

  • Enjoy being a visible, hands-on leader throughout the community.

  • Are interested in continuing to grow your career in senior living operations.

Qualifications

  • 1–3 years of experience in assisted living, memory care, senior living, or a related healthcare setting preferred.

  • A combination of relevant education and experience will be considered.

  • Degree in healthcare administration, business management, healthcare management, or a related field is a plus.

  • Working knowledge of dementia and memory-care services.

  • Knowledge of or ability to develop knowledge of Wisconsin regulations applicable to CBRFs and RCACs.

  • Previous experience hiring, training, coaching, and managing employee performance.

  • Strong leadership, organizational, and time-management skills.

  • Strong customer-service orientation.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Office and Outlook.

  • Sound judgment and demonstrated problem-solving and decision-making abilities.

  • Ability to manage conflict and resolve complex problems professionally.

  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with a leadership team.

  • Ability and willingness to maintain a leadership presence during evenings, weekends, and holidays as community needs require.

  • Ability to meet applicable pre-employment, training, certification, and regulatory requirements.

Benefits & Perks

At Heritage Senior Living, we know exceptional communities start with exceptional leaders. Depending on employment status and applicable eligibility requirements, benefits and perks may include:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Paid holidays and/or holiday pay

  • Retirement savings opportunities

  • Employee assistance and wellness resources

  • Training and professional development

  • Leadership development opportunities

  • Career growth and advancement

  • Employee recognition programs

  • A collaborative and supportive leadership team

  • Meaningful work where you can make a difference every day

Benefit availability and eligibility may vary based on employment status, scheduled hours, location, plan requirements, and other applicable criteria.

Why Heritage Senior Living?

The Assistant Director has the opportunity to influence nearly every part of the community.

One moment you may be helping an employee solve a problem. The next, you may be meeting a prospective family, visiting with residents during lunch, preparing for a regulatory review, helping with staffing, or working alongside the Executive Director on an operational priority.

That variety provides an opportunity to develop a well-rounded understanding of senior living operations and leadership while making a direct impact on residents, families, and employees.

If you're ready to expand your leadership experience and help create an exceptional community for residents and employees, we'd love to meet you.

Apply today and take the next step in your senior living leadership career with Heritage Senior Living!

Essential Functions & Physical Requirements

The following are essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodations may be provided as required by applicable law.

  • Communicate effectively with residents, families, employees, prospective residents, healthcare partners, and community leadership.

  • Read, interpret, prepare, and maintain reports, schedules, regulatory information, employee documentation, resident information, and other business records.

  • Regularly use computers, telephones, and standard office technology.

  • Sit, stand, and walk throughout the community for extended periods as responsibilities require.

  • Bend, reach, stoop, kneel, push, pull, and perform movements necessary for assigned responsibilities.

  • Lift, carry, and move items weighing up to 50 pounds as required.

  • Maintain regular and reliable attendance.

  • Work a flexible schedule based on community needs, including evenings, weekends, holidays, and additional hours when necessary.

Heritage Senior Living is an equal opportunity employer. Employment is subject to applicable pre-employment, training, certification, and ongoing requirements in accordance with federal and state law.

title: Project Manager (Tax Division)
description:
Job Title: Project Manager (Tax Division)

Job Category: Project and Program Management

Time Type: Full time

Minimum Clearance Required to Start: DOJ MBI

Employee Type: Regular

Percentage of Travel Required: None

Type of Travel: None

* * *


The Opportunity:


If you have experience managing eDiscovery projects across the Electronic Discovery Reference Model (EDRM) and are looking to grow and manage multiple high visibility projects for the Department of Justice (DOJ) then this position is for you! In this critical position, you will manage a single high visibility large case or multiple smaller cases for one of the Department of Justice (DOJ) Divisions under the Mega contract. In this position, you will also work closely with US Attorneys, DOJ Case Managers and Contracting Officer Representatives (CORs), Case Managers, and technical teams to discuss project requirements, schedules, budgets, and all litigation support activities for each project. CACI is committed to growing our eDiscovery workforce and has included tuition reimbursement for Relativity certifications, the ACEDS certification and Paralegal Certificates! This is a great opportunity for someone to grow their careers.


Responsibilities:


As a part of a high performing team, CACI’s Litigation Project Managers work with Lead Project Managers and Deputy Division Directors to serve as the primary person responsible for all support provided to a particular case. Project Managers will generally be responsible for more than one active case at a time; a caseload of six to ten moderately active, moderately sized cases will be typical, with several of the cases possibly in the discovery and/or document review stage, one case in trial, several in the deposition preparation/witness binder stage, etc. Additional responsibilities include:


  • This position manages several projects varying in size and complexity that can go through all or some of the phases of the EDRM spectrum, from investigation, intake/acquisition of documents and data (discovery), through trial support.
  • The Project Manager is the Government's primary point of contact for all support for the case.
  • The Project Manager is responsible for planning and managing all support for the case, including monitoring workflow, progress reporting, identifying and assigning staff, budget development and tracking, coordinating technical/data processing and eDiscovery support, and obtaining other required resources.
  • Performs an active quality assurance role to ensure high quality work delivered on time.
  • Ensures that proper security is maintained overall project materials, in accordance with security procedures.
  • Coordinates with other Contractor components to deliver project support.

Qualifications:


Required:

  • 4+ years of progressively more responsible supervisory and management experience on major e-discovery/litigation support projects, including proven capabilities and communication skills to successfully interact with clients and attorneys.
  • Demonstrated experience working in eDiscovery document review platforms such as Relativity, Clearwell, iCONECT, Casepoint, Everlaw, etc.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage numerous complex and time-critical litigation support activities simultaneously, including technical/data processing and eDiscovery support activities.
  • Requires expert knowledge of litigation support; outstanding writing skills; excellent oral communication skills; and excellent management skills.
  • Must be able to anticipate litigation support needs and develop and execute detailed plans for addressing those needs.
  • Requires knowledge of the Government's data processing environment where the work is performed, including PC-based and virtual environments.
  • Familiarity with Electronically Stored Information (ESI) tools and knowledge of eDiscovery procedures and resources required.
  • Should be an expert user of the Government's office and network environment, including but not limited to, word processing, spreadsheet, imaging, and hardware and document review platforms.

Desired:

  • Undergraduate degree and graduate degrees strongly preferred. Substantial relevant experience may in some cases be substituted for degree requirement.
  • Certification in eDiscovery program preferred such as Relativity Certified Administrator (RCA) and Certified eDiscovery Specialist (CEDS).
  • Experience working on a Federal Contract a plus.

This position is contingent on funding and may not be filled immediately. However, this position is representative of positions within CACI that are consistently available. Individuals who apply may also be considered for other positions at CACI.

What You Can Expect:

A culture of integrity.

At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation.

An environment of trust.

CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.


Pay Range:

There are a host of factors that can influence final salary including, but not limited to, geographic location, Federal Government contract labor categories and contract wage rates, relevant prior work experience, specific skills and competencies, education, and certifications. Our employees value the flexibility at CACI that allows them to balance quality work and their personal lives. We offer competitive compensation, benefits and learning and development opportunities. Our broad and competitive mix of benefits options is designed to support and protect employees and their families. At CACI, you will receive comprehensive benefits such as; healthcare, wellness, financial, retirement, family support, continuing education, and time off benefits.

The proposed salary range for this position is:

$78,700 - $165,200

CACI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected characteristic.

title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Cloud Infrastructure
description:
NVIDIA's deep learning platforms are at the forefront of innovation, profoundly impacting various fields and widely adopted by leading academic institutions, startups, and major Internet companies globally. We're seeking an accomplished and highly skilled Technical Program Manager (TPM) to join our NVIDIA DGX Cloud team. This is a great opportunity for a passionate, motivated, and creative individual to deliver outstanding value to our DGX Cloud customers!

We are specifically looking for a TPM with extensive experience in CSP/NCP cloud environments, on-prem infrastructure bring-up, and hardware automation.

What you'll be doing:

As an Infrastructure Technical Program Manager, you'll be a key partner to our external NCP partners as well as key internal teams (Software Engineering, Production Engineering/SRE, and Data Center Operations) and their leadership, driving critical programs related to on-prem infrastructure engineering, bare-metal bring-up, and automation. You'll play a pivotal role in developing and maturing foundational capabilities and processes, spanning critical areas such as hardware validation, remote fleet bootstrapping, operational workflows, and cluster/capacity bring-up. This is a dynamic, fast-paced environment where TPMs are motivated to apply versatile abilities to a range of high-impact programs across the infrastructure lifecycle.

  • Fleet Bring-Up, Automation: Coordinate the end-to-end remote bootstrapping, active bring-up, and validation of large server fleets to take clusters from physical rack-and-stack to a customer-ready state. Drive the adoption of automation tooling for fleet maintenance, node security, and burn-in, while establishing formalized workflows to rapidly triage and resolve day-one deployment issues.

  • NVIDIA Software Integration & Capacity Operations: Partner closely with internal NVIDIA SW teams to integrate and deploy DSX and other core software stacks within on-prem environments. Lead day-to-day capacity operations with a focus on availability, maintenance, and multi-tiered infrastructure workflows. This role includes the potential to scale scope by driving end-to-end capacity onboarding and operations with NCP partners as part of internal DGX Cloud (DGXC) capacity.

  • Cross-Team Roadmap Interception: Work across diverse NVIDIA engineering teams to understand, map, and intercept incoming technology roadmaps against physical data center readiness timelines.

  • Program Governance: Gather detailed requirements, build comprehensive roadmaps, and manage risks under the Product Lifecycle (PLC) framework for bare-metal capacity deployment. Leverage Jira and program management tools to instill structured execution across engineering and data center work.

  • Metrics, Visibility & Communication: Establish clear critical metrics to quantitatively track program velocity, infrastructure availability, and overall cluster health. Develop robust communication strategies—including turning weekly operations reviews into highly collaborative sessions.

What we need to see:

  • 8+ years of technical program management experience, specifically driving the planning and execution of cloud infrastructure programs, with a strong focus on hardware/software integration across many engineering teams.

  • Infrastructure Expertise: Extensive hands-on experience in cloud or on-prem enterprise infrastructure, data center bring-up, bare-metal deployments, and a deep understanding of hardware infrastructure.

  • Tooling Proficiency: Expert-level proficiency with Jira, Smartsheet, or similar program management tools, with the ability to confidently design ticket queues and guide engineering teams within an Agile/Scrum framework.

  • Strategic Leadership: Exceptional strategic and tactical thinking abilities, coupled with a strong capacity to build consensus, establish operational workflows, and drive program success through uncertainty.

  • Communication Skills: Outstanding communication, collaboration, and technical presentation skills, with a proven ability to increase meeting engagement, gather feedback, and align senior multi-functional collaborators.

  • BS or MS in Electrical Engineering or Computer Science, or equivalent experience.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • In-depth knowledge of NVIDIA GPU products, cluster deployment, validation testing, and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure bring-up. Direct experience managing dependencies between pioneering AI software stacks and foundational physical infrastructure.

title: Vice President, Health, Environment, Safety and Security
description:
Margaritaville at Sea sells escape. Our Vice President, HESS makes sure every guest and crew member comes home safe and healthy, and that the ocean we sell is left the way we found it. This is a rare chance to build a cruise line's HESS function from the ground up at a moment of growth: our third ship, Beachcomber, enters service from Miami in January 2027. It is a visible, executive-level role with direct access to senior leadership and fleet-wide stop-work authority.

ABOUT MARGARITAVILLE AT SEA

Classica Cruise Operator, Ltd., doing business as Margaritaville at Sea, operates Bahamas-flagged cruise ships from Florida homeports in Palm Beach, Tampa and Miami.

THE ROLE

Reporting to the Chief Maritime Officer, the Vice President, HESS is the Company's senior executive for health, environment, safety and security across the fleet. You will set the standards, build the team, and give the executive team a clear, data-driven picture of HESS performance and risk.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Lead HESS

  • Set the fleet's HESS strategy, standards, budget and multi-year plan.

  • Build and lead a shoreside HESS team.

  • Report HESS performance and risk to the executive team.

Environment and Public Health

  • Own environmental compliance, including MARPOL, the North American Emission Control Area, and U.S. EPA vessel discharge requirements under the Vessel General Permit and the Vessel Incidental Discharge Act (VIDA).

  • Own public health, including CDC Vessel Sanitation Program readiness and outbreak prevention and response.

Safety, Risk Assessment and Human Factors

  • Own the risk assessment program: the risk assessment library, job safety analysis, permit-to-work and point-of-work assessment.

  • Set occupational health and safety standards for crew, and apply human factors to incident investigation and prevention.

Security and Cyber

  • Oversee shipboard security programs under the ISPS Code and the Cruise Vessel Security and Safety Act (CVSSA).

  • Integrate cyber risk management for vessel operational technology into the Safety Management System.

Ship Manager Assurance and Audit

  • Partner with our third-party ship manager to set HESS performance indicators, and run an assurance and audit program aboard ship and ashore.

Regulators, Incidents and Culture

  • Serve as the Company's senior HESS interface with the flag State, classification society, U.S. Coast Guard, CDC, EPA and external auditors.

  • Lead investigation of significant incidents and drive corrective action to closure.

  • Build a culture in which every crew member is empowered to stop unsafe work, and lead HESS readiness for new vessels entering service.

title: Prime Time Family Service Coordinator
description:
NATURE AND SCOPE OF POSITION

The Family Service Coordinator (FSC) is responsible for engaging all families to partner with us to promote children’s healthy development and school readiness. The FSC uses knowledge of the principles of family engagement to support families in their roles as their child’s primary educator, encourage parent/child interactions that promote children’s school readiness and healthy development, and enhance family well-being. In this role, the FSC will provide more intensive and targeted support to vulnerable families and families of children with chronic health conditions and special needs in order to ensure that our engagement strategies meet their specialized needs.

The Family Service Coordinator will work as part of the program’s broader team to expand family engagement strategies that will create a sense of belonging and shared community among families, with the goal of enhancing the relationships and support that families provide to one another in their shared aspirations for their children and themselves. The position may involve reassignment of caseload and/or locations as deemed necessary for program operations.

JOB FUNCTION ESSENTIAL:

  1. PROMOTE FAMILY ENVIRONMENTS THAT ENHANCE CHILDREN’S DEVELOPMENT
    • Participate in outreach, recruitment, and attendance follow-up activities to engage families in our program and to motivate their active participation
    • Engage families in the Family Partnership Process in order to build relationships and shared accountability for promoting children’s development
    • Individualize family engagement and relationship-building to be appropriate to families’ cultural context, as well as respectful of family circumstances.
    • Engage families in individualized, in-home, and group experiences to enhance parent/child interactions that research shows foster school readiness through consistent family routines, positive guidance and discipline, experience-rich home environments, and literacy activities
    • Utilize in-classroom time and home visits to build a deeper understanding of the relationship between children’s development and their home environments, as well as to model and coach families in positive parent/child interactions
    • Implement a research-based family curriculum that extends our classroom curriculum into the family's home, modeling high-quality adult-child interactions teachers use in their classrooms for families around the four Family Life Practices. Focus on Coordination and collaboration with education
  2. SUPPORT FAMILIES TO MEET SELF-IDENTIFIED GOALS AND NEEDS
    • Utilize family self-assessment information to assist families with self-identified goals to enhance self-sufficiency in areas such as education, employment, housing, and access to community resources
    • Provide more intensive weekly face-to-face or phone contact with vulnerable families on caseload as identified through their self-assessment or family interactions/communication- including home visits. Assure that families receive immediate support during times of crisis, and assist with referrals to community-based resources to meet counseling, treatment, entitlement, or other needs
    • Identify and access services and resources responsive to family interests and goals, and follow up with parents to ensure that services meet their expectations and needs.
    • Analyze self-sufficiency data and utilize data/results to plan and coordinate a variety of parent cohort groups that allow families to support one another to achieve self-sufficiency goals.
    • Coordinate or refer families to opportunities for continuing education, employment training, and other employment services through formal or informal networking in the community.
  3. ENGAGE FAMILIES TO SUPPORT ONE ANOTHER
    • Foster a sense of community and a sense of belonging among families in order to strengthen social capital
    • Conduct group and center-based workshops and activities designed to build social capital and create a welcoming program community committed to family engagement in children’s learning and development
    • Cultivate family leadership and support their efforts through participation in program governance bodies such as Policy Council, as well as neighborhood and community-based advisory groups
    • Work in conjunction with Center staff and families to plan and conduct a wide variety of family engagement activities that provide opportunities for families to support one another, including, but not limited to the following:
    • Conduct, activities, and campaigns that promote children’s school readiness
    • Self-Sufficiency Sector Groups
    • Monthly Family Engagement Network Meetings
  4. ENHANCE PROGRAM COLLABORATION
    • Build relationships that will enhance communication and collaboration among internal and external stakeholders
    • Work side by side with health, early learning, and disability, and other members of the family engagement team to support families to be fully engaged in all aspects of our program
    • Establish regular coordination and communication with Health, Nutrition, and Disabilities team members in order to provide more intensive support to families of children with chronic health conditions and special needs, including targeted goal setting, and assistance with building family skills to navigate community systems of care for their children
    • Work in coordination with Health and Nutrition team members to ensure that all children on caseload are up to date on EPSDT requirements, including receiving timely evaluation and treatment for identified concerns
    • Develop effective communication and collaborative strategies with teaching teams to encourage family engagement in home learning activities, including individualizing activities based upon family interests and children’s developmental status
    • Establish and maintain working relationships with community partners to strengthen access to resources and training identified as priority goal areas by families
  5. MAINTAIN ACCURATE AND TIMELY RECORD KEEPING AND REPORTING
    • Effectively manage workload and ensure accurate record-keeping and documentation
    • Maintain accurate electronic and hard copy records and case notes to support positive child and family outcomes.
    • Document efforts to assist families to identify their strengths, needs, and self-sufficiency goals through completion of the Family Success Roadmap, Family Partnership Agreement, and case notes.
    • Record, monitor, and follow up on referrals for support services for reporting requirements.
    • Submit reports as needed and requested, such as monthly summary tracking reports, etc.
  6. RECRUITMENT
    • Assure timely follow-up on program inquiries and maintain an updated tracking system of potential enrollees
    • Follow up and maintain an updated tracking system for program phone and walk-in inquiries
    • Schedule, plan, and coordinate recruitment activities throughout the year
  7. ELIGIBILITY, SELECTION AND ENROLLMENT
    • Ensure the eligibility, selection, and enrollment processes adhere to HSPS and Prime Time Head Start ISP/PP
    • Review all applications received and work directly with families to ensure that all necessary enrollment/intake forms are completed and obtained in a timely manner for all children/families assigned to their Center(s).
    • Determine the eligibility of children/families, ensuring that all family documentation is accurate and complete
    • Determine family eligibility for extended day services and assist families with completing childcare subsidy applications
    • Enroll children and families based on selection criteria.
    • Maintain an up-to-date and accurate wait list of eligible children to enroll in the event of attrition.
    • Maintain the funded enrollment level and fill vacancies as they occur, and analyze enrollment data to inform the planning process.
    • Keep up to date and knowledgeable of requirements that are communicated through the Office of Head Start communications such as Information Memorandums, Policy Clarifications, and Program Information documents.
  8. ATTENDANCE
    • As schedule permits, provide clerical support in attendance entry and follow-up
    • Assist Family Services Coordinator and/or ERSEA Leads to track Centers whose ADA falls below 85%, and to maintain Attendance Action Plans in Master Binder System
  9. SERVICE COORDINATION
    • Inform Early Learning and Family Services staff regarding children with allergies, chronic health conditions, or special needs to ensure that medical documentation is received, and case conferences occur prior to entry.
    • Build relationships that will enhance communication and collaboration among internal and external stakeholders
    • Work side by side with health, early learning, and disabilities, and other members of the family engagement team to support families to be fully engaged in all aspects of our program
    • Establish regular coordination and communication with Health, Nutrition, and Disabilities team members in order to provide more intensive support to families of children with chronic health conditions and special needs, including targeted goal setting, and assistance with building family skills to navigate community systems of care for their children
    • Work in coordination with Health and Nutrition team members to ensure that all children on caseload are up to date on EPSDT requirements, including receiving timely evaluation and treatment for identified concerns
    • Develop effective communication and collaborative strategies with teaching teams to encourage family engagement in home learning activities, including individualizing activities based upon family interests and children’s developmental status
    • Establish and maintain working relationships with community partners to strengthen access to resources and training identified as priority goal areas by families
    • Coordinate with the Director of Analysis to ensure that all PIR data is up to date in the data system

MARGINAL:

  • Provide courteous and prompt service to all internal and external clients. Prioritize and address requests and assignments in a professional manner to develop cooperative relationships and to ensure that client confidentiality is assured.
  • Identify opportunities and recommend methods to improve service, work processes, and financial performance, e.g., expense management. Assists in the implementation of quality improvement initiatives.
  • Assist co-workers in the completion of tasks and assignments to ensure continuity of service. Orient new co-workers and actively support teamwork throughout the organization.
  • Perform other duties as required.

title: 50/50 Coordinator, MLSE Foundation
description:
Powered by Passion. United by Purpose. Build for Impact.

At Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment Partnership (MLSE), we exist to deliver the ultimate fan experience by lifting trophies, spirits, and communities – united as one.

We're more than a workplace. We are a team of passionate people, boldly building the future of sport and entertainment, together. We believe in the power of play, the strength of collaboration, and the energy that comes from showing up with purpose.

title: Business Information Security Expert, Financial - Mergers & Acquisitions
description:
Job Description Summary

Location: Mexico City, Mexico #LI-Hybrid

Internal job title: Associate Director DDIT ISC FM&A Compliance

This role is based in Mexico City, Mexico. Novartis is unable to offer relocation support for this role: please only apply if this location is accessible for you.

About the Role:
Mergers and acquisitions create some of the most complex and interesting challenges in Information Security. Every transaction presents a different challenge, information may be incomplete, timelines are often compressed, and security decisions need to support the pace and objectives of the deal.
As a Business Information Security Expert (BISE) supporting FM&A, you will operate at the intersection of Information Security, Cybersecurity, Technology, Finance and FM&A execution. Acting as a trusted security adviser and business partner, you will support the organization’s understanding of cyber risk, enabling transactions to proceed securely, intelligently and at business speed.
You will provide Information Security expertise across the FM&A lifecycle, from due diligence and pre-close risk assessments that feed ECN decision making, through Day 1 readiness, integration and post-close remediation as well as supporting divestitures or other transaction types where required.
This is not simply about identifying security issues. You will need to be pragmatic and determine what genuinely matters, translate technical findings into business risk and help identify practical ways forward, often when information is incomplete and decisions need to be made quickly.


Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

  • FM&A Information Security Due Diligence: Assess acquisition targets, rapidly understand unfamiliar technology and security environments, and identify risks that could materially affect the transaction, integration strategy or post-close risk profile.
  • Risk Analysis & Decision Support: Distinguish material risks from lower-priority technical findings and translate complex issues into clear business impact, options and recommendations.
  • Transaction Security Strategy: Define proportionate security priorities, mitigations and escalation requirements, balancing security objectives with transaction timelines and business realities.
  • Day 1 & Integration: Determine what must be addressed before or at closing and what can appropriately be remediated post-close.
  • Third-Party Risk: Identify material risks arising from suppliers and technology partners and coordinate specialist assessment or mitigation where required.
  • Business Partnership: Work closely with Leadership and Technical Experts in FM&A, Information Security, Technology, Finance, Legal, Privacy, Risk and Compliance to develop practical solutions to complex transaction challenges.
  • Security SME Coordination: Recognize when deeper expertise is needed, engage the right specialists and translate their findings into the broader transaction risk picture.
  • Executive Communication: Explain complex security matters clearly and concisely, focusing on what matters, why it matters and what should be done.
  • Continuous Improvement: Apply lessons from transactions to improve FM&A security methodologies, tools and our teams’ ways of working.

Essential Requirements:

  • 8+ years of experience with strong understanding and knowledge of enterprise Information Security and Cybersecurity, with experience in compliance, governance and controls aspects.
  • Ability to assess risk across applications, infrastructure, cloud, identity, data, AI tools and third parties.
  • Strong analytical, investigative and critical-thinking skills, pragmatic proportionate and risk-based decision-making.
  • Ability to rapidly understand unfamiliar technologies, companies and business environments, and judgement to distinguish material risk from technical noise.
  • Confidence making recommendations when information is incomplete, ambiguous or evolving.
  • Excellent written, verbal and executive communication skills, with strong stakeholder-management and influencing capabilities.
  • Ability to work autonomously while knowing when specialist expertise or escalation is required.
  • Intellectual curiosity, ability to learn quickly and comfort operating in fast-moving, complex environments.

Desirable requirements:

  • Experience in M&A transactions, cyber due diligence, technology integration, third-party risk, pharmaceuticals/life sciences or another regulated industry
