Job Description

Role Overview

The 50|50 Staff Supervisor is responsible for leading, developing, and supporting MLSE's part-time 50|50 event staff to deliver an exceptional fan experience while maximizing revenue. This role oversees staffing, scheduling, coaching, and performance management for 50|50 Ambassadors and Team Leads, fostering a positive, high-performing culture across all events. The 50|50 Staff Supervisor maintains a strong on-site presence, ensuring staff are engaged, well-trained, and equipped to execute at the highest level while proactively identifying staffing needs and opportunities for continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the cultural leader for the 50|50 program, setting the tone for a high-energy, positive, and accountable team environment while maintaining a strong and visible presence at events.
  • Lead 50|50 Ambassador performance management by providing individualized coaching, delivering regular training sessions, and creating development plans that improve sales performance, fan engagement, and customer service.
  • Own workforce planning by assessing roster capacity, identifying hiring needs, and making recommendations regarding recruitment to maintain a high-performing team.
  • Partner with the 50|50 Operations Supervisor to ensure staffing plans align with event requirements and operational priorities, supporting optimal coverage across all events.
  • Co-supervise the 50|50 Team Leads alongside the 50|50 Operations Supervisor, ensuring staff are engaged, supported, and consistently executing to program standards.
  • Plan and lead team-building initiatives and recognition programs that strengthen collaboration, reinforce MLSE's values, and foster an inclusive, motivated workplace.

Qualifications

  • Strong people leadership skills with experience coaching, mentoring, or supervising frontline teams.
  • Excellent organizational abilities, with the capacity to manage staffing across a high-volume event calendar.
  • Proven ability to motivate teams and create an engaging, performance-driven culture.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with confidence delivering feedback and resolving employee concerns professionally.
  • Ability to make sound decisions in a fast-paced, live event environment while remaining calm under pressure.
  • Experience in sales, customer service, event operations, or sports and entertainment is considered an asset.
  • Comfortable analyzing individual and team performance to identify coaching opportunities and improve results.
  • Flexible availability, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, to support live events.

Success in This Role Looks Like:

  • A highly engaged, motivated, and high-performing 50|50 team that consistently delivers an energetic and positive fan experience across all events.
  • Strong 50|50 Ambassador performance and development, demonstrated through effective coaching, improved sales results, and continuous growth of individual team members.
  • A strong team culture built on accountability, recognition, and collaboration, where staff feel valued, supported, and connected to the impact of the 50|50 program.
  • Consistent event execution supported by a well-trained and appropriately staffed team, with proactive identification of hiring needs and performance opportunities.
  • Visible and effective leadership on-site, creating an environment where 50|50 Ambassadors are energized, confident, and equipped to maximize fan engagement and revenue.
  • Successful onboarding, training, and retention of part-time staff, building a reliable roster of ambassadors who represent MLSE’s values and community impact.
  • Strong partnership with the 50|50 Operations Supervisor, ensuring alignment between people, culture, and operational requirements across all events.

Town School is seeking a collaborative and experienced educator to serve as an interim third- to fifth-grade Learning Specialist for the remainder of the 2026-27 school year. The Learning Specialist is a specialized practitioner providing a variety of support to students, faculty members, and families. The Learning Specialist supports the academic programs of students with neurodiverse profiles and students requiring intervention. This position works across both the Lower and Upper School Divisions and is a member of the Learning Services Team composed of a director and two other Learning Specialists (K-2, 6-8). Additionally, this position works with faculty and parents to ensure that learning differences and strategies for intervention are well understood and supported in the school community.

title: Director of Quality and Risk Management
description:
About Community Health Partnership of Illinois

Community Health Partnership of Illinois (CHP) is a nonprofit healthcare organization dedicated to providing accessible, high-quality primary medical, dental, and behavioral healthcare services to underserved communities throughout Illinois.

With over 55 years of service, CHP proudly serves more than 10,000 patients across six counties in central and northern Illinois. Our mission is to improve the health and well-being of the communities we serve through compassionate, patient-centered care.

Position Summary

Community Health Partnership of Illinois is seeking an experienced and dedicated Director of Quality and Risk Management to lead and oversee the organization's quality improvement, patient safety, regulatory compliance, and risk management programs.

This leadership position plays a critical role in ensuring compliance with Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) Health Center Program requirements, The Joint Commission accreditation standards, and applicable federal and state healthcare regulations.

The Director will collaborate closely with clinical leadership, Human Resources, and administrative teams to promote patient safety, minimize organizational risk, strengthen clinical performance, and foster a culture of continuous quality improvement across CHP locations.

Key Responsibilities

Quality Improvement & Performance Management

  • Develop, implement, and oversee the organization's Quality Improvement and Quality Assurance (QI/QA) programs.

  • Lead staff and Board Quality Improvement/Quality Assurance Committee meetings.

  • Establish and monitor quality improvement initiatives using data-driven methodologies, including Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycles and Lean Six Sigma principles.

  • Track and improve Uniform Data System (UDS) clinical performance measures, including hypertension control, diabetes management, colorectal cancer screening, and other quality indicators.

  • Supervise the Data Integrity Manager and oversee organizational data analysis activities.

  • Identify opportunities to enhance patient outcomes, operational efficiency, and clinical performance.

Risk Management & Patient Safety

  • Develop, implement, and oversee the organization's Risk Management Program.

  • Manage incident reporting systems, monitor near-miss events, and coordinate proactive risk assessments, including Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA).

  • Oversee the annual Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) deeming application process.

  • Ensure completion of required staff risk management training, including infection control, HIPAA, and other applicable clinical safety topics.

  • Develop and maintain organizational emergency preparedness and Continuity of Operations (COOP) plans.

  • Promote a proactive culture of patient safety, accountability, and risk reduction.

Regulatory Compliance & Accreditation

  • Ensure organizational compliance with the HRSA Health Center Program Compliance Manual and applicable regulatory requirements.

  • Serve as a primary subject matter expert for The Joint Commission accreditation, working collaboratively with the Director of Nursing and clinical leadership.

  • Coordinate accreditation readiness activities, including mock surveys, tracer activities, compliance assessments, and supporting documentation.

  • Oversee Patient-Centered Medical Home (PCMH) certification activities and ambulatory care accreditation requirements.

  • Prepare for and support HRSA Operational Site Visits (OSVs), FTCA deeming reviews, and other regulatory evaluations.

  • Monitor compliance with applicable federal and state healthcare regulations and licensing requirements.

Leadership & Organizational Collaboration

  • Collaborate with Human Resources and clinical leadership to support provider credentialing and peer review processes.

  • Provide guidance to clinical and administrative teams regarding quality improvement, risk management, and regulatory compliance.

  • Develop and maintain organizational policies, procedures, reports, and documentation related to quality and risk management.

  • Promote collaboration, professional accountability, and continuous improvement across all CHP locations.

  • Perform additional duties as assigned by organizational leadership.

Required Qualifications

  • Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) certification.

  • Certified Professional in Healthcare Risk Management (CPHRM) certification.

  • Current Basic Life Support (BLS) and Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support (ACLS) certifications.

  • Strong leadership, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

  • Knowledge of The Joint Commission accreditation standards and Patient-Centered Medical Home (PCMH) certification requirements.

  • Understanding of healthcare regulations, clinical practices, medical terminology, and patient safety principles.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

  • Ability to lead quality and risk management initiatives while maintaining a safe, compliant, and professional healthcare environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Active Registered Nurse (RN) license.

  • In-depth knowledge of HRSA Health Center Program requirements, FTCA guidelines, and UDS reporting.

  • Advanced knowledge of The Joint Commission National Patient Safety Goals (NPSGs) and ambulatory care accreditation standards.

  • Experience with Electronic Health Records (EHR) and healthcare analytics platforms, such as Azara DRVS, i2i, or similar systems.

  • Infection Preventionist certification.

  • Experience working in ambulatory care, Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), or similar healthcare settings.

  • Experience managing quality improvement programs, regulatory compliance initiatives, and organizational risk management activities.

Benefits

CHP offers a comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance

  • Health Savings Account (HSA) and Health Management Tools

  • Paid Time Off (PTO) and Company-Paid Holidays

  • 403(b) Retirement Plan

  • Life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance

  • Short-Term Disability Insurance

  • Accident Insurance

  • Employee Recognition and Rewards Programs

Join Our Team!

Are you an experienced healthcare quality and risk management professional passionate about improving patient safety, strengthening organizational compliance, and driving meaningful healthcare improvements?

At Community Health Partnership of Illinois, you'll have the opportunity to lead impactful quality and risk management initiatives while supporting our mission of providing accessible, compassionate healthcare to communities throughout Illinois.

Apply today and become part of the CHP team!

title: Linux Systems Administrator
description:
Job Title: Linux Systems Administrator

Job Category: Information Technology

Time Type: Full time

Minimum Clearance Required to Start: TS/SCI with Polygraph

Employee Type: Regular

Percentage of Travel Required: None

Type of Travel: None

* * *

We are seeking a highly skilled Linux Systems Administrator to support mission-critical enterprise infrastructure in a secure Department of Defense/Intelligence Community environment. The successful candidate will provide advanced systems administration, network infrastructure support, virtualization, automation, cybersecurity compliance, and enterprise systems maintenance while ensuring high availability, security, and operational readiness.

This position requires an experienced systems engineer capable of working independently, troubleshooting complex infrastructure issues, implementing secure enterprise solutions, and supporting highly classified operational environments.


Required Qualifications

  • Active TS/SCI clearance with a current Polygraph
  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field (additional relevant experience may be substituted for education)
  • 10+ years of progressive Systems Administration experience supporting enterprise IT infrastructure in secure Linux environments
  • DoD 8570/8140 IAT Level II certification (Security+, CySA+, CCNA Security, or equivalent)

Technical Requirements

Candidates should possess strong experience in several of the following areas:

  • Administration and support of Cisco ASA, Cisco Firepower, and Palo Alto firewalls, including security policy management, troubleshooting, and enterprise firewall administration.
  • Configuration, implementation, and maintenance of IPSEC VPNs, secure VPN tunneling (including ASA-to-ASA connectivity), and secure enterprise networking.
  • Administration of VMware or comparable virtualization platforms, including virtual machine provisioning, maintenance, performance tuning, and lifecycle management.
  • Experience developing automation solutions using Python and/or Bash, with hands-on implementation of Ansible and Ansible Playbooks for infrastructure provisioning, configuration management, and operational efficiency.
  • Strong knowledge of enterprise server administration across Windows and Linux platforms, system hardening, patch management, and infrastructure support.
  • Experience performing IAVA patching, vulnerability remediation, STIG implementation, and maintaining compliance with DoD cybersecurity requirements.
  • Working knowledge of Secure The Enterprise (STE) and Secure The Network (STN) processes and security initiatives.
  • Experience utilizing Nessus for vulnerability scanning, analysis, remediation, and continuous security monitoring.
  • Hands-on experience with hardware installation, rack and stack, structured cabling, equipment deployment, and maintaining accurate infrastructure documentation and network diagrams.
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex systems, networks, and security issues while supporting highly available enterprise environments.


Preferred Qualifications

Experience with one or more of the following is highly desirable:

  • Containerization technologies including Docker and Kubernetes
  • Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and configuration management best practices
  • Enterprise monitoring and logging solutions (Splunk, Elastic, SolarWinds, etc.)
  • Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, PKI, LDAP, and certificate management
  • Disaster recovery, backup technologies, and high-availability architectures
  • Cisco (CCNA/CCNP), Palo Alto (PCNSA/PCNSE), VMware (VCP), Red Hat (RHCSA), or equivalent technical certifications

This position is contingent on funding and may not be filled immediately. However, this position is representative of positions within CACI that are consistently available. Individuals who apply may also be considered for other positions at CACI.

What You Can Expect:

A culture of integrity.

At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.

title: National Account Director
description:
The National Account Director is responsible and accountable for the AZ business, product access, profitability, and strategic account management across a defined group of accounts, as well as, ensuring access alignment across the vertically aligned accounts in partnership with the Upstream National Account Director.

The focus of the National Account Director is to create profitable access for AstraZeneca’s portfolio by positively influencing the appropriate formulary placement of AstraZeneca medicines, treatment algorithms, pharmacy policies and medical policies. This includes leading end to end profitable contract negotiations and terms, monitoring performance and optimizing terms to support both patient access and the business objectives.


This role requires deep market insight across therapeutic areas, cross-functional collaboration, and strong external engagement to shape strategy, mitigate access and profitability risks and maximize opportunity across therapeutic areas.

The National Account Director maintains proficiency in marketplace trends, policies, dynamics to stay ahead of any shift in customer business needs and innovative opportunities that are mutually beneficial. The Account Director must facilitate both internal and external stakeholder management.

Typical Accountabilities:

Access & Profitability

  • Deliver on Access and Profitability Goals across assigned accounts
  • Develop and execute tailored access strategies that align with portfolio priorities
  • Lead full contract lifecycle: strategy, negotiation, execution and performance monitoring

Strategic Account Management

  • Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders across accounts across (Trade Directors, Pharmacy, Medical Oncology, CVRM, Resp, Client Services, Case Management, and with internal cross-functional partners that cover additional organizations that influence the account (provider groups, hospital systems, regional payers).
  • Understand and influence customer decision-making to secure favorable formulary and policy positions
  • Leverage data and analytics to inform strategy and optimize contract outcomes

Cross Functional Leadership

  • Collaborate with internal partners (e.g. Portfolio Contract strategy, Access Strategy,Field Reimbursement Team, BBU/OBU teams)
  • Represent the full AZ business at assigned accounts, including sales, market share, rebates, invoicing, and competitive activity
  • Stay ahead of market trends, policy shifts, and customer needs to identify innovative, mutually beneficial opportunities

Travel

  • Travel as needed for customer meetings, conferences and internal collaboration
  • Occasional International Travel may be required

Essential Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree required
  • 8+ years of pharmaceutical or healthcare experience
  • Thorough understanding of market dynamics across multiple therapeutic areas and across various business segments
  • Proven experience in account management, customer facing engagement and cross-functional stakeholder management
  • Strong understanding of the broader healthcare managed markets, legislative environment and ability to strategically apply that knowledge to targeted accounts through development and implementation to accomplish business objectives
  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in a matrix organization and influence senior leaders and peers to shape and execute account strategy
  • Excellent communication, analytical and project management skills
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities across diverse functions and therapeutic areas
  • Experience with organized customers preferably at the C-Suite level
  • Ability to learn and effectively communicate with customer’s detailed clinical information regarding AZ and competitive medicines.​

Desirable:

  • Account management experience with proven negotiation proficiency
  • Managed Care/Market Access Experience
  • Oncology and specialty care marketplace experience reimbursement model
  • Understanding of financial concepts and contracting issues including legal and best price implications
  • Prior experience in sales management
  • Conflict Resolution Skills

title: Senior Developer (MEAN/MERN Stack + AI tools)
description:

Oliver Wyman

Senior Developer (MEAN/MERN Stack + AI tools)

  • Contribute to application development activities to implement new and improve existing web applications that provide direct and measurable value to our users.
  • Build and enhance reliable, scalable software solutions with guidance from senior engineers and architects.
  • Translate requirements through an iterative development process into high-quality code.
  • Write reusable, testable and efficient code and follow secure coding best practices.
  • Participate in code reviews and incorporate feedback to improve code quality and engineering skills.
  • Work with product owners, stakeholders and other engineers to understand requirements, evaluate options and deliver pragmatic solutions.
  • Contribute to software engineering best practices, knowledge sharing, tools and technology evolution, and standards.
  • Work closely with end-users and business staff to investigate and resolve system issues.
  • Learn and apply the technologies underlying current and future enterprise systems.

What you need to have:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, systems analysis or a related field of study, or equivalent training/experience.
  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including internships, co-ops or equivalent hands-on development experience.
  • Working knowledge of modern full stack development technologies, including but not limited to:
  • TypeScript and JavaScript for Node.js web applications, including frameworks such as Express, Angular, or React
  • APIs using REST and/or GraphQL (Apollo)
  • Fundamental understanding of modern system architecture patterns
  • Data management principles and experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases
  • Agile software development practices, source control and continuous integration
  • Using AI-assisted development tools to support design, coding, testing or documentation
  • Writing unit tests and exposure to integration and end-to-end automated testing
  • Basic understanding of DevOps concepts, CI/CD pipelines and tools

What makes you stand out?

  • Exposure to extract, transform and load (ETL) tools or data integration patterns is a plus.
  • Exposure to mobile application development is a plus.
  • Experience working with data flows between databases, APIs and applications is a plus.
  • Cloud, AI or relevant open source technology certifications are a plus.

Why join our team:

  • We help you be your best through professional development opportunities, interesting work and supportive leaders.
  • We foster a vibrant and inclusive culture where you can work with talented colleagues to create new solutions and have impact for colleagues, clients and communities.
  • Our scale enables us to provide a range of career opportunities, as well as benefits and rewards to enhance your well-being.

Marsh (NYSE: MRSH) is a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. description:

The Princess Grace Hospital, London

Full Time, 37.5 hrs/week

13hr shifts (7am to 8pm during the week and Saturdays 8am to 6pm), working 6 on 7 off

Permanent contract

Salary - £28,860 + excellent benefits (pension, health cover, flexible benefits and excellent career development)


We have an exciting role for a Sterile Services Technician to join our team at The Princess Grace Hospital. You will be responsible for providing a comprehensive service of sterile instrument sets and singularly packed instruments for the treatment of patients in theatres and departments located at The Princess Grace Hospital.

In your role as a Sterile Services Technician you will understand the Infection Control requirements in relation to patient care and medical devices.

Above all else, we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life. It’s this guiding vision that influences everything we do at HCA UK.   • Always adhere to the Quality System in operation which is the base for the Departmental Accreditation
  • Repack instrument trays as necessary
  • Monitor output to ensure sterilisation is complete and that standard trays are complete with all instruments present

What you'll bring:

  • Experience working in a sterile services department
  • Knowledge of relevant hospital policies and procedures either within the NHS or private hospital setting
  • Health and Safety training including Lifting and Handling training
  • A real team player who has excellent communication, attention to detail and the ability to recognise and report faults in equipment

Originally founded over 50 years ago by Dr Thomas Frist, HCA has gone on to become one of the world’s leading healthcare providers. In the UK, we’re one of the largest providers of privately funded healthcare and have invested over £500 million in the latest treatments, technology, techniques, medication and facilities. Being part of a large multisite, established healthcare group we can offer you unrivalled opportunities for career progression through internal and external courses, as well as working conditions that prioritise both your mental and physical wellbeing.

By caring for our employees, we empower them to provide exceptional care for our patients. That’s why we offer a host of flexible benefits that reflect the invaluable contribution they make every day. As a Sterile Services Technician, you’ll be eligible for:

  • Critical illness cover
  • Enhanced Maternity and Paternity pay
  • Corporate staff discount for all facilities including Maternity packages at The Portland
  • Comprehensive range of flexible health, protection and lifestyle benefits to suit you

Culture and values

At HCA UK we believe exceptional care starts with our people. We celebrate the unique perspectives and different experiences each of us bring as we know that when you feel seen, heard and supported you can be at your best for our patients, and each other.

Our mission is simple, above all else we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life, a clear statement that extends to both our patients and colleagues. To achieve this, we live and breathe four core values:

title: Claims Control Clerk
description:
ABOUT INSURANCE ADMINISTRATIVE SOLUTIONS
Insurance Administrative Solutions (IAS) is a third-party provider of comprehensive administrative solutions for our clients in the insurance industry. We offer a business process outsourcing solution that helps insurers optimize administrative workload, bolster their industry expertise, leverage emerging technologies, and streamline operations. Here at IAS, we embrace the fact that great things are only accomplished by working as a team. We believe that all of our employees have valuable input no matter the level. Job Summary:

The Claims Control Clerk is responsible for maintaining control of all mail delivered from the mailroom by logging in each batch under the appropriate client code and delivering all batches to the correct areas that may not be scanned into AWD. Faxes and re-batches coming from the claim or customer service area are batched and delivered to designated individuals for processing. Inventory reports are run daily, and information is communicated to claim managers and supervisors, after logging completed claim information in Daily Operation Statistic and inventory tracking reports. title: Deployment Strategist
description:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Sales

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Job Description


Intro

We're Salesforce, the Customer Company, inspiring the future of business with AI + Data + CRM. Leading with our core values, we help companies across every industry blaze new trails and connect with customers in a whole new way. And we empower you to be a Trailblazer too, driving your performance and career growth, charting new paths, and improving the state of the world. If you believe in business as the greatest platform for change and in companies doing well and doing good, you've come to the right place.


About the Role

Customer impact from day one. Strategic clarity and Execution that sticks.


Salesforce is hiring Deployment Strategists — Strategic Builders who are customer-facing advisors, who define AI strategy, shape agentic solutions, and drive measurable adoption for enterprise customers. You'll work as part of a delivery team alongside Forward Deployed Engineers, translating complex business challenges into agentic AI deployments that go live and generate real value. Engagements are focused and time-bound — typically 12 weeks or less — and may span a single strategic account or multiple customers simultaneously. Your impact isn't just getting to deployment. It ensures customers realise lasting, scalable value from the solutions your team builds.


Key Responsibilities

  • Full Lifecycle Ownership: Lead end-to-end customer engagement across the complete value lifecycle — Identify → Commit → Deploy → Consume — owning outcomes at every stage, not just discovery or deal closure
  • AI Strategy & Architecture: Define the customer's Agentic AI strategy and roadmap. Lead design workshops, agent design sessions, and jobs-to-be-done analysis. Architect solutions spanning Salesforce's agentic AI platform, Data Cloud, and enterprise systems, with responsible AI governance baked in from the start.
  • Deployment Oversight & Program Management: Manage engagement delivery end-to-end timelines, stakeholder communication, risk escalation, and progress reporting. You are the operational backbone of your delivery team, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks.
  • Adoption & Consumption: Own adoption, consumption, and expansion metrics within your engagement scope. Identify blockers early and develop strategies to drive measurable value realization
  • Delivery Team Coordination: Partner closely with the Forward Deployed Engineers on your team to align strategy with technical execution. Keep the team focused, unblocked, and on track to hit delivery milestones.
  • AI-Supported Development: You'll be developing real customer solutions supported by leading-edge AI tools: Including
  • Cursor, Claude, and our coding products like Vibes, to accelerate development.
  • Customer Stakeholder Management: Serve as the primary customer-facing contact, building trust-based relationships with senior stakeholders and present proposals, decisions and outcomes in terms of business value, not just technical detail.
  • AI Readiness: Assess customer readiness for AI adoption and guide change management and process transformation to maximise the benefits of intelligent agents
  • Product Feedback Loop: Synthesise field insights and translate them into actionable product feedback that influences Salesforce's Agentic AI platform roadmap.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years experience in strategic solutioning, technical advisory, or delivery leadership or programme management for enterprise cloud or SaaS technology
  • You have a degree in Computer Science or a related field
  • Prior customer-facing delivery experience (consulting, professional services, or technical advisory) - this is a requirement, not a nice-to-have
  • Demonstrated understanding of the Salesforce platform and ecosystem, including Agentic AI capabilities and Data Cloud
  • Working knowledge of one or more programming languages: Python, JavaScript, Java, or Apex
  • Proven ability to lead and own complex, ambiguous engagements end-to-end — from discovery through to measurable outcomes
  • Experience leading AI/LLM solution design, including agentic AI strategy, conversation design, and responsible AI practices
  • Strong project and programme management skills — ability to run multiple workstreams, manage stakeholder expectations, and keep delivery on track in ambiguous environments

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Role Overview

We are looking for a technically strong Security Governance professional who can bridge the gap between Security & Compliance requirements and Engineering implementation.


This role will serve as the technical voice and face of Assurance. You will partner closely with Engineering organizations, PCLs, Product Security, Legal, and other stakeholders to understand how security and compliance requirements are implemented in real systems. You will identify what is working and what is not, and translate those insights back into practical, scalable governance requirements.


The successful candidate will understand systems and architectures deeply enough to move beyond validating whether a control exists. They will evaluate how the control is designed, implemented, operated, and scaled across the enterprise.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Bridge Assurance and Engineering - Serve as a technical liaison between Assurance, Engineering, Product Security, PCLs, Legal, and other stakeholders, ensuring governance requirements are technically feasible, understandable, and implementable.
  • Evaluate Control Implementation - Work directly with Engineering teams to understand how security and compliance controls are implemented within applications, platforms, infrastructure, cloud environments, and engineering workflows.
  • Create the Engineering Feedback Loop - Assess what is working, what is creating unnecessary friction, and where controls or requirements are unclear or difficult to operationalize. Feed those insights back into control design, standards, and governance processes.
  • Make Requirements Engineer-Usable - Translate regulatory, compliance, and security expectations into clear, actionable technical requirements that Engineering teams can consistently implement and validate.
  • Develop Second-Line Oversight - Develop second-line oversight protocols that independently monitor, audit, and validate that all security controls are operational across engineering teams in Salesforce (e.g., attestations, CRE checks).
  • Understand Systems End-to-End - Develop a deep understanding of key platforms, architectures, engineering processes, security capabilities, and control implementations to help Assurance make better risk and compliance decisions.
  • Assess Risk in M&A - Assess control and risk exposure during M&As. Design the assessment to price risk, evaluate compatibility, and deliver an executable activation plan tied back to the risk model.
  • Partner on Emerging Security Requirements - Collaborate with Product Security, Legal, PCEs, Market Enablement, and other teams to understand emerging requirements and determine how they should translate into future security controls and engineering expectations.
  • Track the Direction of Compliance Frameworks - Monitor where regulatory and compliance expectations are heading, including AI governance, the EU AI Act, evolving international requirements, and market-specific regulatory expectations. Proactively identify implications for the organization.
  • Drive Change Management and Enablement - Build the change management, training, and communication needed to shift teams from "go find and interpret a policy" to "know precisely what applies and how to comply."
  • Run Control Incident Management - Stand up a formal incident management practice for control failures. Include postmortems, root-cause analysis, and error budgets for controls, modeled on availability incident response.
  • Influence Future Control Design - Partner with control owners and technical teams to evolve controls based on new technologies, regulatory expectations, architecture changes, and lessons learned from implementation.
  • Drive Security Champion Engagement - Build strong relationships with technical stakeholders across Engineering. Establish a network of security/control champions who can provide implementation feedback, promote requirements, and help scale governance across teams.
  • Report to Executive Leadership - Report on control reliability, coverage, pressure, and systemic risk trends to executive leadership. Feed findings back to the control framework for continuous improvement.
  • Represent Assurance Across Technical Organizations - Act as a trusted technical representative for Assurance in architecture, engineering, security, and governance discussions. Help ensure Assurance is involved early rather than only during audit or compliance validation.

What we're looking for:

  • U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residency required. We're unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role.
  • Strong technical background in security engineering, cloud security, product security, IAM, platform engineering, or security architecture.
  • Ability to understand complex systems, architectures, APIs, infrastructure, cloud environments, and software development processes.
  • Experience translating security, risk, regulatory, or compliance requirements into technical implementation requirements.
  • Strong understanding of security controls and frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, SOC, SOX, FedRAMP, or similar frameworks.
  • Familiarity with emerging technology and regulatory areas such as AI security, AI governance, privacy, and evolving global technology regulations.
  • Ability to work effectively with Engineering while also partnering with Legal, Compliance, Security, Risk, and business stakeholders.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical implementation details to governance teams and translate governance expectations into language Engineering teams can act on.
  • Ability to challenge existing requirements constructively and recommend improvements based on technical realities and risk.
  • Experience with independent control testing, assurance or audit practices, incident or root-cause analysis, or M&A due diligence is a plus.

What Success Looks Like:

Success in this role means creating a strong connection between what Assurance requires and what Engineering can effectively implement. Controls become more technically relevant, and requirements become easier for Engineering teams to consume. Implementation challenges are identified earlier, and emerging security and regulatory expectations are incorporated into the control environment before they become compliance gaps. Control failures are handled with the same rigor as availability incidents, and leadership has clear visibility into control reliability and systemic risk.


Ultimately, this role will help move Assurance from primarily validating compliance to becoming a technical governance partner that actively shapes secure and compliant engineering practices by design.

title: Director, Capital Solutions
description:
RFG Advisory is an innovator in the wealth management industry, partnering with independent financial Advisors across the country and backed by leading private equity investors. The firm is focused on aggressive, disciplined growth through a combination of organic initiatives and strategic acquisitions, and is building a best-in-class corporate development and capital solutions function to support that journey.


The Director, Capital Solutions is a high-visibility, high-expectation role for someone with investment banking, private equity, or corporate development training who can generate and execute strategic transactions as part of RFG's Capital Solutions program. You will own three core areas: sourcing minority investments and tuck-in acquisitions, executing deals from term sheet to close, and serving as the primary Capital Solutions expert for the business development team. The ideal candidate is exceptional at financial modeling and presentation-building, has flawless verbal and written skills, and is comfortable leading senior-level discussions with Advisors with limited supervision.


Location: This role can be in our Birmingham office or remote.

  • If in Birmingham, AL, our office works a hybrid schedule (3 days in-office, 2 remote).
  • If remote, occasional travel to Birmingham will be required including onboarding.


Reports to: Chief Financial Officer

﻿

﻿What You'll Do


Deal Origination & Market Development

  • Build and own a proprietary sourcing engine for tuck-in acquisitions within RFG's existing Advisor base, systematically identifying, prioritizing, and engaging Advisors who are candidates to sell, merge, or consolidate their practices.
  • Coordinate with the business development team to develop a structured pipeline for minority and majority investment opportunities, including target identification, outreach cadence, CRM tracking, and conversion analytics.
  • Cultivate relationships with Advisors, investment bankers, custodians, recruiters, and industry intermediaries to generate proprietary, off-market deal flow.
  • Conduct ongoing market mapping of the independent Advisor landscape to surface actionable acquisition and capital solutions opportunities.


﻿Deal Execution

  • Partner with leadership, finance, and business development teams to structure and advance Capital Solutions opportunities for Advisors in the recruiting pipeline.
  • Build and maintain transaction models including DCF, accretion/dilution, and returns analysis for potential acquisitions, capital investments, and Advisor deals.
  • Analyze target firms' financials, client bases, and business models to support valuation, structuring, and risk assessment.
  • Assist with deal structuring across earn-outs, seller notes, equity structures, and revenue shares, and support transaction execution from term sheet to definitive legal documentation.
  • Prepare IC-style memos, deal summaries, and supporting exhibits for internal and external stakeholders.


﻿Sales Enablement

  • Present the RFG Capital Solutions value proposition credibly to Advisor teams, articulating our programs and the broader RFG story with conviction and gravitas.
  • Build Advisor-level pro-forma models that show economics under RFG's platform versus an Advisor's current economics, and translate deal terms into clear, intuitive financial outputs Advisors can understand.
  • Create and refine pitch materials and presentation decks that combine numbers, narrative, and visuals into a compelling Capital Solutions and RFG story.
  • Partner with the business development team to continuously improve templates, assumptions, and messaging using AI-based automation techniques.

Requirements

Experience

  • 5-10 years of experience in investment banking, private equity, corporate development, or consulting.
  • At least 2-4 years of experience in a similar role at an acquisitive wealth management firm or broker-dealer actively pursuing M&A, minority investments, or Advisor consolidation; required and non-negotiable.
  • Demonstrated experience sourcing high-quality investment and M&A opportunities.
  • Proven track record building detailed models to support minority investments or M&A.
  • Experience generating management or IC-style presentations for senior internal and external stakeholders.


﻿Skills & Competencies

  • Strong understanding of corporate finance, valuation, and complex investment and M&A transaction structures, and the execution process from term sheet to closing.
  • Confident, professional communicator able to sell RFG's capital solutions programs and the broader RFG story to financial Advisors with credibility and gravitas.
  • Exceptional written and verbal skills; able to write clear memos, crisp email updates, and concise commentary for senior executives.
  • High ownership mentality; treats the firm's resources and investments with individual responsibility and accountability for outcomes.
  • Eager to proactively network, attend industry events, and identify opportunities rather than waiting for deals to come to you.
  • Able to turn around complex work products quickly without sacrificing accuracy or quality.
  • Highly organized, reliable, and comfortable managing multiple workstreams simultaneously.
  • Deeply curious about new concepts and technologies, including AI, that can enhance corporate development processes.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and evolving priorities in a fast-paced, PE-backed environment.


﻿Technology & Tools

  • Outstanding Excel skills including fully-linked 3-statement models, sensitivity and scenario analysis, debt schedules, waterfalls, and returns analysis.
  • PowerPoint power user; able to create clean, executive-ready decks with strong structure and visuals.
  • Experience leveraging AI tools including Claude, ChatGPT, or Microsoft Copilot to build financial models, design processes, and conduct data analysis.


﻿Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Engineering, or a related quantitative field.
  • CFA (Level I, II, or III), MBA, or CA designation is a strong plus.

Company

RFG Advisory is a platform for growth-minded Independent Advisors who want to scale without compromise. We're building the RIA of the Future-powered by innovation, collaboration, and execution. We take care of each other first. We show up with servant hearts and growth mindsets. We lead boldly, iterate to excellence, and commit to getting 1% better every day. title: X-Ray / Mammography Technologist
description:

Operates radiologic equipment and performs mammography procedures to assist physicians in the diagnosis of disease. Records the outcomes of results and presents the results and patient history to the physician for his or her interpretation.

  • Explains procedures to the patient to reduce anxieties and obtains patient cooperation.

  • Participates in department specific Quality Assurance programs. Complies with OSHA, universal precautions, and Exposure Control Plan.
  • Maintains patient confidentiality at all times.
  • Processes routine paperwork.
  • Participates in professional development activities and maintains professional affiliations.
  • Prepares all required reports and data pursuant to State requirements.
  • Assists the Radiologist with quality assurance reporting.
  • Attends in-services, meetings, and mandatory trainings as required.
  • Execute verbal and/or written specific assigned tasks requiring similar or lesser skills and abilities some of which are continuing while others are occasional in nature.

  • Planning and strategic foresight
  • Responsible Decision Making
  • Integrity and accountability
  • Innovation and creativity
  • Adaptive and flexible
  • Leadership, teamwork, and conflict resolution

Work Environment

Work is performed in an office environment. Involves frequent personal and telephone contact with patients, physicians, and other healthcare personnel. Work may be stressful at times. Interaction with others is constant and interruptive.

Travel outside of Northshore locations will be rare for this position.

TransUnion's Global Security team protects the company's employees, facilities, operations, critical assets, and reputation across its global footprint. The team develops enterprise security standards, manages risk and resilience programs, and partners across the business to support safe and uninterrupted operations.

This role reports to the Vice President, Global Security.

This is a hybrid position and involves regular performance of job responsibilities virtually as well as in-person at an assigned TU office location for a minimum of two days a week.

Role Overview and Core Responsibilities

  • Lead the design, implementation, and ongoing management of enterprise-wide global security programs, including travel risk, emergency preparedness, physical security, facility safety, event risk, personnel security, crisis management, and security awareness.
  • Build, operate, and continuously enhance the Global Security Operations Center (GSOC), establishing clear operating procedures, escalation protocols, service standards, and performance measures.
  • Oversee global physical security technology and life-safety capabilities, including access control, CCTV, visitor management, intrusion detection, and related building systems.
  • Develop and maintain global security policies, standards, controls, and reporting aligned with ISO 27001 physical security requirements, applicable regulations, and enterprise risk priorities.
  • Direct security incident and emergency response, including footage review, investigations, executive protection, threat management, event security planning, and timely reporting to senior leadership.
  • Manage guard force and third-party security partners, including sourcing, contract governance, service performance, and procurements exceeding $1 million.
  • Develop and manage capital and operating budgets for global security programs, operations, personnel, and technology investments.
  • Partner with Facilities, Procurement, Information Security, Human Resources, Business Continuity, Legal, and regional leaders to assess risk and implement practical security solutions.

title: Research Regulatory Coordinator
description:
Job Description:

The purpose of this position is to provide regulatory research coordination to Intermountain research departments and to support research investigators, managers and directors as needed. The key responsibility of this position is to assure regulatory compliance with Institutional Review Board (IRB), sponsor, federal and state regulations pertaining to the protection of human subjects participating in research as according to Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and International Conference of Harmonization (ICH) guidelines.

Join our research team as a Regulatory Research Coordinator, where you’ll play a key role in supporting investigators and research leaders while helping ensure the highest standards of regulatory compliance and protection for research participants. This position coordinates IRB and regulatory activities in accordance with sponsor, federal and state requirements, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and ICH guidelines.

We’re looking for a collaborative, self-motivated professional who can work effectively both independently and as part of a team. Experience with IRB/regulatory submissions, physician investigators, or coordinating-center activities is highly valued.

This position supports a multi-year, grant-funded research project, with continued employment anticipated for the duration of the project and contingent upon ongoing grant funding and project needs.


Work Schedule

  • Hybrid role – Position requires on-site presence at times for training and meetings.
  • Core business hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.

Essential Functions

  • Research Coordination: Assist in the preparation, submission, and review of regulatory documents, including IRB applications, amendments, and single IRB submissions for multi-site studies. Ensure all study activities comply with regulatory requirements and institutional policies. Contacts and advises study staff and investigators in the preparation and completion of submissions.
  • Compliance Monitoring: Monitor ongoing studies to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, report adverse events, protocol deviations, unanticipated problems, and other events per institutional and sponsor reporting policies.
  • Record Maintenance: Ensures application(s), study approval(s) and other relevant study documentation and information up to date and in compliance with federal, state and institutional requirements. Maintains up to date files (paper and electronic) of all regulatory documents and correspondence. Responsible for meeting with auditors and monitors reviewing regulatory files as requested and/or required on an ongoing basis and/or during the conduct of the clinical investigations.
  • Communication: Communicate effectively with study sites, regulatory bodies, researchers, study teams, IRBs, sponsors, CROs, and other third parties. Acts as liaison to study teams to obtain necessary approvals and documentation.
  • Training Support: Assist in the training of research staff on regulatory requirements, procedures, and best practices. Provide ongoing education on federal policies and regulations impacting human subject’s research.
  • Meeting Coordination: Schedule and coordinate meetings related to study and regulatory compliance. Participate in site visits and audits conducted by sponsors, FDA, NIH, or other regulatory agencies.
  • Document Management: Assist in drafting, reviewing, and maintaining informed consent documents to ensure they meet regulatory standards. Create forms and templates or complete forms as needed to comply with GCP and FDA standards.
  • Regulatory Updates: Stay informed about changes in regulatory requirements and guidelines. Assist management in developing and executing institutional policies and procedures to ensure compliance with federal, state, and local laws and regulations related to research.

Skills

  • Accountability
  • Critical Thinking
  • Work collaboratively
  • Verbal and Written Communication
  • Detail-oriented
  • Prioritization
  • Time-management
  • Proficient in Microsoft
  • Writing
  • Regulatory

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience in a role requiring effective organizational skills; effective follow-through, and commitment to excellence, effective professional communication skills: Ability to communicate with others in a clear, understandable, and professional manner as well as strong interpersonal skills: Ability to work with personnel at all levels to gather information, communicate compliance requirements and handle complex issues within an often-sensitive political environment.
  • Experience working collaboratively in a team environment.
  • Experience using word processing, spreadsheet, database, internet and e-mail and scheduling applications.
  • Demonstrated years’ experience in a regulatory, compliance, healthcare or research role.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in a clinical or life science field, business, or healthcare operations. A degree must be obtained through an accredited institution. Education is verified.
  • Regulatory and compliance experience.
  • Experience in a healthcare or hospital setting.
  • Experience in a role requiring detailed knowledge of human subject research regulations, strong attention to detail and ability to adhere to policies and procedures.

Physical Requirements

  • Interact with others by effectively communicating, both orally and in writing.
  • Frequent interactions with providers, colleagues, customers, patients/clients and visitors that require employees to verbally communicate as well as hear and understand spoken information, needs, and issues quickly and accurately.
  • Manual dexterity of hands and fingers to manipulate complex and delicate equipment with precision and accuracy. This includes frequent computer use for typing, accessing needed information, etc.
  • Ongoing need for employee to see and read information, labels, monitors, identify equipment and supplies, and be able to assess customer needs.

  • May require lifting and transporting objects and office supplies, bending, kneeling and reaching.

title: HR Analyst
description:

Location: Bengaluru

About Ceres India

At Ceres India Private Limited, we support initiatives that help communities recover, rebuild, and strengthen resilience. As part of the Ceres Global network of companies, we contribute to disaster recovery, infrastructure restoration, environmental services, and critical response operations through engineering, technology, innovation, and operational excellence. From India, we help enable faster decisions, stronger delivery, and meaningful outcomes where they matter most. The purpose is at the core of what we do. What to Expect

This is a fast-paced, detail-oriented role focused on delivering a seamless onboarding experience for new hires across the US. title: Director of Data & Performance
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:

The Director of Data & Performance serves as the City’s leader for data-informed decision-making, organizational performance, analytics, and data strategy. The Director leads the Data & Performance division, including the City’s GIS and Business Analytics teams, and manages a citywide portfolio that connects performance management, data governance, program and policy evaluation, process improvement, and emerging technology. Working closely with executive leadership, department directors, and partners across the City, the Director translates complex information into action, helps shape priorities and investments, and builds the systems, practices, and capabilities that improve City operations and outcomes for residents.

You’re the right fit for the position if:

  • You translate complex problems and information into practical, actionable strategies.
  • You move comfortably between executive conversations, operational details, and technical discussions.
  • You build trust, bring people together, and influence across teams even when you do not have direct authority.
  • You balance strategic thinking with practical execution and can lead through ambiguity and change.
  • You are energized by helping others use data, technology, and continuous improvement to deliver better results.

The position reports to the Chief Innovation Officer and is part of the Department of Innovation & Technology. I&T is a nationally recognized government technology and innovation team working at the intersection of digital transformation, analytics, resident experience, and organizational performance. Team members partner directly with City leaders and departments to solve meaningful community challenges, modernize services, and improve quality of life for South Bend residents. Candidates who thrive in the Department bring curiosity, sound judgment, a customer-service mindset, and a commitment to learning. Learn more about the Department here: .

As a leader and employee of the City of South Bend, you are called upon to serve in a manner that supports our core values: Excellence, Accountability, Innovation, Inclusion, and Empowerment as you carry out our primary employee expectations: champion values & organizational pride, champion operational excellence, make sound decisions, embrace coaching and accountability, communicate with excellence, value diverse people and perspectives, embrace personal development, exhibit a positive attitude and own your health, wellness & safety.

SUPERVISION EXERCISED:

Applicable

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

This list represents the types of duties required by the position. Other duties may be assigned as reasonably expected:

  • Lead, manage, and develop the Data & Performance division, including the Business Analytics and GIS teams.
  • Lead the City’s data and performance portfolio, aligning analytics, GIS, data governance, and emerging technologies with organizational priorities.
  • Advise executive leadership and department leaders by translating data, research, and operational insights into clear recommendations, priorities, and investment decisions.
  • Lead the City’s performance management program and strengthen how department leadership set goals, measure progress, evaluate results, and act on findings.
  • Partner across departments to evaluate City operations, programs, services, and policies and identify opportunities for actionable improvement.
  • Establish and maintain standards for data governance, quality, integrity, access, documentation, privacy, and responsible use.
  • Guide the discovery and selection of technology platforms, analytics tools, automation, and artificial intelligence capabilities that improve City operations and resident services.
  • Facilitate organizational change using human-centered design, service design, process improvement, and continuous improvement methods.
  • Manage a portfolio of complex, cross-functional initiatives; set priorities, allocate team capacity, monitor risks and outcomes, and communicate progress to stakeholders.
  • Build data literacy and organizational capability by developing practical tools, standards, training, and partnerships that help City teams make better decisions.

NON-ESSENTIAL/MARGINAL FUNCTIONS:

Perform other duties and assume other responsibilities as apparent or as assigned.

EDUCATION / QUALIFICATIONS:

To perform this position successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty in a satisfactory manner. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience in public administration, business, analytics, data science, statistics, information management, social science, public policy, organizational improvement, or a related field.
  • Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in analytics, performance management, organizational improvement, public-sector innovation, consulting, program evaluation, or a related field.
  • Experience leading teams, major initiatives, or complex cross-functional projects from strategy through implementation.
  • Experience advising leaders and communicating complex information, risks, and recommendations to technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships, facilitate decision-making, and guide stakeholders through change.
  • Experience in local government, public service, civic technology, or a mission-driven organization is preferred but not required.

KNOWLEDGE SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Strategic leadership, sound judgment, and the ability to connect long-term direction with practical execution.
  • Strong people leadership, coaching, project and portfolio management, and organizational skills.
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, facilitation, written communication, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to establish effective working relationships with employees, executive leaders, elected officials, community partners, vendors, and the public.
  • Ability to influence without direct authority, align diverse stakeholders, manage change, and navigate competing demands.
  • Working knowledge of data governance, performance measurement, program evaluation, data management, privacy, and responsible data use.
  • Familiarity with GIS platforms such as Esri; analytics methods and tools such as SQL or Python; and business intelligence tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
  • Familiarity with automation, artificial intelligence, database systems, human-centered design, service design, or continuous improvement methods is preferred.
  • Ability to build organizational capability through clear standards, practical guidance, training, and coaching.
  • Ability to work with sensitive information and apply appropriate safeguards for privacy, security, and confidentiality.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSE, REGISTRATION:

Valid Driver’s license required.

EQUIPMENT:

Desktop computer or laptop, telephone, fax, copy machine, scanner.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit and walk, and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to walk; use hands to fingers, handle or feel objects, tools or controls; and reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required in this job include vision and the ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Work is performed in an office setting with moderate inside temperatures. The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet to moderate in the office. Entire office is smoke free.

This position is based in South Bend, Indiana. This position is eligible for hybrid work in the Department of Innovation & Technology, as long as engagement with city teams and work performance remains high.

DISCLAIMER:

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required of personnel so classified. Nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. The City of South Bend is an at will employer.

REQUIRED:

  • Pre-Employment Drug Screen
  • Employee Background check

Essential Duty: Uphold Core Values

All employees of the City of South Bend are expected to uphold and actively demonstrate the City's Core Values in their daily work, which are summarized below:

  • Excellence – Deliver high-quality service and strive for continuous improvement.
  • Accountability – Take ownership of responsibilities and outcomes.
  • Innovation – Seek creative solutions and embrace new ideas.
  • Inclusion – Promote a respectful, equitable, and welcoming environment.
  • Empowerment – Support and encourage others to grow and succeed.

This duty is fundamental to fostering a positive workplace culture and delivering exceptional public service. These values shape our culture, inform our decisions, and inspire our work every day.

description:
BANK Food and Beverage Assistant

The Harborne Hospital, Birmingham

Shifts between 630am - 9pm, Monday - Sunday

£12.71/ hour


Great service doesn’t change just because the setting does. If you’ve worked in hospitality, retail or any role where people come first, you’ll know the difference a thoughtful interaction can make. And in a hospital, those moments matter even more. As a BANK Food and Beverage Assistant, you’ll bring the same pride, attention to detail and care you’d offer any customer to our patients, supporting them with high-quality, freshly prepared meals and helping them feel well looked after throughout their stay.

Whether you’re guiding someone through the menu or delivering their food with care and attention, you’ll help create an experience that feels calm, personal and reassuring. Our food is prepared to an exceptional standard, and you’ll play a key part in presenting it with the warmth and professionalism it deserves. It takes a special kind of person to do this role, but if you naturally bring a warmth and confidence to the way you interact with others, we’re confident you’ll fit right in here.

Above all else, we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life. It’s this guiding vision that influences everything we do at HCA UK. From the CEO to the colleagues on the floor we all have a part to play in delivering exceptional care to our patients. Other’s may think this is just a role in Hotel Services but to us, you’ll be part of a wider team with a unique sense of purpose, one that helps improve lives on a daily basis.


What you’ll do:

You’ll deliver a standard of service no different to a high-end hotel or restaurant, where the focus is on being attentive and giving people a positive experience. Meals are an important part of any hospital stay, and you’ll help make that experience smooth and comfortable by:

  • Helping patients choose meals, taking orders and delivering food across the hospital
  • Preparing and collecting meal trays promptly
  • Answering phone requests and communicating dietary needs to the kitchen
  • Keeping work areas clean, washing utensils and maintaining hygiene standards
  • Recording additional requests and following all allergen and dietary safety policies

What we’re looking for:

We’re looking for someone who puts people first - someone who knows how to support others in a busy environment and can bring that confidence into patient-facing conversations. As well as this, you’ll:

  • Have previous hospitality, retail or customer-service experience
  • Be confident in speaking with patients and colleagues
  • Take pride in delivering warm, attentive service

  • Have a flexible, reliable approach during busy periods

Why HCA UK?

Originally founded over 50 years ago by Dr Thomas Frist, HCA has gone on to become one of the world’s leading healthcare providers. In the UK, we’re one of the largest providers of privately funded healthcare and have invested over £500 million in the latest treatments, technology, techniques, medication and facilities. Being part of a large multisite, established healthcare group we can offer you unrivalled opportunities for career progression through internal and external courses, as well as working conditions that prioritise both your mental and physical wellbeing.

By caring for our employees, we empower them to provide exceptional care for our patients. That’s why we offer a host of flexible benefits that reflect the invaluable contribution they make every day. As a BANK Food and Beverage Assistant you’ll be eligible for:


Culture and values

At HCA UK we believe exceptional care starts with our people. We celebrate the unique perspectives and different experiences each of us bring as we know that when you feel seen, heard and supported you can be at your best for our patients, and each other.

Our mission is simple, above all else we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life, a clear statement that extends to both our patients and colleagues. To achieve this, we live and breathe four core values:

  • Unique and Individual: We recognise and value everyone as unique and individual
  • Kindness and compassion: We treat people with kindness and compassion
  • Honesty, integrity and fairness: We act with absolute honesty, integrity and fairness
  • Loyalty, respect and dignity: We trust and treat one another as valued members of the HCA UK family with loyalty, respect and dignity

Reasonable adjustments

We believe everyone should feel comfortable to bring their full self to work and be afforded the same opportunities. As a Disability Confident committed organisation, we’re happy to discuss flexible working arrangements to suit your needs as well as offer reasonable adjustments throughout our recruitment process, and in the workplace, to anyone that needs them. Should you require any additional support with applying, please do get in touch.
